. Namo tassa bhagavato arahato sammāsambuddhassa.

Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Enlightened One.

Aṅguttaranikāyo

The Numerical Discourses of the Buddha

Dasakanipātapāḷi

The Book of the Tens

1. Paṭhamapaṇṇāsakaṃ

1. The First Fifty

1. Ānisaṃsavaggo

1. The Chapter on Benefits

1. Kimatthiyasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on What Purpose

1. Evaṃ [T 5.0001][V 3.0001][P 5.0001][M 3.0257] me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

1. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:

“Kimatthiyāni[V 3.0002], bhante, kusalāni sīlāni kimānisaṃsānī”ti? “Avippaṭisāratthāni kho, ānanda, kusalāni sīlāni avippaṭisārānisaṃsānī”ti.

“Venerable sir, for what purpose are wholesome virtues, and what is their benefit?” “Ānanda, wholesome virtues have non-remorse as their purpose and non-remorse as their benefit.”

“Avippaṭisāro pana, bhante, kimatthiyo kimānisaṃso”ti? “Avippaṭisāro kho, ānanda, pāmojjattho pāmojjānisaṃso”ti pāmujjattho pāmujjānisaṃsoti (sī. syā. pī.) a. ni. 11.1.

“But, venerable sir, what is the purpose and benefit of non-remorse?” “Ānanda, non-remorse has gladness as its purpose and gladness as its benefit.”

“Pāmojjaṃ pana, bhante, kimatthiyaṃ kimānisaṃsa”nti? “Pāmojjaṃ kho, ānanda, pītatthaṃ pītānisaṃsa”nti.

“But, venerable sir, what purpose does gladness have, and what is its benefit?” “Ānanda, gladness has rapture as its purpose and rapture as its benefit.”

“Pīti pana, bhante, kimatthiyā kimānisaṃsā”ti? “Pīti kho, ānanda, passaddhatthā passaddhānisaṃsā”ti.

“But, venerable sir, for what purpose is rapture? What is its benefit?” “Ānanda, rapture has tranquility as its purpose and tranquility as its benefit.”

“Passaddhi [M 3.0258] pana, bhante, kimatthiyā kimānisaṃsā”ti? “Passaddhi kho[T 5.0002], ānanda, sukhatthā sukhānisaṃsā”ti.

“But, venerable sir, for what purpose is tranquility? What is its benefit?” “Ānanda, tranquility has happiness as its purpose and happiness as its benefit.”

“Sukhaṃ pana, bhante, kimatthiyaṃ kimānisaṃsa”nti? “Sukhaṃ kho, ānanda, samādhatthaṃ samādhānisaṃsa”nti[P 5.0002].

“But, venerable sir, for what purpose is happiness, and what is its benefit?” “Ānanda, happiness has concentration as its purpose and concentration as its benefit.”

“Samādhi pana, bhante, kimatthiyo kimānisaṃso”ti? “Samādhi kho, ānanda, yathābhūtañāṇadassanattho yathābhūtañāṇadassanānisaṃso”ti.

“But, venerable sir, for what purpose is concentration, and what is its benefit?” “Ānanda, concentration has knowledge and vision of things as they truly are as its purpose, and knowledge and vision of things as they truly are as its benefit.”

“Yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṃ pana, bhante, kimatthiyaṃ kimānisaṃsa”nti? “Yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṃ kho, ānanda, nibbidāvirāgatthaṃ nibbidāvirāgānisaṃsa”nti.

“But, venerable sir, for what purpose is knowledge and vision of things as they truly are, and what is its benefit?” “Ānanda, knowledge and vision of things as they truly are has disenchantment and dispassion as its purpose and disenchantment and dispassion as its benefit.”

“Nibbidāvirāgo pana, bhante kimatthiyo kimānisaṃso”ti? “Nibbidāvirāgo kho, ānanda, vimuttiñāṇadassanattho vimuttiñāṇadassanānisaṃso … nisaṃsoti (sī. ka.).

“But, venerable sir, for what purpose are disenchantment and dispassion, and what is their benefit?” “Ānanda, disenchantment and dispassion have knowledge and vision of liberation as their purpose, and knowledge and vision of liberation as their benefit.”

“Iti kho, ānanda, kusalāni sīlāni avippaṭisāratthāni avippaṭisārānisaṃsāni; avippaṭisāro [V 3.0003] pāmojjattho pāmojjānisaṃso; pāmojjaṃ pītatthaṃ pītānisaṃsaṃ; pīti passaddhatthā passaddhānisaṃsā; passaddhi sukhatthā sukhānisaṃsā; sukhaṃ samādhatthaṃ samādhānisaṃsaṃ; samādhi yathābhūtañāṇadassanattho yathābhūtañāṇadassanānisaṃso; yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṃ nibbidāvirāgatthaṃ nibbidāvirāgānisaṃsaṃ; nibbidāvirāgo vimuttiñāṇadassanattho vimuttiñāṇadassanānisaṃso. Iti kho, ānanda, kusalāni sīlāni anupubbena aggāya parentī”ti arahattāya pūrentīti (syā.). Paṭhamaṃ.

“Thus, Ānanda, wholesome virtues have non-remorse as their purpose and non-remorse as their benefit; non-remorse has gladness as its purpose and gladness as its benefit; gladness has rapture as its purpose and rapture as its benefit; rapture has tranquility as its purpose and tranquility as its benefit; tranquility has happiness as its purpose and happiness as its benefit; happiness has concentration as its purpose and concentration as its benefit; concentration has knowledge and vision of things as they truly are as its purpose and knowledge and vision of things as they truly are as its benefit; knowledge and vision of things as they truly are has disenchantment and dispassion as its purpose and disenchantment and dispassion as its benefit; disenchantment and dispassion have knowledge and vision of liberation as their purpose and knowledge and vision of liberation as their benefit. Thus, Ānanda, wholesome virtues lead sequentially to the supreme goal.”

2. Cetanākaraṇīyasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Volition

2. a. ni. 11.2 “Sīlavato, bhikkhave, sīlasampannassa na cetanāya karaṇīyaṃ – ‘avippaṭisāro me uppajjatū’ti. Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṃ sīlavato sīlasampannassa avippaṭisāro uppajjati. Avippaṭisārissa, bhikkhave, na cetanāya karaṇīyaṃ – ‘pāmojjaṃ me uppajjatū’ti. Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṃ avippaṭisārissa pāmojjaṃ jāyati. Pamuditassa, bhikkhave, na cetanāya [T 5.0003] karaṇīyaṃ – ‘pīti me uppajjatū’ti. Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṃ pamuditassa pīti [P 5.0003] uppajjati. Pītimanassa, bhikkhave, na cetanāya karaṇīyaṃ – ‘kāyo me passambhatū’ti. Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṃ pītimanassa [M 3.0259] kāyo passambhati. Passaddhakāyassa, bhikkhave, na cetanāya karaṇīyaṃ – ‘sukhaṃ vediyāmī’ti. Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṃ passaddhakāyo sukhaṃ vediyati. Sukhino, bhikkhave, na cetanāya karaṇīyaṃ – ‘cittaṃ me samādhiyatū’ti. Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṃ sukhino cittaṃ samādhiyati. Samāhitassa, bhikkhave, na cetanāya karaṇīyaṃ – ‘yathābhūtaṃ jānāmi passāmī’ti. Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṃ samāhito yathābhūtaṃ jānāti passati. Yathābhūtaṃ, bhikkhave, jānato passato na cetanāya karaṇīyaṃ – ‘nibbindāmi virajjāmī’ti. Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṃ yathābhūtaṃ jānaṃ passaṃ nibbindati virajjati. Nibbinnassa nibbindassa (sī. ka.), bhikkhave, virattassa na cetanāya karaṇīyaṃ – ‘vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ sacchikaromī’ti. Dhammatā esā, bhikkhave, yaṃ nibbinno nibbindo (sī. ka.) viratto vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ sacchikaroti.

2. “Bhikkhus, for one who is virtuous, accomplished in virtue, it is not necessary to form the intention: ‘May non-remorse arise in me.’ It is the nature of things, bhikkhus, that non-remorse arises in one who is virtuous, accomplished in virtue. For one who has non-remorse, bhikkhus, it is not necessary to form the intention: ‘May gladness arise in me.’ It is the nature of things, bhikkhus, that gladness arises in one who has non-remorse. For one who is gladdened, bhikkhus, it is not necessary to form the intention: ‘May rapture arise in me.’ It is the nature of things, bhikkhus, that rapture arises in one who is gladdened. For one with a rapturous mind, bhikkhus, it is not necessary to form the intention: ‘May my body become tranquil.’ It is the nature of things, bhikkhus, that the body of one with a rapturous mind becomes tranquil. For one whose body is tranquil, bhikkhus, it is not necessary to form the intention: ‘May I feel happiness.’ It is the nature of things, bhikkhus, that one whose body is tranquil feels happiness. For one who is happy, bhikkhus, it is not necessary to form the intention: ‘May my mind become concentrated.’ It is the nature of things, bhikkhus, that the mind of one who is happy becomes concentrated. For one whose mind is concentrated, bhikkhus, it is not necessary to form the intention: ‘May I know and see things as they truly are.’ It is the nature of things, bhikkhus, that one whose mind is concentrated knows and sees things as they truly are. For one who knows and sees things as they truly are, bhikkhus, it is not necessary to form the intention: ‘May I become disenchanted and dispassionate.’ It is the nature of things, bhikkhus, that one who knows and sees things as they truly are becomes disenchanted and dispassionate. For one who is disenchanted and dispassionate, bhikkhus, it is not necessary to form the intention: ‘May I realize the knowledge and vision of liberation.’ It is the nature of things, bhikkhus, that one who is disenchanted and dispassionate realizes the knowledge and vision of liberation.”

“Iti kho, bhikkhave, nibbidāvirāgo vimuttiñāṇadassanattho vimuttiñāṇadassanānisaṃso; yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṃ nibbidāvirāgatthaṃ nibbidāvirāgānisaṃsaṃ; samādhi yathābhūtañāṇadassanattho yathābhūtañāṇadassanānisaṃso; sukhaṃ samādhatthaṃ samādhānisaṃsaṃ; passaddhi sukhatthā [V 3.0004] sukhānisaṃsā; pīti passaddhatthā passaddhānisaṃsā; pāmojjaṃ pītatthaṃ pītānisaṃsaṃ; avippaṭisāro pāmojjattho pāmojjānisaṃso; kusalāni sīlāni avippaṭisāratthāni avippaṭisārānisaṃsāni[T 5.0004]. Iti kho, bhikkhave, dhammā dhamme [P 5.0004] abhisandenti, dhammā dhamme paripūrenti apārā pāraṃ gamanāyā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Thus, bhikkhus, disenchantment and dispassion have the knowledge and vision of liberation as their purpose and as their benefit. Knowledge and vision of things as they truly are have disenchantment and dispassion as their purpose and as their benefit. Concentration has the knowledge and vision of things as they truly are as its purpose and as its benefit. Happiness has concentration as its purpose and as its benefit. Tranquility has happiness as its purpose and as its benefit. Rapture has tranquility as its purpose and as its benefit. Gladness has rapture as its purpose and as its benefit. Non-remorse has gladness as its purpose and as its benefit. Wholesome virtues have non-remorse as their purpose and as their benefit. In this way, bhikkhus, states lead on to subsequent states, states fulfill subsequent states, for the sake of going from the near shore to the far shore.”

3. Paṭhamaupanisasuttaṃ

3. The First Discourse on Supporting Conditions

3. a. ni. 5.24; 11.3 “Dussīlassa, bhikkhave, sīlavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti avippaṭisāro; avippaṭisāre asati avippaṭisāravipannassa hatūpanisaṃ hoti pāmojjaṃ; pāmojje asati pāmojjavipannassa hatūpanisā hoti pīti; pītiyā asati pītivipannassa hatūpanisā hoti passaddhi; passaddhiyā asati passaddhivipannassa hatūpanisaṃ hoti sukhaṃ; sukhe asati sukhavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti sammāsamādhi; sammāsamādhimhi asati sammāsamādhivipannassa hatūpanisaṃ hoti yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṃ; yathābhūtañāṇadassane asati yathābhūtañāṇadassanavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti nibbidāvirāgo[M 3.0260]; nibbidāvirāge asati nibbidāvirāgavipannassa hatūpanisaṃ hoti vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, rukkho sākhāpalāsavipanno. Tassa papaṭikāpi na pāripūriṃ gacchati, tacopi… pheggupi… sāropi na pāripūriṃ gacchati. Evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, dussīlassa sīlavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti avippaṭisāro; avippaṭisāre asati avippaṭisāravipannassa hatūpanisaṃ hoti…pe… vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ.

3. “Bhikkhus, for an immoral person, one whose virtue is corrupted, non-remorse has its supporting condition destroyed. When non-remorse is absent, for one whose non-remorse is corrupted, gladness has its supporting condition destroyed. When gladness is absent, for one whose gladness is corrupted, rapture has its supporting condition destroyed. When rapture is absent, for one whose rapture is corrupted, tranquility has its supporting condition destroyed. When tranquility is absent, for one whose tranquility is corrupted, happiness has its supporting condition destroyed. When happiness is absent, for one whose happiness is corrupted, right concentration has its supporting condition destroyed. When right concentration is absent, for one whose right concentration is corrupted, the knowledge and vision of things as they truly are has its supporting condition destroyed. When the knowledge and vision of things as they truly are is absent, for one whose knowledge and vision of things as they truly are is corrupted, disenchantment and dispassion have their supporting condition destroyed. When disenchantment and dispassion are absent, for one whose disenchantment and dispassion are corrupted, the knowledge and vision of liberation has its supporting condition destroyed. Just as, bhikkhus, if a tree’s branches and leaves are corrupted, its outer bark does not come to fulfillment, nor its inner bark, nor its sapwood, nor its heartwood. In the same way, bhikkhus, for an immoral person, one whose virtue is corrupted, non-remorse has its supporting condition destroyed... the knowledge and vision of liberation has its supporting condition destroyed.”

“Sīlavato, bhikkhave, sīlasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti avippaṭisāro; avippaṭisāre sati avippaṭisārasampannassa upanisasampannaṃ hoti pāmojjaṃ; pāmojje sati pāmojjasampannassa upanisasampannā hoti pīti; pītiyā sati pītisampannassa upanisasampannā hoti passaddhi; passaddhiyā sati passaddhisampannassa [T 5.0005] upanisasampannaṃ hoti sukhaṃ; sukhe sati sukhasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti sammāsamādhi[P 5.0005]; sammāsamādhimhi sati sammāsamādhisampannassa upanisasampannaṃ hoti yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṃ; yathābhūtañāṇadassane sati yathābhūtañāṇadassanasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti nibbidāvirāgo; nibbidāvirāge sati nibbidāvirāgasampannassa upanisasampannaṃ hoti vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, rukkho sākhāpalāsasampanno. Tassa papaṭikāpi pāripūriṃ gacchati, tacopi… pheggupi… sāropi pāripūriṃ [V 3.0005] gacchati. Evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sīlavato sīlasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti avippaṭisāro; avippaṭisāre sati avippaṭisārasampannassa upanisasampannaṃ hoti…pe… vimuttiñāṇadassana”nti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, for a virtuous person, one accomplished in virtue, non-remorse has its condition fulfilled. When non-remorse is present, for one accomplished in non-remorse, gladness has its condition fulfilled. When gladness is present, for one accomplished in gladness, rapture has its condition fulfilled. When rapture is present, for one accomplished in rapture, tranquility has its condition fulfilled. When tranquility is present, for one accomplished in tranquility, happiness has its condition fulfilled. When happiness is present, for one accomplished in happiness, right concentration has its condition fulfilled. When right concentration is present, for one accomplished in right concentration, the knowledge and vision of things as they truly are has its condition fulfilled. When the knowledge and vision of things as they truly are is present, for one accomplished in the knowledge and vision of things as they truly are, disenchantment and dispassion have their condition fulfilled. When disenchantment and dispassion are present, for one accomplished in disenchantment and dispassion, the knowledge and vision of liberation has its condition fulfilled. Just as, bhikkhus, if a tree is endowed with branches and leaves, its outer bark comes to fulfillment, as do its inner bark, its sapwood, and its heartwood. In the same way, bhikkhus, for a virtuous person, one accomplished in virtue, non-remorse has its condition fulfilled... the knowledge and vision of liberation has its condition fulfilled.”

4. Dutiyaupanisasuttaṃ

4. The Second Discourse on Supporting Conditions

4. a. ni. 11.4 Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi – “dussīlassa, āvuso, sīlavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti avippaṭisāro; avippaṭisāre asati avippaṭisāravipannassa hatūpanisaṃ hoti…pe… vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, rukkho sākhāpalāsavipanno. Tassa papaṭikāpi na pāripūriṃ gacchati, tacopi… pheggupi… sāropi na pāripūriṃ gacchati. Evamevaṃ kho, āvuso, dussīlassa sīlavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti avippaṭisāro; avippaṭisāre asati avippaṭisāravipannassa hatūpanisaṃ hoti…pe… vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ.

4. There, the Venerable Sāriputta addressed the bhikkhus: ‘Friends, for an immoral person, one with corrupted virtue, non-remorse has its supporting condition destroyed. When non-remorse is absent, for one whose non-remorse is corrupted, gladness has its supporting condition destroyed... the knowledge and vision of liberation has its supporting condition destroyed. Just as, friends, for a tree with corrupted branches and leaves, its outer bark does not come to fulfillment, nor its inner bark, nor its sapwood, nor its heartwood. In the same way, friends, for an immoral person, one with corrupted virtue, non-remorse has its supporting condition destroyed. When non-remorse is absent, for one whose non-remorse is corrupted, gladness has its supporting condition destroyed... the knowledge and vision of liberation has its supporting condition destroyed.’

“Sīlavato[M 3.0261], āvuso, sīlasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti avippaṭisāro; avippaṭisāre sati avippaṭisārasampannassa upanisasampannaṃ hoti…pe. [T 5.0006]… vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, rukkho sākhāpalāsasampanno. Tassa papaṭikāpi pāripūriṃ gacchati, tacopi… pheggupi… sāropi pāripūriṃ gacchati. Evamevaṃ kho, āvuso, sīlavato sīlasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti avippaṭisāro; avippaṭisāre sati avippaṭisārasampannassa upanisasampannaṃ hoti…pe… vimuttiñāṇadassana”nti. Catutthaṃ.

“Friends, for a virtuous person, one accomplished in virtue, non-remorse has its condition fulfilled. When non-remorse is present, for one accomplished in non-remorse, gladness has its condition fulfilled... the knowledge and vision of liberation has its condition fulfilled. Just as, friends, for a tree endowed with branches and leaves, its outer bark comes to fulfillment, and its inner bark, and its sapwood, and its heartwood come to fulfillment. In the same way, friends, for a virtuous person, one accomplished in virtue, non-remorse has its condition fulfilled. When non-remorse is present, for one accomplished in non-remorse, gladness has its condition fulfilled... the knowledge and vision of liberation has its condition fulfilled.” Fourth.

5. Tatiyaupanisasuttaṃ

5. The Third Discourse on Supporting Conditions

5. a. ni. 11.5 Tatra [T 5.0007][P 5.0006] kho āyasmā ānando bhikkhū āmantesi – “dussīlassa, āvuso, sīlavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti avippaṭisāro; avippaṭisāre asati avippaṭisāravipannassa hatūpanisaṃ hoti pāmojjaṃ; pāmojje asati pāmojjavipannassa hatūpanisā hoti pīti; pītiyā asati pītivipannassa hatūpanisā hoti passaddhi; passaddhiyā asati passaddhivipannassa hatūpanisaṃ hoti sukhaṃ; sukhe asati sukhavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti sammāsamādhi; sammāsamādhimhi asati sammāsamādhivipannassa hatūpanisaṃ hoti yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṃ; yathābhūtañāṇadassane asati yathābhūtañāṇadassanavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti nibbidāvirāgo; nibbidāvirāge asati nibbidāvirāgavipannassa hatūpanisaṃ hoti vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, rukkho sākhāpalāsavipanno. Tassa papaṭikāpi na pāripūriṃ gacchati, tacopi… pheggupi… sāropi na pāripūriṃ gacchati. Evamevaṃ kho, āvuso, dussīlassa sīlavipannassa hatūpaniso hoti avippaṭisāro; avippaṭisāre asati avippaṭisāravipannassa hatūpanisaṃ hoti…pe… vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ.

5. There, the Venerable Ānanda addressed the bhikkhus: ‘Friends, for an immoral person, one with corrupted virtue, non-remorse has its supporting condition destroyed. When non-remorse is absent, for one whose non-remorse is corrupted, gladness has its supporting condition destroyed. When gladness is absent, for one whose gladness is corrupted, rapture has its supporting condition destroyed. When rapture is absent, for one whose rapture is corrupted, tranquility has its supporting condition destroyed. When tranquility is absent, for one whose tranquility is corrupted, happiness has its supporting condition destroyed. When happiness is absent, for one whose happiness is corrupted, right concentration has its supporting condition destroyed. When right concentration is absent, for one whose right concentration is corrupted, the knowledge and vision of things as they truly are has its supporting condition destroyed. When the knowledge and vision of things as they truly are is absent, for one whose knowledge and vision of things as they truly are is corrupted, disenchantment and dispassion have their supporting condition destroyed. When disenchantment and dispassion are absent, for one whose disenchantment and dispassion are corrupted, the knowledge and vision of liberation has its supporting condition destroyed. Just as, friends, for a tree with corrupted branches and leaves, its outer bark does not come to fulfillment, nor its inner bark, nor its sapwood, nor its heartwood. In the same way, friends, for an immoral person, one with corrupted virtue, non-remorse has its supporting condition destroyed. When non-remorse is absent, for one whose non-remorse is corrupted, gladness has its supporting condition destroyed... the knowledge and vision of liberation has its supporting condition destroyed.’

“Sīlavato, āvuso, sīlasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti avippaṭisāro; avippaṭisāre sati avippaṭisārasampannassa upanisasampannaṃ hoti pāmojjaṃ; pāmojje sati pāmojjasampannassa upanisasampannā hoti pīti; pītiyā sati pītisampannassa upanisasampannā hoti passaddhi; passaddhiyā sati passaddhisampannassa upanisasampannaṃ hoti sukhaṃ; sukhe sati sukhasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti sammāsamādhi[T 5.0008]; sammāsamādhimhi sati sammāsamādhisampannassa upanisasampannaṃ hoti yathābhūtañāṇadassanaṃ[V 3.0006]; yathābhūtañāṇadassane [M 3.0262] sati yathābhūtañāṇadassanasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti nibbidāvirāgo; nibbidāvirāge sati nibbidāvirāgasampannassa upanisasampannaṃ hoti vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, rukkho sākhāpalāsasampanno[P 5.0007]. Tassa papaṭikāpi pāripūriṃ gacchati, tacopi… pheggupi… sāropi pāripūriṃ gacchati. Evamevaṃ kho, āvuso, sīlavato sīlasampannassa upanisasampanno hoti avippaṭisāro; avippaṭisāre sati avippaṭisārasampannassa upanisasampannaṃ hoti…pe… vimuttiñāṇadassana”nti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Friends, for a virtuous person, one endowed with virtue, the supporting condition for freedom from remorse is fulfilled. When freedom from remorse is present, for one endowed with freedom from remorse, the supporting condition for joy is fulfilled. When joy is present, for one endowed with joy, the supporting condition for rapture is fulfilled. When rapture is present, for one endowed with rapture, the supporting condition for tranquility is fulfilled. When tranquility is present, for one endowed with tranquility, the supporting condition for happiness is fulfilled. When happiness is present, for one endowed with happiness, the supporting condition for right concentration is fulfilled. When right concentration is present, for one endowed with right concentration, the supporting condition for the knowledge and vision of things as they truly are is fulfilled. When the knowledge and vision of things as they truly are is present, for one endowed with the knowledge and vision of things as they truly are, the supporting condition for disenchantment and dispassion is fulfilled. When disenchantment and dispassion are present, for one endowed with disenchantment and dispassion, the supporting condition for the knowledge and vision of liberation is fulfilled. Just as, friends, for a tree endowed with branches and leaves, its outer bark comes to fulfillment, its inner bark, its sapwood, and its heartwood also come to fulfillment; in the same way, friends, for a virtuous person, one endowed with virtue, the supporting condition for freedom from remorse is fulfilled. When freedom from remorse is present, for one endowed with freedom from remorse, the supporting condition for joy is fulfilled… and so on… the knowledge and vision of liberation.” Fifth.

6. Samādhisuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Concentration

6. a. ni. 11.18 Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami…pe… ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “siyā nu kho, bhante, bhikkhuno tathārūpo samādhipaṭilābho yathā neva pathaviyaṃ pathavisaññī paṭhavisaññī (sī.), paṭhavīsaññī (syā.) assa, na āpasmiṃ āposaññī assa, na tejasmiṃ tejosaññī assa, na vāyasmiṃ vāyosaññī assa, na ākāsānañcāyatane ākāsānañcāyatanasaññī assa, na viññāṇañcāyatane viññāṇañcāyatanasaññī assa, na ākiñcaññāyatane ākiñcaññāyatanasaññī assa, na nevasaññānāsaññāyatane nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññī assa, na idhaloke idhalokasaññī assa, na paraloke paralokasaññī assa[V 3.0007]; saññī ca pana assā”ti? “Siyā, ānanda, bhikkhuno tathārūpo samādhipaṭilābho [T 5.0009] yathā neva pathaviyaṃ pathavisaññī assa, na āpasmiṃ āposaññī assa, na tejasmiṃ tejosaññī assa, na vāyasmiṃ vāyosaññī assa, na ākāsānañcāyatane ākāsānañcāyatanasaññī assa, na viññāṇañcāyatane viññāṇañcāyatanasaññī assa, na ākiñcaññāyatane ākiñcaññāyatanasaññī assa, na nevasaññānāsaññāyatane nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññī assa, na idhaloke idhalokasaññī assa, na paraloke paralokasaññī assa; saññī ca pana assā”ti.

6. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One… and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, could there be for a bhikkhu such an attainment of concentration that he would not be percipient of earth in earth, not be percipient of water in water, not be percipient of fire in fire, not be percipient of air in air; not be percipient of the base of the infinity of space in the base of the infinity of space, not be percipient of the base of the infinity of consciousness in the base of the infinity of consciousness, not be percipient of the base of nothingness in the base of nothingness, not be percipient of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; not be percipient of this world in this world, nor of the other world in the other world—and yet he would be percipient?” “There could be, Ānanda. For a bhikkhu, there could be such an attainment of concentration that he would not be percipient of earth in earth, not be percipient of water in water, not be percipient of fire in fire, not be percipient of air in air; not be percipient of the base of the infinity of space in the base of the infinity of space, not be percipient of the base of the infinity of consciousness in the base of the infinity of consciousness, not be percipient of the base of nothingness in the base of nothingness, not be percipient of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; not be percipient of this world in this world, nor of the other world in the other world—and yet he would be percipient.”

“Yathā kathaṃ pana, bhante, siyā bhikkhuno tathārūpo samādhipaṭilābho yathā neva pathaviyaṃ pathavisaññī assa, na āpasmiṃ āposaññī assa na tejasmiṃ tejosaññī assa[P 5.0008], na vāyasmiṃ vāyosaññī assa, na ākāsānañcāyatane ākāsānañcāyatanasaññī assa, na [M 3.0263] viññāṇañcāyatane viññāṇañcāyatanasaññī assa, na ākiñcaññāyattane ākiñcaññāyatanasaññī assa, na nevasaññānāsaññāyatane nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññī assa, na idhaloke idhalokasaññī assa, na paraloke paralokasaññī assa; saññī ca pana assā”ti?

“But in what way, venerable sir, could there be for a bhikkhu such an attainment of concentration that he would not be percipient of earth in earth, not be percipient of water in water, not be percipient of fire in fire, not be percipient of air in air; not be percipient of the base of the infinity of space in the base of the infinity of space, not be percipient of the base of the infinity of consciousness in the base of the infinity of consciousness, not be percipient of the base of nothingness in the base of nothingness, not be percipient of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; not be percipient of this world in this world, nor of the other world in the other world—and yet he would be percipient?”

“Idhānanda, bhikkhu evaṃsaññī hoti – ‘etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ paṇītaṃ yadidaṃ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nirodho nibbāna’nti. Evaṃ kho, ānanda, siyā bhikkhuno tathārūpo samādhipaṭilābho yathā neva pathaviyaṃ pathavisaññī assa, na āpasmiṃ āposaññī assa, na tejasmiṃ tejosaññī assa, na vāyasmiṃ [T 5.0010] vāyosaññī assa, na ākāsānañcāyatane ākāsānañcāyatanasaññī assa, na viññāṇañcāyatane viññāṇañcāyatanasaññī assa, na ākiñcaññāyatane ākiñcaññāyatanasaññī assa, na nevasaññānāsaññāyatane nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññī assa, na idhaloke idhalokasaññī assa, na paraloke paralokasaññī assa; saññī ca pana assā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu is percipient thus: ‘This is peaceful, this is sublime, that is, the stilling of all formations, the relinquishment of all acquisitions, the destruction of craving, dispassion, cessation, Nibbāna.’ In this way, Ānanda, there could be for a bhikkhu such an attainment of concentration that he would not be percipient of earth in earth, not be percipient of water in water, not be percipient of fire in fire, not be percipient of air in air; not be percipient of the base of the infinity of space in the base of the infinity of space, not be percipient of the base of the infinity of consciousness in the base of the infinity of consciousness, not be percipient of the base of nothingness in the base of nothingness, not be percipient of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; not be percipient of this world in this world, nor of the other world in the other world—and yet he would be percipient.” Sixth.

7. Sāriputtasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse with Sāriputta

7. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā [V 3.0008] sāriputtena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca –

7. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Venerable Sāriputta. Having approached, he exchanged courteous greetings with the Venerable Sāriputta. After concluding this courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Venerable Sāriputta:

“Siyā nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, bhikkhuno tathārūpo samādhipaṭilābho yathā neva pathaviyaṃ pathavisaññī assa, na āpasmiṃ āposaññī assa, na tejasmiṃ tejosaññī assa, na vāyasmiṃ vāyosaññī assa, na ākāsānañcāyatane ākāsānañcāyatanasaññī [P 5.0009] assa, na viññāṇañcāyatane viññāṇañcāyatanasaññī assa, na ākiñcaññāyatane ākiñcaññāyatanasaññī assa, na nevasaññānāsaññāyatane nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññī assa, na idhaloke idhalokasaññī assa, na paraloke paralokasaññī assa; saññī ca pana assā”ti?

“Friend Sāriputta, could there be for a bhikkhu an attainment of concentration of such a kind that he would be percipient neither of earth in earth, nor of water in water, nor of fire in fire, nor of air in air; nor of the base of the infinity of space in the base of the infinity of space, nor of the base of the infinity of consciousness in the base of the infinity of consciousness, nor of the base of nothingness in the base of nothingness, nor of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception; nor of this world in this world, nor of the other world in the other world—and yet he would still be percipient?”

“Siyā[M 3.0264], āvuso ānanda, bhikkhuno tathārūpo samādhipaṭilābho yathā neva pathaviyaṃ pathavisaññī assa…pe… na paraloke paralokasaññī assa; saññī [T 5.0011] ca pana assā”ti.

“It is possible, friend Ānanda, for a bhikkhu to have an attainment of concentration of such a kind that he would be percipient neither of earth in the earth element… nor of a world beyond in a world beyond—and yet he would still be percipient.”

“Yathā kathaṃ pana, āvuso sāriputta, siyā bhikkhuno tathārūpo samādhipaṭilābho yathā neva pathaviyaṃ pathavisaññī assa…pe… saññī ca pana assā”ti? “Ekamidāhaṃ, āvuso ānanda, samayaṃ idheva sāvatthiyaṃ viharāmi andhavanasmiṃ. Tatthāhaṃ athāhaṃ (ka.) tathārūpaṃ samādhiṃ samāpajjiṃ paṭilabhāmi (ka.) yathā neva pathaviyaṃ pathavisaññī ahosiṃ, na āpasmiṃ āposaññī ahosiṃ, na tejasmiṃ tejosaññī ahosiṃ, na vāyasmiṃ vāyosaññī ahosiṃ, na ākāsānañcāyatane ākāsānañcāyatanasaññī ahosiṃ, na viññāṇañcāyatane viññāṇañcāyatanasaññī ahosiṃ, na ākiñcaññāyatane ākiñcaññāyatanasaññī ahosiṃ, na nevasaññānāsaññāyatane nevasaññānāsaññāyatanasaññī ahosiṃ, na idhaloke idhalokasaññī ahosiṃ, na paraloke paralokasaññī ahosiṃ; saññī ca pana ahosi”nti.

“But in what way, friend Sāriputta, could there be for a bhikkhu an attainment of concentration of such a kind that he would be percipient neither of earth in the earth element… and yet he would still be percipient?” “On one occasion, friend Ānanda, I was dwelling right here in Sāvatthī in the Andhavana. There I attained such a concentration that I was percipient neither of earth in the earth element, nor of water in the water element, nor of fire in the fire element, nor of air in the air element, nor of the base of the infinity of space in the base of the infinity of space, nor of the base of the infinity of consciousness in the base of the infinity of consciousness, nor of the base of nothingness in the base of nothingness, nor of the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception in the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception, nor of this world in this world, nor of a world beyond in a world beyond—and yet I was still percipient.”

“Kiṃsaññī panāyasmā sāriputto kiṃ saññī panāvuso sāriputta (ka.) tasmiṃ samaye ahosī”ti? “Bhavanirodho nibbānaṃ bhavanirodho nibbāna”nti kho me, āvuso, aññāva saññā uppajjati aññāva saññā nirujjhati. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, sakalikaggissa jhāyamānassa aññāva acci uppajjati aññāva acci nirujjhati; evamevaṃ kho, āvuso, ‘bhavanirodho nibbānaṃ bhavanirodho nibbāna’nti [V 3.0009] aññāva saññā uppajjati [P 5.0010] aññāva saññā nirujjhati. ‘Bhavanirodho nibbāna’nti nibbānaṃ (sī. ka.) saññī ca panāhaṃ, āvuso, tasmiṃ samaye ahosi”nti. Sattamaṃ.

“Of what was the Venerable Sāriputta percipient at that time?” “Friend, the perception ‘The cessation of becoming is Nibbāna; the cessation of becoming is Nibbāna’ occurred to me, as one perception arose and another ceased. Just as, friend, for a burning fire of wood-splinters, one flame arises and another ceases; even so, friend, the perception ‘The cessation of becoming is Nibbāna; the cessation of becoming is Nibbāna’ occurred, as one perception arose and another ceased. And, friend, at that time I was percipient of ‘The cessation of becoming is Nibbāna’.”

8. Jhānasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Jhāna

8. “Saddho ca imasmiṃ vākye ayaṃ ca kāro natthi syāmapotthake, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hoti, no ca no (syā.) evamuparipi. a. ni. 8.71 sīlavā; evaṃ so tenaṅgena [T 5.0012] aparipūro hoti. Tena taṃ aṅgaṃ paripūretabbaṃ – ‘kintāhaṃ saddho ca assaṃ, sīlavā cā’ti! Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti sīlavā ca, evaṃ so tenaṅgena paripūro hoti.

8. “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is endowed with faith, but is not endowed with virtue; thus he is incomplete in that factor. That factor should be fulfilled by him, reflecting thus: ‘How might I be one who is endowed with faith and also endowed with virtue?’ And when, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is endowed with faith and is also endowed with virtue, he is thus complete in that factor.

“Saddho [M 3.0265] ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hoti sīlavā ca, no ca bahussuto…pe… bahussuto ca, no ca dhammakathiko… dhammakathiko ca, no ca parisāvacaro… parisāvacaro ca, no ca visārado parisāya dhammaṃ deseti… visārado ca parisāya dhammaṃ deseti, no ca vinayadharo… vinayadharo ca, no ca āraññiko āraññako (ka.) pantasenāsano… āraññiko ca pantasenāsano, no ca catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī… catunnañca jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, no ca āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Evaṃ so tenaṅgena aparipūro hoti. Tena taṃ aṅgaṃ paripūretabbaṃ – ‘kintāhaṃ saddho ca assaṃ, sīlavā ca, bahussuto ca, dhammakathiko ca, parisāvacaro ca, visārado ca parisāya dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ, vinayadharo ca, āraññiko ca pantasenāsano, catunnañca jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ [P 5.0011] diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī assaṃ akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyya’nti.

“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is endowed with faith and is endowed with virtue, but is not learned... is learned, but is not a speaker of the Dhamma... is a speaker of the Dhamma, but does not frequent assemblies... frequents assemblies, but does not teach the Dhamma in an assembly with confidence... teaches the Dhamma in an assembly with confidence, but is not an expert in the Vinaya... is an expert in the Vinaya, but is not a forest-dweller, one who resorts to remote lodgings... is a forest-dweller, one who resorts to remote lodgings, but is not an obtainer at will, without trouble, without difficulty, of the four jhānas which pertain to the higher mind and are pleasant abidings in this very life... obtains at will, without trouble, without difficulty, the four jhānas which pertain to the higher mind and are pleasant abidings in this very life, but does not, through the destruction of the taints, in this very life, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge, enter and abide in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom. Thus he is incomplete in that factor. That factor should be fulfilled by him, reflecting thus: ‘How might I be one who is endowed with faith, endowed with virtue, learned, a speaker of the Dhamma, one who frequents assemblies, and who teaches the Dhamma in an assembly with confidence; an expert in the Vinaya; a forest-dweller, one who resorts to remote lodgings; an obtainer at will, without trouble, without difficulty, of the four jhānas which pertain to the higher mind and are pleasant abidings in this very life; and how might I, through the destruction of the taints, in this very life, having realized it for myself with direct knowledge, enter and abide in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom?’”

“Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti, sīlavā ca, bahussuto [T 5.0013] ca, dhammakathiko ca, parisāvacaro ca, visārado ca parisāya dhammaṃ deseti, vinayadharo ca, āraññiko ca pantasenāsano, catunnañca jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī [V 3.0010] hoti akicchalābhī akasiralābhī, āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati; evaṃ so tenaṅgena paripūro hoti. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu samantapāsādiko ca hoti sabbākāraparipūro cā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“And when, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is endowed with faith, is endowed with virtue, is learned, is a speaker of the Dhamma, frequents assemblies, teaches the Dhamma in an assembly with confidence, is an expert in the Vinaya, is a forest-dweller who resorts to remote lodgings, is an obtainer at will, without trouble, without difficulty, of the four jhānas which pertain to the higher mind and are pleasant abidings in this very life, and, through the destruction of the taints, in this very life, having realized it for himself with direct knowledge, enters and abides in the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom—thus he is complete in that factor. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these ten qualities is completely inspiring and complete in all aspects.”

9. Santavimokkhasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Peaceful Liberation

9. “Saddho ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hoti, no ca sīlavā…pe… sīlavā ca, no ca bahussuto… bahussuto ca, no ca dhammakathiko… dhammakathiko ca, no [M 3.0266] ca parisāvacaro… parisāvacaro ca, no ca visārado parisāya dhammaṃ deseti… visārado ca parisāya dhammaṃ deseti, no ca vinayadharo… vinayadharo ca, no ca āraññiko pantasenāsano… āraññiko ca pantasenāsano, no ca ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā te kāyena phusitvā viharati… ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā [P 5.0012] te ca kāyena phusitvā viharati, no ca āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Evaṃ so tenaṅgena aparipūro hoti. Tena taṃ aṅgaṃ paripūretabbaṃ – ‘kintāhaṃ saddho ca assaṃ, sīlavā ca, bahussuto ca, dhammakathiko ca, parisāvacaro ca, visārado ca parisāya dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ, vinayadharo ca, āraññiko ca pantasenāsano, ye [T 5.0014] te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā te ca kāyena phusitvā vihareyyaṃ, āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyya’nti.

9. “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is faithful, but not virtuous… he is virtuous, but not learned… he is learned, but not a teacher of the Dhamma… he is a teacher of the Dhamma, but does not frequent assemblies… he frequents assemblies, but is not confident when teaching the Dhamma to an assembly… he is confident when teaching the Dhamma to an assembly, but is not an expert in the Vinaya… he is an expert in the Vinaya, but is not a forest-dweller who uses remote lodgings… he is a forest-dweller who uses remote lodgings, but does not dwell having touched with the body and abiding in those peaceful, formless liberations that transcend form… he dwells having touched with the body and abiding in those peaceful, formless liberations that transcend form, but does not, through the destruction of the taints, realize for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, and dwell having attained it. In this way, he is incomplete in that factor. That factor should be fulfilled by him, thinking: ‘How might I be faithful and virtuous, learned, a teacher of the Dhamma, one who frequents assemblies, confident when teaching the Dhamma to an assembly, an expert in the Vinaya, a forest-dweller who uses remote lodgings; and how might I dwell having touched with the body and abiding in those peaceful, formless liberations that transcend form; and how might I, through the destruction of the taints, realize for myself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, and dwell having attained it?’”

“Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti, sīlavā ca, bahussuto ca, dhammakathiko ca, parisāvacaro ca, visārado ca parisāya dhammaṃ deseti, vinayadharo ca, āraññiko ca pantasenāsano, ye te santā vimokkhā atikkamma rūpe āruppā te ca kāyena phusitvā viharati, āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati; evaṃ so tenaṅgena paripūro hoti. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu samantapāsādiko ca hoti sabbākāraparipūro cā”ti. Navamaṃ.

“But when, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is faithful, virtuous, learned, a teacher of the Dhamma, one who frequents assemblies, confident when teaching the Dhamma to an assembly, an expert in the Vinaya, a forest-dweller who uses remote lodgings; and he dwells having touched with the body and abiding in those peaceful, formless liberations that transcend form; and through the destruction of the taints, he realizes for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, and dwells having attained it; in this way, he is complete in that factor. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these ten qualities is inspiring on all sides and complete in all respects.” The ninth.

10. Vijjāsuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Knowledge

10. “Saddho [V 3.0011] ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hoti, no ca sīlavā. Evaṃ so tenaṅgena aparipūro hoti. Tena taṃ aṅgaṃ paripūretabbaṃ – ‘kintāhaṃ saddho ca assaṃ sīlavā cā’ti. Yato [P 5.0013] ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti, sīlavā ca, evaṃ so tenaṅgena paripūro hoti.

10. “Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is faithful, but not virtuous. In this way, he is incomplete in that factor. That factor should be fulfilled by him, thinking: ‘How might I be faithful and also virtuous?’ And when, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is both faithful and virtuous, in this way he is complete in that factor.

“Saddho ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu hoti sīlavā ca, no ca bahussuto bahussuto ca, no ca dhammakathiko dhammakathiko ca, no ca parisāvacaro parisāvacaro ca, no ca visārado parisāya dhammaṃ deseti visārado [M 3.0267] ca parisāya dhammaṃ deseti, no ca vinayadharo vinayadharo ca, no ca anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti [T 5.0015] sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Anekavihitañca…pe… pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, no ca dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena…pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti dibbena ca cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena…pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti, no ca āsavānaṃ khayā…pe… sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Evaṃ so tenaṅgena aparipūro hoti. Tena taṃ aṅgaṃ paripūretabbaṃ – ‘kintāhaṃ saddho ca assaṃ, sīlavā ca, bahussuto ca, dhammakathiko ca, parisāvacaro ca, visārado ca parisāya dhammaṃ deseyyaṃ, vinayadharo ca, anekavihitañca pubbenivāsaṃ anussareyyaṃ, seyyathidaṃ, ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussareyyaṃ, dibbena ca cakkhunā visuddhena [P 5.0014] atikkantamānusakena…pe… yathākammūpage satte pajāneyyaṃ, āsavānañca khayā…pe… sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyya’nti.

“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is faithful and virtuous, but not learned… he is learned, but not a teacher of the Dhamma… he is a teacher of the Dhamma, but does not frequent assemblies… he frequents assemblies, but is not confident when teaching the Dhamma to an assembly… he is confident when teaching the Dhamma to an assembly, but is not an expert in the Vinaya… he is an expert in the Vinaya, but does not recollect his manifold past lives, that is, one birth, two births… and so, with their aspects and details, recollects his manifold past lives… he recollects his manifold past lives, but with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he does not see… beings passing on and being reborn according to their kamma… with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees… beings passing on and being reborn according to their kamma, but does not, through the destruction of the taints… realize for himself and dwell having attained it. In this way, he is incomplete in that factor. That factor should be fulfilled by him, thinking: ‘How might I be faithful, virtuous, learned, a teacher of the Dhamma, one who frequents assemblies, confident when teaching the Dhamma to an assembly, and an expert in the Vinaya; and how might I recollect my manifold past lives… with their aspects and details; and with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human… know beings passing on and being reborn according to their kamma; and through the destruction of the taints… realize for myself and dwell having attained it?’”

“Yato ca kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti, sīlavā ca, bahussuto ca, dhammakathiko ca, parisāvacaro ca, visārado ca parisāya dhammaṃ deseti, vinayadharo ca, anekavihitañca pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, dibbena ca cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena…pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti, āsavānañca khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ [T 5.0016][V 3.0012] paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Evaṃ so tenaṅgena paripūro hoti. Imehi, kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato bhikkhu samantapāsādiko ca hoti sabbākāraparipūro cā”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“But when, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is faithful, virtuous, learned, a teacher of the Dhamma, one who frequents assemblies, confident when teaching the Dhamma to an assembly, and an expert in the Vinaya; and he recollects his manifold past lives, that is, one birth, two births… and so, with their aspects and details, recollects his manifold past lives; and with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human… he knows beings passing on and being reborn according to their kamma; and through the destruction of the taints, he realizes for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, and dwells having attained it; in this way, he is complete in that factor. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu endowed with these ten qualities is inspiring on all sides and complete in all respects.” The tenth.

Ānisaṃsavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on Benefits.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The Summary:

Kimatthiyaṃ cetanā ca, tayo upanisāpi ca;

Samādhi sāriputto ca, jhānaṃ santena vijjayāti.

For What Purpose?, Volition, and three on Proximate Cause; Concentration, Sāriputta, Faith, the Secluded, and Knowledge.

2. Nāthavaggo

2. The Chapter on a Protector

1. Senāsanasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Lodgings

11. “Pañcaṅgasamannāgato[V 3.0013][M 3.0268][P 5.0015], bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcaṅgasamannāgataṃ senāsanaṃ sevamāno bhajamāno nacirasseva āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyya.

11. Monks, a monk endowed with five factors, by frequenting and resorting to a dwelling endowed with five factors, would, before long, through the destruction of the taints, having realized for himself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, enter upon and abide therein.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcaṅgasamannāgato hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saddho hoti; saddahati tathāgatassa bodhiṃ – ‘itipi so bhagavā…pe… bhagavā’ti; appābādho hoti appātaṅko, samavepākiniyā gahaṇiyā samannāgato nātisītāya nāccuṇhāya majjhimāya padhānakkhamāya; asaṭho hoti amāyāvī, yathābhūtaṃ attānaṃ āvikattā satthari vā viññūsu vā sabrahmacārīsu; āraddhavīriyo [T 5.0017] viharati, akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadāya; thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu; paññavā hoti, udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcaṅgasamannāgato hoti.

And how, monks, is a monk endowed with five factors? Here, monks, a monk has faith; he believes in the enlightenment of the Tathāgata, thus: ‘For this reason, the Blessed One is... a Blessed One.’ He is without illness, without affliction, endowed with a digestive power that functions evenly, being neither too cold nor too hot, but moderate and suitable for striving. He is not fraudulent or deceitful; he reveals himself as he truly is to the Teacher or to his wise companions in the holy life. He dwells with energy aroused for the abandoning of unwholesome states and for the attainment of wholesome states; he is strong, of firm exertion, not shirking the burden in regard to wholesome states. He is wise, endowed with wisdom that discerns arising and passing away, which is noble, penetrative, and leads rightly to the complete destruction of suffering. In this way, monks, a monk is endowed with five factors.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, senāsanaṃ pañcaṅgasamannāgataṃ hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, senāsanaṃ nātidūraṃ hoti nāccāsannaṃ gamanāgamanasampannaṃ divā appākiṇṇaṃ rattiṃ appasaddaṃ appanigghosaṃ appaḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassaṃ appaḍaṃsa… siriṃsapasamphassaṃ (sī. syā. pī.); tasmiṃ kho pana senāsane viharantassa appakasirena uppajjanti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārā; tasmiṃ kho pana senāsane therā bhikkhū viharanti bahussutā āgatāgamā dhammadharā [P 5.0016] vinayadharā mātikādharā; te kālena kālaṃ upasaṅkamitvā paripucchati paripañhati – ‘idaṃ, bhante, kathaṃ, imassa ko attho’ti; tassa te āyasmanto avivaṭañceva vivaranti anuttānīkatañca uttāniṃ karonti anekavihitesu ca kaṅkhāṭhāniyesu dhammesu kaṅkhaṃ paṭivinodenti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, senāsanaṃ pañcaṅgasamannāgataṃ hoti. Pañcaṅgasamannāgato kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcaṅgasamannāgataṃ senāsanaṃ sevamāno [V 3.0014] bhajamāno nacirasseva [M 3.0269] āsavānaṃ khayā…pe… sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyyā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

And how, monks, is a lodging endowed with five factors? Here, monks, a lodging is neither too far nor too near, and is convenient for coming and going. By day it is not crowded, and by night it is quiet and without clamor. There is little contact from gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and creeping things. Moreover, for one dwelling in that lodging, the requisites of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicines for the sick arise without difficulty. Furthermore, in that lodging dwell elder monks who are learned, who have mastered the traditions, bearers of the Dhamma, bearers of the Vinaya, and bearers of the Mātikās. From time to time, he approaches them to ask and inquire: ‘Venerable sirs, how is this? What is the meaning of this?’ Those venerable ones then clarify what was unclear, reveal what was undisclosed, and dispel doubt regarding various matters that are grounds for doubt. In this way, monks, a lodging is endowed with five factors. Monks, a monk endowed with five factors, by frequenting and resorting to a lodging endowed with five factors, would, before long, through the destruction of the taints... enter upon and abide therein.

2. Pañcaṅgasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Five Factors

12. “Pañcaṅgavippahīno, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcaṅgasamannāgato imasmiṃ [T 5.0018] dhammavinaye ‘kevalī vusitavā uttamapuriso’ti vuccati. Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcaṅgavippahīno hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno kāmacchando pahīno hoti, byāpādo pahīno hoti, thinamiddhaṃ thīnamiddhaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) pahīnaṃ hoti, uddhaccakukkuccaṃ pahīnaṃ hoti, vicikicchā pahīnā hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcaṅgavippahīno hoti.

12. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who has abandoned five factors and is endowed with five factors is called in this Dhamma and Vinaya ‘one who is complete, who has lived the holy life, a supreme person.’ And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu one who has abandoned five factors? Here, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu, sensual desire is abandoned, ill will is abandoned, sloth and torpor are abandoned, restlessness and worry are abandoned, and doubt is abandoned. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is one who has abandoned five factors.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcaṅgasamannāgato hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asekhena sīlakkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekhena samādhikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekhena paññākkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekhena vimuttikkhandhena samannāgato hoti, asekhena vimuttiñāṇadassanakkhandhena samannāgato hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcaṅgasamannāgato hoti.

And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu endowed with five factors? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is endowed with the aggregate of virtue of one beyond training, the aggregate of concentration of one beyond training, the aggregate of wisdom of one beyond training, the aggregate of liberation of one beyond training, and the aggregate of the knowledge and vision of liberation of one beyond training. In this way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is endowed with five factors.

“Pañcaṅgavippahīno kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcaṅgasamannāgato imasmiṃ dhammavinaye ‘kevalī vusitavā uttamapuriso’ti vuccati.

Indeed, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who has abandoned five factors and is endowed with five factors is called in this Dhamma and Vinaya ‘one who is complete, who has lived the holy life, a supreme person.’

“Kāmacchando ca byāpādo, thinamiddhañca bhikkhuno;

Uddhaccaṃ vicikicchā ca, sabbasova na vijjati.

Sensual desire and ill will,

sloth and torpor, restlessness,

and doubt—for a bhikkhu,

these are not found at all.

“Asekhena [P 5.0017] ca sīlena, asekhena samādhinā;

Vimuttiyā ca sampanno, ñāṇena ca tathāvidho.

Endowed with the virtue of one beyond training,

and with the concentration of one beyond training,

and with liberation; and likewise

with such knowledge.

“Sa ve pañcaṅgasampanno, pañca aṅge pañcaṅgāni (syā.) vivajjayaṃ vivajjiya (ka.);

Imasmiṃ dhammavinaye, kevalī iti vuccatī”ti. dutiyaṃ;

He indeed, endowed with five factors,

while abandoning five factors,

is called ‘the complete one’

in this Dhamma and Vinaya.

3. Saṃyojanasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Fetters

13. “Dasayimāni[V 3.0015], bhikkhave, saṃyojanāni. Katamāni dasa? Pañcorambhāgiyāni [T 5.0019] saṃyojanāni, pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni. Katamāni pañcorambhāgiyāni [M 3.0270] saṃyojanāni? Sakkāyadiṭṭhi, vicikicchā, sīlabbataparāmāso, kāmacchando, byāpādo – imāni pañcorambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni.

13. Bhikkhus, there are these ten fetters. What ten? The five lower fetters and the five higher fetters. What are the five lower fetters? Identity view, doubt, clinging to precepts and practices, sensual desire, and ill will—these are the five lower fetters.

“Katamāni pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni? Rūparāgo, arūparāgo, māno, uddhaccaṃ, avijjā – imāni pañcuddhambhāgiyāni saṃyojanāni. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, dasa saṃyojanānī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

What are the five higher fetters? Lust for form, lust for the formless, conceit, restlessness, and ignorance—these are the five higher fetters. Indeed, bhikkhus, these are the ten fetters.

4. Cetokhilasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Mental Barrenness

14. “Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā pañca cetokhilā appahīnā pañca cetasovinibandhā asamucchinnā, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no vuddhi.

14. Bhikkhus, for whatever bhikkhu or bhikkhuni the five states of mental barrenness are unabandoned and the five bonds of the mind are unsevered, for them, as night and day pass, a decline in wholesome states is to be expected, not growth.

“Katamassa pañca cetokhilā appahīnā honti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari kaṅkhati vicikicchati nādhimuccati na sampasīdati, tassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya [P 5.0018] padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ paṭhamo cetokhilo appahīno hoti.

For whom are the five states of mental barrenness unabandoned? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu doubts the Teacher, is uncertain, is not resolved, and is not confident. Bhikkhus, for that bhikkhu who doubts the Teacher, is uncertain, is not resolved, and is not confident, his mind does not incline towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving. For one whose mind does not incline towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving, in this way for him this first state of mental barrenness is unabandoned.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhamme kaṅkhati…pe… saṅghe kaṅkhati… sikkhāya kaṅkhati… sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīsu kupito hoti anattamano āhatacitto khilajāto, tassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya [V 3.0016] anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ pañcamo cetokhilo appahīno hoti. Imassa pañca [T 5.0020] cetokhilā appahīnā honti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu doubts the Dhamma... he doubts the Sangha... he doubts the training... he is angry with his companions in the holy life, displeased, resentful, and his mind has become barren. Bhikkhus, for that bhikkhu who is angry with his companions in the holy life, displeased, resentful, and whose mind has become barren, his mind does not incline towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving. For one whose mind does not incline towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving, in this way for him this fifth state of mental barrenness is unabandoned. For him, these five states of mental barrenness are unabandoned.

“Katamassa pañca cetasovinibandhā asamucchinnā honti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāmesu avītarāgo hoti avigatacchando avigatapemo avigatapipāso avigatapariḷāho avigatataṇho. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāmesu avītarāgo hoti avigatacchando avigatapemo avigatapipāso avigatapariḷāho avigatataṇho[M 3.0271], tassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ paṭhamo cetasovinibandho asamucchinno hoti.

For whom are the five bonds of the mind unsevered? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not free from passion for sensual pleasures; his desire has not departed, his affection has not departed, his thirst has not departed, his fever has not departed, and his craving has not departed. Bhikkhus, for that bhikkhu who is not free from passion for sensual pleasures, whose desire, affection, thirst, fever, and craving have not departed, his mind does not incline towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving. For one whose mind does not incline towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving, in this way for him this first bond of the mind is unsevered.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye avītarāgo hoti…pe… rūpe avītarāgo hoti…pe… yāvadatthaṃ udarāvadehakaṃ bhuñjitvā seyyasukhaṃ passasukhaṃ middhasukhaṃ anuyutto viharati… aññataraṃ devanikāyaṃ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṃ carati – ‘imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu aññataraṃ devanikāyaṃ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṃ carati – ‘imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti, tassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya [P 5.0019] anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ na namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ pañcamo cetasovinibandho asamucchinno hoti. Imassa pañca cetasovinibandhā asamucchinnā honti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not free from passion for the body... he is not free from passion for forms... having eaten to his belly's content, as much as he desires, he dwells devoted to the pleasure of lying down, the pleasure of lying on his side, and the pleasure of drowsiness... he practices the holy life aspiring to some order of devas, thinking: ‘By this virtue, or this observance, or this austerity, or this holy life, I will become a deva or some other kind of deva.’ Bhikkhus, for that bhikkhu who practices the holy life aspiring to some order of devas... his mind does not incline towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving. For one whose mind does not incline towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving, in this way for him this fifth bond of the mind is unsevered. For him, these five bonds of the mind are unsevered.

“Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā ime pañca cetokhilā appahīnā ime pañca [T 5.0021] cetasovinibandhā asamucchinnā, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no vuddhi.

Bhikkhus, for whatever bhikkhu or bhikkhuni these five states of mental barrenness are unabandoned and these five bonds of the mind are unsevered, for them, as night and day pass, only a decline in wholesome states is to be expected, not growth.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kāḷapakkhe candassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāyateva vaṇṇena hāyati maṇḍalena hāyati ābhāya hāyati ārohapariṇāhena; evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, yassa kassaci bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā ime pañca cetokhilā appahīnā ime [V 3.0017] pañca cetasovinibandhā asamucchinnā, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no vuddhi.

Just as, bhikkhus, during the waning fortnight, as night and day pass for the moon, it wanes in beauty, wanes in its orb, wanes in its radiance, and wanes in its height and breadth; even so, bhikkhus, for whatever bhikkhu or bhikkhuni these five states of mental barrenness are unabandoned and these five bonds of the mind are unsevered, for them, as night and day pass, only a decline in wholesome states is to be expected, not growth.

“Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā pañca cetokhilā pahīnā pañca cetasovinibandhā susamucchinnā, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for whatever bhikkhu or bhikkhuni the five states of mental barrenness are abandoned and the five bonds of the mind are well severed, for them, as night and day pass, only growth in wholesome states is to be expected, not decline.

“Katamassa [M 3.0272] pañca cetokhilā pahīnā honti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari na kaṅkhati na vicikicchati, adhimuccati sampasīdati. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satthari na kaṅkhati na vicikicchati adhimuccati sampasīdati, tassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ paṭhamo cetokhilo pahīno hoti.

For whom are the five states of mental barrenness abandoned? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not doubt the Teacher, is not uncertain, is resolved, and is confident. Bhikkhus, for that bhikkhu who does not doubt the Teacher, is not uncertain, is resolved, and is confident, his mind inclines towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving. For one whose mind inclines towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving, in this way for him this first state of mental barrenness is abandoned.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhamme na kaṅkhati…pe… saṅghe na kaṅkhati… sikkhāya na kaṅkhati [P 5.0020]… sabrahmacārīsu na kupito hoti attamano na āhatacitto na khilajāto. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīsu na kupito hoti attamano na āhatacitto na khilajāto[T 5.0022], tassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ pañcamo cetokhilo pahīno hoti. Imassa pañca cetokhilā pahīnā honti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu does not doubt the Dhamma... he does not doubt the Sangha... he does not doubt the training... he is not angry with his companions in the holy life, is pleased, not resentful, and his mind has not become barren. Bhikkhus, for that bhikkhu who is not angry with his companions in the holy life, is pleased, not resentful, and whose mind has not become barren, his mind inclines towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving. For one whose mind inclines towards ardor, application, perseverance, and striving, in this way for him this fifth state of mental barrenness is abandoned. For him, these five states of mental barrenness are abandoned.

“Katamassa pañca cetasovinibandhā susamucchinnā honti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāmesu vītarāgo hoti vigatacchando vigatapemo vigatapipāso vigatapariḷāho vigatataṇho. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāmesu vītarāgo hoti vigatacchando vigatapemo vigatapipāso vigatapariḷāho vigatataṇho, tassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ paṭhamo cetasovinibandho susamucchinno hoti.

And what, for him, are the five bonds of the mind that are completely cut off? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is devoid of lust for sensual pleasures, without desire, without affection, without thirst, without feverish burning, and without craving. Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu who is devoid of lust for sensual pleasures, without desire, without affection, without thirst, without feverish burning, and without craving, his mind inclines to ardor, to application, to perseverance, and to striving. For one whose mind inclines to ardor, application, perseverance, and striving, in this way this first bond of the mind is completely cut off for him.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kāye vītarāgo hoti…pe… rūpe vītarāgo hoti [V 3.0018] …pe… na yāvadatthaṃ udarāvadehakaṃ bhuñjitvā seyyasukhaṃ passasukhaṃ middhasukhaṃ anuyutto viharati, na aññataraṃ devanikāyaṃ paṇidhāya brahmacariyaṃ carati – ‘imināhaṃ sīlena vā vatena vā tapena vā brahmacariyena vā devo vā bhavissāmi devaññataro vā’ti. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na aññataraṃ devanikāyaṃ paṇidhāya…pe… devaññataro vāti, tassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya. Yassa cittaṃ namati ātappāya anuyogāya sātaccāya padhānāya, evamassāyaṃ pañcamo cetasovinibandho [M 3.0273] susamucchinno hoti. Imassa pañca [T 5.0023] cetasovinibandhā susamucchinnā honti.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is without lust for the body… and so on… without lust for forms… and so on… he does not, after eating his fill, dwell devoted to the pleasure of lying down, the pleasure of lying on his side, and the pleasure of drowsiness. He does not lead the holy life aspiring to some group of devas, thinking: ‘By this virtue, or vow, or austerity, or holy life, I will become a deva or some other deva.’ Bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu who does not lead the holy life aspiring to some group of devas… or some other deva, his mind inclines toward ardor, application, perseverance, and striving. For one whose mind inclines toward ardor, application, perseverance, and striving, in this way this fifth bond of the mind is completely cut off for him. For him, these five bonds of the mind are completely cut off.

“Yassa kassaci, bhikkhave, bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā ime pañca cetokhilā pahīnā ime pañca cetasovinibandhā susamucchinnā[P 5.0021], tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no parihāni.

Bhikkhus, for any bhikkhu or bhikkhuni for whom these five mental barrennesses are abandoned and these five bonds of the mind are completely cut off, for them, whatever night or day comes, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, juṇhapakkhe candassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vaḍḍhateva vaṇṇena vaḍḍhati maṇḍalena vaḍḍhati ābhāya vaḍḍhati ārohapariṇāhena; evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, yassa kassaci bhikkhussa vā bhikkhuniyā vā ime pañca cetokhilā pahīnā ime pañca cetasovinibandhā susamucchinnā, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no parihānī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

Just as, bhikkhus, during the bright fortnight, as night and day pass for the moon, it only increases in beauty, increases in its orb, increases in its radiance, and increases in its height and breadth; so too, bhikkhus, for any bhikkhu or bhikkhuni for whom these five mental barrennesses are abandoned and these five bonds of the mind are completely cut off, for them, whatever night or day comes, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline.” Fourth.

5. Appamādasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Heedfulness

15. “Yāvatā, bhikkhave, sattā apadā vā dvipadā vā catuppadā vā bahuppadā vā rūpino vā arūpino vā saññino vā asaññino vā nevasaññināsaññino vā, tathāgato tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho; evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te appamādamūlakā appamādasamosaraṇā. Appamādo tesaṃ tesaṃ dhammānaṃ (sī. ka.) saṃ. ni. 5.139 aggamakkhāyati.

15. Bhikkhus, as many beings as there are—footless, two-footed, four-footed, or many-footed; with form or formless; percipient, non-percipient, or neither-percipient-nor-non-percipient—the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, is declared the foremost among them. So too, bhikkhus, whatever wholesome states there are, they are all rooted in heedfulness and converge on heedfulness. Heedfulness is declared the foremost among them.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yāni kānici jaṅgalānaṃ jaṅgamānaṃ (sī. pī.) saṃ. ni. 5.139 pāṇānaṃ padajātāni, sabbāni tāni hatthipade samodhānaṃ gacchanti, hatthipadaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati, yadidaṃ mahantattena; evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave[V 3.0019], ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te appamādamūlakā appamādasamosaraṇā. Appamādo tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati.

Just as, bhikkhus, the footprints of all living beings that roam the jungle can be placed within an elephant’s footprint, and the elephant’s footprint is declared the foremost among them in terms of size; so too, bhikkhus, whatever wholesome states there are, they are all rooted in heedfulness and converge on heedfulness. Heedfulness is declared the foremost among them.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, kūṭāgārassa yā kāci gopānasiyo [T 5.0024] sabbā tā kūṭaṅgamā kūṭaninnā kūṭasamosaraṇā, kūṭo tāsaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te appamādamūlakā appamādasamosaraṇā. Appamādo tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati.

Just as, bhikkhus, in a peaked-roof house, whatever rafters there are all lead to the peak, incline towards the peak, and converge on the peak, and the peak is declared the foremost among them; so too, bhikkhus, whatever wholesome states there are, they are all rooted in heedfulness and converge on heedfulness. Heedfulness is declared the foremost among them.

“Seyyathāpi[M 3.0274][P 5.0022], bhikkhave, ye keci mūlagandhā, kāḷānusāriyaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evamevaṃ kho bhikkhave…pe….

Just as, bhikkhus, of all root fragrances, black tagara is declared the foremost; so too, bhikkhus… and so on…

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci sāragandhā, lohitacandanaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evamevaṃ kho bhikkhave…pe….

Just as, bhikkhus, of all heartwood fragrances, red sandalwood is declared the foremost; so too, bhikkhus… and so on…

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci pupphagandhā, vassikaṃ tesaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evamevaṃ kho bhikkhave…pe….

Just as, bhikkhus, of all flower fragrances, jasmine is declared the foremost; so too, bhikkhus… and so on…

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ye keci khuddarājāno kuḍḍarājāno (sī. syā. pī.), kuṭṭarājāno, kūṭarājāno (ka.) a. ni. 6.53, sabbe te rañño cakkavattissa anuyantā bhavanti, rājā tesaṃ cakkavattī aggamakkhāyati; evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Just as, bhikkhus, all petty kings are followers of a wheel-turning monarch, and the wheel-turning monarch is declared the foremost among them; so too, bhikkhus… and so on…

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, yā kāci tārakarūpānaṃ pabhā, sabbā tā candappabhāya kalaṃ nāgghanti soḷasiṃ, candappabhā tāsaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Just as, bhikkhus, the radiance of all the stars does not amount to a sixteenth part of the moon’s radiance, and the moon’s radiance is declared the foremost among them; so too, bhikkhus… and so on…

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, saradasamaye viddhe vigatavalāhake deve ādicco nabhaṃ abbhussakkamāno abbhussukkamāno (sī.) saṃ. ni. 5.146-148 sabbaṃ ākāsagataṃ tamagataṃ abhivihacca bhāsate ca tapate ca virocati ca; evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave…pe….

Just as, bhikkhus, in the autumn, when the sky is clear and cloudless, the sun, ascending into the firmament, dispels all darkness from space and shines and burns and radiates; so too, bhikkhus… and so on…

“Seyyathāpi[V 3.0020], bhikkhave, yā kāci mahānadiyo, seyyathidaṃ – gaṅgā, yamunā, aciravatī, sarabhū, mahī, sabbā tā samuddaṅgamā samuddaninnā samuddapoṇā samuddapabbhārā, mahāsamuddo tāsaṃ aggamakkhāyati; evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, ye keci kusalā dhammā, sabbe te appamādamūlakā appamādasamosaraṇā. Appamādo tesaṃ aggamakkhāyatī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

Just as, bhikkhus, the great rivers—that is, the Ganges, Yamunā, Aciravatī, Sarabhū, and Mahī—all lead to the ocean, slope towards the ocean, incline towards the ocean, and tend towards the ocean, and the great ocean is declared the foremost among them; so too, bhikkhus, whatever wholesome states there are, all are rooted in heedfulness and converge on heedfulness. Heedfulness is declared the foremost among them.” Fifth.

6. Āhuneyyasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Those Worthy of Offerings

16. “Dasayime[T 5.0025][P 5.0023], bhikkhave, puggalā āhuneyyā pāhuneyyā dakkhiṇeyyā añjalikaraṇīyā anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassa. Katame dasa? Tathāgato arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, paccekabuddho, ubhatobhāgavimutto, paññāvimutto, kāyasakkhī, diṭṭhippatto, saddhāvimutto, saddhānusārī, dhammānusārī, gotrabhū – ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa puggalā āhuneyyā…pe… anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

16. Bhikkhus, these ten individuals are worthy of offerings, worthy of hospitality, worthy of gifts, worthy of reverential salutation, an unsurpassed field of merit for the world. Which ten? The Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One; a Paccekabuddha; one liberated in both ways; one liberated by wisdom; a body-witness; one who has attained the view; one liberated by faith; a faith-follower; a Dhamma-follower; and one who has attained the change-of-lineage. These, bhikkhus, are the ten individuals worthy of offerings... an unsurpassed field of merit for the world. Sixth.

7. Paṭhamanāthasuttaṃ

7. The First Discourse on a Refuge

17. dī. ni. 3.345, 360 “Sanāthā[M 3.0275], bhikkhave, viharatha, mā anāthā. Dukkhaṃ, bhikkhave, anātho viharati. Dasayime, bhikkhave, nāthakaraṇā dhammā. Katame dasa? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti…pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu, ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

17. Dwell with a refuge, bhikkhus, not without a refuge. One without a refuge, bhikkhus, dwells in suffering. These ten, bhikkhus, are qualities that make a refuge. Which ten? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is virtuous; he dwells restrained by the Pātimokkha restraint, is perfect in conduct and resort, and sees danger in the slightest faults, undertaking and training in the training rules. That a bhikkhu is virtuous... undertaking and training in the training rules—this too is a quality that makes a refuge.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ sātthā sabyañjanā (sī.) kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā bahū sutā (?) honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti…pe… diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā, ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is learned, retaining what he has heard and accumulating what he has heard. Those teachings that are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with right meaning and phrasing, which proclaim the holy life that is utterly complete and pure—such teachings he has heard in abundance, has retained, recited verbally, examined with the mind, and thoroughly penetrated with wisdom. That a bhikkhu is learned... and thoroughly penetrated with wisdom—this too is a quality that makes a refuge.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇasahāyo [P 5.0024] kalyāṇasampavaṅko[V 3.0021]. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko, ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo[T 5.0026].

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has good friends, good companions, and is inclined towards good friends. That a bhikkhu has good friends, good companions, and is inclined towards good friends—this too is a quality that makes a refuge.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu suvaco hoti sovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgato, khamo padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaniṃ. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu suvaco hoti…pe… anusāsaniṃ, ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is easy to admonish, endowed with qualities that make him easy to admonish; he is patient and receives instruction respectfully. That a bhikkhu is easy to admonish... and receives instruction respectfully—this too is a quality that makes a refuge.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāni tāni sabrahmacārīnaṃ uccāvacāni kiṃkaraṇīyāni, tattha dakkho hoti analaso tatrūpāyāya vīmaṃsāya samannāgato, alaṃ kātuṃ alaṃ saṃvidhātuṃ. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāni tāni sabrahmacārīnaṃ…pe… alaṃ kātuṃ alaṃ saṃvidhātuṃ, ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is skillful and not lazy in the various duties for his companions in the holy life, whether high or low. He is endowed with the wisdom to investigate the means for accomplishing them, and is capable of doing them and of organizing them.
