That a bhikkhu is skillful... and is capable of doing them and of organizing them—this too is a quality that makes a refuge.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammakāmo hoti piyasamudāhāro, abhidhamme abhivinaye uḷārapāmojjo. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammakāmo hoti [M 3.0276] piyasamudāhāro, abhidhamme abhivinaye uḷārapāmojjo, ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is a lover of the Dhamma, his speech is endearing, and he has great joy in the higher Dhamma and the higher Vinaya. That a bhikkhu is a lover of the Dhamma, his speech is endearing, and he has great joy in the higher Dhamma and the higher Vinaya—this too is a quality that makes a refuge.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu, ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells with energy aroused for the abandoning of unwholesome qualities and for the attainment of wholesome qualities; he is strong, firm in his exertion, not casting off the burden in regard to wholesome qualities. That a bhikkhu dwells with energy aroused... not casting off the burden in regard to wholesome qualities—this too is a quality that makes a refuge.

“Puna [P 5.0025] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena, ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is content with whatever robe, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick he may get. That a bhikkhu is content with whatever robe, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick he may get—this too is a quality that makes a refuge.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satimā hoti [T 5.0027] paramena satinepakkena samannāgato cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satimā hoti paramena [V 3.0022] satinepakkena samannāgato cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā, ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is mindful, endowed with supreme mindfulness and prudence, able to remember and recollect what was done and said long ago. That a bhikkhu is mindful... able to remember and recollect what was done and said long ago—this too is a quality that makes a refuge.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā, ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is wise, endowed with wisdom regarding arising and passing away, which is noble, penetrative, and leads rightly to the complete destruction of suffering. That a bhikkhu is wise... and leads rightly to the complete destruction of suffering—this too is a quality that makes a refuge.

“Sanāthā, bhikkhave, viharatha, mā anāthā. Dukkhaṃ, bhikkhave, anātho viharati. Ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa nāthakaraṇā dhammā”ti. Sattamaṃ.

Dwell with a refuge, bhikkhus, not without a refuge. One without a refuge, bhikkhus, dwells in suffering. These, bhikkhus, are indeed the ten qualities that make a refuge. Seventh.

8. Dutiyanāthasuttaṃ

8. The Second Discourse on a Refuge

18. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

18. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: 'Bhikkhus!' 'Venerable sir,' those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Sanāthā[M 3.0277], bhikkhave, viharatha, mā anāthā. Dukkhaṃ, bhikkhave, anātho viharati. Dasayime, bhikkhave, nāthakaraṇā dhammā. Katame dasa? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti…pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu. ‘Sīlavā vatāyaṃ bhikkhu pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesū’ti therāpi naṃ bhikkhū vattabbaṃ [P 5.0026] anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti, majjhimāpi bhikkhū… navāpi bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti. Tassa therānukampitassa majjhimānukampitassa navānukampitassa vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no parihāni. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

“Dwell with a protector, bhikkhus, not without one. One without a protector dwells in suffering, bhikkhus. These ten, bhikkhus, are qualities that make a protector. What ten? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is virtuous... he trains, having undertaken the training rules. ‘Indeed, this bhikkhu is virtuous; he dwells restrained by the Pātimokkha restraint, accomplished in conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults; he trains, having undertaken the training rules.’ Thus, the elder bhikkhus consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed; the middle bhikkhus... and the new bhikkhus consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed. For him, who is regarded with compassion by the elder, middle, and new bhikkhus, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline. This, too, is a quality that makes a protector.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti…pe… diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā. ‘Bahussuto vatāyaṃ bhikkhu sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā [T 5.0028][V 3.0023] sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā’ti therāpi naṃ bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti, majjhimāpi bhikkhū… navāpi bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti. Tassa therānukampitassa majjhimānukampitassa navānukampitassa vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no parihāni. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is one of great learning... they are well penetrated by wisdom. ‘Indeed, this bhikkhu is one of great learning, a bearer of what has been heard, an accumulator of what has been heard. Those teachings that are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, which proclaim the holy life that is utterly complete and pure—such teachings have been much heard by him, borne in mind, practiced by speech, examined by the mind, and well penetrated by wisdom.’ Thus, the elder bhikkhus consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed; the middle bhikkhus... and the new bhikkhus consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed. For him, who is regarded with compassion by the elder, middle, and new bhikkhus, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline. This, too, is a quality that makes a protector.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko. ‘Kalyāṇamitto vatāyaṃ bhikkhu kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko’ti therāpi naṃ bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti, majjhimāpi bhikkhū… navāpi bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti. Tassa therānukampitassa majjhimānukampitassa navānukampitassa vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no parihāni. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has good friends, good companions, and is devoted to good friends. ‘Indeed, this bhikkhu has good friends, good companions, and is devoted to good friends.’ Thus, the elder bhikkhus consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed; the middle bhikkhus... and the new bhikkhus consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed. For him, who is regarded with compassion by the elder, middle, and new bhikkhus, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline. This, too, is a quality that makes a protector.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu suvaco hoti sovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgato, khamo padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaniṃ. ‘Suvaco vatāyaṃ bhikkhu sovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgato, khamo padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsani’nti therāpi naṃ bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ [P 5.0027] maññanti, majjhimāpi bhikkhū… navāpi bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti. Tassa therānukampitassa majjhimānukampitassa [M 3.0278] navānukampitassa vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no parihāni. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is easy to admonish, endowed with qualities that make one easy to admonish; he is patient and accepts instruction respectfully. ‘Indeed, this bhikkhu is easy to admonish, endowed with qualities that make one easy to admonish; he is patient and accepts instruction respectfully.’ Thus, the elder bhikkhus consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed; the middle bhikkhus... and the new bhikkhus consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed. For him, who is regarded with compassion by the elder, middle, and new bhikkhus, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline. This, too, is a quality that makes a protector.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāni tāni sabrahmacārīnaṃ uccāvacāni [T 5.0029] kiṃkaraṇīyāni, tattha dakkho hoti analaso, tatrūpāyāya vīmaṃsāya samannāgato, alaṃ kātuṃ alaṃ saṃvidhātuṃ. ‘Yāni tāni sabrahmacārīnaṃ uccāvacāni kiṃkaraṇīyāni, tattha dakkho vatāyaṃ bhikkhu analaso, tatrūpāyāya vīmaṃsāya samannāgato, alaṃ kātuṃ alaṃ saṃvidhātu’nti therāpi naṃ bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti, majjhimāpi bhikkhū… navāpi bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti. Tassa therānukampitassa majjhimānukampitassa navānukampitassa vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no parihāni. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is skilled and not lazy in the various duties, great and small, for his companions in the holy life; he is endowed with an inquiring wisdom suitable for the task, and is competent to carry it out and to organize it. ‘Indeed, this bhikkhu is skilled and not lazy in the various duties, great and small, for his companions in the holy life; he is endowed with an inquiring wisdom suitable for the task, and is competent to carry it out and to organize it.’ Thus, the elder bhikkhus consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed; the middle bhikkhus... and the new bhikkhus consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed. For him, who is regarded with compassion by the elder, middle, and new bhikkhus, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline. This, too, is a quality that makes a protector.

“Puna [V 3.0024] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammakāmo hoti piyasamudāhāro, abhidhamme abhivinaye uḷārapāmojjo. ‘Dhammakāmo vatāyaṃ bhikkhu piyasamudāhāro, abhidhamme abhivinaye uḷārapāmojjo’ti therāpi naṃ bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti, majjhimāpi bhikkhū… navāpi bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti. Tassa therānukampitassa majjhimānukampitassa navānukampitassa vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no parihāni. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is a lover of the Dhamma, one whose conversation is dear, and who has great joy in the higher Dhamma and the higher Vinaya. ‘Indeed, this bhikkhu is a lover of the Dhamma, one whose conversation is dear, and who has great joy in the higher Dhamma and the higher Vinaya.’ Thus, the elder bhikkhus consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed; the middle bhikkhus... and the new bhikkhus consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed. For him, who is regarded with compassion by the elder, middle, and new bhikkhus, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline. This, too, is a quality that makes a protector.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu ‘āraddhavīriyo vatāyaṃ bhikkhu viharati akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya, kusalānaṃ [P 5.0028] dhammānaṃ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesū’ti therāpi naṃ bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti, majjhimāpi bhikkhū… navāpi bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti[T 5.0030]. Tassa therānukampitassa majjhimānukampitassa navānukampitassa vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no parihāni. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells with aroused energy for the abandoning of unwholesome qualities and for the attainment of wholesome qualities; he is strong, of steadfast exertion, not laying down the burden in regard to wholesome qualities. ‘Indeed, this bhikkhu dwells with aroused energy for the abandoning of unwholesome qualities and for the attainment of wholesome qualities; he is strong, of steadfast exertion, not laying down the burden in regard to wholesome qualities.’ Thus, the elder bhikkhus consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed; the middle bhikkhus... and the new bhikkhus consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed. For him, who is regarded with compassion by the elder, middle, and new bhikkhus, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline. This, too, is a quality that makes a protector.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena. ‘Santuṭṭho vatāyaṃ bhikkhu itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārenā’ti therāpi [M 3.0279] naṃ bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti, majjhimāpi bhikkhū… navāpi bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti. Tassa therānukampitassa majjhimānukampitassa navānukampitassa vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no parihāni. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is content with whatever kind of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick he may receive. ‘Indeed, this bhikkhu is content with whatever kind of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick he may receive’—thus thinking, the senior bhikkhus, too, consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed; the middle bhikkhus... the junior bhikkhus, too, consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed. For him, who is regarded with compassion by the senior, middle, and junior bhikkhus, only growth is to be expected in wholesome states, not decline. This quality, too, is one that makes a protector.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satimā hoti paramena satinepakkena samannāgato, cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā. ‘Satimā vatāyaṃ bhikkhu paramena satinepakkena samannāgato, cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā’ti therāpi naṃ bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti, majjhimāpi bhikkhū… navāpi bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti. Tassa therānukampitassa majjhimānukampitassa navānukampitassa vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu, no parihāni. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is mindful, endowed with supreme mindfulness and discretion; he is one who remembers and recollects what was done and said long ago. ‘Indeed, this bhikkhu is mindful, endowed with supreme mindfulness and discretion; he is one who remembers and recollects what was done and said long ago’—thus thinking, the senior bhikkhus, too, consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed; the middle bhikkhus... the junior bhikkhus, too, consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed. For him, who is regarded with compassion by the senior, middle, and junior bhikkhus, only growth is to be expected in wholesome states, not decline. This quality, too, is one that makes a protector.

“Puna [V 3.0025] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paññavā hoti udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā. ‘Paññavā vatāyaṃ bhikkhu udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā’ti therāpi naṃ bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ maññanti, majjhimāpi bhikkhū… navāpi [T 5.0031] bhikkhū vattabbaṃ anusāsitabbaṃ [P 5.0029] maññanti. Tassa therānukampitassa…pe… no parihāni. Ayampi dhammo nāthakaraṇo.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is wise, endowed with wisdom that discerns arising and passing away, which is noble, penetrative, and rightly leads to the complete destruction of suffering. ‘Indeed, this bhikkhu is wise, endowed with wisdom that discerns arising and passing away, which is noble, penetrative, and rightly leads to the complete destruction of suffering’—thus thinking, the senior bhikkhus, too, consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed; the middle bhikkhus... the junior bhikkhus, too, consider him fit to be spoken to and instructed. For him, who is regarded with compassion by the senior, middle, and junior bhikkhus, only growth is to be expected in wholesome states, not decline. This quality, too, is one that makes a protector.

“Sanāthā, bhikkhave, viharatha, mā anāthā. Dukkhaṃ, bhikkhave, anātho viharati. Ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa nāthakaraṇā dhammā”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Attamanā te bhikkhū bhagavato bhāsitaṃ abhinandunti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Dwell with a protector, bhikkhus, not without one. One without a protector, bhikkhus, dwells in suffering. These, indeed, bhikkhus, are the ten qualities that make a protector.” The Blessed One said this. With delighted minds, those bhikkhus rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words. The Eighth.

9. Paṭhamaariyāvāsasuttaṃ

9. The First Discourse on the Abodes of the Noble Ones

19. dī. ni. 3.348, 360 “Dasayime, bhikkhave, ariyāvāsā, ye ariyā āvasiṃsu vā āvasanti vā āvasissanti vā. Katame dasa? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcaṅgavippahīno hoti, chaḷaṅgasamannāgato, ekārakkho, caturāpasseno, paṇunnapaccekasacco panuṇṇapaccekasacco (ka.), samavayasaṭṭhesano, anāvilasaṅkappo, passaddhakāyasaṅkhāro, suvimuttacitto, suvimuttapañño. Ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa ariyāvāsā[M 3.0280], ye ariyā āvasiṃsu vā āvasanti vā āvasissanti vā”ti. Navamaṃ.

19. “Bhikkhus, these are the ten abodes of the noble ones, in which the noble ones have dwelt, dwell, or will dwell. Which ten? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is one who has abandoned five factors, is endowed with six factors, has a single guard, has four supports, is one whose individual truths have been dispelled, is one whose quests have been completely stilled, is one whose intentions are unclouded, is one whose bodily formations are tranquilized, is one whose mind is well liberated, and is one whose wisdom is well liberated. These, bhikkhus, are the ten abodes of the noble ones, in which the noble ones have dwelt, dwell, or will dwell.” The ninth.

10. Dutiyaariyāvāsasuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse on the Abodes of the Noble Ones

20. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kurūsu viharati kammāsadhammaṃ [P 5.0030] nāma kurūnaṃ nigamo. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi…pe….

20. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Kurus, at a market town of the Kurus named Kammāsadhamma. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus...

“Dasayime, bhikkhave, ariyāvāsā, ye ariyā āvasiṃsu vā āvasanti vā āvasissanti vā. Katame dasa? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcaṅgavippahīno hoti, chaḷaṅgasamannāgato[V 3.0026], ekārakkho, caturāpasseno, paṇunnapaccekasacco, samavayasaṭṭhesano, anāvilasaṅkappo, passaddhakāyasaṅkhāro, suvimuttacitto, suvimuttapañño.

“Bhikkhus, these are the ten abodes of the noble ones, in which the noble ones have dwelt, dwell, or will dwell. What are the ten? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is one who has abandoned five factors, is endowed with six factors, has a single guard, has four supports, is one whose individual truths have been dispelled, is one whose quests have been completely stilled, is one whose intentions are unclouded, is one whose bodily formations are tranquilized, is one whose mind is well liberated, and is one whose wisdom is well liberated.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcaṅgavippahīno hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno kāmacchando [T 5.0032] pahīno hoti, byāpādo pahīno hoti, thinamiddhaṃ pahīnaṃ hoti, uddhaccakukkuccaṃ pahīnaṃ hoti, vicikicchā pahīnā hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pañcaṅgavippahīno hoti.

“And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu one who has abandoned five factors? Here, bhikkhus, for a bhikkhu, sensual desire is abandoned, ill will is abandoned, sloth and torpor are abandoned, restlessness and remorse are abandoned, and doubt is abandoned. Thus, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is one who has abandoned five factors.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chaḷaṅgasamannāgato hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno. Sotena saddaṃ sutvā… ghānena gandhaṃ ghāyitvā… jivhāya rasaṃ sāyitvā… kāyena phoṭṭhabbaṃ phusitvā… manasā dhammaṃ viññāya neva sumano hoti na dummano, upekkhako viharati sato sampajāno. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu chaḷaṅgasamannāgato hoti.

“And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu endowed with six factors? Here, bhikkhus, having seen a form with the eye, a bhikkhu is neither pleased nor displeased but dwells equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending. Having heard a sound with the ear… having smelled an odor with the nose… having tasted a flavor with the tongue… having touched a tangible object with the body… having cognized a mental phenomenon with the mind, he is neither pleased nor displeased but dwells equanimous, mindful, and clearly comprehending. Thus, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is endowed with six factors.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ekārakkho hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satārakkhena cetasā samannāgato hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ekārakkho hoti.

“And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu one with a single guard? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is endowed with a mind guarded by mindfulness. Thus, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is one with a single guard.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu caturāpasseno hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṅkhāyekaṃ paṭisevati, saṅkhāyekaṃ adhivāseti, saṅkhāyekaṃ parivajjeti, saṅkhāyekaṃ vinodeti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu caturāpasseno hoti.

“And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu one with four supports? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, with discernment, makes use of certain things; with discernment, he endures certain things; with discernment, he avoids certain things; with discernment, he dispels certain things. Thus, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is one with four supports.

“Kathañca[M 3.0281][P 5.0031], bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṇunnapaccekasacco hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno yāni tāni puthusamaṇabrāhmaṇānaṃ puthupaccekasaccāni, seyyathidaṃ – ‘sassato loko’ti vā, ‘asassato loko’ti vā, ‘antavā loko’ti vā, ‘anantavā loko’ti vā, ‘taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīra’nti vā, ‘aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīra’nti vā, ‘hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, ‘neva hoti [T 5.0033] na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā’ti vā, sabbāni tāni nunnāni honti paṇunnāni [V 3.0027] nuṇṇāni honti panuṇṇāni (?) cattāni vantāni muttāni pahīnāni paṭinissaṭṭhāni. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṇunnapaccekasacco hoti.

“And how, monks, is a monk one whose individual truths have been dispelled? Here, monks, for a monk, whatever various individual truths there are of the many ascetics and brahmins—such as, ‘the world is eternal,’ or ‘the world is not eternal,’ ‘the world is finite,’ or ‘the world is infinite,’ ‘the soul is the same as the body,’ or ‘the soul is different from the body,’ ‘a being exists after death,’ or ‘a being does not exist after death,’ ‘a being both exists and does not exist after death,’ or ‘a being neither exists nor does not exist after death’—all these have been dispelled, well dispelled, discarded, disgorged, released, abandoned, and relinquished. Thus, monks, a monk is one whose individual truths have been dispelled.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu samavayasaṭṭhesano hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno kāmesanā pahīnā hoti, bhavesanā pahīnā hoti, brahmacariyesanā paṭippassaddhā. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu samavayasaṭṭhesano hoti.

“And how, monks, is a monk one whose quests have been completely stilled? Here, monks, for a monk, the quest for sensual pleasures is abandoned, the quest for existence is abandoned, and the quest for the holy life is pacified. Thus, monks, a monk is one whose quests have been completely stilled.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anāvilasaṅkappo hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno kāmasaṅkappo pahīno hoti, byāpādasaṅkappo pahīno hoti, vihiṃsāsaṅkappo pahīno hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu anāvilasaṅkappo hoti.

“And how, monks, is a monk one whose intentions are unclouded? Here, monks, for a monk, sensual intention is abandoned, the intention of ill will is abandoned, and the intention of harming is abandoned. Thus, monks, a monk is one whose intentions are unclouded.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu passaddhakāyasaṅkhāro hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sukhassa ca pahānā dukkhassa ca pahānā pubbeva somanassadomanassānaṃ atthaṅgamā adukkhamasukhaṃ upekkhāsatipārisuddhiṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ upasampajja viharati. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu passaddhakāyasaṅkhāro hoti.

“And how, monks, is a monk one whose bodily formations are tranquilized? Here, monks, with the abandoning of pleasure and pain, and with the previous disappearance of joy and sorrow, a monk enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna, which is neither-painful-nor-pleasant and has purity of mindfulness due to equanimity. Thus, monks, a monk is one whose bodily formations are tranquilized.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu suvimuttacitto hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno rāgā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ hoti, dosā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ hoti, mohā cittaṃ vimuttaṃ hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu suvimuttacitto hoti.

“And how, monks, is a monk one whose mind is well liberated? Here, monks, a monk’s mind is liberated from lust, liberated from hatred, and liberated from delusion. Thus, monks, a monk is one whose mind is well liberated.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu suvimuttapañño hoti? Idha[P 5.0032], bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘rāgo me pahīno ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṃkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo’ti pajānāti, doso me pahīno…pe… ‘moho [M 3.0282] me pahīno [T 5.0034] ucchinnamūlo tālāvatthukato anabhāvaṃkato āyatiṃ anuppādadhammo’ti pajānāti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhu suvimuttapañño hoti.

“And how, monks, is a monk one whose wisdom is well liberated? Here, monks, a monk understands: ‘My lust has been abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, and is of a nature not to arise in the future.’ He understands: ‘My hatred has been abandoned...’ He understands: ‘My delusion has been abandoned, its root cut off, made like a palm stump, brought to a state of non-existence, and is of a nature not to arise in the future.’ Thus, monks, a monk is one whose wisdom is well liberated.

“Ye hi keci, bhikkhave, atītamaddhānaṃ ariyā ariyāvāse āvasiṃsu, sabbe te imeva dasa ariyāvāse āvasiṃsu; ye hi keci, bhikkhave, anāgatamaddhānaṃ ariyā ariyāvāse āvasissanti, sabbe te imeva dasa ariyāvāse āvasissanti; ye hi yepi (?) keci, bhikkhave[V 3.0028], etarahi ariyā ariyāvāse āvasanti, sabbe te imeva dasa ariyāvāse āvasanti. Ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa ariyāvāsā, ye ariyā āvasiṃsu vā āvasanti vā āvasissanti vā”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“Monks, whatever noble ones in the past have dwelt in noble abodes, all have dwelt in these same ten noble abodes. Whatever noble ones in the future will dwell in noble abodes, all will dwell in these same ten noble abodes. Whatever noble ones at present dwell in noble abodes, all dwell in these same ten noble abodes. These, monks, are the ten noble abodes in which noble ones have dwelt, are dwelling, or will dwell.” Tenth.

Nāthavaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter on Protectors.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary for this is:

Senāsanañca pañcaṅgaṃ, saṃyojanākhilena ca;

Appamādo āhuneyyo, dve nāthā dve ariyāvāsāti.

Lodging, the five factors, fetters and barrenness; Heedfulness, worthy of offerings, two on protectors, and two on noble abodes.

3. Mahāvaggo

3. The Great Chapter

1. Sīhanādasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Lion’s Roar

21. “Sīho[V 3.0029], bhikkhave, migarājā sāyanhasamayaṃ āsayā nikkhamati. Āsayā nikkhamitvā vijambhati. Vijambhitvā samantā catuddisaṃ catuddisā (syā. ka.) a. ni. 6.64 anuviloketi. Samantā catuddisaṃ catuddisā (syā. ka.) a. ni. 6.64 anuviloketvā [P 5.0033] tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ nadati. Tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ naditvā gocarāya pakkamati. Taṃ kissa hetu? ‘Māhaṃ khuddake pāṇe visamagate saṅghātaṃ āpādesi’nti!

21. “Monks, the lion, the king of beasts, emerges from his lair in the evening. Having emerged from his lair, he stretches. Having stretched, he surveys the four directions all around. Having surveyed the four directions all around, he lets out a lion’s roar three times. Having let out a lion’s roar three times, he sets out in search of prey. For what reason? ‘May I not cause the destruction of small creatures that have gone to a precarious place!’”

“‘Sīho’ti, kho bhikkhave, tathāgatassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ arahato sammāsambuddhassa. Yaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tathāgato [T 5.0035] parisāya dhammaṃ deseti, idamassa hoti sīhanādasmiṃ.

“‘The Lion,’ monks, is a designation for the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly and Completely Awakened One. When the Tathāgata teaches the Dhamma to an assembly, this is his lion’s roar.”

ma. ni. 1.148; vibha. 760; paṭi. ma. 2.44 “Dasayimāni[M 3.0283], bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalāni, yehi balehi samannāgato tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti. Katamāni dasa? Idha, bhikkhave, tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

“Monks, there are these ten powers of a Tathāgata, endowed with which the Tathāgata claims the supreme position, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the excellent Wheel of Dhamma. What are the ten? Here, monks, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, cause as cause and what is not a cause as not a cause. That the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, cause as cause and what is not a cause as not a cause—this, monks, is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the supreme position, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the excellent Wheel of Dhamma.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

“Furthermore, monks, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the result of the undertaking of past, future, and present kamma, with its supporting conditions and its root causes. That the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the result of the undertaking of past, future, and present kamma, with its supporting conditions and its root causes—this, monks, is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the supreme position, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the excellent Wheel of Dhamma.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi, bhikkhave[V 3.0030], tathāgato sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

“Furthermore, Bhikkhus, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the path that leads to all destinations. That the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the path that leads to all destinations—this, Bhikkhus, is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the supreme position, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the excellent Wheel of Dhamma.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato anekadhātuṃ nānādhātuṃ [P 5.0034] lokaṃ anekadhātunānādhātulokaṃ (sī. ka.) yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato anekadhātuṃ nānādhātuṃ lokaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ [T 5.0036] hoti…pe… brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

“Furthermore, Bhikkhus, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the world with its many and various elements. That the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the world with its many and various elements—this, Bhikkhus, is a power of the Tathāgata… and sets in motion the excellent Wheel of Dhamma.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikataṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikataṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti…pe… brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

“Furthermore, Bhikkhus, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the various dispositions of beings. That the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the various dispositions of beings—this, Bhikkhus, is a power of the Tathāgata… and sets in motion the excellent Wheel of Dhamma.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ [M 3.0284] indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti…pe… brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

“Furthermore, Bhikkhus, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the state of maturity and immaturity of the faculties of other beings and other persons. That the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the state of maturity and immaturity of the faculties of other beings and other persons—this, Bhikkhus, is a power of the Tathāgata… and sets in motion the excellent Wheel of Dhamma.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampi…pe… pajānāti, idampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti…pe… brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

“Furthermore, Bhikkhus, the Tathāgata understands, as it really is, the defilement, purification, and emergence concerning the absorptions, liberations, concentrations, and attainments. That the Tathāgata understands this… this, Bhikkhus, is a power of the Tathāgata… and sets in motion the excellent Wheel of Dhamma.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo tissopi jātiyo catassopi jātiyo pañcapi jātiyo dasapi jātiyo vīsampi jātiyo tiṃsampi jātiyo cattālīsampi jātiyo [P 5.0035] paññāsampi jātiyo jātisatampi jātisahassampi jātisatasahassampi anekepi [T 5.0037] saṃvaṭṭakappe anekepi vivaṭṭakappe anekepi saṃvaṭṭavivaṭṭakappe, ‘amutrāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto amutra udapādiṃ; tatrāpāsiṃ evaṃnāmo evaṃgotto evaṃvaṇṇo evamāhāro evaṃsukhadukkhappaṭisaṃvedī evamāyupariyanto, so tato cuto idhūpapanno’ti, iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Yampi [V 3.0031] bhikkhave, tathāgato anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, idampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

“Furthermore, Bhikkhus, the Tathāgata recollects his manifold past abodes, that is to say: one birth, two births, three births, four births, five births, ten births, twenty births, thirty births, forty births, fifty births, a hundred births, a thousand births, a hundred thousand births; many eons of cosmic contraction, many eons of cosmic expansion, and many eons of cosmic contraction and expansion. ‘In that existence I had such a name, belonged to such a clan, had such an appearance, was sustained by such food, experienced such pleasure and pain, and had such a lifespan. Passing away from there, I was reborn in another existence. There too I had such a name, belonged to such a clan, had such an appearance, was sustained by such food, experienced such pleasure and pain, and had such a lifespan. Passing away from there, I have been reborn here.’ Thus he recollects his manifold past abodes with their aspects and details. That the Tathāgata, Bhikkhus, recollects his manifold past abodes, that is to say: one birth, two births… and so on… thus he recollects his manifold past abodes with their aspects and details—this, Bhikkhus, is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the supreme position, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the excellent Wheel of Dhamma.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti – ‘ime vata bhonto sattā kāyaduccaritena samannāgatā vacīduccaritena samannāgatā manoduccaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ upavādakā micchādiṭṭhikā micchādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapannā; ime vā pana bhonto sattā kāyasucaritena [M 3.0285] samannāgatā vacīsucaritena samannāgatā manosucaritena samannāgatā ariyānaṃ anupavādakā sammādiṭṭhikā sammādiṭṭhikammasamādānā, te kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ [T 5.0038] upapannā’ti. Iti dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena satte passati cavamāne upapajjamāne hīne paṇīte suvaṇṇe dubbaṇṇe, sugate duggate yathākammūpage satte pajānāti. Yampi[P 5.0036], bhikkhave, tathāgato dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena…pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti, idampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

“Furthermore, Bhikkhus, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, the Tathāgata sees beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, bound for a good destination and a bad destination—and he understands beings who fare according to their kamma: ‘Indeed, these beings—who were endowed with misconduct of body, speech, and mind, who reviled the noble ones, held wrong view, and undertook actions based on wrong view—with the breakup of the body, after death, have been reborn in the plane of deprivation, in a bad destination, in a state of ruin, in hell. Or indeed, these beings—who were endowed with good conduct of body, speech, and mind, who did not revile the noble ones, held right view, and undertook actions based on right view—with the breakup of the body, after death, have been reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world.’ Thus, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, he sees beings passing away and being reborn—inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, bound for a good destination and a bad destination—and he understands beings who fare according to their kamma. That the Tathāgata, Bhikkhus, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human… and so on… understands beings who fare according to their kamma—this, Bhikkhus, is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the supreme position, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the excellent Wheel of Dhamma.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, tathāgato āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Yampi, bhikkhave, tathāgato āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati, idampi, bhikkhave, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

“Furthermore, Bhikkhus, the Tathāgata, through the destruction of the taints, having realized for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, dwells having attained it. That the Tathāgata, Bhikkhus, through the destruction of the taints, having realized for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, dwells having attained it—this, Bhikkhus, is a power of the Tathāgata. Relying on this power, the Tathāgata claims the supreme position, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the excellent Wheel of Dhamma.

“Imāni kho, bhikkhave, dasa tathāgatassa tathāgatabalāni, yehi balehi samannāgato tathāgato [V 3.0032] āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavattetī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“These, monks, are the ten powers of the Tathāgata, endowed with which the Tathāgata claims the foremost position, roars his lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the supreme wheel.” The First.

2. Adhivuttipadasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Grounds for Declaration

22. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ bhagavā etadavoca –

22. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. The Blessed One then said this to the Venerable Ānanda, who was seated to one side:

“Ye te, ānanda, dhammā tesaṃ tesaṃ adhivuttipadānaṃ adhimuttipadānaṃ (ka.) abhiññā sacchikiriyāya saṃvattanti, visārado ahaṃ, ānanda, tattha paṭijānāmi. ‘Tesaṃ tesaṃ tathā tathā dhammaṃ desetuṃ [T 5.0039] yathā yathā paṭipanno santaṃ vā atthīti ñassati, asantaṃ vā natthīti ñassati, hīnaṃ vā hīnanti ñassati[M 3.0286], paṇītaṃ vā paṇītanti ñassati, sauttaraṃ vā sauttaranti ñassati, anuttaraṃ vā anuttaranti ñassati; yathā yathā vā pana taṃ ñāteyyaṃ vā daṭṭheyyaṃ [P 5.0037] vā sacchikareyyaṃ vā, tathā tathā ñassati vā dakkhati vā sacchikarissati vā’ti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati. Etadānuttariyaṃ, ānanda, ñāṇānaṃ yadidaṃ tattha tattha yathābhūtañāṇaṃ. Etasmā cāhaṃ, ānanda, ñāṇā aññaṃ ñāṇaṃ uttaritaraṃ vā paṇītataraṃ vā natthīti vadāmi.

“Ānanda, concerning those principles that conduce to the direct knowledge and realization of the various grounds for declaration, I am confident, Ānanda, in making this claim: ‘To teach the Dhamma in such and such a way that one who practices accordingly will know what is present as ‘it is present,’ and what is not present as ‘it is not present’; what is inferior as ‘it is inferior,’ and what is sublime as ‘it is sublime’; what is surpassable as ‘it is surpassable,’ and what is unsurpassable as ‘it is unsurpassable.’ And in whatever way a thing is to be known, to be seen, or to be realized, in that very way one will know it, will see it, or will realize it. This possibility exists. This, Ānanda, is the unsurpassed among knowledges, namely, the knowledge of things as they truly are in each case. And I declare, Ānanda, that there is no other knowledge higher or more excellent than this knowledge.

“Dasayimāni, ānanda, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalāni, yehi balehi samannāgato tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti. Katamāni dasa? Idhānanda, tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampānanda, tathāgato ṭhānañca ṭhānato aṭṭhānañca aṭṭhānato yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti, idampānanda, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

“Ānanda, these are the ten powers of a Tathāgata, possessed of which the Tathāgata claims the foremost position, utters the lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the supreme wheel. What are the ten? Here, Ānanda, the Tathāgata understands as it truly is cause as cause, and non-cause as non-cause. Ānanda, that the Tathāgata understands as it truly is cause as cause, and non-cause as non-cause—this, Ānanda, is a power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the foremost position, utters the lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the supreme wheel.

“Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, tathāgato atītānāgatapaccuppannānaṃ kammasamādānānaṃ ṭhānaso hetuso vipākaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampānanda…pe… idampānanda…pe….

“Furthermore, Ānanda, the Tathāgata understands as it truly is, by way of condition and cause, the result of actions undertaken in the past, future, and present. And that, Ānanda… this, Ānanda…

“Puna [V 3.0033] caparaṃ, ānanda, tathāgato sabbatthagāminiṃ paṭipadaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampānanda…pe… idampānanda…pe….

“Furthermore, Ānanda, the Tathāgata understands as it truly is the path that leads to all destinations. And that, Ānanda… this, Ānanda…

“Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, tathāgato anekadhātuṃ nānādhātuṃ lokaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampānanda [T 5.0040] …pe… idampānanda…pe….

“Furthermore, Ānanda, the Tathāgata understands as it truly is the world with its many elements and various elements. And that, Ānanda… this, Ānanda…

“Puna [P 5.0038] caparaṃ, ānanda, tathāgato sattānaṃ nānādhimuttikataṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampānanda…pe… idampānanda…pe….

“Furthermore, Ānanda, the Tathāgata understands as it truly is the diverse dispositions of beings. And that, Ānanda… this, Ānanda…

“Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, tathāgato parasattānaṃ parapuggalānaṃ indriyaparopariyattaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampānanda…pe… idampānanda…pe….

“Furthermore, Ānanda, the Tathāgata understands as it truly is the state of maturity and immaturity of the faculties of other beings and other individuals. And that, Ānanda… this, Ānanda…

“Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, tathāgato jhānavimokkhasamādhisamāpattīnaṃ saṃkilesaṃ vodānaṃ vuṭṭhānaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti. Yampānanda…pe… idampānanda…pe….

“Furthermore, Ānanda, the Tathāgata understands as it truly is the defilement, purification, and emergence of the absorptions, liberations, concentrations, and attainments. And that, Ānanda… this, Ānanda…

“Puna [M 3.0287] caparaṃ, ānanda, tathāgato anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati, seyyathidaṃ – ekampi jātiṃ dvepi jātiyo…pe… iti sākāraṃ sauddesaṃ anekavihitaṃ pubbenivāsaṃ anussarati. Yampānanda…pe… idampānanda…pe….

“Furthermore, Ānanda, the Tathāgata recollects his manifold past abodes, that is to say: one birth, two births… and so on… thus with their aspects and details he recollects his manifold past abodes. And that, Ānanda… this, Ānanda…

“Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, tathāgato dibbena cakkhunā visuddhena atikkantamānusakena…pe… yathākammūpage satte pajānāti. Yampānanda…pe… idampānanda…pe….

“Furthermore, Ānanda, the Tathāgata, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human… and so on… understands beings who fare according to their kamma. And that, Ānanda… this, Ānanda…

“Puna caparaṃ, ānanda, tathāgato āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Yampānanda, tathāgato āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ…pe… sacchikatvā upasampajja viharati. Idampānanda, tathāgatassa tathāgatabalaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti, parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavatteti.

“Furthermore, Ānanda, the Tathāgata, through the destruction of the taints, having realized for himself with direct knowledge in this very life the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, abides having attained it. And that, Ānanda, the Tathāgata, through the destruction of the taints… abides having attained it. This, Ānanda, is a power of the Tathāgata, relying on which power the Tathāgata claims the foremost position, utters the lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the supreme wheel.

“Imāni [V 3.0034] kho, ānanda, dasa tathāgatassa tathāgatabalāni, yehi balehi samannāgato tathāgato āsabhaṃ ṭhānaṃ paṭijānāti[T 5.0041], parisāsu sīhanādaṃ nadati, brahmacakkaṃ pavattetī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“These, indeed, Ānanda, are the ten powers of a Tathāgata, possessed of which the Tathāgata claims the foremost position, utters the lion’s roar in the assemblies, and sets in motion the supreme wheel.” The Second.

3. Kāyasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Body

23. “Atthi[P 5.0039], bhikkhave, dhammā kāyena pahātabbā, no vācāya. Atthi, bhikkhave, dhammā vācāya pahātabbā, no kāyena. Atthi, bhikkhave, dhammā neva kāyena pahātabbā no vācāya, paññāya disvā disvā disvā (sī. syā.) pahātabbā.

23. “Monks, there are phenomena that are to be abandoned by the body, not by speech. Monks, there are phenomena that are to be abandoned by speech, not by the body. Monks, there are phenomena that are to be abandoned neither by the body nor by speech, but are to be abandoned by seeing with wisdom.

“Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā kāyena pahātabbā, no vācāya? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akusalaṃ āpanno hoti kiñci desaṃ kañci deva desaṃ (sī. syā.) kāyena. Tamenaṃ anuvicca viññū sabrahmacārī evamāhaṃsu – ‘āyasmā kho akusalaṃ āpanno kiñci desaṃ kāyena. Sādhu vatāyasmā kāyaduccaritaṃ pahāya kāyasucaritaṃ bhāvetū’ti. So anuvicca viññūhi sabrahmacārīhi vuccamāno kāyaduccaritaṃ pahāya kāyasucaritaṃ bhāveti. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, dhammā kāyena pahātabbā, no vācāya.

“And what, monks, are the phenomena that are to be abandoned by the body, not by speech? Here, monks, a bhikkhu has fallen into some unwholesome group of offenses by way of the body. His wise fellow practitioners, having investigated, say to him: ‘The venerable one has indeed fallen into some unwholesome group of offenses by way of the body. It would be good, venerable sir, if you were to abandon bodily misconduct and develop bodily good conduct.’ Being spoken to thus by his wise fellow practitioners who have investigated, he abandons bodily misconduct and develops bodily good conduct. These, monks, are called the phenomena that are to be abandoned by the body, not by speech.

“Katame [M 3.0288] ca, bhikkhave, dhammā vācāya pahātabbā, no kāyena? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akusalaṃ āpanno hoti kiñci desaṃ vācāya. Tamenaṃ anuvicca viññū sabrahmacārī evamāhaṃsu – ‘āyasmā kho akusalaṃ āpanno kiñci desaṃ vācāya. Sādhu vatāyasmā vacīduccaritaṃ pahāya vacīsucaritaṃ bhāvetū’ti. So anuvicca viññūhi sabrahmacārīhi vuccamāno vacīduccaritaṃ pahāya vacīsucaritaṃ bhāveti. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, dhammā vācāya pahātabbā, no kāyena.

“And what, monks, are the phenomena that are to be abandoned by speech, not by the body? Here, monks, a bhikkhu has fallen into some unwholesome group of offenses by way of speech. His wise fellow practitioners, having investigated, say to him: ‘The venerable one has indeed fallen into some unwholesome group of offenses by way of speech. It would be good, venerable sir, if you were to abandon verbal misconduct and develop verbal good conduct.’ Being spoken to thus by his wise fellow practitioners who have investigated, he abandons verbal misconduct and develops verbal good conduct. These, monks, are called the phenomena that are to be abandoned by speech, not by the body.

“Katame ca, bhikkhave, dhammā neva kāyena pahātabbā no vācāya, paññāya disvā pahātabbā? Lobho, bhikkhave, neva kāyena pahātabbo no vācāya, paññāya disvā pahātabbo. Doso[T 5.0042], bhikkhave…pe… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso [P 5.0040]… macchariyaṃ, bhikkhave, neva kāyena pahātabbaṃ no vācāya, paññāya disvā pahātabbaṃ.

“And what, monks, are the phenomena that are to be abandoned neither by the body nor by speech, but are to be abandoned by seeing with wisdom? Greed, monks, is to be abandoned neither by the body nor by speech, but is to be abandoned by seeing with wisdom. Hatred, monks… delusion… anger… resentment… denigration… spiteful rivalry… stinginess, monks, is to be abandoned neither by the body nor by speech, but is to be abandoned by seeing with wisdom.

“Pāpikā[V 3.0035], bhikkhave, issā neva kāyena pahātabbā no vācāya, paññāya disvā pahātabbā. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, pāpikā issā? Idha, bhikkhave, ijjhati gahapatissa vā gahapatiputtassa vā dhanena vā dhaññena vā rajatena vā jātarūpena vā. Tatrāññatarassa dāsassa vā upavāsassa vā evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vatimassa gahapatissa vā gahapatiputtassa vā na ijjheyya dhanena vā dhaññena vā rajatena vā jātarūpena vā’ti. Samaṇo vā pana brāhmaṇo vā lābhī hoti cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṃ. Tatrāññatarassa samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā evaṃ hoti – ‘aho vata ayamāyasmā na lābhī assa cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārāna’nti. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, pāpikā issā.

“Evil envy, monks, is to be abandoned neither by the body nor by speech, but is to be abandoned by seeing with wisdom. And what, monks, is evil envy? Here, monks, a householder or a householder’s son prospers with wealth, grain, silver, or gold. Therein, a certain slave or dependent thinks: ‘Oh, may this householder or householder’s son not prosper with wealth, grain, silver, or gold!’ Or a recluse or brahmin is an obtainer of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick. Therein, a certain recluse or brahmin thinks: ‘Oh, may this venerable one not be an obtainer of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick!’ This, monks, is called evil envy.

“Pāpikā, bhikkhave, icchā neva kāyena pahātabbā no vācāya, paññāya disvā pahātabbā. Katamā ca, bhikkhave, pāpikā icchā? vibha. 851 Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco assaddho samāno ‘saddhoti maṃ jāneyyu’nti icchati; dussīlo samāno ‘sīlavāti maṃ jāneyyu’nti icchati; appassuto samāno ‘bahussutoti maṃ jāneyyu’nti icchati; saṅgaṇikārāmo samāno ‘pavivittoti [T 5.0043] maṃ jāneyyu’nti icchati; kusīto samāno ‘āraddhavīriyoti maṃ jāneyyu’nti icchati; muṭṭhassati samāno ‘upaṭṭhitassatīti maṃ jāneyyu’nti icchati; asamāhito samāno ‘samāhitoti maṃ [M 3.0289] jāneyyu’nti icchati; duppañño samāno ‘paññavāti maṃ jāneyyu’nti icchati; akhīṇāsavo samāno ‘khīṇāsavoti maṃ jāneyyu’nti icchati. Ayaṃ [P 5.0041] vuccati, bhikkhave, pāpikā icchā. Ime vuccanti, bhikkhave, dhammā neva kāyena pahātabbā no vācāya, paññāya disvā pahātabbā.

“Evil desire, monks, is to be abandoned neither by the body nor by speech, but is to be abandoned by seeing with wisdom. And what, monks, is evil desire? Here, monks, a certain person, being without faith, desires: ‘May they know me as one with faith!’ Being immoral, he desires: ‘May they know me as virtuous!’ Being of little learning, he desires: ‘May they know me as very learned!’ Delighting in company, he desires: ‘May they know me as secluded!’ Being lazy, he desires: ‘May they know me as energetic!’ Being of lapsed mindfulness, he desires: ‘May they know me as one whose mindfulness is established!’ Being unconcentrated, he desires: ‘May they know me as concentrated!’ Being unwise, he desires: ‘May they know me as wise!’ Not being one whose taints are destroyed, he desires: ‘May they know me as one whose taints are destroyed!’ This, monks, is called evil desire. These, monks, are called the phenomena that are to be abandoned neither by the body nor by speech, but are to be abandoned by seeing with wisdom.

“Tañce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ lobho abhibhuyya iriyati, doso… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā abhibhuyya iriyati. So evamassa veditabbo – ‘nāyamāyasmā tathā pajānāti yathā pajānato lobho na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ lobho abhibhuyya iriyati; nāyamāyasmā tathā pajānāti yathā pajānato doso na hoti… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ pāpikā icchā abhibhuyya iriyatī’ti.

“If, monks, greed arises having overcome that bhikkhu, or hatred… delusion… anger… resentment… denigration… spiteful rivalry… stinginess… evil envy… or evil desire arises having overcome him, he should be understood thus: ‘This venerable one does not understand in such a way that for one who understands, greed does not arise; that is why greed arises having overcome this venerable one. This venerable one does not understand in such a way that for one who understands, hatred… delusion… anger… resentment… denigration… spiteful rivalry… stinginess… evil envy… or evil desire does not arise; that is why evil desire arises having overcome this venerable one.’”

“Tañce[V 3.0036], bhikkhave, bhikkhuṃ lobho nābhibhuyya iriyati, doso… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā nābhibhuyya iriyati, so evamassa veditabbo – ‘tathā ayamāyasmā pajānāti yathā pajānato lobho na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ lobho nābhibhuyya iriyati; tathā ayamāyasmā pajānāti yathā pajānato doso na hoti… moho… kodho [T 5.0044]… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ pāpikā icchā nābhibhuyya iriyatī’”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“If, monks, greed does not arise having overcome that bhikkhu, or hatred… delusion… anger… resentment… denigration… spiteful rivalry… stinginess… evil envy… or evil desire does not arise having overcome him, he should be understood thus: ‘This venerable one understands in such a way that for one who understands, greed does not arise; that is why greed does not arise having overcome this venerable one. This venerable one understands in such a way that for one who understands, hatred… delusion… anger… resentment… denigration… spiteful rivalry… stinginess… evil envy… or evil desire does not arise; that is why evil desire does not arise having overcome this venerable one.’” The third.

4. Mahācundasuttaṃ

4. The Mahācunda Sutta

24. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā mahācundo cetīsu viharati sahajātiyaṃ. Tatra kho āyasmā mahācundo bhikkhū āmantesi – “āvuso bhikkhave”ti. “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū [P 5.0042] āyasmato mahācundassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā mahācundo etadavoca –

24. At one time, the Venerable Mahācunda was dwelling in Ceti at Sahajāti. There, the Venerable Mahācunda addressed the bhikkhus: “Friends, bhikkhus!” “Friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Mahācunda. The Venerable Mahācunda said this:

“Ñāṇavādaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu vadamāno – ‘jānāmimaṃ dhammaṃ, passāmimaṃ dhamma’nti. Tañce, āvuso, bhikkhuṃ lobho abhibhuyya tiṭṭhati, doso… moho [M 3.0290] … kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā abhibhuyya tiṭṭhati, so evamassa veditabbo – ‘nāyamāyasmā tathā pajānāti yathā pajānato lobho na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ lobho abhibhuyya tiṭṭhati; nāyamāyasmā tathā pajānāti yathā pajānato doso na hoti… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ pāpikā icchā abhibhuyya tiṭṭhatī’ti.

“Friends, when a bhikkhu makes a claim to knowledge, saying: ‘I know this Dhamma, I see this Dhamma’—but if greed overcomes and remains in that bhikkhu, or hatred… or delusion… or anger… or resentment… or denigration… or spiteful rivalry… or stinginess… or evil envy… or evil desire overcomes and remains in him, then he should be understood thus: ‘This venerable one does not understand in such a way that for one who understands, greed does not arise; that is why greed overcomes and remains in this venerable one. This venerable one does not understand in such a way that for one who understands, hatred… or delusion… or anger… or resentment… or denigration… or spiteful rivalry… or stinginess… or evil envy… or evil desire does not arise; that is why evil desire overcomes and remains in this venerable one.’”

“Bhāvanāvādaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu vadamāno – ‘bhāvitakāyomhi bhāvitasīlo bhāvitacitto bhāvitapañño’ti. Tañce, āvuso, bhikkhuṃ lobho abhibhuyya tiṭṭhati, doso… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā abhibhuyya tiṭṭhati, so evamassa veditabbo – ‘nāyamāyasmā tathā pajānāti yathā pajānato lobho na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ lobho abhibhuyya tiṭṭhati; nāyamāyasmā tathā pajānāti yathā pajānato doso [T 5.0045] na hoti… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso [V 3.0037] … macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ pāpikā icchā abhibhuyya tiṭṭhatī’ti.

“Friends, when a bhikkhu makes a claim to development, saying: ‘I am one with a developed body, developed virtue, developed mind, and developed wisdom’—but if greed overcomes and remains in that bhikkhu, or hatred… or delusion… or anger… or enmity… or denigration… or contempt… or stinginess… or evil envy… or evil desire overcomes and remains in him, then he should be understood thus: ‘This venerable one does not know in such a way that for one who knows, greed does not arise; for that is why greed overcomes and remains in this venerable one. This venerable one does not know in such a way that for one who knows, hatred… or delusion… or anger… or enmity… or denigration… or contempt… or stinginess… or evil envy… or evil desire does not arise; for that is why evil desire overcomes and remains in this venerable one.’”

“Ñāṇavādañca, āvuso, bhikkhu vadamāno bhāvanāvādañca – ‘jānāmimaṃ dhammaṃ, passāmimaṃ dhammaṃ, bhāvitakāyomhi bhāvitasīlo bhāvitacitto bhāvitapañño’ti. Tañce, āvuso, bhikkhuṃ lobho abhibhuyya tiṭṭhati, doso… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā abhibhuyya [P 5.0043] tiṭṭhati, so evamassa veditabbo – ‘nāyamāyasmā tathā pajānāti yathā pajānato lobho na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ lobho abhibhuyya tiṭṭhati; nāyamāyasmā tathā pajānāti yathā pajānato doso na hoti… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ pāpikā icchā abhibhuyya tiṭṭhatī’ti.

“Friends, when a bhikkhu makes a claim to knowledge and a claim to development, saying: ‘I know this Dhamma, I see this Dhamma; I am one with a developed body, developed virtue, developed mind, and developed wisdom’—but if greed overcomes and remains in that bhikkhu, or hatred… or delusion… or anger… or enmity… or denigration… or contempt… or stinginess… or evil envy… or evil desire overcomes and remains in him, then he should be understood thus: ‘This venerable one does not know in such a way that for one who knows, greed does not arise; for that is why greed overcomes and remains in this venerable one. This venerable one does not know in such a way that for one who knows, hatred… or delusion… or anger… or enmity… or denigration… or contempt… or stinginess… or evil envy… or evil desire does not arise; for that is why evil desire overcomes and remains in this venerable one.’”

“Seyyathāpi[M 3.0291], āvuso, puriso daliddova samāno aḍḍhavādaṃ vadeyya, adhanova samāno dhanavāvādaṃ vadeyya, abhogova samāno bhogavāvādaṃ vadeyya. So kismiñcideva dhanakaraṇīye samuppanne na sakkuṇeyya upanīhātuṃ dhanaṃ vā dhaññaṃ vā rajataṃ vā jātarūpaṃ vā. Tamenaṃ evaṃ jāneyyuṃ – ‘daliddova ayamāyasmā samāno aḍḍhavādaṃ vadeti, adhanova ayamāyasmā samāno dhanavāvādaṃ vadeti, abhogavāva ayamāyasmā samāno bhogavāvādaṃ vadeti. Taṃ [T 5.0046] kissa hetu? Tathā hi ayamāyasmā kismiñcideva dhanakaraṇīye samuppanne na sakkoti upanīhātuṃ dhanaṃ vā dhaññaṃ vā rajataṃ vā jātarūpaṃ vā’ti.

“Just as, friends, a man who is poor might claim to be rich, or a man without wealth might claim to be wealthy, or a man without possessions might claim to be opulent. When some matter arises requiring wealth, he would be unable to bring forth wealth, or grain, or silver, or gold. Then they would know him thus: ‘This man, though poor, claims to be rich; this man, though without wealth, claims to be wealthy; this man, though without possessions, claims to be opulent. For what reason? Because when some matter arises requiring wealth, this man is unable to bring forth wealth, or grain, or silver, or gold.’”

“Evamevaṃ kho, āvuso, ñāṇavādañca bhikkhu vadamāno bhāvanāvādañca – ‘jānāmimaṃ dhammaṃ, passāmimaṃ dhammaṃ, bhāvitakāyomhi bhāvitasīlo bhāvitacitto bhāvitapañño’ti. Taṃ ce, āvuso, bhikkhuṃ lobho abhibhuyya tiṭṭhati, doso… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā abhibhuyya tiṭṭhati, so evamassa veditabbo – ‘nāyamāyasmā tathā pajānāti yathā pajānato lobho na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ lobho abhibhuyya tiṭṭhati; nāyamāyasmā tathā pajānāti yathā pajānato doso na hoti… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā [P 5.0044] issā [V 3.0038] … pāpikā icchā na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ pāpikā icchā abhibhuyya tiṭṭhatī’ti.

“In the very same way, friends, when a bhikkhu makes a claim to knowledge and a claim to development, saying: ‘I know this Dhamma, I see this Dhamma; I am one with a developed body, developed virtue, developed mind, and developed wisdom’—but if greed overcomes and remains in that bhikkhu, or hatred… or delusion… or anger… or enmity… or denigration… or contempt… or stinginess… or evil envy… or evil desire overcomes and remains in him, then he should be understood thus: ‘This venerable one does not know in such a way that for one who knows, greed does not arise; for that is why greed overcomes and remains in this venerable one. This venerable one does not know in such a way that for one who knows, hatred… or delusion… or anger… or enmity… or denigration… or contempt… or stinginess… or evil envy… or evil desire does not arise; for that is why evil desire overcomes and remains in this venerable one.’”

“Ñāṇavādaṃ, āvuso, bhikkhu vadamāno – ‘jānāmimaṃ dhammaṃ, passāmimaṃ dhamma’nti. Tañce, āvuso, bhikkhuṃ lobho nābhibhuyya tiṭṭhati, doso… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā nābhibhuyya tiṭṭhati, so evamassa veditabbo – ‘ayamāyasmā tathā pajānāti yathā pajānato lobho na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ lobho nābhibhuyya tiṭṭhati; tathā ayamāyasmā pajānāti yathā pajānato doso na hoti… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ [T 5.0047] pāpikā icchā nābhibhuyya tiṭṭhatī’ti.

“Friends, when a bhikkhu makes a claim to knowledge, saying: ‘I know this Dhamma, I see this Dhamma’—and if greed does not overcome and remain in that bhikkhu, and if hatred… or delusion… or anger… or enmity… or denigration… or contempt… or stinginess… or evil envy… or evil desire does not overcome and remain in him, then he should be understood thus: ‘This venerable one knows in such a way that for one who knows, greed does not arise; for that is why greed does not overcome and remain in this venerable one. This venerable one knows in such a way that for one who knows, hatred… or delusion… or anger… or enmity… or denigration… or contempt… or stinginess… or evil envy… or evil desire does not arise; for that is why evil desire does not overcome and remain in this venerable one.’”

“Bhāvanāvādaṃ[M 3.0292], āvuso, bhikkhu vadamāno – ‘bhāvitakāyomhi bhāvitasīlo bhāvitacitto bhāvitapañño’ti. Tañce, āvuso, bhikkhuṃ lobho nābhibhuyya tiṭṭhati, doso… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā nābhibhuyya tiṭṭhati, so evamassa veditabbo – ‘tathā ayamāyasmā pajānāti yathā pajānato lobho na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ lobho nābhibhuyya tiṭṭhati; tathā ayamāyasmā pajānāti yathā pajānato doso na hoti… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ pāpikā icchā nābhibhuyya tiṭṭhatī’ti.

“Friends, when a bhikkhu makes a claim to development, saying: ‘I have a developed body, developed virtue, a developed mind, and developed wisdom’—and if greed does not overcome and remain in that bhikkhu, and if hatred… or delusion… or anger… or enmity… or denigration… or contempt… or stinginess… or evil envy… or evil desire does not overcome and remain in him, then he should be understood thus: ‘This venerable one knows in such a way that for one who knows, greed does not arise; for that is why greed does not overcome and remain in this venerable one. This venerable one knows in such a way that for one who knows, hatred… or delusion… or anger… or enmity… or denigration… or contempt… or stinginess… or evil envy… or evil desire does not arise; for that is why evil desire does not overcome and remain in this venerable one.’”

“Ñāṇavādañca, āvuso, bhikkhu vadamāno bhāvanāvādañca – ‘jānāmimaṃ dhammaṃ, passāmimaṃ dhammaṃ, bhāvitakāyomhi bhāvitasīlo bhāvitacitto bhāvitapañño’ti. Tañce, āvuso, bhikkhuṃ lobho nābhibhuyya tiṭṭhati, doso… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā nābhibhuyya tiṭṭhati, so evamassa veditabbo – ‘tathā ayamāyasmā pajānāti yathā pajānato lobho na hoti, tathāhimaṃ [P 5.0045] āyasmantaṃ lobho nābhibhuyya tiṭṭhati; tathā ayamāyasmā pajānāti yathā pajānato doso hoti… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ pāpikā icchā nābhibhuyya tiṭṭhatī’ti.

Friends, when a bhikkhu speaks of knowledge and of cultivation, saying: ‘I know this Dhamma, I see this Dhamma; I have a developed body, developed virtue, a developed mind, and developed wisdom’—and if greed does not overcome and persist in that bhikkhu, nor hatred… nor delusion… nor anger… nor enmity… nor contempt… nor rivalry… nor stinginess… nor evil envy… nor evil desire overcomes and persists in him, then he should be understood thus: ‘This venerable one knows in such a way that for one who knows thus, greed does not arise; for that reason, greed does not overcome and persist in this venerable one. This venerable one knows in such a way that for one who knows thus, hatred does not arise… nor delusion… nor anger… nor enmity… nor contempt… nor rivalry… nor stinginess… nor evil envy… nor evil desire does not arise; for that reason, evil desire does not overcome and persist in this venerable one.’

“Seyyathāpi[V 3.0039], āvuso, puriso aḍḍhova samāno aḍḍhavādaṃ [T 5.0048] vadeyya, dhanavāva samāno dhanavāvādaṃ vadeyya, bhogavāva samāno bhogavāvādaṃ vadeyya. So kismiñcideva dhanakaraṇīye samuppanne sakkuṇeyya upanīhātuṃ dhanaṃ vā dhaññaṃ vā rajataṃ vā jātarūpaṃ vā. Tamenaṃ evaṃ jāneyyuṃ – ‘aḍḍhova ayamāyasmā samāno aḍḍhavādaṃ vadeti, dhanavāva ayamāyasmā samāno dhanavāvādaṃ vadeti, bhogavāva ayamāyasmā samāno bhogavāvādaṃ vadeti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathā hi ayamāyasmā kismiñcideva dhanakaraṇīye samuppanne sakkoti upanīhātuṃ dhanaṃ vā dhaññaṃ vā rajataṃ vā jātarūpaṃ vā’ti.

Friends, just as a man who is affluent might speak of affluence, one who is wealthy might speak of wealth, and one who is opulent might speak of opulence. If some business to be done with wealth were to arise, he would be able to supply wealth, or grain, or silver, or gold. They would know him thus: ‘This venerable one, being affluent, speaks of affluence; this venerable one, being wealthy, speaks of wealth; this venerable one, being opulent, speaks of opulence. For what reason? Because this venerable one is able to supply wealth, or grain, or silver, or gold whenever some business to be done with wealth arises.’

Evamevaṃ [M 3.0293] kho, āvuso, ñāṇavādañca bhikkhu vadamāno bhāvanāvādañca – ‘jānāmimaṃ dhammaṃ, passāmimaṃ dhammaṃ, bhāvitakāyomhi bhāvitasīlo bhāvitacitto bhāvitapañño’ti. Tañce, āvuso, bhikkhuṃ lobho nābhibhuyya tiṭṭhati, doso… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā nābhibhuyya tiṭṭhati, so evamassa veditabbo – ‘tathā ayamāyasmā pajānāti yathā pajānato lobho na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ lobho nābhibhuyya tiṭṭhati; tathā ayamāyasmā pajānāti yathā pajānato doso na hoti… moho… kodho… upanāho… makkho… paḷāso… macchariyaṃ… pāpikā issā… pāpikā icchā na hoti, tathāhimaṃ āyasmantaṃ pāpikā icchā nābhibhuyya tiṭṭhatī’”ti. Catutthaṃ.

In this very same way, friends, when a bhikkhu speaks of knowledge and of cultivation, saying: ‘I know this Dhamma, I see this Dhamma; I have a developed body, developed virtue, a developed mind, and developed wisdom’—and if greed does not overcome and persist in that bhikkhu, nor hatred… nor delusion… nor anger… nor enmity… nor contempt… nor rivalry… nor stinginess… nor evil envy… nor evil desire overcomes and persists in him, then he should be understood thus: ‘This venerable one knows in such a way that for one who knows thus, greed does not arise; for that reason, greed does not overcome and persist in this venerable one. This venerable one knows in such a way that for one who knows thus, hatred does not arise… nor delusion… nor anger… nor enmity… nor contempt… nor rivalry… nor stinginess… nor evil envy… nor evil desire does not arise; for that reason, evil desire does not overcome and persist in this venerable one.’ The fourth.

5. Kasiṇasuttaṃ

5. The Kasiṇa Sutta

25. dī. ni. 3.346, 360; a. ni. 10.29 “Dasayimāni[P 5.0046], bhikkhave, kasiṇāyatanāni. Katamāni dasa? Pathavīkasiṇameko sañjānāti uddhaṃ adho tiriyaṃ advayaṃ appamāṇaṃ; āpokasiṇameko sañjānāti…pe… tejokasiṇameko sañjānāti… vāyokasiṇameko [T 5.0049] sañjānāti… nīlakasiṇameko sañjānāti… pītakasiṇameko sañjānāti… lohitakasiṇameko sañjānāti… odātakasiṇameko sañjānāti… ākāsakasiṇameko sañjānāti… viññāṇakasiṇameko sañjānāti uddhaṃ adho tiriyaṃ advayaṃ appamāṇaṃ. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, dasa kasiṇāyatanānī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

25. “Bhikkhus, there are these ten kasiṇa bases. What ten? One perceives the earth kasiṇa above, below, and across, as non-dual and immeasurable. One perceives the water kasiṇa… the fire kasiṇa… the air kasiṇa… the blue kasiṇa… the yellow kasiṇa… the red kasiṇa… the white kasiṇa… the space kasiṇa… one perceives the consciousness kasiṇa above, below, and across, as non-dual and immeasurable. These, indeed, bhikkhus, are the ten kasiṇa bases.” Fifth.

6. Kāḷīsuttaṃ

6. The Kāḷī Sutta

26. Ekaṃ [V 3.0040] samayaṃ āyasmā mahākaccāno avantīsu viharati kuraraghare gulaghare (ka.) kururaghare mahāva. 257 pavatte pabbate. Atha kho kāḷī upāsikā kuraragharikā yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho kāḷī upāsikā [M 3.0294] kuraragharikā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etadavoca – “vuttamidaṃ, bhante, bhagavatā kumāripañhesu –

26. At one time the Venerable Mahākaccāna was dwelling among the Avantis at Kuraraghara on the Pavatta mountain. Then the female lay follower Kāḷī of Kuraraghara approached the Venerable Mahākaccāna, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the female lay follower Kāḷī of Kuraraghara said to the Venerable Mahākaccāna: “Venerable sir, this was stated by the Blessed One in the Questions of the Maiden:”

‘Atthassa pattiṃ hadayassa santiṃ,

Jetvāna senaṃ piyasātarūpaṃ;

Ekohaṃ ekāhaṃ (ka.) jhāyaṃ sukhamanubodhiṃ,

Tasmā janena na karomi sakkhiṃ sakhiṃ (ka.) saṃ. ni. 1.161 passitabbaṃ;

Sakkhī sakhī (ka.) na sampajjati kenaci me’ti.

“‘Having conquered the army of pleasant and agreeable forms, meditating alone, I have awakened to happiness: the attainment of the goal, the peace of the heart. Therefore, I do not form an intimacy with people; no intimacy is established for me with anyone.’”

“Imassa [P 5.0047] kho, bhante, bhagavatā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa kathaṃ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti?

“Venerable sir, how is the meaning of this, which was spoken in brief by the Blessed One, to be understood in detail?”

“Pathavīkasiṇasamāpattiparamā kho, bhagini, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā ‘attho’ti abhinibbattesuṃ atthābhinibbattesuṃ (sī. syā.). Yāvatā kho, bhagini, pathavīkasiṇasamāpattiparamatā[T 5.0050], tadabhiññāsi bhagavā. Tadabhiññāya bhagavā assādamaddasa ādimaddasa (sī. syā.) ādīnavamaddasa nissaraṇamaddasa maggāmaggañāṇadassanamaddasa. Tassa assādadassanahetu ādīnavadassanahetu nissaraṇadassanahetu maggāmaggañāṇadassanahetu atthassa patti hadayassa santi viditā hoti.

“Sister, some ascetics and brahmins have regarded the supreme attainment of the earth kasiṇa as the goal. The Blessed One directly knew the full extent of the supremacy of the earth kasiṇa attainment. Having directly known it, the Blessed One saw its gratification, its danger, and the escape from it; he saw the knowledge and vision of the path and not-path. Because he saw its gratification, its danger, and the escape, and because he saw the knowledge and vision of the path and not-path, the attainment of the goal and the peace of heart became known to him.

“Āpokasiṇasamāpattiparamā kho, bhagini…pe… tejokasiṇasamāpattiparamā kho, bhagini… vāyokasiṇasamāpattiparamā kho, bhagini… nīlakasiṇasamāpattiparamā kho, bhagini… pītakasiṇasamāpattiparamā kho, bhagini… lohitakasiṇasamāpattiparamā kho, bhagini… odātakasiṇasamāpattiparamā kho, bhagini… ākāsakasiṇasamāpattiparamā kho, bhagini… viññāṇakasiṇasamāpattiparamā kho, bhagini, eke samaṇabrāhmaṇā ‘attho’ti abhinibbattesuṃ[V 3.0041]. Yāvatā kho, bhagini, viññāṇakasiṇasamāpattiparamatā, tadabhiññāsi bhagavā. Tadabhiññāya bhagavā assādamaddasa ādīnavamaddasa nissaraṇamaddasa maggāmaggañāṇadassanamaddasa. Tassa assādadassanahetu ādīnavadassanahetu nissaraṇadassanahetu maggāmaggañāṇadassanahetu atthassa patti hadayassa santi viditā hoti. Iti kho, bhagini, yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ bhagavatā kumāripañhesu –

“Sister, some ascetics and brahmins have produced the supreme attainment of the water kasiṇa, thinking, ‘This is the goal.’… the supreme attainment of the fire kasiṇa… the supreme attainment of the air kasiṇa… the supreme attainment of the blue kasiṇa… the supreme attainment of the yellow kasiṇa… the supreme attainment of the red kasiṇa… the supreme attainment of the white kasiṇa… the supreme attainment of the space kasiṇa… some ascetics and brahmins have produced the supreme attainment of the consciousness kasiṇa, thinking, ‘This is the goal.’ The Blessed One directly knew the full extent of the supremacy of the consciousness kasiṇa attainment. Having directly known it, the Blessed One saw its gratification, its danger, and the escape from it; he saw the knowledge and vision of the path and not-path. Because he saw its gratification, its danger, and the escape, and because he saw the knowledge and vision of the path and not-path, the attainment of the goal and the peace of heart became known to him. Thus, sister, what was said by the Blessed One in the Questions of the Maiden is as follows:”

‘Atthassa [M 3.0295] pattiṃ hadayassa santiṃ,

Jetvāna senaṃ piyasātarūpaṃ;

Ekohaṃ jhāyaṃ sukhamanubodhiṃ,

Tasmā [P 5.0048] janena na karomi sakkhiṃ;

Sakkhī na sampajjati kenaci me’ti.

“‘Having conquered the army of pleasant and agreeable forms, meditating alone, I have awakened to happiness: the attainment of the goal, the peace of the heart. Therefore, I do not form an intimacy with people; no intimacy is established for me with anyone.’”

“Imassa [T 5.0051] kho, bhagini, bhagavatā saṃkhittena bhāsitassa evaṃ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Sister, this is how the meaning of that brief statement spoken by the Blessed One is to be understood in detail.” Sixth.

7. Paṭhamamahāpañhāsuttaṃ

7. The First Discourse on the Great Questions

27. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho sambahulā bhikkhū pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya sāvatthiṃ piṇḍāya pavisiṃsu. Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “atippago kho tāva sāvatthiyaṃ piṇḍāya carituṃ; yaṃnūna mayaṃ yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ ārāmo tenupasaṅkameyyāmā”ti.

27. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Then a number of bhikkhus, having dressed in the morning, took their bowls and robes and entered Sāvatthī for almsfood. Then this thought occurred to those bhikkhus: ‘It is still too early to wander for almsfood in Sāvatthī. What if we were to approach the park of the wanderers of other sects?’”

Atha kho te bhikkhū yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ ārāmo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho te bhikkhū te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā etadavocuṃ –

Then those bhikkhus approached the park of the wanderers of other sects. Having approached, they exchanged joyful greetings with those wanderers of other sects. Having concluded the joyful and memorable talk, they sat down to one side. To those bhikkhus who were seated to one side, those wanderers of other sects said this:
