Furthermore, the Pātimokkha is well-mastered by him in detail, well-analyzed, well-recited, and well-adjudicated, both according to the rules and according to the details. He is capable of attending to a sick person or of having him attended to. He is capable of dispelling discontent or of having it dispelled. He is capable of dispelling arisen remorse in accordance with the Dhamma. He is capable of removing an arisen wrong view in accordance with the Dhamma. He is capable of establishing others in the higher virtue. He is capable of establishing others in the higher mind. He is capable of establishing others in the higher wisdom. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these ten qualities may give ordination.” The fourth.

5. Nissayasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Dependence

35. “Katihi [P 5.0073] nu kho, bhante, dhammehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nissayo [T 5.0077] dātabbo”ti? “Dasahi kho, upāli, dhammehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nissayo dātabbo. Katamehi dasahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti…pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu; bahussuto hoti…pe… diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā; pātimokkhaṃ kho panassa vitthārena svāgataṃ hoti suvibhattaṃ suppavattaṃ suvinicchitaṃ suttaso anubyañjanaso; paṭibalo hoti gilānaṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ vā upaṭṭhāpetuṃ vā; paṭibalo hoti anabhiratiṃ vūpakāsetuṃ vā vūpakāsāpetuṃ vā; paṭibalo hoti uppannaṃ kukkuccaṃ dhammato vinodetuṃ; paṭibalo hoti uppannaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ dhammato vivecetuṃ; paṭibalo hoti adhisīle…pe… adhicitte… adhipaññāya samādapetuṃ. Imehi kho, upāli, dasahi dhammehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā nissayo dātabbo”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

35. “Venerable sir, with how many qualities should a bhikkhu be endowed to give dependence?” “Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with ten qualities should give dependence. What ten? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu is virtuous… he undertakes and trains in the training rules. He is of great learning… well penetrated by view. Furthermore, the Pātimokkha is well-mastered by him in detail, well-analyzed, well-recited, and well-adjudicated, both according to the rules and according to the details. He is capable of attending to a sick person or of having him attended to. He is capable of dispelling discontent or of having it dispelled. He is capable of dispelling arisen remorse in accordance with the Dhamma. He is capable of removing an arisen wrong view in accordance with the Dhamma. He is capable of establishing others in the higher virtue… in the higher mind… and in the higher wisdom. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these ten qualities should give dependence.” The fifth.

6. Sāmaṇerasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Novice

36. “Katihi [M 3.0314] nu kho, bhante, dhammehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo”ti? “Dasahi kho, upāli, dhammehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo. Katamehi dasahi? Idhupāli, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti…pe… samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu; bahussuto hoti…pe… diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā; pātimokkhaṃ kho panassa vitthārena svāgataṃ hoti suvibhattaṃ suppavattaṃ suvinicchitaṃ suttaso anubyañjanaso; paṭibalo hoti gilānaṃ upaṭṭhātuṃ vā upaṭṭhāpetuṃ vā; paṭibalo hoti anabhiratiṃ vūpakāsetuṃ vā vūpakāsāpetuṃ vā; paṭibalo hoti uppannaṃ kukkuccaṃ dhammato vinodetuṃ; paṭibalo hoti uppannaṃ diṭṭhigataṃ dhammato vivecetuṃ; paṭibalo hoti adhisīle samādapetuṃ; paṭibalo hoti adhicitte [V 3.0061] samādapetuṃ; paṭibalo hoti adhipaññāya samādapetuṃ. Imehi kho, upāli, dasahi dhammehi samannāgatena bhikkhunā sāmaṇero upaṭṭhāpetabbo”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

36. “Venerable sir, with how many qualities should a bhikkhu be endowed to be attended upon by a novice?” “Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with ten qualities may be attended upon by a novice. What ten? Here, Upāli, a bhikkhu is virtuous… he undertakes and trains in the training rules. He is of great learning… well penetrated by view. Furthermore, the Pātimokkha is well-mastered by him in detail, well-analyzed, well-recited, and well-adjudicated, both according to the rules and according to the details. He is capable of attending to a sick person or of having him attended to. He is capable of dispelling discontent or of having it dispelled. He is capable of dispelling arisen remorse in accordance with the Dhamma. He is capable of removing an arisen wrong view in accordance with the Dhamma. He is capable of establishing others in the higher virtue. He is capable of establishing others in the higher mind. He is capable of establishing others in the higher wisdom. Upāli, a bhikkhu endowed with these ten qualities may be attended upon by a novice.” Sixth.

7. Saṅghabhedasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Schism in the Saṅgha

37. “‘Saṅghabhedo saṅghabhedo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, saṅgho bhinno hotī”ti? “Idhupāli, bhikkhū adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpenti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpenti, avinayaṃ vinayoti [P 5.0074] dīpenti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpenti, abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, apaññattaṃ tathāgatena paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti[T 5.0078], paññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti. Te imehi dasahi vatthūhi avakassanti apakassanti āveni āveniṃ (cūḷava. 352) āveṇi, āveṇikaṃ (tattheva adholipi) kammāni karonti āveni pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Ettāvatā kho, upāli, saṅgho bhinno hotī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

37. “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘schism in the Saṅgha, schism in the Saṅgha.’ To what extent, venerable sir, is the Saṅgha in schism?” “Here, Upāli, bhikkhus declare what is not the Dhamma to be the Dhamma, and what is the Dhamma to be not the Dhamma; they declare what is not the discipline to be the discipline, and what is the discipline to be not the discipline; they declare what was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata to have been spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata, and what was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata not to have been spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata; they declare what was not practiced by the Tathāgata to have been practiced by the Tathāgata, and what was practiced by the Tathāgata not to have been practiced by the Tathāgata; they declare what was not laid down by the Tathāgata to have been laid down by the Tathāgata, and what was laid down by the Tathāgata not to have been laid down by the Tathāgata. On the basis of these ten grounds, they draw others away and pull them apart, perform formal acts separately, and recite the Pātimokkha separately. It is to this extent, Upāli, that the Saṅgha is in schism.” Seventh.

8. Saṅghasāmaggīsuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Concord in the Saṅgha

38. cūḷava. 353 “‘Saṅghasāmaggī [M 3.0315] saṅghasāmaggī’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, saṅgho samaggo hotī”ti? “Idhupāli, bhikkhū adhammaṃ adhammoti dīpenti, dhammaṃ dhammoti dīpenti, avinayaṃ avinayoti dīpenti, vinayaṃ vinayoti dīpenti, abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, apaññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, paññattaṃ tathāgatena paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti. Te imehi dasahi vatthūhi na avakassanti na apakassanti na āveni kammāni karonti na āveni pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Ettāvatā kho, upāli, saṅgho samaggo hotī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

38. “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘concord in the Saṅgha, concord in the Saṅgha.’ To what extent, venerable sir, is the Saṅgha in concord?” “Here, Upāli, bhikkhus explain what is not the Dhamma as not the Dhamma, and what is the Dhamma as the Dhamma; they explain what is not the discipline as not the discipline, and what is the discipline as the discipline; they explain what was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as not having been spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata, and what was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as having been spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata; they explain what was not practiced by the Tathāgata as not having been practiced by the Tathāgata, and what was practiced by the Tathāgata as having been practiced by the Tathāgata; they explain what was not laid down by the Tathāgata as not having been laid down by the Tathāgata, and what was laid down by the Tathāgata as having been laid down by the Tathāgata. On the basis of these ten points, they do not draw away and do not pull apart, they do not perform legal acts separately, and they do not recite the Pātimokkha separately. It is to this extent, Upāli, that the Saṅgha is in concord.” Eighth.

9. Paṭhamaānandasuttaṃ

9. The First Discourse to Ānanda

39. Atha [V 3.0062][P 5.0075] kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “‘saṅghabhedo saṅghabhedo’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, saṅgho bhinno hotī”ti[T 5.0079]? “Idhānanda, bhikkhū adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpenti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpenti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpenti…pe… paññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti. Te imehi dasahi vatthūhi avakassanti apakassanti āveni kammāni karonti āveni pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Ettāvatā kho, ānanda, saṅgho bhinno hotī”ti.

39. Then the Venerable Ānanda went to the Blessed One, and after paying homage to him, sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘schism of the Saṅgha, schism of the Saṅgha.’ To what extent, venerable sir, is the Saṅgha divided?” “Here, Ānanda, bhikkhus explain what is not the Dhamma as ‘the Dhamma,’ and the Dhamma as ‘not the Dhamma’; they explain what is not the discipline as ‘the discipline’... and what was laid down by the Tathāgata as ‘not laid down by the Tathāgata.’ On the basis of these ten points, they draw away and pull apart, perform legal acts separately, and recite the Pātimokkha separately. It is to this extent, Ānanda, that the Saṅgha is divided.”

“Samaggaṃ pana, bhante, saṅghaṃ bhinditvā kiṃ so pasavatī”ti? “Kappaṭṭhikaṃ, ānanda, kibbisaṃ pasavatī”ti. “Kiṃ pana, bhante, kappaṭṭhikaṃ kibbisa”nti? “Kappaṃ, ānanda, nirayamhi paccatīti –

“But, venerable sir, what does one generate by splitting a concordant Saṅgha?” “Ānanda, one generates a grievous evil that endures for an aeon.” “But, venerable sir, what is the grievous evil that endures for an aeon?” “Ānanda, one is tormented in hell for an aeon—”

“Āpāyiko [P 5.0076] nerayiko, kappaṭṭho saṅghabhedako;

Vaggarato adhammaṭṭho, yogakkhemā padhaṃsati;

Saṅghaṃ samaggaṃ bhinditvā bhetvāna (sī. syā.), bhitvāna (ka.) cūḷava. 354; itivu. 18; kathāva. 657 kappaṃ nirayamhi paccatī”ti. navamaṃ;

“A maker of schism is bound for the plane of misery, for hell, to remain for an aeon. Delighting in factions, established in what is not the Dhamma, he falls away from security from the yokes. Having split a concordant Saṅgha, he is tormented in hell for an aeon.” Ninth.

10. Dutiyaānandasuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse to Ānanda

40. “‘Saṅghasāmaggī [M 3.0316] saṅghasāmaggī’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, bhante, saṅgho samaggo hotī”ti? “Idhānanda, bhikkhū adhammaṃ adhammoti dīpenti, dhammaṃ dhammoti dīpenti, avinayaṃ avinayoti dīpenti[T 5.0080], vinayaṃ vinayoti dīpenti, abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, apaññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, paññattaṃ tathāgatena paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti. Te imehi dasahi vatthūhi [V 3.0063] na avakassanti na apakassanti na āveni kammāni karonti na āveni pātimokkhaṃ uddisanti. Ettāvatā kho, ānanda, saṅgho samaggo hotī”ti.

40. “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘concord in the Saṅgha, concord in the Saṅgha.’ To what extent, venerable sir, is the Saṅgha in concord?” “Here, Ānanda, bhikkhus explain what is not the Dhamma as not the Dhamma, and the Dhamma as the Dhamma; they explain what is not the discipline as not the discipline, and the discipline as the discipline; they explain what was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as not having been spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata, and what was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as having been spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata; they explain what was not practiced by the Tathāgata as not having been practiced by the Tathāgata, and what was practiced by the Tathāgata as having been practiced by the Tathāgata; they explain what was not laid down by the Tathāgata as not having been laid down by the Tathāgata, and what was laid down by the Tathāgata as having been laid down by the Tathāgata. On the basis of these ten points, they do not draw away and do not pull apart, they do not perform legal acts separately, and they do not recite the Pātimokkha separately. It is to this extent, Ānanda, that the Saṅgha is in concord.”

“Bhinnaṃ pana, bhante, saṅghaṃ samaggaṃ katvā kiṃ so pasavatī”ti? “Brahmaṃ, ānanda, puññaṃ pasavatī”ti. “Kiṃ pana, bhante, brahmaṃ puñña”nti? “Kappaṃ, ānanda, saggamhi modatīti –

“Venerable sir, by making a divided Saṅgha concordant, what does one generate?” “One generates sublime merit, Ānanda.” “But, venerable sir, what is sublime merit?” “For an aeon, Ānanda, one rejoices in heaven—”

“Sukhā [P 5.0077] saṅghassa sāmaggī, samaggānañca anuggaho;

Samaggarato dhammaṭṭho, yogakkhemā na dhaṃsati;

Saṅghaṃ samaggaṃ katvāna, kappaṃ saggamhi modatī”ti. dasamaṃ;

“Happy is the concord of the Saṅgha, and the support for those in concord. Delighting in concord, established in the Dhamma, one does not fall away from security from the yokes. Having made the Saṅgha concordant, one rejoices in heaven for an aeon.” Tenth.

Upālivaggo catuttho.

The Chapter on Upāli—the Fourth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Upāli ṭhapanā ubbāho, upasampadanissayā;

Sāmaṇero ca dve bhedā, ānandehi pare duveti.

Upāli, Suspension, Appointment, Ordination, Dependence, the Novice, and two on Schism; and the other two from Ānanda.

5. Akkosavaggo

5. The Chapter on Reviling

1. Vivādasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Disputes

41. Atha [T 5.0081][V 3.0064] kho āyasmā upāli yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho [M 3.0317] āyasmā upāli bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo, yena saṅghe bhaṇḍanakalahaviggahavivādā uppajjanti, bhikkhū ca na phāsu phāsuṃ (?) viharantī”ti? “Idhupāli, bhikkhū adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpenti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpenti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpenti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpenti, abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, apaññattaṃ tathāgatena paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti [P 5.0078] dīpenti, paññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti. Ayaṃ kho, upāli, hetu ayaṃ paccayo, yena saṅghe bhaṇḍanakalahaviggahavivādā uppajjanti, bhikkhū ca na phāsu viharantī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

41. Then the Venerable Upāli went to the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Upāli said to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, what is the cause and what is the condition whereby quarrels, conflicts, contentions, and disputes arise in the Saṅgha, and the bhikkhus do not dwell at ease?” “Here, Upāli, bhikkhus declare what is not the Dhamma as the Dhamma, and the Dhamma as not the Dhamma; they declare what is not the discipline as the discipline, and the discipline as not the discipline; they declare what was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata, and what was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata; they declare what was not practiced by the Tathāgata as practiced by the Tathāgata, and what was practiced by the Tathāgata as not practiced by the Tathāgata; they declare what was not laid down by the Tathāgata as laid down by the Tathāgata, and what was laid down by the Tathāgata as not laid down by the Tathāgata. This, Upāli, is the cause and this is the condition whereby quarrels, conflicts, contentions, and disputes arise in the Saṅgha, and the bhikkhus do not dwell at ease.” First.

2. Paṭhamavivādamūlasuttaṃ

2. The First Discourse on the Roots of Disputes

42. “Kati nu kho, bhante, vivādamūlānī”ti? “Dasa kho, upāli, vivādamūlāni. Katamāni dasa? Idhupāli, bhikkhū adhammaṃ dhammoti dīpenti, dhammaṃ adhammoti dīpenti, avinayaṃ vinayoti dīpenti, vinayaṃ avinayoti dīpenti, abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatena bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti[T 5.0082], bhāsitaṃ lapitaṃ tathāgatena abhāsitaṃ alapitaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, āciṇṇaṃ tathāgatena anāciṇṇaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, apaññattaṃ tathāgatena paññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti, paññattaṃ tathāgatena apaññattaṃ tathāgatenāti dīpenti. Imāni kho, upāli, dasa vivādamūlānī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

42. “Venerable sir, how many roots of disputes are there?” “Upāli, there are ten roots of disputes. What ten? Here, Upāli, bhikkhus declare what is not the Dhamma as the Dhamma, and the Dhamma as not the Dhamma; they declare what is not the Discipline as the Discipline, and the Discipline as not the Discipline; they declare what was not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata, and what was spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata as not spoken or uttered by the Tathāgata; they declare what was not practiced by the Tathāgata as practiced by the Tathāgata, and what was practiced by the Tathāgata as not practiced by the Tathāgata; they declare what was not laid down by the Tathāgata as laid down by the Tathāgata, and what was laid down by the Tathāgata as not laid down by the Tathāgata. These, Upāli, are the ten roots of disputes.” Second.

3. Dutiyavivādamūlasuttaṃ

3. The Second Discourse on the Roots of Disputes

43. “Kati [V 3.0065] nu kho, bhante, vivādamūlānī”ti? “Dasa kho, upāli, vivādamūlāni. Katamāni dasa? Idhupāli, bhikkhū anāpattiṃ āpattīti dīpenti, āpattiṃ anāpattīti dīpenti, lahukaṃ āpattiṃ garukāpattīti dīpenti[M 3.0318], garukaṃ āpattiṃ lahukāpattīti dīpenti, duṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ aduṭṭhullāpattīti dīpenti, aduṭṭhullaṃ āpattiṃ duṭṭhullāpattīti dīpenti, sāvasesaṃ āpattiṃ anavasesāpattīti dīpenti, anavasesaṃ āpattiṃ sāvasesāpattīti dīpenti[P 5.0079], sappaṭikammaṃ āpattiṃ appaṭikammāpattīti dīpenti, appaṭikammaṃ āpattiṃ sappaṭikammāpattīti dīpenti. Imāni kho, upāli, dasa vivādamūlānī”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

43. “Venerable sir, how many roots of disputes are there?” “Upāli, there are ten roots of disputes. What ten? Here, Upāli, bhikkhus declare a non-offense to be an offense, and an offense to be a non-offense; they declare a minor offense to be a grave offense, and a grave offense to be a minor offense; they declare a gross offense to be a non-gross offense, and a non-gross offense to be a gross offense; they declare an offense with a remainder to be an offense without a remainder, and an offense without a remainder to be an offense with a remainder; they declare a remediable offense to be an irremediable offense, and an irremediable offense to be a remediable offense. These, Upāli, are the ten roots of disputes.” Third.

4. Kusinārasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse at Kusinārā

44. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kusinārāyaṃ viharati baliharaṇe vanasaṇḍe. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

44. On one occasion, the Blessed One was dwelling in Kusinārā, in the Baliharaṇa forest grove. There, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

cūḷava. 399; pari. 436 “Codakena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ paccavekkhitvā pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā paro codetabbo. Katame pañca dhammā ajjhattaṃ [T 5.0083] paccavekkhitabbā? Codakena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘parisuddhakāyasamācāro nu khomhi, parisuddhenamhi kāyasamācārena samannāgato acchiddena appaṭimaṃsena. Saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti? No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu parisuddhakāyasamācāro hoti parisuddhena kāyasamācārena samannāgato acchiddena appaṭimaṃsena, tassa bhavanti vattāro – ‘iṅgha tāva āyasmā kāyikaṃ sikkhassū’ti, itissa bhavanti vattāro.

“Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who wishes to reprove another should, having reviewed five qualities in himself and having established five qualities in himself, then reprove the other. What are the five qualities to be reviewed in himself? Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who wishes to reprove another should review thus: ‘Am I of pure bodily conduct? Am I endowed with pure bodily conduct that is unbroken and irreproachable? Does this quality exist in me, or does it not?’ If, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not of pure bodily conduct, not endowed with pure bodily conduct that is unbroken and irreproachable, there will be those who say to him: ‘Come, venerable sir, first train in bodily conduct.’ Thus, there will be those who speak to him.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, codakena bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘parisuddhavacīsamācāro nu khomhi, parisuddhenamhi vacīsamācārena samannāgato acchiddena appaṭimaṃsena. Saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti? No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu [V 3.0066] parisuddhavacīsamācāro hoti parisuddhena vacīsamācārena samannāgato acchiddena appaṭimaṃsena, tassa bhavanti vattāro – ‘iṅgha tāva āyasmā vācasikaṃ sikkhassū’ti, itissa bhavanti vattāro.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who wishes to reprove another should review thus: ‘Am I of pure verbal conduct? Am I endowed with pure verbal conduct that is unbroken and irreproachable? Does this quality exist in me, or does it not?’ If, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not of pure verbal conduct, not endowed with pure verbal conduct that is unbroken and irreproachable, there will be those who say to him: ‘Come, venerable sir, first train in verbal conduct.’ Thus, there will be those who speak to him.

“Puna [P 5.0080] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, codakena bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘mettaṃ nu kho me cittaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ sabrahmacārīsu anāghātaṃ. Saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti? No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno [M 3.0319] mettaṃ cittaṃ paccupaṭṭhitaṃ hoti sabrahmacārīsu anāghātaṃ, tassa bhavanti vattāro – ‘iṅgha tāva āyasmā sabrahmacārīsu mettaṃ cittaṃ upaṭṭhāpehī’ti, itissa bhavanti vattāro.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who wishes to reprove another should review thus: ‘Is my mind, free from animosity, established with loving-kindness towards my companions in the holy life? Does this quality exist in me, or does it not?’ If, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu’s mind, free from animosity, is not established with loving-kindness towards his companions in the holy life, there will be those who say to him: ‘Come, venerable sir, first establish a mind of loving-kindness towards your companions in the holy life.’ Thus, there will be those who speak to him.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, codakena bhikkhunā [T 5.0084] paraṃ codetukāmena evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘bahussuto nu khomhi sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpā me dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā. Saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti? No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā, tassa bhavanti vattāro – ‘iṅgha tāva āyasmā āgamaṃ pariyāpuṇassū’ti, itissa bhavanti vattāro.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who wishes to reprove another should review thus: ‘Am I learned, a bearer of the teachings, an accumulator of the teachings? Those teachings that are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with right meaning and phrasing, which proclaim the holy life that is utterly complete and pure—have such teachings been learned by me, retained, recited, mentally investigated, and well penetrated by wisdom? Does this quality exist in me, or does it not?’ If, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not learned, a bearer of the teachings, an accumulator of the teachings; and if such teachings that are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with right meaning and phrasing, which proclaim the holy life that is utterly complete and pure, have not been learned by him, retained, recited, mentally investigated, and well penetrated by wisdom, there will be those who say to him: ‘Come, venerable sir, first learn the scriptural tradition.’ Thus, there will be those who speak to him.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, codakena bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena evaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ – ‘ubhayāni kho pana me pātimokkhāni vitthārena svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso. Saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti? No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno ubhayāni pātimokkhāni vitthārena [P 5.0081] svāgatāni honti suvibhattāni suppavattīni suvinicchitāni suttaso anubyañjanaso, ‘idaṃ panāyasmā, kattha vuttaṃ bhagavatā’ti, iti puṭṭho na sampāyissati. Tassa bhavanti vattāro – ‘iṅgha tāva āyasmā [V 3.0067] vinayaṃ sikkhassū’ti, itissa bhavanti vattāro. Ime pañca dhammā ajjhattaṃ paccavekkhitabbā.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who wishes to reprove another should review thus: ‘Have both Pātimokkhas been well learned by me in detail, well distinguished, well established, and well determined, rule by rule and phrase by phrase? Does this quality exist in me, or does it not?’ If, bhikkhus, both Pātimokkhas have not been well learned by the bhikkhu in detail, well distinguished, well established, and well determined, rule by rule and phrase by phrase, then when asked, ‘Venerable sir, where was this spoken by the Blessed One?’ he will be unable to answer satisfactorily. There will be those who say to him: ‘Come, venerable sir, first train in the Vinaya.’ Thus, there will be those who speak to him. These five qualities are to be reviewed in oneself.

“Katame pañca [T 5.0085] dhammā ajjhattaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbā? ‘Kālena vakkhāmi, no akālena; bhūtena vakkhāmi, no abhūtena; saṇhena vakkhāmi, no pharusena; atthasaṃhitena vakkhāmi, no anatthasaṃhitena; mettacitto vakkhāmi, no dosantaro’ti – ime pañca dhammā ajjhattaṃ upaṭṭhāpetabbā. Codakena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā paraṃ codetukāmena ime pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ paccavekkhitvā ime pañca dhamme ajjhattaṃ upaṭṭhāpetvā paro codetabbo”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“What five qualities should be established in oneself? ‘I will speak at the right time, not at the wrong time; I will speak truthfully, not falsely; I will speak gently, not harshly; I will speak what is beneficial, not what is unbeneficial; I will speak with a mind of loving-kindness, not with inner hate.’ These are the five qualities to be established in oneself. Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu who wishes to reprove another should reprove the other only after having reviewed these five qualities in himself and established these five qualities in himself.” Fourth.

5. Rājantepurappavesanasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Entering the Royal Inner Palace

45. pāci. 497 “Dasayime[M 3.0320], bhikkhave, ādīnavā rājantepurappavesane. Katame dasa? Idha, bhikkhave, rājā mahesiyā saddhiṃ nisinno hoti. Tatra bhikkhu pavisati. Mahesī vā bhikkhuṃ disvā sitaṃ pātukaroti, bhikkhu vā mahesiṃ disvā sitaṃ pātukaroti. Tattha rañño evaṃ hoti – ‘addhā imesaṃ kataṃ vā karissanti vā’ti! Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, paṭhamo ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

45. “Bhikkhus, there are these ten drawbacks in entering the royal inner palace. What ten? Here, bhikkhus, a king is seated together with his chief queen. A bhikkhu enters. The chief queen, seeing the bhikkhu, smiles, or the bhikkhu, seeing the chief queen, smiles. Then the king thinks: ‘Surely, these two have either done something or will do something!’ This, bhikkhus, is the first drawback in entering the royal inner palace.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rājā bahukicco bahukaraṇīyo aññataraṃ itthiṃ gantvā na sarati – ‘sā tena gabbhaṃ gaṇhāti’. Tattha rañño evaṃ hoti – ‘na kho idha añño [P 5.0082] koci pavisati, aññatra pabbajitena. Siyā nu kho pabbajitassa kamma’nti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, dutiyo ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a king is busy with many duties and affairs. He has relations with a certain woman but does not remember it, and she becomes pregnant by him. Then the king thinks: ‘No one else enters here except a renunciate. Could this be the renunciate’s doing?’ This, bhikkhus, is the second drawback in entering the royal inner palace.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rañño antepure aññataraṃ ratanaṃ nassati. Tattha rañño evaṃ hoti – ‘na kho idha añño koci pavisati, aññatra pabbajitena. Siyā nu kho pabbajitassa kamma’nti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, tatiyo ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a certain jewel is lost in the king’s inner palace. Then the king thinks: ‘No one else enters here except a renunciate. Could this be the renunciate’s doing?’ This, bhikkhus, is the third drawback in entering the royal inner palace.

“Puna [T 5.0086] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rañño antepure abbhantarā guyhamantā bahiddhā sambhedaṃ gacchanti. Tattha rañño evaṃ hoti – ‘na kho idha añño koci pavisati, aññatra pabbajitena[V 3.0068]. Siyā nu kho pabbajitassa kamma’nti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, catuttho ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, secret internal counsels in the king’s inner palace are leaked outside. Then the king thinks: ‘No one else enters here except a renunciate. Could this be the renunciate’s doing?’ This, bhikkhus, is the fourth drawback in entering the royal inner palace.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rañño antepure pitā vā puttaṃ pattheti putto vā pitaraṃ pattheti. Tesaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘na kho idha añño koci pavisati, aññatra pabbajitena. Siyā nu kho pabbajitassa kamma’nti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, pañcamo ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, in the king’s inner palace, a father plots against his son, or a son plots against his father. They think: ‘No one else enters here except a renunciate. Could this be the renunciate’s doing?’ This, bhikkhus, is the fifth drawback in entering the royal inner palace.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rājā nīcaṭṭhāniyaṃ ucce ṭhāne ṭhapeti. Yesaṃ taṃ amanāpaṃ tesaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘rājā kho pabbajitena saṃsaṭṭho. Siyā nu kho pabbajitassa kamma’nti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, chaṭṭho ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a king places a person of low station in a high position. Those to whom this is displeasing think: ‘The king associates with the renunciate. Could this be the renunciate’s doing?’ This, bhikkhus, is the sixth drawback in entering the royal inner palace.

“Puna [M 3.0321] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rājā uccaṭṭhāniyaṃ nīce ṭhāne ṭhapeti. Yesaṃ taṃ amanāpaṃ tesaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘rājā kho pabbajitena saṃsaṭṭho. Siyā nu kho pabbajitassa kamma’nti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, sattamo ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a king places a person of high station in a low position. Those to whom this is displeasing think: ‘The king associates with the renunciate. Could this be the renunciate’s doing?’ This, bhikkhus, is the seventh drawback in entering the royal inner palace.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rājā akāle senaṃ uyyojeti. Yesaṃ taṃ amanāpaṃ tesaṃ evaṃ hoti – ‘rājā kho pabbajitena saṃsaṭṭho. Siyā nu kho pabbajitassa kamma’nti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, aṭṭhamo ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a king sends out the army at an inopportune time. Those to whom this is displeasing think: ‘The king associates with the renunciate. Could this be the renunciate’s doing?’ This, bhikkhus, is the eighth drawback in entering the royal inner palace.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rājā kāle senaṃ uyyojetvā antarāmaggato nivattāpeti. Yesaṃ taṃ amanāpaṃ tesaṃ evaṃ [P 5.0083] hoti – ‘rājā kho pabbajitena saṃsaṭṭho. Siyā nu [T 5.0087] kho pabbajitassa kamma’nti. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, navamo ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a king sends out the army at an opportune time but has it turn back midway. Those to whom this is displeasing think: ‘The king associates with the renunciate. Could this be the renunciate’s doing?’ This, bhikkhus, is the ninth drawback in entering the royal inner palace.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, rañño antepuraṃ hatthisammaddaṃ assasammaddaṃ rathasammaddaṃ rajanīyāni rūpasaddagandharasaphoṭṭhabbāni, yāni na pabbajitassa sāruppāni. Ayaṃ, bhikkhave, dasamo ādīnavo rājantepurappavesane. Ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa ādīnavā rājantepurappavesane”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, the king’s inner palace is full of the commotion of elephants, horses, and chariots, and with alluring sights, sounds, odors, tastes, and tactile objects that are unsuitable for a renunciate. This, bhikkhus, is the tenth drawback in entering the royal inner palace. These, bhikkhus, are the ten drawbacks in entering the royal inner palace.” Fifth.

6. Sakkasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse to Sakka

46. Ekaṃ [V 3.0069] samayaṃ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṃ nigrodhārāme. Atha kho sambahulā sakkā upāsakā tadahuposathe yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinne kho sakke upāsake bhagavā etadavoca – “api nu tumhe, sakkā, aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṃ uposathaṃ upavasathā”ti? “Appekadā mayaṃ, bhante, aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṃ uposathaṃ upavasāma, appekadā na upavasāmā”ti. “Tesaṃ vo, sakkā, alābhā tesaṃ dulladdhaṃ, ye tumhe evaṃ sokasabhaye jīvite maraṇasabhaye jīvite appekadā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṃ uposathaṃ upavasatha, appekadā na upavasatha.

46. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Park. Then, on that Uposatha day, many Sakyan lay followers approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. The Blessed One then said to them: “Sakyans, do you observe the Uposatha endowed with eight factors?” “Sometimes we do, venerable sir, and sometimes we do not.” “It is a loss for you, Sakyans, it is a misfortune for you that in this life fraught with sorrow and fear, fraught with death and fear, you sometimes observe the Uposatha endowed with eight factors and sometimes do not.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, sakkā, idha puriso yena kenaci kammaṭṭhānena anāpajja akusalaṃ divasaṃ aḍḍhakahāpaṇaṃ nibbiseyya. Dakkho [P 5.0084] puriso uṭṭhānasampannoti alaṃ vacanāyā”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, Sakyans? Suppose a man here, by whatever means of livelihood, without resorting to the unwholesome, might earn half a kahāpaṇa a day. Would it be right to call him a skillful man, endowed with energy?” “So it is, venerable sir.”

“Taṃ [M 3.0322] kiṃ maññatha, sakkā, idha puriso yena kenaci kammaṭṭhānena anāpajja akusalaṃ divasaṃ kahāpaṇaṃ nibbiseyya. Dakkho puriso uṭṭhānasampannoti alaṃ vacanāyā”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, Sakyans? Suppose a man here, by whatever means of livelihood, without resorting to the unwholesome, might earn a kahāpaṇa a day. Would it be right to call him a skillful man, endowed with energy?” “So it is, venerable sir.”

“Taṃ kiṃ, maññatha, sakkā, idha puriso yena kenaci kammaṭṭhānena anāpajja akusalaṃ divasaṃ dve kahāpaṇe nibbiseyya [T 5.0088]… tayo kahāpaṇe nibbiseyya… cattāro kahāpaṇe nibbiseyya… pañca kahāpaṇe nibbiseyya… cha kahāpaṇe nibbiseyya… satta kahāpaṇe nibbiseyya… aṭṭha kahāpaṇe nibbiseyya… nava kahāpaṇe nibbiseyya… dasa kahāpaṇe nibbiseyya… vīsa kahāpaṇe nibbiseyya… tiṃsa kahāpaṇe nibbiseyya… cattārīsaṃ kahāpaṇe nibbiseyya… paññāsaṃ kahāpaṇe nibbiseyya… kahāpaṇasataṃ nibbiseyya. Dakkho puriso uṭṭhānasampannoti alaṃ vacanāyā”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, Sakyans? Suppose a man here, by whatever means of livelihood, without resorting to the unwholesome, might earn two kahāpaṇas a day… three kahāpaṇas… four kahāpaṇas… five kahāpaṇas… six kahāpaṇas… seven kahāpaṇas… eight kahāpaṇas… nine kahāpaṇas… ten kahāpaṇas… twenty kahāpaṇas… thirty kahāpaṇas… forty kahāpaṇas… fifty kahāpaṇas… a hundred kahāpaṇas a day. Would it be right to call him a skillful man, endowed with energy?” “So it is, venerable sir.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, sakkā, api nu so puriso divase divase kahāpaṇasataṃ kahāpaṇasahassaṃ [V 3.0070] nibbisamāno laddhaṃ laddhaṃ nikkhipanto vassasatāyuko vassasatajīvī mahantaṃ bhogakkhandhaṃ adhigaccheyyā”ti? “Evaṃ, bhante”.

“What do you think, Sakyans? If that man, earning a hundred kahāpaṇas, a thousand kahāpaṇas day by day, were to set aside whatever he got, and if he had a lifespan of a hundred years, living for a hundred years, would he acquire a great mass of wealth?” “So it is, venerable sir.”

“Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, sakkā, api nu so puriso bhogahetu bhoganidānaṃ bhogādhikaraṇaṃ ekaṃ vā rattiṃ ekaṃ vā divasaṃ upaḍḍhaṃ vā rattiṃ upaḍḍhaṃ vā divasaṃ ekantasukhappaṭisaṃvedī vihareyyā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”. “Taṃ kissa hetu”? “Kāmā hi, bhante, aniccā tucchā musā mosadhammā”ti.

“What do you think, Sakyans? For the sake of that wealth, because of that wealth, on account of that wealth, could that man dwell experiencing exclusive happiness even for a single night or a single day, or for half a night or half a day?” “Certainly not, venerable sir.” “For what reason?” “Because, venerable sir, sensual pleasures are impermanent, empty, false, and of a deceptive nature.”

“Idha pana vo, sakkā, mama sāvako dasa vassāni appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto yathā mayānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno satampi vassāni satampi vassasatāni satampi [P 5.0085] vassasahassāni ekantasukhappaṭisaṃvedī vihareyya. So ca khvassa sakadāgāmī vā anāgāmī vā apaṇṇakaṃ vā sotāpanno. Tiṭṭhantu, sakkā, dasa vassāni.

“But here, Sakyans, a disciple of mine, dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute for ten years, practicing in accordance with my instructions, could dwell experiencing exclusive happiness for a hundred years, for ten thousand years, for a hundred thousand years. And he would be a once-returner, or a non-returner, or unfailingly a stream-enterer. Let the ten years stand, Sakyans.”

Idha mama sāvako nava vassāni… aṭṭha vassāni… satta vassāni… cha vassāni… pañca vassāni cattāri vassāni… tīṇi vassāni… dve vassāni… ekaṃ vassaṃ appamatto ātāpī [T 5.0089] pahitatto viharanto yathā mayānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno satampi vassāni satampi vassasatāni satampi vassasahassāni ekantasukhappaṭisaṃvedī vihareyya, so ca khvassa sakadāgāmī [M 3.0323] vā anāgāmī vā apaṇṇakaṃ vā sotāpanno. Tiṭṭhatu, sakkā, ekaṃ vassaṃ.

“Here, a disciple of mine, dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute for nine years… eight years… seven years… six years… five years… four years… three years… two years… one year, practicing in accordance with my instructions, could dwell experiencing exclusive happiness for a hundred years, for ten thousand years, for a hundred thousand years. And he would be a once-returner, or a non-returner, or unfailingly a stream-enterer. Let the one year stand, Sakyans.”

Idha mama sāvako dasa māse appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto yathā mayānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno satampi vassāni satampi vassasatāni satampi vassasahassāni ekantasukhappaṭisaṃvedī vihareyya, so ca khvassa sakadāgāmī vā anāgāmī vā apaṇṇakaṃ vā sotāpanno. Tiṭṭhantu, sakkā, dasa māsā.

“Here, a disciple of mine, dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute for ten months, practicing in accordance with my instructions, could dwell experiencing exclusive happiness for a hundred years, for ten thousand years, for a hundred thousand years. And he would be a once-returner, or a non-returner, or unfailingly a stream-enterer. Let the ten months stand, Sakyans.”

Idha mama sāvako nava māse… aṭṭha māse… satta māse… cha māse… pañca māse… cattāro māse… tayo māse… dve māse… ekaṃ māsaṃ… aḍḍhamāsaṃ appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto yathā mayānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno satampi vassāni satampi vassasatāni [V 3.0071] satampi vassasahassāni ekantasukhappaṭisaṃvedī vihareyya, so ca khvassa sakadāgāmī vā anāgāmī vā apaṇṇakaṃ vā sotāpanno. Tiṭṭhatu, sakkā, aḍḍhamāso.

“Here, a disciple of mine, dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute for nine months… eight months… seven months… six months… five months… four months… three months… two months… one month… for half a month, practicing in accordance with my instructions, could dwell experiencing exclusive happiness for a hundred years, for ten thousand years, for a hundred thousand years. And he would be a once-returner, or a non-returner, or unfailingly a stream-enterer. Let the half a month stand, Sakyans.”

Idha mama sāvako dasa rattindive rattidive (ka.) appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto yathā mayānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno satampi vassāni satampi vassasatāni satampi vassasahassāni ekantasukhappaṭisaṃvedī vihareyya, so ca khvassa sakadāgāmī vā anāgāmī vā apaṇṇakaṃ vā sotāpanno. Tiṭṭhantu, sakkā, dasa rattindivā.

“Here, a disciple of mine, dwelling diligent, ardent, and resolute for ten days and nights, practicing in accordance with my instructions, could dwell experiencing exclusive happiness for a hundred years, for ten thousand years, for a hundred thousand years. And he would be a once-returner, or a non-returner, or unfailingly a stream-enterer. Let the ten days and nights stand, Sakyans.”

Idha mama sāvako nava rattindive… aṭṭha rattindive… satta rattindive… cha [P 5.0086] rattindive… pañca rattindive… cattāro [T 5.0090] rattindive… tayo rattindive… dve rattindive… ekaṃ rattindivaṃ appamatto ātāpī pahitatto viharanto yathā mayānusiṭṭhaṃ tathā paṭipajjamāno satampi vassāni satampi vassasatāni satampi vassasahassāni ekantasukhappaṭisaṃvedī vihareyya, so ca khvassa sakadāgāmī vā anāgāmī vā apaṇṇakaṃ vā sotāpanno. Tesaṃ vo, sakkā, alābhā tesaṃ dulladdhaṃ, ye tumhe evaṃ sokasabhaye jīvite maraṇasabhaye jīvite appekadā aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṃ uposathaṃ upavasatha, appekadā na upavasathā”ti. “Ete mayaṃ, bhante, ajjatagge aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṃ uposathaṃ upavasissāmā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

Herein, a disciple of mine, dwelling heedful, ardent, and with a resolute mind for nine nights and days... for eight nights and days... for seven nights and days... for six nights and days... for five nights and days... for four nights and days... for three nights and days... for two nights and days... or for one night and day, practicing in accordance with what was instructed by me, might dwell experiencing exclusive happiness for a hundred years, for ten thousand years, or for one hundred thousand years. And that disciple of mine would be a once-returner, or a non-returner, or, for certain, a stream-enterer. It is your loss, O Sakyans, it is your misfortune, that in this life which has fear through sorrow, in this life which has fear through death, you sometimes observe the Uposatha endowed with the eight factors, and sometimes you do not observe it.” “Venerable Sir, from this day forward, we will observe the Uposatha endowed with the eight factors.” The Sixth.

7. Mahālisuttaṃ

7. The Discourse to Mahāli

47. Ekaṃ [M 3.0324] samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ. Atha kho mahāli licchavi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho mahāli licchavi bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante hetu, ko paccayo pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyā”ti? “Lobho kho, mahāli, hetu, lobho paccayo pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyā. Doso kho, mahāli, hetu, doso paccayo pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyā. Moho kho, mahāli, hetu, moho paccayo pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyā. Ayoniso manasikāro kho, mahāli, hetu, ayoniso manasikāro paccayo [P 5.0087] pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa [T 5.0091] pavattiyā. Micchāpaṇihitaṃ [V 3.0072] kho, mahāli, cittaṃ hetu, micchāpaṇihitaṃ cittaṃ paccayo pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyāti. Ayaṃ kho, mahāli, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo pāpassa kammassa kiriyāya pāpassa kammassa pavattiyā”ti.

47. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Wood, in the Hall with the Gabled Roof. Then the Licchavi Mahāli approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Licchavi Mahāli said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, what is the cause and what is the condition for the doing of evil action, for the occurrence of evil action?” “Greed, Mahāli, is a cause, and greed is a condition for the doing of evil action, for the occurrence of evil action. Hatred, Mahāli, is a cause, and hatred is a condition for the doing of evil action, for the occurrence of evil action. Delusion, Mahāli, is a cause, and delusion is a condition for the doing of evil action, for the occurrence of evil action. Unwise attention, Mahāli, is a cause, and unwise attention is a condition for the doing of evil action, for the occurrence of evil action. A wrongly directed mind, Mahāli, is a cause, and a wrongly directed mind is a condition for the doing of evil action, for the occurrence of evil action. This, Mahāli, is the cause and this is the condition for the doing of evil action, for the occurrence of evil action.”

“Ko pana, bhante, hetu ko paccayo kalyāṇassa kammassa kiriyāya kalyāṇassa kammassa pavattiyā”ti? “Alobho kho, mahāli, hetu, alobho paccayo kalyāṇassa kammassa kiriyāya kalyāṇassa kammassa pavattiyā. Adoso kho, mahāli, hetu, adoso paccayo kalyāṇassa kammassa kiriyāya kalyāṇassa kammassa pavattiyā. Amoho kho, mahāli, hetu, amoho paccayo kalyāṇassa kammassa kiriyāya kalyāṇassa kammassa pavattiyā. Yoniso manasikāro kho, mahāli, hetu, yoniso manasikāro paccayo kalyāṇassa kammassa kiriyāya kalyāṇassa kammassa pavattiyā. Sammāpaṇihitaṃ kho, mahāli, cittaṃ hetu, sammāpaṇihitaṃ cittaṃ paccayo kalyāṇassa kammassa kiriyāya kalyāṇassa kammassa pavattiyā. Ayaṃ kho, mahāli, hetu, ayaṃ paccayo kalyāṇassa kammassa kiriyāya kalyāṇassa kammassa pavattiyā. Ime ca, mahāli, dasa dhammā loke na saṃvijjeyyuṃ, nayidha paññāyetha adhammacariyāvisamacariyāti vā dhammacariyāsamacariyāti vā. Yasmā ca kho, mahāli, ime dasa dhammā loke [M 3.0325] saṃvijjanti, tasmā paññāyati adhammacariyāvisamacariyāti vā dhammacariyāsamacariyāti vā”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“And what, Venerable Sir, is the cause and what is the condition for the doing of wholesome action, for the occurrence of wholesome action?” “Non-greed, Mahāli, is a cause, and non-greed is a condition for the doing of wholesome action, for the occurrence of wholesome action. Non-hatred, Mahāli, is a cause, and non-hatred is a condition for the doing of wholesome action, for the occurrence of wholesome action. Non-delusion, Mahāli, is a cause, and non-delusion is a condition for the doing of wholesome action, for the occurrence of wholesome action. Wise attention, Mahāli, is a cause, and wise attention is a condition for the doing of wholesome action, for the occurrence of wholesome action. A rightly directed mind, Mahāli, is a cause, and a rightly directed mind is a condition for the doing of wholesome action, for the occurrence of wholesome action. This, Mahāli, is the cause and this is the condition for the doing of wholesome action, for the occurrence of wholesome action. And if, Mahāli, these ten things did not exist in the world, then unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct, or righteous conduct and even conduct, would not be discerned herein. But because, Mahāli, these ten things do exist in the world, therefore unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct, or righteous conduct and even conduct, are discerned.” The Seventh.

8. Pabbajitaabhiṇhasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on Frequent Reflection for One Gone Forth

48. “Dasayime, bhikkhave, dhammā pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbā[T 5.0092]. Katame dasa? ‘Vevaṇṇiyamhi ajjhupagato’ti pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ; ‘parapaṭibaddhā me jīvikā’ti pabbajitena [P 5.0088] abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ; ‘añño me ākappo karaṇīyo’ti pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ; ‘kacci nu kho me attā sīlato na upavadatī’ti pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ; ‘kacci nu kho maṃ anuvicca viññū sabrahmacārī sīlato na upavadantī’ti pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ; ‘sabbehi me piyehi manāpehi nānābhāvo vinābhāvo’ti pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ; ‘kammassakomhi kammadāyādo kammayoni kammabandhu kammapaṭisaraṇo, yaṃ kammaṃ karissāmi kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakaṃ vā [V 3.0073] tassa dāyādo bhavissāmī’ti pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ; ‘kathaṃbhūtassa me rattindivā vītivattantī’ti pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ; ‘kacci nu kho ahaṃ suññāgāre abhiramāmī’ti pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ; ‘atthi nu kho me uttari manussadhammo alamariyañāṇadassanaviseso adhigato, yenāhaṃ yohaṃ (sī. pī. ka.), sohaṃ (syā.) pacchime kāle sabrahmacārīhi puṭṭho na maṅku bhavissāmī’ti pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbaṃ. Ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa dhammā pabbajitena abhiṇhaṃ paccavekkhitabbā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

48. “Bhikkhus, these ten things should be frequently reflected upon by one who has gone forth. What ten? ‘I have attained a state of altered appearance’—this should be frequently reflected upon by one who has gone forth. ‘My livelihood is dependent on others’—this should be frequently reflected upon by one who has gone forth. ‘My conduct must be different’—this should be frequently reflected upon by one who has gone forth. ‘Does my own self not reproach me in regard to virtue?’—this should be frequently reflected upon by one who has gone forth. ‘After investigation, do wise spiritual companions not reproach me in regard to virtue?’—this should be frequently reflected upon by one who has gone forth. ‘There is otherness and separation from all that is dear and pleasing to me’—this should be frequently reflected upon by one who has gone forth. ‘I am the owner of my kamma, heir to my kamma, kamma is my origin, kamma is my kinsman, kamma is my refuge. Whatever kamma I shall do, for good or for ill, I will be its heir’—this should be frequently reflected upon by one who has gone forth. ‘In what state are my days and nights passing?’—this should be frequently reflected upon by one who has gone forth. ‘Do I delight in secluded dwellings?’—this should be frequently reflected upon by one who has gone forth. ‘Have I attained any superhuman state, a distinction in knowledge and vision worthy of the noble ones, so that when questioned by my spiritual companions in my last days, I will not be disconcerted?’—this should be frequently reflected upon by one who has gone forth. These, bhikkhus, are the ten things that should be frequently reflected upon by one who has gone forth.” The Eighth.

9. Sarīraṭṭhadhammasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Things Existing in the Body

49. “Dasayime, bhikkhave, dhammā sarīraṭṭhā. Katame dasa? Sītaṃ, uṇhaṃ, jighacchā, pipāsā, uccāro, passāvo, kāyasaṃvaro, vacīsaṃvaro, ājīvasaṃvaro, ponobhaviko ponobbhaviko (ka.) bhavasaṅkhāro – ime [T 5.0093] kho, bhikkhave, dasa dhammā sarīraṭṭhā”ti. Navamaṃ.

49. “Bhikkhus, these ten things are based in the body. What ten? Cold, heat, hunger, thirst, defecation, urination, bodily restraint, verbal restraint, restraint of livelihood, and the kamma-formation that leads to renewed existence. These, bhikkhus, are the ten things based in the body.” The ninth.

10. Bhaṇḍanasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Quarrels

50. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā [P 5.0089] bhikkhū pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā [M 3.0326] upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannisinnā sannipatitā bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharanti.

50. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, a number of bhikkhus, after their meal, on returning from their alms round, had gathered and were sitting together in the meeting hall, where they had become quarrelsome, had become contentious, and had fallen into dispute, piercing each other with verbal spears.

Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena upaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “kāya nuttha, bhikkhave, etarahi kathāya sannisinnā sannipatitā, kā ca pana vo antarākathā vippakatā”ti?

Then, in the evening, the Blessed One rose from seclusion and went to the meeting hall. Having arrived, he sat down on the prepared seat. Having sat down, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “For what discussion are you gathered and assembled here now, bhikkhus? And what was the unfinished conversation among you?”

“Idha mayaṃ, bhante, pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannisinnā sannipatitā bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā viharāmā”ti. “Na kho panetaṃ, bhikkhave, tumhākaṃ patirūpaṃ kulaputtānaṃ saddhāya agārasmā anagāriyaṃ [V 3.0074] pabbajitānaṃ, yaṃ tumhe bhaṇḍanajātā kalahajātā vivādāpannā aññamaññaṃ mukhasattīhi vitudantā vihareyyātha.

“Venerable sir, here we are, after the meal, having returned from the alms round, sitting together in the meeting hall, gathered together, having become quarrelsome, having become contentious, and having fallen into dispute, piercing each other with verbal spears.” “Bhikkhus, it is not fitting for you, clansmen who have gone forth from the household life into homelessness out of faith, that you should dwell having become quarrelsome, having become contentious, and having fallen into dispute, piercing each other with verbal spears.”

“Dasayime, bhikkhave, dhammā sāraṇīyā piyakaraṇā garukaraṇā piyakarāṇā garukarāṇā (?) saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattanti. Katame dasa? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti, pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvuto viharati ācāragocarasampanno aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvī, samādāya sikkhati sikkhāpadesu. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sīlavā hoti…pe… samādāya sikkhati [T 5.0094] sikkhāpadesu, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

“Bhikkhus, these ten things are to be remembered; they create affection and respect, and lead to cohesion, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity. What ten? Here, a bhikkhu is virtuous; he dwells restrained by the Pātimokkha, possessed of good conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults. He undertakes and trains in the training rules. That a bhikkhu is virtuous… undertakes and trains in the training rules, this too is a thing to be remembered, that creates affection and respect, and leads to cohesion, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity.”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā [P 5.0090] manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu bahussuto hoti…pe… diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is learned, a preserver of what he has learned, a treasurer of what he has learned. He has learned much about those teachings that are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, which proclaim the perfectly complete and pure spiritual life; he has retained them, recited them, mentally examined them, and penetrated them well with wisdom. That a bhikkhu is learned… and penetrated them well with wisdom, this too is a thing to be remembered, that creates affection and respect, and leads to cohesion, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity.”

“Puna [M 3.0327] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kalyāṇamitto hoti kalyāṇasahāyo kalyāṇasampavaṅko, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has good friends, good companions, and is inclined to good friends. That a bhikkhu has good friends, good companions, and is inclined to good friends, this too is a thing to be remembered, that creates affection and respect, and leads to cohesion, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity.”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu suvaco hoti sovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgato khamo padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaniṃ. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu suvaco hoti sovacassakaraṇehi dhammehi samannāgato khamo padakkhiṇaggāhī anusāsaniṃ, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is easy to admonish, possessing qualities that make him so; he is patient and respectfully receptive to instruction. That a bhikkhu is easy to admonish… and respectfully receptive to instruction, this too is a thing to be remembered, that creates affection and respect, and leads to cohesion, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity.”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāni tāni sabrahmacārīnaṃ uccāvacāni kiṃkaraṇīyāni [V 3.0075] – tattha dakkho hoti analaso, tatrūpāyāya vīmaṃsāya samannāgato alaṃ kātuṃ alaṃ saṃvidhātuṃ. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yāni tāni [T 5.0095] sabrahmacārīnaṃ uccāvacāni kiṃkaraṇīyāni – tattha dakkho hoti analaso tatrūpāyāya vīmaṃsāya samannāgato alaṃ kātuṃ alaṃ saṃvidhātuṃ, ayampi dhammo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is skilled and diligent in the various duties for his companions in the holy life; he is endowed with investigative wisdom into the means for accomplishing them, and is able to do them and to arrange for them to be done. That a bhikkhu is skilled and diligent in the various duties for his companions in the holy life, is endowed with investigative wisdom into the means for accomplishing them, and is able to do them and to arrange for them to be done—this too is a thing to be remembered, that creates affection and respect, and leads to cohesion, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity.”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammakāmo hoti piyasamudāhāro, abhidhamme abhivinaye uḷārapāmojjo. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammakāmo hoti piyasamudāhāro, abhidhamme abhivinaye uḷārapāmojjo, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is a lover of the Dhamma, has agreeable conversation, and has great joy in the higher Dhamma and the higher discipline. That a bhikkhu is a lover of the Dhamma, has agreeable conversation, and has great joy in the higher Dhamma and the higher discipline, this too is a thing to be remembered, that creates affection and respect, and leads to cohesion, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity.”

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu āraddhavīriyo viharati akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya [P 5.0091] kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ upasampadāya, thāmavā daḷhaparakkamo anikkhittadhuro kusalesu dhammesu, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo piyakaraṇo garukaraṇo saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells with energy aroused for the abandoning of unwholesome states and for the attainment of wholesome states; he is strong, resolute in endeavor, and does not cast off the burden in regard to wholesome states. That a bhikkhu dwells with energy aroused for the abandoning of unwholesome states and for the attainment of wholesome states; is strong, resolute in endeavor, and does not cast off the burden in regard to wholesome states, this too is a thing to be remembered, that creates affection and respect, and leads to cohesion, to non-dispute, to concord, and to unity.”

“Puna [M 3.0328] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu santuṭṭho hoti itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārena, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo…pe… saṃvattati.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is content with whatever kind of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick. That a bhikkhu is content with whatever kind of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick—this quality, too, is worthy of being remembered, creates affection and respect, and leads to cohesion, non-dispute, concord, and unity.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu satimā hoti, paramena satinepakkena samannāgato, cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā. Yampi[T 5.0096], bhikkhave, bhikkhu satimā hoti, paramena satinepakkena samannāgato, cirakatampi cirabhāsitampi saritā anussaritā, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo…pe… saṃvattati.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is mindful, endowed with supreme mindfulness and sagacity; he is one who remembers and recollects what was done and said long ago. That a bhikkhu is mindful, endowed with supreme mindfulness and sagacity, and is one who remembers and recollects what was done and said long ago—this quality, too, is worthy of being remembered, creates affection and respect, and leads to cohesion, non-dispute, concord, and unity.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paññavā hoti, udayatthagāminiyā paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paññavā hoti, udayatthagāminiyā [V 3.0076] paññāya samannāgato ariyāya nibbedhikāya sammā dukkhakkhayagāminiyā, ayampi dhammo sāraṇīyo…pe… saṃvattati. Ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa dhammā sāraṇīyā piyakaraṇā garukaraṇā saṅgahāya avivādāya sāmaggiyā ekībhāvāya saṃvattantī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is wise; he is endowed with wisdom concerning arising and passing away, which is noble, penetrative, and leads rightly to the complete destruction of suffering. That a bhikkhu is wise; that he is endowed with wisdom concerning arising and passing away, which is noble, penetrative, and leads rightly to the complete destruction of suffering—this quality, too, is worthy of being remembered, creates affection and respect, and leads to cohesion, non-dispute, concord, and unity. Indeed, bhikkhus, these are the ten qualities that are worthy of being remembered, create affection and respect, and lead to cohesion, non-dispute, concord, and unity. Tenth.

Akkosavaggo pañcamo.

The Chapter on Abuse, the Fifth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Vivādā [P 5.0092] dve ca mūlāni, kusinārapavesane;

Sakko mahāli abhiṇhaṃ, sarīraṭṭhā ca bhaṇḍanāti.

Disputes, and two on Roots, at Kusinārā; Sakka, Mahāli, Constantly; Established in the Body, and Quarrels.

Paṭhamapaṇṇāsakaṃ samattaṃ.

The First Fifty is completed.

2. Dutiyapaṇṇāsakaṃ

2. The Second Fifty

(6) 1. Sacittavaggo

(6) 1. The Chapter on One’s Own Mind

1. Sacittasuttaṃ

1. On One’s Own Mind

51. Ekaṃ [T 5.0097][M 3.0329][V 3.0077] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

51. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus!” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied. The Blessed One said this:

“No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paracittapariyāyakusalo hoti, atha ‘sacittapariyāyakusalo bhavissāmī’ti bhavissāmāti (syā.) – evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu is not skilled in the ways of others’ minds, then you should train thus: ‘I will be skilled in the ways of my own mind.’ This, bhikkhus, is how you should train.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sacittapariyāyakusalo hoti? Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, itthī vā puriso vā daharo yuvā maṇḍanakajātiko ādāse vā parisuddhe pariyodāte acche vā udakapatte sakaṃ mukhanimittaṃ paccavekkhamāno sace tattha passati rajaṃ vā aṅgaṇaṃ vā, tasseva rajassa vā aṅgaṇassa vā pahānāya vāyamati. No ce tattha passati rajaṃ vā aṅgaṇaṃ vā, tenevattamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo – ‘lābhā vata me, parisuddhaṃ vata me’ti. Evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno paccavekkhaṇā bahukārā bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno bahukāro (ka.) hoti kusalesu dhammesu – ‘abhijjhālu nu [P 5.0093] kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, anabhijjhālu nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, byāpannacitto nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, abyāpannacitto nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhito nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, vigatathinamiddho nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi[T 5.0098], uddhato nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, anuddhato nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, vicikiccho nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, tiṇṇavicikiccho nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, kodhano nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, akkodhano nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, saṃkiliṭṭhacitto nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, asaṃkiliṭṭhacitto nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi[V 3.0078], sāraddhakāyo nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, asāraddhakāyo nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, kusīto nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, āraddhavīriyo nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, asamāhito nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, samāhito nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmī’ti.

“And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu skilled in the ways of his own mind? Just as a woman or a man—young, youthful, fond of adornment—would examine the reflection of their own face in a clean, bright mirror or in a clear bowl of water. If they see any dust or blemish there, they strive to remove that very dust or blemish. But if they do not see any dust or blemish there, on that account they are pleased, their intention fulfilled, thinking, ‘It is a gain for me! I am pure!’ In the same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu's reflection is of great benefit in regard to wholesome qualities: ‘Do I often dwell with covetousness, or without covetousness? With a mind of ill will, or without a mind of ill will? Beset by sloth and torpor, or free from sloth and torpor? Agitated, or unagitated? Doubtful, or having overcome doubt? Angry, or not angry? With a defiled mind, or an undefiled mind? With an agitated body, or an unagitated body? Lazy, or with energy aroused? Unconcentrated, or concentrated?’”

“Sace[M 3.0330], bhikkhave, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘abhijjhālu bahulaṃ viharāmi, byāpannacitto bahulaṃ viharāmi, thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhito bahulaṃ viharāmi, uddhato bahulaṃ viharāmi, vicikiccho bahulaṃ viharāmi, kodhano bahulaṃ viharāmi, saṃkiliṭṭhacitto bahulaṃ viharāmi, sāraddhakāyo bahulaṃ viharāmi, kusīto bahulaṃ viharāmi, asamāhito bahulaṃ viharāmī’ti, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ādittacelo vā ādittasīso vā. Tasseva celassa vā sīsassa vā nibbāpanāya adhimattaṃ chandañca vāyāmañca ussāhañca ussoḷhiñca appaṭivāniñca satiñca sampajaññañca kareyya. Evamevaṃ kho [T 5.0099] tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṃ.

“If, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘I frequently dwell with covetousness, with a mind of ill will, beset by sloth and torpor, agitated, doubtful, angry, with a defiled mind, with an agitated body, lazy, and unconcentrated,’ then, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu should apply extraordinary desire, effort, enthusiasm, exertion, perseverance, mindfulness, and clear comprehension for the abandoning of those very evil, unwholesome qualities. Just as, bhikkhus, if one’s cloth or head were on fire, one would apply extraordinary desire, effort, enthusiasm, exertion, perseverance, mindfulness, and clear comprehension to extinguish it. In the same way, that bhikkhu should apply extraordinary desire, effort, enthusiasm, exertion, perseverance, mindfulness, and clear comprehension for the abandoning of those very evil, unwholesome qualities.

“Sace [P 5.0094] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘anabhijjhālu bahulaṃ viharāmi, abyāpannacitto bahulaṃ viharāmi, vigatathinamiddho bahulaṃ viharāmi, anuddhato bahulaṃ viharāmi, tiṇṇavicikiccho bahulaṃ viharāmi, akkodhano bahulaṃ viharāmi, asaṃkiliṭṭhacitto bahulaṃ viharāmi, asāraddhakāyo bahulaṃ viharāmi, āraddhavīriyo bahulaṃ viharāmi, samāhito bahulaṃ viharāmī’ti, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tesuyeva kusalesu dhammesu patiṭṭhāya uttari āsavānaṃ khayāya yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“But if, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, upon reflecting, knows thus: ‘I often dwell without covetousness, without a mind of ill will, free from sloth and torpor, unagitated, having overcome doubt, without anger, with an undefiled mind, with an unagitated body, with aroused energy, and concentrated,’ then, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu, having established himself in these very wholesome qualities, should apply further effort for the destruction of the taints.” First.

2. Sāriputtasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse with Sāriputta

52. Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi – “āvuso bhikkhave”ti. “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca –

52. Then the Venerable Sāriputta addressed the bhikkhus: “Friends, bhikkhus!” “Friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Sāriputta. The Venerable Sāriputta said this:

“No [V 3.0079] ce, āvuso, bhikkhu paracittapariyāyakusalo hoti, atha ‘sacittapariyāyakusalo bhavissāmī’ti – evañhi vo, āvuso, sikkhitabbaṃ.

“If, friends, a bhikkhu is not skilled in the ways of others’ minds, then he should train himself thus: ‘I will become skilled in the ways of my own mind.’ This, friends, is how you should train yourselves.”

“Kathañcāvuso[M 3.0331], bhikkhu sacittapariyāyakusalo hoti? Seyyathāpi, āvuso, itthī vā puriso vā daharo yuvā maṇḍanakajātiko ādāse vā parisuddhe pariyodāte acche vā udapatte sakaṃ mukhanimittaṃ paccavekkhamāno sace tattha passati rajaṃ vā aṅgaṇaṃ vā, tasseva rajassa vā aṅgaṇassa vā pahānāya vāyamati. No ce tattha passati rajaṃ [T 5.0100] vā aṅgaṇaṃ vā, tenevattamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo – ‘lābhā vata me, parisuddhaṃ vata me’ti.

“And how, friends, is a bhikkhu skilled in the ways of his own mind? Suppose, friends, a woman or a man—young, youthful, and fond of adornment—were to examine the reflection of their own face in a clean, bright mirror or in a clear bowl of water. If they see any dust or a blemish there, they strive to remove that very dust or blemish. But if they do not see any dust or a blemish there, they are pleased and their wish is fulfilled, thinking: ‘It is a gain for me that I am pure!’

Evamevaṃ kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno paccavekkhaṇā bahukārā hoti kusalesu dhammesu – ‘abhijjhālu nu kho bahulaṃ [P 5.0095] viharāmi, anabhijjhālu nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, byāpannacitto nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, abyāpannacitto nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhito nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, vigatathinamiddho nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, uddhato nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, anuddhato nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, vicikiccho nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, tiṇṇavicikiccho nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, kodhano nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, akkodhano nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, saṃkiliṭṭhacitto nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, asaṃkiliṭṭhacitto nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, sāraddhakāyo nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, asāraddhakāyo nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, kusīto nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, āraddhavīriyo nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, samāhito nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, asamāhito nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmī’ti.

“In the same way, friends, a bhikkhu’s reflection is of great help in regard to wholesome qualities. He reflects: ‘Do I often dwell with covetousness, or do I often dwell without covetousness? Do I often dwell with a mind of ill will, or do I often dwell with a mind free from ill will? Do I often dwell overcome by sloth and torpor, or do I often dwell free from sloth and torpor? Do I often dwell with agitation, or do I often dwell without agitation? Do I often dwell with doubt, or do I often dwell having crossed over doubt? Do I often dwell with anger, or do I often dwell without anger? Do I often dwell with a defiled mind, or do I often dwell with an undefiled mind? Do I often dwell with an agitated body, or do I often dwell with an unagitated body? Do I often dwell lazily, or do I often dwell with aroused energy? Do I often dwell unconcentrated, or do I often dwell concentrated?’”

“Sace, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘abhijjhālu bahulaṃ viharāmi…pe… asamāhito bahulaṃ viharāmī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṃ. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, ādittacelo vā ādittasīso vā. Tasseva celassa vā sīsassa vā nibbāpanāya [T 5.0101] adhimattaṃ chandañca vāyāmañca ussāhañca ussoḷhiñca appaṭivāniñca satiñca sampajaññañca kareyya. Evamevaṃ kho, āvuso, tena bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya adhimatto chando [V 3.0080] ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṃ.

“If, friends, on reflecting, a bhikkhu knows thus: ‘I often dwell with covetousness … I often dwell unconcentrated,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu should apply extraordinary desire, effort, enthusiasm, zeal, relentlessness, mindfulness, and clear comprehension for the abandoning of those same evil, unwholesome qualities. Just as, friends, a person whose clothes or head were on fire would apply extraordinary desire, effort, enthusiasm, zeal, relentlessness, mindfulness, and clear comprehension to extinguish the fire on his clothes or head, in the same way, friends, that bhikkhu should apply extraordinary desire, effort, enthusiasm, zeal, relentlessness, mindfulness, and clear comprehension for the abandoning of those same evil, unwholesome qualities.”

“Sace [M 3.0332] panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘anabhijjhālu bahulaṃ viharāmi…pe… samāhito bahulaṃ viharāmī’ti, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā tesuyeva kusalesu dhammesu patiṭṭhāya uttari āsavānaṃ khayāya yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“But if, friends, on reflecting, a bhikkhu knows thus: ‘I often dwell without covetousness … I often dwell concentrated,’ then, friends, that bhikkhu, having established himself in those same wholesome qualities, should apply himself further to the destruction of the taints.” Second.

3. Ṭhitisuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Stability

53. “Ṭhitimpāhaṃ[P 5.0096], bhikkhave, na vaṇṇayāmi kusalesu dhammesu, pageva parihāniṃ. Vuḍḍhiñca kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, vaṇṇayāmi kusalesu dhammesu, no ṭhitiṃ no hāniṃ.

53. “Bhikkhus, I do not praise stability in wholesome qualities, still less decline. I praise growth in wholesome qualities, not stability and not decline.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, hāni hoti kusalesu dhammesu, no ṭhiti no vuḍḍhi? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yattako hoti saddhāya sīlena sutena cāgena paññāya paṭibhānena, tassa te dhammā neva tiṭṭhanti no vaḍḍhanti. Hānimetaṃ, bhikkhave, vadāmi kusalesu dhammesu, no ṭhitiṃ no vuḍḍhiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, hāni hoti kusalesu dhammesu, no ṭhiti no vuḍḍhi.

“And how, bhikkhus, is there decline in wholesome qualities, not stability and not growth? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has a certain amount of faith, virtue, learning, generosity, wisdom, and eloquence. These qualities of his neither remain stable nor grow. This, I say, is decline in wholesome qualities, not stability and not growth. This is how, bhikkhus, there is decline in wholesome qualities, not stability and not growth.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave ṭhiti hoti kusalesu dhammesu, no hāni no vuḍḍhi? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yattako hoti saddhāya sīlena sutena cāgena paññāya paṭibhānena, tassa te dhammā neva hāyanti no vaḍḍhanti[T 5.0102]. Ṭhitimetaṃ, bhikkhave, vadāmi kusalesu dhammesu, no hāniṃ no vuḍḍhiṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, ṭhiti hoti kusalesu dhammesu, no vuḍḍhi no hāni.

“And how, bhikkhus, is there stability in wholesome qualities, not decline and not growth? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has a certain amount of faith, virtue, learning, generosity, wisdom, and eloquence. These qualities of his neither decline nor grow. This, I say, is stability in wholesome qualities, not decline and not growth. This is how, bhikkhus, there is stability in wholesome qualities, not growth and not decline.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, vuḍḍhi hoti kusalesu dhammesu, no ṭhiti no hāni? Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu yattako hoti saddhāya sīlena sutena cāgena paññāya paṭibhānena, tassa te dhammā neva tiṭṭhanti no hāyanti. Vuḍḍhimetaṃ, bhikkhave, vadāmi kusalesu dhammesu, no ṭhitiṃ no hāniṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, vuḍḍhi hoti kusalesu dhammesu, no ṭhiti no hāni.

“And how, bhikkhus, is there growth in wholesome qualities, not stability and not decline? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has a certain amount of faith, virtue, learning, generosity, wisdom, and eloquence. These qualities of his neither remain stable nor decline. This, I say, is growth in wholesome qualities, not stability and not decline. This is how, bhikkhus, there is growth in wholesome qualities, not stability and not decline.”

“No [V 3.0081] ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paracittapariyāyakusalo hoti, atha ‘sacittapariyāyakusalo bhavissāmī’ti – evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ.

“If, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not skilled in the ways of others’ minds, then he should train himself thus: ‘I will become skilled in the ways of my own mind.’ This, bhikkhus, is how you should train yourselves.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sacittapariyāyakusalo hoti? Seyyathāpi[P 5.0097], bhikkhave, itthī vā puriso vā daharo yuvā maṇḍanakajātiko ādāse vā [M 3.0333] parisuddhe pariyodāte acche vā udapatte sakaṃ mukhanimittaṃ paccavekkhamāno sace tattha passati rajaṃ vā aṅgaṇaṃ vā, tasseva rajassa vā aṅgaṇassa vā pahānāya vāyamati. No ce tattha passati rajaṃ vā aṅgaṇaṃ vā, tenevattamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo – ‘lābhā vata me, parisuddhaṃ vata me’ti. Evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno paccavekkhaṇā bahukārā hoti kusalesu dhammesu – ‘abhijjhālu nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, anabhijjhālu nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, byāpannacitto nu [T 5.0103] kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, abyāpannacitto nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhito nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, vigatathinamiddho nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, uddhato nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, anuddhato nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, vicikiccho nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, tiṇṇavicikiccho nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, kodhano nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, akkodhano nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, saṃkiliṭṭhacitto nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, asaṃkiliṭṭhacitto nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, sāraddhakāyo nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, asāraddhakāyo nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, kusīto nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, āraddhavīriyo nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, samāhito nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, asamāhito nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmī’ti.

“And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu skilled in the ways of his own mind? Suppose, bhikkhus, a woman or a man—young, youthful, and fond of ornaments—were to examine the reflection of their own face in a clean, bright mirror or in a clear bowl of water. If they see any adventitious dust or a blemish there, they strive to remove it. But if they do not see any adventitious dust or a blemish there, they are pleased and their wish is fulfilled, and they think: ‘It is a gain for me that I am pure!’ In the same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu’s reflection is of great help in regard to wholesome qualities. He reflects: ‘Do I often dwell with covetousness, or do I often dwell without covetousness? Do I often dwell with a mind of ill will, or do I often dwell with a mind free from ill will? Do I often dwell overcome by sloth and torpor, or do I often dwell free from sloth and torpor? Do I often dwell with restlessness, or do I often dwell without restlessness? Do I often dwell with doubt, or do I often dwell having crossed over doubt? Do I often dwell with anger, or do I often dwell without anger?
