Do I often dwell with a defiled mind, or do I often dwell with an undefiled mind? Do I often dwell with an agitated body, or do I often dwell with an unagitated body? Do I often dwell lazily, or do I often dwell with energy aroused? Do I often dwell concentrated, or do I often dwell unconcentrated?’”

“Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘abhijjhālu bahulaṃ viharāmi, byāpannacitto bahulaṃ viharāmi, thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhito bahulaṃ viharāmi, uddhato bahulaṃ viharāmi, vicikiccho bahulaṃ viharāmi, kodhano bahulaṃ viharāmi, saṃkiliṭṭhacitto bahulaṃ viharāmi, sāraddhakāyo bahulaṃ viharāmi, kusīto bahulaṃ viharāmi, asamāhito bahulaṃ viharāmī’ti, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya [P 5.0098] adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ādittacelo vā ādittasīso vā. Tasseva celassa vā sīsassa vā nibbāpanāya adhimattaṃ chandañca [T 5.0104] vāyāmañca ussāhañca ussoḷhiñca appaṭivāniñca satiñca sampajaññañca kareyya; evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tena bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva [V 3.0082] pāpakānaṃ akusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ pahānāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṃ.

“If, bhikkhus, on reflecting, a bhikkhu knows thus: ‘I often dwell with covetousness, with a mind of ill will, overcome by sloth and torpor, with restlessness, with doubt, with anger, with a defiled mind, with an agitated body, lazily, and unconcentrated,’ then, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu should apply extraordinary desire, effort, enthusiasm, zeal, relentlessness, mindfulness, and clear comprehension for the abandoning of those same evil unwholesome qualities. Just as, bhikkhus, a person whose clothes or head were on fire would apply extraordinary desire, effort, enthusiasm, zeal, relentlessness, mindfulness, and clear comprehension to extinguish the fire on his clothes or head; in the same way, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu should apply extraordinary desire, effort, enthusiasm, zeal, relentlessness, mindfulness, and clear comprehension for the abandoning of those same evil unwholesome qualities.”

“Sace [M 3.0334] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘anabhijjhālu bahulaṃ viharāmi, abyāpannacitto bahulaṃ viharāmi, vigatathinamiddho bahulaṃ viharāmi, anuddhato bahulaṃ viharāmi, tiṇṇavicikiccho bahulaṃ viharāmi, akkodhano bahulaṃ viharāmi, asaṃkiliṭṭhacitto bahulaṃ viharāmi, asāraddhakāyo bahulaṃ viharāmi, āraddhavīriyo bahulaṃ viharāmi, samāhito bahulaṃ viharāmī’ti, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tesuyeva kusalesu dhammesu patiṭṭhāya uttari āsavānaṃ khayāya yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“But if, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, on reviewing, knows thus: ‘I often dwell without covetousness, with a mind free from ill will, free from sloth and torpor, without restlessness, with doubt overcome, without anger, with an undefiled mind, with an untroubled body, with energy aroused, and concentrated,’ then, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu, being established in these very wholesome qualities, should make a further effort for the destruction of the taints.” The Third.

4. Samathasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Serenity

54. “No ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paracittapariyāyakusalo hoti, atha ‘sacittapariyāyakusalo bhavissāmī’ti – evañhi vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ.

54. “If, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not skilled in the ways of others’ minds, then he should train himself thus: ‘I will become skilled in the ways of my own mind.’ This, bhikkhus, is how you should train yourselves.”

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sacittapariyāyakusalo hoti? Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, itthī vā puriso vā daharo yuvā maṇḍanakajātiko ādāse vā parisuddhe pariyodāte acche vā udapatte sakaṃ mukhanimittaṃ paccavekkhamāno sace tattha passati rajaṃ vā aṅgaṇaṃ vā, tasseva rajassa vā aṅgaṇassa vā pahānāya vāyamati. No ce tattha passati rajaṃ vā aṅgaṇaṃ vā, tenevattamano hoti [P 5.0099] paripuṇṇasaṅkappo – ‘lābhā vata me, parisuddhaṃ vata me’ti. Evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno paccavekkhaṇā bahukārā hoti [T 5.0105] kusalesu dhammesu – ‘lābhī nu khomhi ajjhattaṃ cetosamathassa, na nu khomhi lābhī ajjhattaṃ cetosamathassa, lābhī nu khomhi adhipaññādhammavipassanāya, na nu khomhi lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāyā’ti.

And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu skilled in the ways of his own mind? Suppose, bhikkhus, a woman or a man—young, youthful, and fond of adornment—were to examine the image of their own face in a clean, bright mirror or in a bowl of clear water. If they see any dust or blemish there, they strive for the removal of that very dust or blemish. But if they do not see any dust or blemish there, they are pleased on that account and their intention is fulfilled, thinking: ‘Indeed, it is a gain for me! Indeed, it is pure!’ In the very same way, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu’s reviewing is of great benefit in regard to wholesome qualities: ‘Am I a gainer of internal serenity of mind, or am I not a gainer of internal serenity of mind? Am I a gainer of insight into phenomena through higher wisdom, or am I not a gainer of insight into phenomena through higher wisdom?’

“Sace, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘lābhīmhi ajjhattaṃ cetosamathassa, na lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāyā’ti, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā ajjhattaṃ cetosamathe patiṭṭhāya adhipaññādhammavipassanāya yogo karaṇīyo. So aparena samayena lābhī ceva hoti ajjhattaṃ cetosamathassa lābhī ca adhipaññādhammavipassanāya.

If, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, on reviewing, knows thus: ‘I am a gainer of internal serenity of mind, but not a gainer of insight into phenomena through higher wisdom,’ then, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu, being established in internal serenity of mind, should make an effort for insight into phenomena through higher wisdom. At a later time, he becomes a gainer of both internal serenity of mind and insight into phenomena through higher wisdom.

“Sace [V 3.0083] pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘lābhīmhi adhipaññādhammavipassanāya, na lābhī ajjhattaṃ cetosamathassā’ti, tena, bhikkhave[M 3.0335], bhikkhunā adhipaññādhammavipassanāya patiṭṭhāya ajjhattaṃ cetosamathe yogo karaṇīyo. So aparena samayena lābhī ceva hoti adhipaññādhammavipassanāya lābhī ca ajjhattaṃ cetosamathassa.

But if, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, on reviewing, knows thus: ‘I am a gainer of insight into phenomena through higher wisdom, but not a gainer of internal serenity of mind,’ then, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu, being established in insight into phenomena through higher wisdom, should make an effort for internal serenity of mind. At a later time, he becomes a gainer of both insight into phenomena through higher wisdom and internal serenity of mind.

“Sace, pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘na lābhī ajjhattaṃ cetosamathassa, na lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāyā’ti, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ paṭilābhāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṃ. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, ādittacelo vā ādittasīso vā. Tasseva celassa vā sīsassa vā nibbāpanāya adhimattaṃ chandañca vāyāmañca ussāhañca ussoḷhiñca appaṭivāniñca satiñca sampajaññañca kareyya. Evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tena [T 5.0106] bhikkhunā tesaṃyeva kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ paṭilābhāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo [P 5.0100] ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṃ. So aparena samayena lābhī ceva hoti ajjhattaṃ cetosamathassa lābhī ca adhipaññādhammavipassanāya.

But if, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, on reviewing, knows thus: ‘I am not a gainer of internal serenity of mind, and I am not a gainer of insight into phenomena through higher wisdom,’ then, bhikkhus, for the attainment of those very wholesome qualities, that bhikkhu should apply extraordinary desire, effort, enthusiasm, ardour, persistence, mindfulness, and clear comprehension. Suppose, bhikkhus, one whose robe or head was on fire would apply extraordinary desire, effort, enthusiasm, ardour, persistence, mindfulness, and clear comprehension to extinguish the fire on that very robe or head. In the very same way, bhikkhus, for the attainment of those very wholesome qualities, that bhikkhu should apply extraordinary desire, effort, enthusiasm, ardour, persistence, mindfulness, and clear comprehension. At a later time, he becomes a gainer of both internal serenity of mind and insight into phenomena through higher wisdom.

“Sace pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno evaṃ jānāti – ‘lābhīmhi ajjhattaṃ cetosamathassa, lābhī adhipaññādhammavipassanāyā’ti, tena, bhikkhave, bhikkhunā tesuyeva kusalesu dhammesu patiṭṭhāya uttari āsavānaṃ khayāya yogo karaṇīyo.

But if, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu, on reviewing, knows thus: ‘I am a gainer of internal serenity of mind, and I am a gainer of insight into phenomena through higher wisdom,’ then, bhikkhus, that bhikkhu, being established in these very wholesome qualities, should make a further effort for the destruction of the taints.

“Cīvarampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampi. Piṇḍapātampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampi. Senāsanampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampi. Gāmanigamampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampi. Janapadapadesampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampi. Puggalampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampi.

Bhikkhus, I speak of two kinds of robes: to be used and not to be used. I speak of two kinds of almsfood: to be used and not to be used. I speak of two kinds of lodgings: to be used and not to be used. I speak of two kinds of villages and towns: to be resorted to and not to be resorted to. I speak of two kinds of countries and regions: to be resorted to and not to be resorted to. I speak of two kinds of persons: to be associated with and not to be associated with.

“‘Cīvarampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampī’ti, iti kho [V 3.0084] panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Tattha yaṃ jaññā cīvaraṃ – ‘idaṃ kho me cīvaraṃ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evarūpaṃ cīvaraṃ na sevitabbaṃ. Tattha yaṃ jaññā cīvaraṃ – ‘idaṃ kho me [M 3.0336] cīvaraṃ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evarūpaṃ cīvaraṃ sevitabbaṃ. ‘Cīvarampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampī’ti, iti yaṃ [T 5.0107] taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.

‘Bhikkhus, I speak of two kinds of robes: to be used and not to be used.’ Indeed, this was said. And in reference to what was this said? Therein, should one know of a certain robe: ‘Indeed, for me, by using this robe, unwholesome qualities increase and wholesome qualities decline,’ such a robe should not be used. Therein, should one know of a certain robe: ‘Indeed, for me, by using this robe, unwholesome qualities decline and wholesome qualities increase,’ such a robe should be used. ‘Bhikkhus, I speak of two kinds of robes: to be used and not to be used’—that which was said thus, was said in reference to this.

“‘Piṇḍapātampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampī’ti, iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Tattha yaṃ jaññā piṇḍapātaṃ – ‘imaṃ kho me piṇḍapātaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā [P 5.0101] parihāyantī’ti, evarūpo piṇḍapāto na sevitabbo. Tattha yaṃ jaññā piṇḍapātaṃ – ‘imaṃ kho me piṇḍapātaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evarūpo piṇḍapāto sevitabbo. ‘Piṇḍapātampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampī’ti, iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.

‘Bhikkhus, I speak of two kinds of almsfood: to be used and not to be used.’ Indeed, this was said. And in reference to what was this said? Therein, should one know of certain almsfood: ‘Indeed, for me, by using this almsfood, unwholesome qualities increase and wholesome qualities decline,’ such almsfood should not be used. Therein, should one know of certain almsfood: ‘Indeed, for me, by using this almsfood, unwholesome qualities decline and wholesome qualities increase,’ such almsfood should be used. ‘Bhikkhus, I speak of two kinds of almsfood: to be used and not to be used’—that which was said thus, was said in reference to this.

“‘Senāsanampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampī’ti, iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Tattha yaṃ jaññā senāsanaṃ – ‘idaṃ kho me senāsanaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evarūpaṃ senāsanaṃ na sevitabbaṃ. Tattha yaṃ jaññā senāsanaṃ – ‘idaṃ kho me senāsanaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evarūpaṃ senāsanaṃ sevitabbaṃ. ‘Senāsanampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampī’ti, iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, I say that lodgings are of two kinds: those to be resorted to and those not to be resorted to.’ Indeed, this was said. And in reference to what was this said? Therein, should one know of a certain lodging: ‘Indeed, for me, by resorting to this lodging, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states decline,’ such a lodging should not be resorted to. Therein, should one know of a certain lodging: ‘Indeed, for me, by resorting to this lodging, unwholesome states decline and wholesome states increase,’ such a lodging should be resorted to. ‘Bhikkhus, I say that lodgings are of two kinds: those to be resorted to and those not to be resorted to’—that which was said thus, was said in reference to this.

“‘Gāmanigamampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampī’ti, iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Tattha yaṃ jaññā gāmanigamaṃ – ‘imaṃ kho me gāmanigamaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti[T 5.0108], evarūpo gāmanigamo na sevitabbo. Tattha yaṃ jaññā gāmanigamaṃ – ‘imaṃ kho me gāmanigamaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evarūpo gāmanigamo sevitabbo[V 3.0085]. ‘Gāmanigamampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampī’ti, iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, I say that villages and towns are of two kinds: those to be resorted to and those not to be resorted to.’ Indeed, this was said. And in reference to what was this said? Therein, should one know of a certain village or town: ‘Indeed, for me, by resorting to this village or town, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states decline,’ such a village or town should not be resorted to. Therein, should one know of a certain village or town: ‘Indeed, for me, by resorting to this village or town, unwholesome states decline and wholesome states increase,’ such a village or town should be resorted to. ‘Bhikkhus, I say that villages and towns are of two kinds: those to be resorted to and those not to be resorted to’—that which was said thus, was said in reference to this.

“‘Janapadapadesampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampī’ti, iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Tattha yaṃ jaññā janapadapadesaṃ – ‘imaṃ kho me janapadapadesaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā [M 3.0337][P 5.0102] dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evarūpo janapadapadeso na sevitabbo. Tattha yaṃ jaññā janapadapadesaṃ – ‘imaṃ kho me janapadapadesaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evarūpo janapadapadeso sevitabbo. ‘Janapadapadesampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampī’ti, iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, I say that regions are of two kinds: those to be resorted to and those not to be resorted to.’ Indeed, this was said. And in reference to what was this said? Therein, should one know of a certain region: ‘Indeed, for me, by resorting to this region, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states decline,’ such a region should not be resorted to. Therein, should one know of a certain region: ‘Indeed, for me, by resorting to this region, unwholesome states decline and wholesome states increase,’ such a region should be resorted to. ‘Bhikkhus, I say that regions are of two kinds: those to be resorted to and those not to be resorted to’—that which was said thus, was said in reference to this.

“‘Puggalampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampī’ti, iti kho panetaṃ vuttaṃ. Kiñcetaṃ paṭicca vuttaṃ? Tattha yaṃ jaññā puggalaṃ – ‘imaṃ kho me puggalaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhanti, kusalā dhammā parihāyantī’ti, evarūpo puggalo na sevitabbo. Tattha yaṃ jaññā puggalaṃ – ‘imaṃ kho me puggalaṃ sevato akusalā dhammā parihāyanti, kusalā dhammā abhivaḍḍhantī’ti, evarūpo puggalo sevitabbo[T 5.0109]. ‘Puggalampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duvidhena vadāmi – sevitabbampi asevitabbampī’ti, iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vutta”nti. Catutthaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, I say that persons are of two kinds: those to be resorted to and those not to be resorted to.’ Indeed, this was said. And in reference to what was this said? Therein, should one know of a certain person: ‘Indeed, for me, by resorting to this person, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states decline,’ such a person should not be resorted to. Therein, should one know of a certain person: ‘Indeed, for me, by resorting to this person, unwholesome states decline and wholesome states increase,’ such a person should be resorted to. ‘Bhikkhus, I say that persons are of two kinds: those to be resorted to and those not to be resorted to’—that which was said thus, was said in reference to this.” The fourth.

5. Parihānasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Decline

55. Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi – “āvuso bhikkhave”ti bhikkhavoti (sī. syā.). “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca –

55. Then the Venerable Sāriputta addressed the bhikkhus: “Friends, bhikkhus.” “Friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Sāriputta. The Venerable Sāriputta said this:

“‘Parihānadhammo puggalo, parihānadhammo puggalo’ti, āvuso, vuccati. ‘Aparihānadhammo puggalo, aparihānadhammo puggalo’ti, āvuso, vuccati. Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, parihānadhammo puggalo vutto bhagavatā, kittāvatā ca pana aparihānadhammo puggalo vutto [V 3.0086] bhagavatā”ti? “Dūratopi kho mayaṃ, āvuso, āgacchāma āyasmato sāriputtassa santike etassa bhāsitassa atthamaññātuṃ. Sādhu vatāyasmantaṃyeva sāriputtaṃ paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho[P 5.0103]. Āyasmato sāriputtassa sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.

“‘Friends, it is said: “A person of a nature to decline, a person of a nature to decline.” And it is said: “A person not of a nature to decline, a person not of a nature to decline.” To what extent, friends, has a person of a nature to decline been spoken of by the Blessed One, and to what extent has a person not of a nature to decline been spoken of by the Blessed One?’ ‘Friend, we would come even from afar to the presence of the Venerable Sāriputta to know the meaning of this statement. It would be good indeed if the meaning of this statement would become clear to the Venerable Sāriputta himself. Having heard it from the Venerable Sāriputta, the bhikkhus will bear it in mind.’”

“Tenahāvuso[M 3.0338], suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca –

“Well then, friends, listen and attend closely; I will speak.” “Yes, friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Sāriputta. The Venerable Sāriputta said this:

“Kittāvatā nu kho, āvuso, parihānadhammo puggalo vutto bhagavatā? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu assutañceva dhammaṃ na suṇāti, sutā cassa dhammā sammosaṃ gacchanti, ye cassa dhammā pubbe cetaso asamphuṭṭhapubbā te cassa na samudācaranti, aviññātañceva na vijānāti. Ettāvatā kho, āvuso, parihānadhammo puggalo vutto bhagavatā.

“To what extent, friends, has a person of a nature to decline been spoken of by the Blessed One? Here, friends, a bhikkhu does not hear a teaching he has not heard before; the teachings he has heard are lost to him; those teachings not previously contacted by his mind do not arise; and he does not understand what was not understood. To this extent, friends, a person of a nature to decline has been spoken of by the Blessed One.

“Kittāvatā ca panāvuso, aparihānadhammo puggalo vutto bhagavatā? Idhāvuso, bhikkhu assutañceva dhammaṃ suṇāti, sutā cassa dhammā [T 5.0110] na sammosaṃ gacchanti, ye cassa dhammā pubbe cetaso asamphuṭṭhapubbā te cassa samudācaranti, aviññātañceva vijānāti. Ettāvatā kho, āvuso, aparihānadhammo puggalo vutto bhagavatā.

“And to what extent, friends, has a person not of a nature to decline been spoken of by the Blessed One? Here, friends, a bhikkhu hears a teaching he has not heard before; the teachings he has heard are not lost to him; those teachings not previously contacted by his mind do arise; and he understands what was not understood. To this extent, friends, a person not of a nature to decline has been spoken of by the Blessed One.

“No ce, āvuso, bhikkhu paracittapariyāyakusalo hoti, atha ‘sacittapariyāyakusalo bhavissāmī’ti – evañhi vo, āvuso, sikkhitabbaṃ.

“Friends, if a bhikkhu is not skilled in the ways of others’ minds, then he should train thus: ‘I will become skilled in the ways of my own mind.’ This, friends, is how you should train.”

“Kathañcāvuso, bhikkhu sacittapariyāyakusalo hoti? Seyyathāpi, āvuso, itthī vā puriso vā daharo yuvā maṇḍanakajātiko ādāse vā parisuddhe pariyodāte acche vā udapatte sakaṃ mukhanimittaṃ paccavekkhamāno sace tattha passati rajaṃ vā aṅgaṇaṃ vā, tasseva rajassa vā aṅgaṇassa vā pahānāya vāyamati. No ce tattha passati rajaṃ vā aṅgaṇaṃ vā, tenevattamano hoti paripuṇṇasaṅkappo [P 5.0104] – ‘lābhā vata me, parisuddhaṃ vata me’ti. Evameva kho, āvuso, bhikkhuno paccavekkhaṇā bahukārā hoti kusalesu dhammesu – ‘anabhijjhālu nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no, abyāpannacitto nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no, vigatathinamiddho nu kho bahulaṃ [V 3.0087] viharāmi, saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no, anuddhato nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no, tiṇṇavicikiccho nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no, akkodhano nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, saṃvijjati [M 3.0339] nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu [T 5.0111] no, asaṃkiliṭṭhacitto nu kho bahulaṃ viharāmi, saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no, lābhī nu khomhi ajjhattaṃ dhammapāmojjassa, saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no, lābhī nu khomhi ajjhattaṃ cetosamathassa, saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no, lābhī nu khomhi adhipaññādhammavipassanāya, saṃvijjati nu kho me eso dhammo udāhu no’ti.

“And how, friends, is a bhikkhu skilled in the ways of his own mind? Suppose, friends, a woman or a man—young, youthful, and fond of adornments—were to examine the image of their own face in a clean, bright mirror or in a clear bowl of water. If they see any dust or blemish on it, they strive to remove that very dust or blemish. But if they do not see any dust or blemish on it, for that very reason they are pleased and their intention is fulfilled: ‘It is a gain for me! I am pure!’ So too, friends, a bhikkhu’s reflection is of great benefit in regard to wholesome qualities. He reflects: ‘Do I often dwell without covetousness? Is this quality found in me or not? Do I often dwell with a mind free of ill will? Is this quality found in me or not? Do I often dwell free from sloth and torpor? Is this quality found in me or not? Do I often dwell unagitated? Is this quality found in me or not? Do I often dwell having crossed over doubt? Is this quality found in me or not? Do I often dwell without anger? Is this quality found in me or not? Do I often dwell with an undefiled mind? Is this quality found in me or not? Am I an obtainer of internal joy in the Dhamma? Is this quality found in me or not? Am I an obtainer of internal serenity of mind? Is this quality found in me or not? Am I an obtainer of insight into phenomena pertaining to higher wisdom? Is this quality found in me or not?’”

“Sace pana, āvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno sabbepime kusale dhamme attani na samanupassati, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā sabbesaṃyeva imesaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ paṭilābhāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṃ. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, ādittacelo vā ādittasīso vā. Tasseva celassa vā sīsassa vā nibbāpanāya adhimattaṃ chandañca vāyāmañca ussāhañca ussoḷhiñca appaṭivāniñca satiñca sampajaññañca kareyya. Evamevaṃ kho, āvuso, tena bhikkhunā sabbesaṃyeva kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ paṭilābhāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṃ.

“But if, friends, a bhikkhu, on reflection, does not see any of these wholesome qualities in himself, then that bhikkhu should apply extraordinary desire, effort, zeal, enthusiasm, indefatigability, mindfulness, and clear comprehension for the acquisition of all these wholesome qualities. Suppose, friends, a person whose clothes or head were on fire would apply extraordinary desire, effort, zeal, enthusiasm, indefatigability, mindfulness, and clear comprehension to extinguish the fire on their clothes or head. In the same way, that bhikkhu should apply extraordinary desire, effort, zeal, enthusiasm, indefatigability, mindfulness, and clear comprehension for the acquisition of all these wholesome qualities.

“Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno ekacce kusale dhamme attani samanupassati, ekacce kusale dhamme attani [P 5.0105] na samanupassati, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā ye kusale dhamme attani samanupassati tesu kusalesu dhammesu patiṭṭhāya, ye kusale dhamme attani na samanupassati tesaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ paṭilābhāya adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho [T 5.0112] ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṃ. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, ādittacelo vā ādittasīso vā. Tasseva celassa vā sīsassa vā nibbāpanāya adhimattaṃ chandañca vāyāmañca ussāhañca ussoḷhiñca appaṭivāniñca satiñca sampajaññañca kareyya. Evamevaṃ kho, āvuso, tena bhikkhunā ye kusale dhamme attani samanupassati tesu kusalesu dhammesu patiṭṭhāya, ye kusale dhamme attani na samanupassati tesaṃ kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ paṭilābhāya [V 3.0088] adhimatto chando ca vāyāmo ca ussāho ca ussoḷhī ca appaṭivānī ca sati ca sampajaññañca karaṇīyaṃ.

“If, friends, a bhikkhu, on reflection, sees some wholesome qualities in himself but does not see others, he should, being established in those wholesome qualities that he sees in himself, apply extraordinary desire, effort, zeal, enthusiasm, indefatigability, mindfulness, and clear comprehension for the acquisition of those wholesome qualities that he does not see in himself. Just as, friends, a person whose garment or head was on fire would apply extraordinary desire, effort, zeal, enthusiasm, indefatigability, mindfulness, and clear comprehension to extinguish the fire on his garment or head; in the very same way, friends, that bhikkhu, being established in those wholesome qualities that he sees in himself, should apply extraordinary desire, effort, zeal, enthusiasm, indefatigability, mindfulness, and clear comprehension for the acquisition of those wholesome qualities that he does not see in himself.

“Sace panāvuso, bhikkhu paccavekkhamāno sabbepime kusale dhamme attani samanupassati, tenāvuso, bhikkhunā sabbesveva imesu kusalesu [M 3.0340] dhammesu patiṭṭhāya uttari āsavānaṃ khayāya yogo karaṇīyo”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“If, friends, a bhikkhu, on reflection, sees all these wholesome qualities in himself, then that bhikkhu, being established in all these wholesome qualities, should apply himself further to the destruction of the taints.” Fifth.

6. Paṭhamasaññāsuttaṃ

6. The First Sutta on Perceptions

56. “Dasayimā, bhikkhave, saññā bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā honti mahānisaṃsā amatogadhā amatapariyosānā. Katamā dasa? Asubhasaññā, maraṇasaññā, āhāre paṭikūlasaññā, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññā, aniccasaññā, anicce dukkhasaññā, dukkhe anattasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā, nirodhasaññā – imā kho, bhikkhave, dasa saññā bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā honti mahānisaṃsā amatogadhā amatapariyosānā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

56. “Bhikkhus, these ten perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit and great benefit, have the deathless as their destination and the deathless as their consummation. What ten? The perception of unattractiveness, the perception of death, the perception of repulsiveness in food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in the impermanent, the perception of not-self in what is suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, and the perception of cessation. These, bhikkhus, are the ten perceptions that, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit and great benefit, have the deathless as their destination and the deathless as their consummation.” Sixth.

7. Dutiyasaññāsuttaṃ

7. The Second Sutta on Perceptions

57. “Dasayimā[P 5.0106], bhikkhave, saññā bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā honti [T 5.0113] mahānisaṃsā amatogadhā amatapariyosānā. Katamā dasa? Aniccasaññā, anattasaññā, maraṇasaññā, āhāre paṭikūlasaññā, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññā, aṭṭhikasaññā, puḷavakasaññā pulavakasaññā (sī. pī.), puḷuvakasaññā (ka.), a. ni. 1.463-472, vinīlakasaññā, vicchiddakasaññā, uddhumātakasaññā – imā kho, bhikkhave, dasa saññā bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā honti mahānisaṃsā amatogadhā amatapariyosānā”ti. Sattamaṃ.

57. “Bhikkhus, these ten perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit and great benefit, have the deathless as their destination, and the deathless as their final end. What ten? The perception of impermanence, the perception of not-self, the perception of death, the perception of the repulsiveness of food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of a skeleton, the perception of a worm-infested corpse, the perception of a livid corpse, the perception of a fissured corpse, and the perception of a bloated corpse. These, bhikkhus, are the ten perceptions that, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit and great benefit, have the deathless as their destination, and the deathless as their final end.” Seventh.

8. Mūlakasuttaṃ

8. The Sutta on Roots

58. a. ni. 8.83 “Sace, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘kiṃmūlakā, āvuso, sabbe dhammā, kiṃsambhavā sabbe dhammā, kiṃsamudayā sabbe dhammā, kiṃsamosaraṇā sabbe dhammā, kiṃpamukhā sabbe dhammā, kiṃadhipateyyā sabbe dhammā, kiṃuttarā sabbe dhammā, kiṃsārā sabbe dhammā, kiṃogadhā sabbe dhammā, kiṃpariyosānā sabbe dhammā’ti, evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave[V 3.0089], tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ kinti byākareyyāthā”ti? “Bhagavaṃmūlakā no, bhante, dhammā bhagavaṃnettikā bhagavaṃpaṭisaraṇā. Sādhu vata, bhante, bhagavantaṃyeva paṭibhātu etassa bhāsitassa attho. Bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.

58. “Bhikkhus, if wanderers of other sects were to ask you: ‘Friends, what is the root of all phenomena? What is their origin? What is their source? What is their confluence? What is their chief? What is their sovereign? What is their superior? What is their essence? What is their immersion? What is their final end?’—being asked thus, bhikkhus, how would you answer those wanderers of other sects?” “Venerable sir, our teachings have the Blessed One as their root, the Blessed One as their guide, the Blessed One as their refuge. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One himself would clarify the meaning of this statement. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the bhikkhus will bear it in mind.”

“Tena [M 3.0341] hi, bhikkhave, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

“Well then, bhikkhus, listen and pay close attention. I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Sace, bhikkhave, aññatitthiyā paribbājakā evaṃ puccheyyuṃ – ‘kiṃmūlakā, āvuso, sabbe dhammā, kiṃsambhavā sabbe dhammā, kiṃsamudayā [T 5.0114] sabbe dhammā, kiṃsamosaraṇā sabbe [P 5.0107] dhammā kiṃpamukhā sabbe dhammā, kiṃ adhipateyyā sabbe dhammā, kiṃuttarā sabbe dhammā, kiṃsārā sabbe dhammā, kiṃogadhā sabbe dhammā, kiṃpariyosānā sabbe dhammā’ti, evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyātha – ‘chandamūlakā, āvuso, sabbe dhammā, manasikārasambhavā sabbe dhammā, phassasamudayā sabbe dhammā, vedanāsamosaraṇā sabbe dhammā, samādhippamukhā sabbe dhammā, satādhipateyyā sabbe dhammā, paññuttarā sabbe dhammā, vimuttisārā sabbe dhammā, amatogadhā sabbe dhammā, nibbānapariyosānā sabbe dhammā’ti. Evaṃ puṭṭhā tumhe, bhikkhave, tesaṃ aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ evaṃ byākareyyāthā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if wanderers of other sects were to ask you: ‘Friends, what is the root of all phenomena? What is their origin? What is their source? What is their confluence? What is their chief? What is their sovereign? What is their superior? What is their essence? What is their immersion? What is their final end?’—being asked thus, bhikkhus, you should answer those wanderers of other sects thus: ‘Friends, all phenomena are rooted in desire. They originate from attention. They arise from contact. They converge on feeling. They have concentration as their chief. They have mindfulness as their sovereign. They have wisdom as their superior. They have liberation as their essence. They are immersed in the Deathless. They have Nibbāna as their final end.’ Being asked thus, bhikkhus, this is how you should answer those wanderers of other sects.” Eighth.

9. Pabbajjāsuttaṃ

9. 9. The Discourse on the Going Forth

59. “Tasmātiha, bhikkhave, evaṃ sikkhitabbaṃ – ‘yathāpabbajjāparicitañca no cittaṃ bhavissati, na cuppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā cittaṃ pariyādāya ṭhassanti; aniccasaññāparicitañca no cittaṃ bhavissati, anattasaññāparicitañca no cittaṃ bhavissati, asubhasaññāparicitañca no cittaṃ bhavissati, ādīnavasaññāparicitañca no cittaṃ bhavissati, lokassa samañca visamañca ñatvā taṃsaññāparicitañca no cittaṃ bhavissati, lokassa bhavañca sambhavañca (sī. syā.) vibhavañca ñatvā taṃsaññāparicitañca no cittaṃ bhavissati, lokassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca ñatvā taṃsaññāparicitañca no cittaṃ bhavissati, pahānasaññāparicitañca [T 5.0115] no cittaṃ bhavissati, virāgasaññāparicitañca no cittaṃ bhavissati, nirodhasaññāparicitañca no cittaṃ bhavissatī’ti – evañhi [P 5.0108] vo, bhikkhave, sikkhitabbaṃ.

59. “Therefore, bhikkhus, you should train yourselves thus: ‘Our mind will be familiar with what is in accordance with the going forth, and evil, unwholesome states that have arisen will not persist, having overcome the mind. Our mind will be familiar with the perception of impermanence. Our mind will be familiar with the perception of not-self. Our mind will be familiar with the perception of foulness. Our mind will be familiar with the perception of drawback. Having known the world’s evenness and unevenness, our mind will be familiar with that perception. Having known the world’s coming-to-be and passing-away, our mind will be familiar with that perception. Having known the world’s origination and cessation, our mind will be familiar with that perception. Our mind will be familiar with the perception of abandoning. Our mind will be familiar with the perception of dispassion. Our mind will be familiar with the perception of cessation.’ This, bhikkhus, is how you should train yourselves.”

“Yato [M 3.0342][V 3.0090] kho, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno yathāpabbajjāparicitañca cittaṃ hoti na cuppannā pāpakā akusalā dhammā cittaṃ pariyādāya tiṭṭhanti, aniccasaññāparicitañca cittaṃ hoti, anattasaññāparicitañca cittaṃ hoti, asubhasaññāparicitañca cittaṃ hoti, ādīnavasaññāparicitañca cittaṃ hoti, lokassa samañca visamañca ñatvā taṃsaññāparicitañca cittaṃ hoti, lokassa bhavañca vibhavañca ñatvā taṃsaññāparicitañca cittaṃ hoti, lokassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca ñatvā taṃsaññāparicitañca cittaṃ hoti, pahānasaññāparicitañca cittaṃ hoti, virāgasaññāparicitañca cittaṃ hoti, nirodhasaññāparicitañca cittaṃ hoti, tassa dvinnaṃ phalānaṃ aññataraṃ phalaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – diṭṭheva dhamme aññā, sati vā upādisese anāgāmitā”ti. Navamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu's mind is familiar with what is in accordance with the going forth, and evil, unwholesome states that have arisen do not persist, having overcome his mind; when his mind is familiar with the perception of impermanence, with the perception of not-self, with the perception of foulness, with the perception of drawback; when, having known the world’s evenness and unevenness, his mind is familiar with that perception; when, having known the world’s coming-to-be and passing-away, his mind is familiar with that perception; when, having known the world’s origination and cessation, his mind is familiar with that perception; when his mind is familiar with the perception of abandoning, with the perception of dispassion, with the perception of cessation—one of two fruits is to be expected for him: either final knowledge in this very life or, if there is a residue of clinging, the state of a non-returner.” Ninth.

10. Girimānandasuttaṃ

10. 10. The Discourse to Girimānanda

60. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā girimānando ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

60. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time the Venerable Girimānanda was sick, afflicted, and gravely ill. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Having sat down to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:

“Āyasmā, bhante, girimānando ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno[T 5.0116]. Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā yenāyasmā girimānando tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṃ upādāyā”ti. “Sace kho tvaṃ, ānanda, girimānandassa bhikkhuno dasa saññā bhāseyyāsi, ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati yaṃ girimānandassa bhikkhuno dasa saññā sutvā so ābādho ṭhānaso paṭippassambheyya.

“Venerable sir, the Venerable Girimānanda is sick, afflicted, and gravely ill. It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would approach the Venerable Girimānanda out of compassion.” “Ānanda, if you were to speak of ten perceptions to the bhikkhu Girimānanda, it is possible that upon his hearing them, that illness would immediately subside.

“Katamā dasa? Aniccasaññā[P 5.0109], anattasaññā, asubhasaññā, ādīnavasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā, nirodhasaññā, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññā anabhiratisaññā (ka.), sabbasaṅkhāresu anicchāsaññā, ānāpānassati.

“What ten? The perception of impermanence, the perception of not-self, the perception of foulness, the perception of drawback, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of undesirability in all formations, and mindfulness of breathing.

“Katamā cānanda, aniccasaññā? Idhānanda, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘rūpaṃ aniccaṃ, vedanā aniccā[M 3.0343], saññā aniccā[V 3.0091], saṅkhārā aniccā, viññāṇaṃ anicca’nti. Iti imesu pañcasu upādānakkhandhesu aniccānupassī viharati. Ayaṃ vuccatānanda, aniccasaññā.

“And what, Ānanda, is the perception of impermanence? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu, having gone to the forest, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, reflects thus: ‘Form is impermanent, feeling is impermanent, perception is impermanent, formations are impermanent, consciousness is impermanent.’ Thus he dwells contemplating impermanence in these five aggregates of clinging. This, Ānanda, is called the perception of impermanence.

“Katamā cānanda, anattasaññā? Idhānanda, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘cakkhu anattā, rūpā anattā, sotaṃ anattā, saddā anattā, ghānaṃ anattā, gandhā anattā, jivhā anattā, rasā anattā, kāyā anattā, phoṭṭhabbā anattā, mano anattā, dhammā anattā’ti. Iti imesu chasu ajjhattikabāhiresu āyatanesu anattānupassī viharati. Ayaṃ vuccatānanda, anattasaññā.

“And what, Ānanda, is the perception of not-self? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu, having gone to the forest, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, reflects thus: ‘The eye is not-self, forms are not-self; the ear is not-self, sounds are not-self; the nose is not-self, odors are not-self; the tongue is not-self, tastes are not-self; the body is not-self, tangible objects are not-self; the mind is not-self, mental objects are not-self.’ Thus he dwells contemplating not-self in these six internal and external sense bases. This, Ānanda, is called the perception of not-self.

“Katamā [T 5.0117] cānanda, asubhasaññā? Idhānanda, bhikkhu imameva kāyaṃ uddhaṃ pādatalā adho kesamatthakā tacapariyantaṃ pūraṃ nānāppakārassa asucino paccavekkhati – ‘atthi imasmiṃ kāye kesā lomā nakhā dantā taco maṃsaṃ nhāru aṭṭhi aṭṭhimiñjaṃ vakkaṃ hadayaṃ yakanaṃ kilomakaṃ pihakaṃ papphāsaṃ antaṃ antaguṇaṃ udariyaṃ karīsaṃ pittaṃ semhaṃ pubbo lohitaṃ sedo medo assu vasā kheḷo siṅghāṇikā lasikā mutta’nti. Iti imasmiṃ kāye asubhānupassī viharati. Ayaṃ vuccatānanda, asubhasaññā.

“And what, Ānanda, is the perception of foulness? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu reviews this very body upward from the soles of the feet and downward from the top of the hair, enclosed in skin and full of many kinds of impurity: ‘In this body there are head hairs, body hairs, nails, teeth, skin, flesh, sinews, bones, bone marrow, kidneys, heart, liver, pleura, spleen, lungs, intestines, mesentery, contents of the stomach, feces, bile, phlegm, pus, blood, sweat, fat, tears, grease, saliva, snot, synovial fluid, and urine.’ Thus he dwells contemplating foulness in this body. This, Ānanda, is called the perception of foulness.

“Katamā cānanda, ādīnavasaññā? Idhānanda, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘bahudukkho kho ayaṃ [P 5.0110] kāyo bahuādīnavo? Iti imasmiṃ kāye vividhā ābādhā uppajjanti, seyyathidaṃ – cakkhurogo sotarogo ghānarogo jivhārogo kāyarogo sīsarogo kaṇṇarogo mukharogo dantarogo oṭṭharogo kāso sāso pināso ḍāho ḍaho (sī. syā.) jaro kucchirogo mucchā pakkhandikā sūlā visūcikā kuṭṭhaṃ gaṇḍo kilāso soso apamāro daddu kaṇḍu kacchu nakhasā vitacchikā lohitaṃ pittaṃ lohitapittaṃ (sī.) madhumeho aṃsā piḷakā bhagandalā pittasamuṭṭhānā ābādhā semhasamuṭṭhānā ābādhā vātasamuṭṭhānā ābādhā sannipātikā ābādhā utupariṇāmajā ābādhā visamaparihārajā ābādhā opakkamikā ābādhā kammavipākajā ābādhā sītaṃ uṇhaṃ jighacchā pipāsā uccāro passāvo’ti. Iti [M 3.0344] imasmiṃ kāye ādīnavānupassī viharati. Ayaṃ vuccatānanda, ādīnavasaññā.

“And what, Ānanda, is the perception of danger? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu, having gone to the forest, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, reflects thus: ‘This body has much suffering, much danger. For in this body various diseases arise, such as these: eye disease, ear disease, nose disease, tongue disease, body disease, head disease, external ear disease, mouth disease, tooth disease, lip disease, cough, asthma, nasal catarrh, burning fever, fever, stomach disease, fainting, dysentery, sharp pain, cholera, leprosy, tumors, eczema, consumption, epilepsy, ringworm, itch, scabies, nail-scratch disease, scaly skin disease, disease of blood and bile, diabetes, piles, carbuncles, and fistula; diseases originating from bile, diseases originating from phlegm, diseases originating from wind, diseases from their combination; diseases born of seasonal change, diseases born of uneven care of the body, diseases born of external assaults, and diseases born of kamma-result; as well as cold, heat, hunger, thirst, defecation, and urination.’ Thus he dwells contemplating danger in this body. This, Ānanda, is called the perception of danger.”

“Katamā [T 5.0118] cānanda, pahānasaññā? Idhānanda, bhikkhu uppannaṃ kāmavitakkaṃ nādhivāseti, pajahati[V 3.0092], vinodeti, byantīkaroti, anabhāvaṃ gameti. Uppannaṃ byāpādavitakkaṃ nādhivāseti, pajahati, vinodeti, byantīkaroti, anabhāvaṃ gameti. Uppannaṃ vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ nādhivāseti, pajahati, vinodeti, byantīkaroti, anabhāvaṃ gameti. Uppannuppanne pāpake akusale dhamme nādhivāseti, pajahati, vinodeti, byantīkaroti, anabhāvaṃ gameti. Ayaṃ vuccatānanda, pahānasaññā.

“And what, Ānanda, is the perception of abandoning? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu does not tolerate an arisen thought of sensual desire; he abandons it, dispels it, makes an end of it, and causes it to go to non-existence. He does not tolerate an arisen thought of ill will; he abandons it, dispels it, makes an end of it, and causes it to go to non-existence. He does not tolerate an arisen thought of cruelty; he abandons it, dispels it, makes an end of it, and causes it to go to non-existence. He does not tolerate any evil unwholesome states that have arisen; he abandons them, dispels them, makes an end of them, and causes them to go to non-existence. This, Ānanda, is called the perception of abandoning.”

“Katamā cānanda, virāgasaññā? Idhānanda, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ paṇītaṃ yadidaṃ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhippaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo virāgo nibbāna’nti. Ayaṃ vuccatānanda, virāgasaññā.

“And what, Ānanda, is the perception of dispassion? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu, having gone to the forest, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, reflects thus: ‘This is peaceful, this is sublime, namely, the stilling of all formations, the relinquishing of all substrates of existence, the destruction of craving, dispassion, Nibbāna.’ This, Ānanda, is called the perception of dispassion.”

“Katamā cānanda, nirodhasaññā? Idhānanda, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘etaṃ santaṃ etaṃ [P 5.0111] paṇītaṃ yadidaṃ sabbasaṅkhārasamatho sabbūpadhippaṭinissaggo taṇhākkhayo nirodho nibbāna’nti. Ayaṃ vuccatānanda, nirodhasaññā.

“And what, Ānanda, is the perception of cessation? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu, having gone to the forest, or to the root of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, reflects thus: ‘This is peaceful, this is sublime, namely, the stilling of all formations, the relinquishing of all substrates of existence, the destruction of craving, cessation, Nibbāna.’ This, Ānanda, is called the perception of cessation.”

“Katamā cānanda, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññā? Idhānanda, bhikkhu ye loke upādānā cetaso adhiṭṭhānābhinivesānusayā, te pajahanto viharati anupādiyanto. Ayaṃ vuccatānanda, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññā.

“And what, Ānanda, is the perception of non-delight in the whole world? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu dwells abandoning and not grasping those clingings, mental standpoints, adherences, and underlying tendencies in the world. This, Ānanda, is called the perception of non-delight in the whole world.”

“Katamā cānanda, sabbasaṅkhāresu anicchāsaññā? Idhānanda, bhikkhu sabbasaṅkhāresu aṭṭīyati harāyati jigucchati. Ayaṃ vuccatānanda, sabbasaṅkhāresu [T 5.0119] anicchāsaññā.

“And what, Ānanda, is the perception of undesirability toward all formations? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu is weary of, ashamed of, and disgusted with all formations. This, Ānanda, is called the perception of undesirability toward all formations.”

“Katamā cānanda, ānāpānassati? Idhānanda, bhikkhu araññagato vā rukkhamūlagato vā suññāgāragato vā nisīdati pallaṅkaṃ ābhujitvā ujuṃ kāyaṃ paṇidhāya parimukhaṃ satiṃ upaṭṭhapetvā. So satova assasati satova passasati. Dīghaṃ vā assasanto ‘dīghaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti. Dīghaṃ vā passasanto ‘dīghaṃ passasāmī’ti pajānāti. Rassaṃ vā assasanto ‘rassaṃ assasāmī’ti pajānāti. Rassaṃ vā passasanto ‘rassaṃ [M 3.0345] passasāmī’ti pajānāti. ‘Sabbakāyapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati. ‘Sabbakāyapaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati. ‘Passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati. ‘Passambhayaṃ kāyasaṅkhāraṃ [V 3.0093] passasissāmī’ti sikkhati. ‘Pītipaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati. ‘Pītipaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati. ‘Sukhapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati. ‘Sukhapaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati. ‘Cittasaṅkhārapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati. ‘Cittasaṅkhārapaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati. ‘Passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāraṃ assasissāmī’ti sikkhati. ‘Passambhayaṃ cittasaṅkhāraṃ passasissāmī’ti sikkhati. ‘Cittapaṭisaṃvedī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati. ‘Cittapaṭisaṃvedī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati[P 5.0112]. Abhippamodayaṃ cittaṃ…pe… samādahaṃ cittaṃ…pe… vimocayaṃ cittaṃ…pe… aniccānupassī…pe… virāgānupassī…pe… nirodhānupassī…pe… ‘paṭinissaggānupassī assasissāmī’ti sikkhati. ‘Paṭinissaggānupassī passasissāmī’ti sikkhati. Ayaṃ vuccatānanda, ānāpānassati.

“And what, Ānanda, is mindfulness of breathing? Here, Ānanda, a bhikkhu, having gone to the forest, or to the foot of a tree, or to an empty dwelling, sits down. Having folded his legs crosswise, set his body erect, and established mindfulness before him, ever mindful he breathes in, mindful he breathes out. Breathing in long, he knows: ‘I breathe in long’; or breathing out long, he knows: ‘I breathe out long.’ Breathing in short, he knows: ‘I breathe in short’; or breathing out short, he knows: ‘I breathe out short.’ He trains himself: ‘I will breathe in experiencing the whole body.’ He trains himself: ‘I will breathe out experiencing the whole body.’ He trains himself: ‘I will breathe in calming the bodily formation.’ He trains himself: ‘I will breathe out calming the bodily formation.’ He trains himself: ‘I will breathe in experiencing rapture.’ He trains himself: ‘I will breathe out experiencing rapture.’ He trains himself: ‘I will breathe in experiencing pleasure.’ He trains himself: ‘I will breathe out experiencing pleasure.’ He trains himself: ‘I will breathe in experiencing the mental formation.’ He trains himself: ‘I will breathe out experiencing the mental formation.’ He trains himself: ‘I will breathe in calming the mental formation.’ He trains himself: ‘I will breathe out calming the mental formation.’ He trains himself: ‘I will breathe in experiencing the mind.’ He trains himself: ‘I will breathe out experiencing the mind.’ He trains himself: ‘I will breathe in gladdening the mind.’… He trains himself: ‘I will breathe in concentrating the mind.’… He trains himself: ‘I will breathe in liberating the mind.’… He trains himself: ‘I will breathe in contemplating impermanence.’… He trains himself: ‘I will breathe in contemplating dispassion.’… He trains himself: ‘I will breathe in contemplating cessation.’… He trains himself: ‘I will breathe in contemplating relinquishment.’ He trains himself: ‘I will breathe out contemplating relinquishment.’ This, Ānanda, is called mindfulness of breathing.”

“Sace kho tvaṃ, ānanda, girimānandassa bhikkhuno imā [T 5.0120] dasa saññā bhāseyyāsi, ṭhānaṃ kho panetaṃ vijjati yaṃ girimānandassa bhikkhuno imā dasa saññā sutvā so ābādho ṭhānaso paṭippassambheyyā”ti.

“Indeed, Ānanda, if you were to speak of these ten perceptions to the bhikkhu Girimānanda, it is possible that upon hearing these ten perceptions, his illness would be instantly pacified.”

Atha kho āyasmā ānando bhagavato santike imā dasa saññā uggahetvā yenāyasmā girimānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmato girimānandassa imā dasa saññā abhāsi. Atha kho āyasmato girimānandassa dasa saññā sutvā so ābādho ṭhānaso paṭippassambhi. Vuṭṭhahi cāyasmā girimānando tamhā ābādhā. Tathā pahīno ca panāyasmato girimānandassa so ābādho ahosī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

Then the Venerable Ānanda, having learned these ten perceptions in the Blessed One’s presence, approached the Venerable Girimānanda and spoke these ten perceptions to him. Then, when the Venerable Girimānanda heard these ten perceptions, his affliction subsided on the spot. The Venerable Girimānanda rose up from that affliction, and that affliction of the Venerable Girimānanda was thus abandoned. The tenth.

Sacittavaggo paṭhamo.

The Chapter on One’s Own Mind is the first.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary of this is:

Sacittañca sāriputta, ṭhiti ca samathena ca;

Parihāno ca dve saññā, mūlā pabbajitaṃ girīti.

One’s Own Mind, Sāriputta, Stability, and With Serenity; Decline, two on Perceptions, Roots, the Renunciant, and Giri.

(7) 2. Yamakavaggo

(7) 2. The Chapter on Pairs

1. Avijjāsuttaṃ

1. The Sutta on Ignorance

61. “Purimā[M 3.0346][V 3.0094][P 5.0113], bhikkhave, koṭi na paññāyati avijjāya – ‘ito pubbe avijjā nāhosi, atha pacchā samabhavī’ti. Evañcetaṃ, bhikkhave, vuccati, atha ca pana paññāyati – ‘idappaccayā avijjā’ti.

61. “Bhikkhus, a prior point of ignorance is not discerned, of which it can be said: ‘Before this, ignorance was not; afterwards, it came to be.’ And so this is said, bhikkhus, and yet it is discerned that: ‘Ignorance is conditioned by this.’”

“Avijjampāhaṃ avijjampahaṃ (sī. syā.), bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro avijjāya? ‘Pañca nīvaraṇā’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Pañcapāhaṃ, bhikkhave, nīvaraṇe sāhāre vadāmi[T 5.0121], no anāhāre. Ko cāhāro pañcannaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ? ‘Tīṇi duccaritānī’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Tīṇipāhaṃ, bhikkhave, duccaritāni sāhārāni vadāmi, no anāhārāni. Ko cāhāro tiṇṇaṃ duccaritānaṃ? ‘Indriyaasaṃvaro’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Indriyaasaṃvarampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro indriyaasaṃvarassa? ‘Asatāsampajañña’ntissa vacanīyaṃ. Asatāsampajaññampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro asatāsampajaññassa? ‘Ayonisomanasikāro’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Ayonisomanasikārampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro ayonisomanasikārassa? ‘Assaddhiya’ntissa vacanīyaṃ. Assaddhiyampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro assaddhiyassa? ‘Asaddhammassavana’ntissa vacanīyaṃ. Asaddhammassavanampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro asaddhammassavanassa? ‘Asappurisasaṃsevo’tissa vacanīyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, I say that ignorance is with nutriment, not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for ignorance? ‘The five hindrances,’ it should be said. I say, bhikkhus, that the five hindrances are with nutriment, not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for the five hindrances? ‘The three kinds of misconduct,’ it should be said. I say, bhikkhus, that the three kinds of misconduct are with nutriment, not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for the three kinds of misconduct? ‘Non-restraint of the sense faculties,’ it should be said. I say, bhikkhus, that non-restraint of the sense faculties is with nutriment, not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for non-restraint of the sense faculties? ‘Lack of mindfulness and clear comprehension,’ it should be said. I say, bhikkhus, that lack of mindfulness and clear comprehension is with nutriment, not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for lack of mindfulness and clear comprehension? ‘Injudicious attention,’ it should be said. I say, bhikkhus, that injudicious attention is with nutriment, not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for injudicious attention? ‘Lack of faith,’ it should be said. I say, bhikkhus, that lack of faith is with nutriment, not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for lack of faith? ‘Hearing the false Dhamma,’ it should be said. I say, bhikkhus, that hearing the false Dhamma is with nutriment, not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for hearing the false Dhamma? ‘Association with untrue persons,’ it should be said.”

“Iti kho, bhikkhave, asappurisasaṃsevo paripūro asaddhammassavanaṃ paripūreti, asaddhammassavanaṃ paripūraṃ assaddhiyaṃ paripūreti, assaddhiyaṃ paripūraṃ ayonisomanasikāraṃ paripūreti, ayonisomanasikāro paripūro asatāsampajaññaṃ paripūreti, asatāsampajaññaṃ paripūraṃ indriyaasaṃvaraṃ [P 5.0114] paripūreti, indriyaasaṃvaro paripūro tīṇi duccaritāni paripūreti, tīṇi [V 3.0095] duccaritāni paripūrāni pañca nīvaraṇe paripūrenti, pañca nīvaraṇā paripūrā avijjaṃ paripūrenti. Evametissā avijjāya āhāro hoti, evañca pāripūri.

“Thus, bhikkhus, association with untrue persons, being fulfilled, fulfills hearing the false Dhamma; hearing the false Dhamma, being fulfilled, fulfills lack of faith; lack of faith, being fulfilled, fulfills injudicious attention; injudicious attention, being fulfilled, fulfills lack of mindfulness and clear comprehension; lack of mindfulness and clear comprehension, being fulfilled, fulfills non-restraint of the sense faculties; non-restraint of the sense faculties, being fulfilled, fulfills the three kinds of misconduct; the three kinds of misconduct, being fulfilled, fulfill the five hindrances; the five hindrances, being fulfilled, fulfill ignorance. Thus there is nutriment for this ignorance, and thus there is its fulfillment.”

“Seyyathāpi[M 3.0347], bhikkhave, uparipabbate thullaphusitake [T 5.0122] deve vassante ( ) (galagalāyante) (sī.), (gaḷagaḷāyante) (syā.) taṃ udakaṃ yathāninnaṃ pavattamānaṃ pabbatakandarapadarasākhā paripūreti, pabbatakandarapadarasākhā paripūrā kusobbhe kussubbhe (sī.), kusubbhe (syā.), kusombhe (ka.) a. ni. 3.96 paripūrenti. Kusobbhā paripūrā mahāsobbhe mahāsombhe (ka.) paripūrenti, mahāsobbhā paripūrā kunnadiyo paripūrenti, kunnadiyo paripūrā mahānadiyo paripūrenti, mahānadiyo paripūrā mahāsamuddaṃ sāgaraṃ paripūrenti; evametassa mahāsamuddassa sāgarassa āhāro hoti, evañca pāripūri.

“Suppose, bhikkhus, when it rains with heavy drops on a mountain top, that water, flowing according to the slope, fills the mountain clefts, crevices, and gullies. When the mountain clefts, crevices, and gullies are full, they fill the small pools. When the small pools are full, they fill the large pools. When the large pools are full, they fill the small rivers. When the small rivers are full, they fill the great rivers. When the great rivers are full, they fill the great ocean, the sea. Thus there is nutriment for this great ocean, the sea, and thus there is its fulfillment.

“Evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, asappurisasaṃsevo paripūro asaddhammassavanaṃ paripūreti, asaddhammassavanaṃ paripūraṃ assaddhiyaṃ paripūreti, assaddhiyaṃ paripūraṃ ayonisomanasikāraṃ paripūreti, ayonisomanasikāro paripūro asatāsampajaññaṃ paripūreti, asatāsampajaññaṃ paripūraṃ indriyaasaṃvaraṃ paripūreti, indriyaasaṃvaro paripūro tīṇi duccaritāni paripūreti, tīṇi duccaritāni paripūrāni pañca nīvaraṇe paripūrenti, pañca nīvaraṇā paripūrā avijjaṃ paripūrenti; evametissā avijjāya āhāro hoti, evañca pāripūri.

“So too, bhikkhus, association with untrue persons, being fulfilled, fulfills hearing the false Dhamma; hearing the false Dhamma, being fulfilled, fulfills lack of faith; lack of faith, being fulfilled, fulfills injudicious attention; injudicious attention, being fulfilled, fulfills lack of mindfulness and clear comprehension; lack of mindfulness and clear comprehension, being fulfilled, fulfills non-restraint of the sense faculties; non-restraint of the sense faculties, being fulfilled, fulfills the three kinds of misconduct; the three kinds of misconduct, being fulfilled, fulfill the five hindrances; the five hindrances, being fulfilled, fulfill ignorance. Thus there is nutriment for this ignorance, and thus there is its fulfillment.”

“Vijjāvimuttimpāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro vijjāvimuttiyā? ‘Satta bojjhaṅgā’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Sattapāhaṃ, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅge sāhāre vadāmi, no anāhāre. Ko cāhāro sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ? ‘Cattāro satipaṭṭhānā’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Cattāropāhaṃ, bhikkhave, satipaṭṭhāne sāhāre vadāmi, no anāhāre. Ko cāhāro catunnaṃ satipaṭṭhānānaṃ? ‘Tīṇi sucaritānī’tissa [P 5.0115] vacanīyaṃ. Tīṇipāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sucaritāni sāhārāni vadāmi, no anāhārāni. Ko cāhāro tiṇṇaṃ sucaritānaṃ? ‘Indriyasaṃvaro’tissa [T 5.0123] vacanīyaṃ. Indriyasaṃvarampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro indriyasaṃvarassa? ‘Satisampajañña’ntissa vacanīyaṃ. Satisampajaññampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro satisampajaññassa? ‘Yonisomanasikāro’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Yonisomanasikārampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro yonisomanasikārassa? ‘Saddhā’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Saddhampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro saddhāya[M 3.0348]? ‘Saddhammassavana’ntissa vacanīyaṃ. Saddhammassavanampāhaṃ, bhikkhave[V 3.0096], sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro saddhammassavanassa? ‘Sappurisasaṃsevo’tissa vacanīyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, I declare that knowledge and liberation has a nutriment; it is not without a nutriment. And what is the nutriment for knowledge and liberation? ‘The seven factors of enlightenment,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that the seven factors of enlightenment have a nutriment; they are not without a nutriment. And what is the nutriment for the seven factors of enlightenment? ‘The four establishments of mindfulness,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that the four establishments of mindfulness have a nutriment; they are not without a nutriment. And what is the nutriment for the four establishments of mindfulness? ‘The three kinds of good conduct,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that the three kinds of good conduct have a nutriment; they are not without a nutriment. And what is the nutriment for the three kinds of good conduct? ‘Restraint of the faculties,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that restraint of the faculties has a nutriment; it is not without a nutriment. And what is the nutriment for restraint of the faculties? ‘Mindfulness and clear comprehension,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that mindfulness and clear comprehension has a nutriment; it is not without a nutriment. And what is the nutriment for mindfulness and clear comprehension? ‘Wise attention,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that wise attention has a nutriment; it is not without a nutriment. And what is the nutriment for wise attention? ‘Faith,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that faith has a nutriment; it is not without a nutriment. And what is the nutriment for faith? ‘Hearing the good Dhamma,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that hearing the good Dhamma has a nutriment; it is not without a nutriment. And what is the nutriment for hearing the good Dhamma? ‘Association with good people,’ it should be said.

“Iti kho, bhikkhave, sappurisasaṃsevo paripūro saddhammassavanaṃ paripūreti, saddhammassavanaṃ paripūraṃ saddhaṃ paripūreti, saddhā paripūrā yonisomanasikāraṃ paripūreti, yonisomanasikāro paripūro satisampajaññaṃ paripūreti, satisampajaññaṃ paripūraṃ indriyasaṃvaraṃ paripūreti, indriyasaṃvaro paripūro tīṇi sucaritāni paripūreti, tīṇi sucaritāni paripūrāni cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrenti, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā paripūrā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti, satta bojjhaṅgā paripūrā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrenti; evametissā vijjāvimuttiyā āhāro hoti, evañca pāripūri.

“Thus, bhikkhus, association with good people, being fulfilled, fulfills hearing the good Dhamma; hearing the good Dhamma, being fulfilled, fulfills faith; faith, being fulfilled, fulfills wise attention; wise attention, being fulfilled, fulfills mindfulness and clear comprehension; mindfulness and clear comprehension, being fulfilled, fulfills restraint of the faculties; restraint of the faculties, being fulfilled, fulfills the three kinds of good conduct; the three kinds of good conduct, being fulfilled, fulfill the four establishments of mindfulness; the four establishments of mindfulness, being fulfilled, fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment; the seven factors of enlightenment, being fulfilled, fulfill knowledge and liberation. Thus there is nutriment for this knowledge and liberation, and thus there is its fulfillment.”

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, uparipabbate thullaphusitake deve vassante taṃ udakaṃ yathāninnaṃ pavattamānaṃ pabbatakandarapadarasākhā paripūreti, pabbatakandarapadarasākhā paripūrā kusobbhe paripūrenti, kusobbhā paripūrā mahāsobbhe [T 5.0124] paripūrenti, mahāsobbhā paripūrā kunnadiyo paripūrenti, kunnadiyo paripūrā mahānadiyo paripūrenti, mahānadiyo paripūrā mahāsamuddaṃ [P 5.0116] sāgaraṃ paripūrenti; evametassa mahāsamuddassa sāgarassa āhāro hoti, evañca pāripūri.

“Just as, bhikkhus, when it rains in heavy drops on a mountaintop, that water, flowing down, fills the mountain clefts, crevices, and gullies. When these are full, they fill the small pools. When the small pools are full, they fill the large pools. When the large pools are full, they fill the small rivers. When the small rivers are full, they fill the great rivers. When the great rivers are full, they fill the great ocean, the sea. Thus there is nutriment for this great ocean, the sea, and thus there is its fulfillment.”

“Evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sappurisasaṃsevo paripūro saddhammassavanaṃ paripūreti, saddhammassavanaṃ paripūraṃ saddhaṃ paripūreti, saddhā paripūrā yonisomanasikāraṃ paripūreti, yonisomanasikāro paripūro satisampajaññaṃ paripūreti, satisampajaññaṃ paripūraṃ indriyasaṃvaraṃ paripūreti, indriyasaṃvaro paripūro tīṇi sucaritāni paripūreti, tīṇi sucaritāni paripūrāni cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrenti, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā paripūrā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti, satta bojjhaṅgā paripūrā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrenti; evametissā vijjāvimuttiyā āhāro hoti, evañca pāripūrī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“In this very same way, bhikkhus, association with good people, being fulfilled, fulfills hearing the good Dhamma; hearing the good Dhamma, being fulfilled, fulfills faith; faith, being fulfilled, fulfills wise attention; wise attention, being fulfilled, fulfills mindfulness and clear comprehension; mindfulness and clear comprehension, being fulfilled, fulfills restraint of the faculties; restraint of the faculties, being fulfilled, fulfills the three kinds of good conduct; the three kinds of good conduct, being fulfilled, fulfill the four establishments of mindfulness; the four establishments of mindfulness, being fulfilled, fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment; the seven factors of enlightenment, being fulfilled, fulfill knowledge and liberation. Thus there is nutriment for this knowledge and liberation, and thus there is its fulfillment.” The first.

2. Taṇhāsuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Craving

62. “Purimā, bhikkhave, koṭi na paññāyati bhavataṇhāya – ‘ito pubbe bhavataṇhā nāhosi[V 3.0097], atha pacchā samabhavī’ti. Evañcetaṃ, bhikkhave, vuccati, atha ca pana paññāyati – ‘idappaccayā bhavataṇhā’ti.

62. “Bhikkhus, a first point of craving for existence is not discerned, such that one could say: ‘Before this, craving for existence was not; it arose afterwards.’ And though this is said, bhikkhus, it is nevertheless discerned: ‘Craving for existence is conditioned by this.’”

“Bhavataṇhāmpāhaṃ[M 3.0349], bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro bhavataṇhāya? ‘Avijjā’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Avijjampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro avijjāya? ‘Pañca nīvaraṇā’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Pañca nīvaraṇepāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāre vadāmi, no anāhāre. Ko cāhāro pañcannaṃ nīvaraṇānaṃ? ‘Tīṇi duccaritānī’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Tīṇipāhaṃ, bhikkhave[T 5.0125], duccaritāni sāhārāni vadāmi, no anāhārāni. Ko cāhāro tiṇṇannaṃ duccaritānaṃ? ‘Indriyaasaṃvaro’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Indriyaasaṃvarampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ[P 5.0117]. Ko cāhāro indriyaasaṃvarassa? ‘Asatāsampajañña’ntissa vacanīyaṃ. Asatāsampajaññampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro asatā sampajaññassa? ‘Ayonisomanasikāro’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Ayonisomanasikārampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro ayonisomanasikārassa? ‘Assaddhiya’ntissa vacanīyaṃ. Assaddhiyampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro assaddhiyassa? ‘Assaddhammassavana’ntissa vacanīyaṃ. Assaddhammassavanampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro assaddhammassavanassa? ‘Asappurisasaṃsevo’tissa vacanīyaṃ.

“I declare, bhikkhus, that craving for existence has a nutriment; it is not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for craving for existence? ‘Ignorance,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that ignorance has a nutriment; it is not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for ignorance? ‘The five hindrances,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that the five hindrances have a nutriment; they are not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for the five hindrances? ‘The three kinds of misconduct,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that the three kinds of misconduct have a nutriment; they are not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for the three kinds of misconduct? ‘Non-restraint of the sense faculties,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that non-restraint of the sense faculties has a nutriment; it is not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for non-restraint of the sense faculties? ‘Lack of mindfulness and clear comprehension,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that lack of mindfulness and clear comprehension has a nutriment; it is not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for lack of mindfulness and clear comprehension? ‘Unwise attention,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that unwise attention has a nutriment; it is not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for unwise attention? ‘Lack of faith,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that lack of faith has a nutriment; it is not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for lack of faith? ‘Hearing the untrue Dhamma,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that hearing the untrue Dhamma has a nutriment; it is not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for hearing the untrue Dhamma? ‘Association with untrue persons,’ it should be said.

“Iti kho, bhikkhave, asappurisasaṃsevo paripūro assaddhammassavanaṃ paripūreti, assaddhammassavanaṃ paripūraṃ assaddhiyaṃ paripūreti, assaddhiyaṃ paripūraṃ ayonisomanasikāraṃ paripūreti, ayonisomanasikāro paripūro asatāsampajaññaṃ paripūreti, asatāsampajaññaṃ paripūraṃ indriyaasaṃvaraṃ paripūreti, indriyaasaṃvaro paripūro tīṇi duccaritāni paripūreti, tīṇi duccaritāni paripūrāni pañca nīvaraṇe paripūrenti, pañca nīvaraṇā paripūrā avijjaṃ paripūrenti, avijjā paripūrā bhavataṇhaṃ paripūreti; evametissā bhavataṇhāya āhāro hoti, evañca pāripūri.

“Thus, bhikkhus, association with untrue persons, being fulfilled, fulfills hearing the untrue Dhamma; hearing the untrue Dhamma, being fulfilled, fulfills lack of faith; lack of faith, being fulfilled, fulfills unwise attention; unwise attention, being fulfilled, fulfills lack of mindfulness and clear comprehension; lack of mindfulness and clear comprehension, being fulfilled, fulfills non-restraint of the sense faculties; non-restraint of the sense faculties, being fulfilled, fulfills the three kinds of misconduct; the three kinds of misconduct, being fulfilled, fulfill the five hindrances; the five hindrances, being fulfilled, fulfill ignorance; ignorance, being fulfilled, fulfills craving for existence. In this way there is nutriment for this craving for existence, and in this way it is fulfilled.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, uparipabbate thullaphusitake deve vassante taṃ udakaṃ yathāninnaṃ [T 5.0126] pavattamānaṃ pabbatakandarapadarasākhā paripūreti, pabbatakandarapadarasākhā paripūrā kusobbhe paripūrenti[V 3.0098], kusobbhā paripūrā mahāsobbhe paripūrenti, mahāsobbhā paripūrā kunnadiyo paripūrenti, kunnadiyo paripūrā mahānadiyo paripūrenti, mahānadiyo paripūrā mahāsamuddaṃ [M 3.0350] sāgaraṃ paripūrenti; evametassa mahāsamuddassa sāgarassa āhāro hoti, evañca pāripūri.

“Just as, bhikkhus, when a cloud with heavy drops rains upon a mountain top, the water, flowing down the slope, fills the mountain clefts, fissures, and gullies. When the mountain clefts, fissures, and gullies are full, they fill the small pools; when the small pools are full, they fill the large pools; when the large pools are full, they fill the small rivers; when the small rivers are full, they fill the great rivers; and when the great rivers are full, they fill the great ocean, the sea. Thus there is nutriment for this great ocean, the sea, and in this way it comes to fulfillment.

“Evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, asappurisasaṃsevo paripūro assaddhammassavanaṃ paripūreti, assaddhammassavanaṃ paripūraṃ assaddhiyaṃ [P 5.0118] paripūreti, assaddhiyaṃ paripūraṃ ayonisomanasikāraṃ paripūreti, ayonisomanasikāro paripūro asatāsampajaññaṃ paripūreti, asatāsampajaññaṃ paripūraṃ indriyaasaṃvaraṃ paripūreti, indriyaasaṃvaro paripūro tīṇi duccaritāni paripūreti, tīṇi duccaritāni paripūrāni pañca nīvaraṇe paripūrenti, pañca nīvaraṇā paripūrā avijjaṃ paripūrenti, avijjā paripūrā bhavataṇhaṃ paripūreti; evametissā bhavataṇhāya āhāro hoti, evañca pāripūri.

“In the very same way, bhikkhus, association with untrue persons, being fulfilled, fulfills hearing the untrue Dhamma; hearing the untrue Dhamma, being fulfilled, fulfills lack of faith; lack of faith, being fulfilled, fulfills unwise attention; unwise attention, being fulfilled, fulfills lack of mindfulness and clear comprehension; lack of mindfulness and clear comprehension, being fulfilled, fulfills non-restraint of the sense faculties; non-restraint of the sense faculties, being fulfilled, fulfills the three kinds of misconduct; the three kinds of misconduct, being fulfilled, fulfill the five hindrances; the five hindrances, being fulfilled, fulfill ignorance; ignorance, being fulfilled, fulfills craving for existence. Thus there is nutriment for this craving for existence, and in this way it is fulfilled.

“Vijjāvimuttimpāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro vijjāvimuttiyā? ‘Satta bojjhaṅgā’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Sattapāhaṃ, bhikkhave, bojjhaṅge sāhāre vadāmi, no anāhāre. Ko cāhāro sattannaṃ bojjhaṅgānaṃ? ‘Cattāro satipaṭṭhānā’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Cattāropāhaṃ, bhikkhave, satipaṭṭhāne sāhāre vadāmi, no anāhāre. Ko cāhāro catunnaṃ satipaṭṭhānānaṃ? ‘Tīṇi sucaritānī’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Tīṇipāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sucaritāni sāhārāni vadāmi, no anāhārāni. Ko cāhāro tiṇṇannaṃ [T 5.0127] sucaritānaṃ? ‘Indriyasaṃvaro’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Indriyasaṃvarampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro indriyasaṃvarassa? ‘Satisampajañña’ntissa vacanīyaṃ. Satisampajaññampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro satisampajaññassa? ‘Yonisomanasikāro’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Yonisomanasikārampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro yonisomanasikārassa? ‘Saddhā’tissa vacanīyaṃ. Saddhampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro saddhāya? ‘Saddhammassavana’ntissa vacanīyaṃ. Saddhammassavanampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sāhāraṃ vadāmi, no anāhāraṃ. Ko cāhāro saddhammassavanassa? ‘Sappurisasaṃsevo’tissa vacanīyaṃ.

“I declare, bhikkhus, that true knowledge and liberation have a nutriment; they are not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for true knowledge and liberation? ‘The seven factors of enlightenment,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that the seven factors of enlightenment have a nutriment; they are not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for the seven factors of enlightenment? ‘The four establishments of mindfulness,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that the four establishments of mindfulness have a nutriment; they are not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for the four establishments of mindfulness? ‘The three kinds of good conduct,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that the three kinds of good conduct have a nutriment; they are not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for the three kinds of good conduct? ‘Restraint of the sense faculties,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that restraint of the sense faculties has a nutriment; it is not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for restraint of the sense faculties? ‘Mindfulness and clear comprehension,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that mindfulness and clear comprehension have a nutriment; it is not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for mindfulness and clear comprehension? ‘Wise attention,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that wise attention has a nutriment; it is not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for wise attention? ‘Faith,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that faith has a nutriment; it is not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for faith? ‘Hearing the true Dhamma,’ it should be said. I declare, bhikkhus, that hearing the true Dhamma has a nutriment; it is not without nutriment. And what is the nutriment for hearing the true Dhamma? ‘Association with true persons,’ it should be said.

“Iti kho, bhikkhave, sappurisasaṃsevo paripūro saddhammassavanaṃ paripūreti, saddhammassavanaṃ [V 3.0099] paripūraṃ saddhaṃ paripūreti, saddhā paripūrā yonisomanasikāraṃ paripūreti, yonisomanasikāro paripūro satisampajaññaṃ paripūreti, satisampajaññaṃ [M 3.0351] paripūraṃ indriyasaṃvaraṃ paripūreti, indriyasaṃvaro paripūro tīṇi sucaritāni paripūreti, tīṇi sucaritāni paripūrāni cattāro satipaṭṭhāne paripūrenti, cattāro satipaṭṭhānā paripūrā satta bojjhaṅge paripūrenti[P 5.0119], satta bojjhaṅgā paripūrā vijjāvimuttiṃ paripūrenti; evametissā vijjāvimuttiyā āhāro hoti, evañca pāripūri.

“Thus, bhikkhus, association with true persons, being fulfilled, fulfills hearing the true Dhamma; hearing the true Dhamma, being fulfilled, fulfills faith; faith, being fulfilled, fulfills wise attention; wise attention, being fulfilled, fulfills mindfulness and clear comprehension; mindfulness and clear comprehension, being fulfilled, fulfills restraint of the sense faculties; restraint of the sense faculties, being fulfilled, fulfills the three kinds of good conduct; the three kinds of good conduct, being fulfilled, fulfill the four establishments of mindfulness; the four establishments of mindfulness, being fulfilled, fulfill the seven factors of enlightenment; the seven factors of enlightenment, being fulfilled, fulfill knowledge and liberation. Thus, for this knowledge and liberation, there is nutriment, and thus there is fulfillment.”

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, uparipabbate thullaphusitake deve vassante taṃ udakaṃ yathāninnaṃ pavattamānaṃ…pe… evametassa mahāsamuddassa sāgarassa āhāro hoti, evañca pāripūri. Evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, sappurisasaṃsevo paripūro saddhammassavanaṃ paripūreti…pe… [T 5.0128] evametissā vijjāvimuttiyā āhāro hoti, evañca pāripūrī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Just as, bhikkhus, when it rains with heavy drops on a mountaintop, the water, flowing down along the slope … thus there is nutriment for this great ocean, and in this way it comes to fulfillment. So too, bhikkhus, association with true persons, being fulfilled, fulfills hearing the true Dhamma … thus there is nutriment for this knowledge and liberation, and in this way it comes to fulfillment.” Second.

3. Niṭṭhaṅgatasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Finality

63. “Ye keci, bhikkhave, mayi niṭṭhaṃ gatā sabbe te diṭṭhisampannā. Tesaṃ diṭṭhisampannānaṃ pañcannaṃ idha niṭṭhā, pañcannaṃ idha vihāya niṭṭhā. Katamesaṃ pañcannaṃ idha niṭṭhā? Sattakkhattuparamassa[P 5.0120], kolaṃkolassa, ekabījissa, sakadāgāmissa, yo ca diṭṭheva dhamme arahā – imesaṃ pañcannaṃ idha niṭṭhā. Katamesaṃ pañcannaṃ idha vihāya niṭṭhā? Antarāparinibbāyissa, upahaccaparinibbāyissa, asaṅkhāraparinibbāyissa, sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyissa, uddhaṃsotassa akaniṭṭhagāmino – imesaṃ pañcannaṃ idha vihāya niṭṭhā. Ye keci, bhikkhave, mayi niṭṭhaṃ gatā, sabbe te diṭṭhisampannā. Tesaṃ diṭṭhisampannānaṃ imesaṃ pañcannaṃ idha niṭṭhā, imesaṃ pañcannaṃ idha vihāya niṭṭhā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

63. “Bhikkhus, whoever has reached the end in me, all of them are accomplished in view. Of those accomplished in view, for five there is finality here, and for five there is finality after passing away from here. For which five is there finality here? The seven-times-at-most, the family-to-family, the one-seeder, the once-returner, and the one who is an Arahant in this very life—for these five, there is finality here. For which five is there finality after passing away from here?
