The one who attains final Nibbāna in the interval, the one who attains final Nibbāna upon landing, the one who attains final Nibbāna without exertion, the one who attains final Nibbāna with exertion, and the one who is bound upstream, heading for the Akaniṭṭha realm—for these five, there is finality after passing away from here. Bhikkhus, whoever has reached the end in me, all of them are accomplished in view. Of those accomplished in view, for these five there is finality here, and for these five there is finality after passing away from here.” The third.

4. Aveccappasannasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Unwavering Confidence

64. “Ye keci, bhikkhave, mayi aveccappasannā, sabbe te sotāpannā. Tesaṃ sotāpannānaṃ pañcannaṃ idha niṭṭhā, pañcannaṃ idha vihāya niṭṭhā. Katamesaṃ pañcannaṃ idha niṭṭhā? Sattakkhattuparamassa, kolaṃkolassa, ekabījissa, sakadāgāmissa, yo ca diṭṭheva dhamme arahā [V 3.0100] – imesaṃ pañcannaṃ idha niṭṭhā. Katamesaṃ pañcannaṃ idha vihāya niṭṭhā? Antarāparinibbāyissa, upahaccaparinibbāyissa, asaṅkhāraparinibbāyissa, sasaṅkhāraparinibbāyissa, uddhaṃsotassa akaniṭṭhagāmino – imesaṃ pañcannaṃ idha vihāya niṭṭhā. Ye keci, bhikkhave[T 5.0129], mayi aveccappasannā sabbe te sotāpannā. Tesaṃ [M 3.0352] sotāpannānaṃ imesaṃ pañcannaṃ idha niṭṭhā, imesaṃ pañcannaṃ idha vihāya niṭṭhā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

64. “Bhikkhus, whoever has unwavering confidence in me, all are stream-enterers. Among those stream-enterers, for five there is finality here, and for five there is finality after passing away from here. For which five is there finality here? The seven-times-at-most, the family-to-family, the one-seeder, the once-returner, and one who is an arahant in this very life—for these five, there is finality here. For which five is there finality after passing away from here? The one who attains final Nibbāna in the interval, the one who attains final Nibbāna upon landing, the one who attains final Nibbāna without exertion, the one who attains final Nibbāna with exertion, and the one who is bound upstream, heading for the Akaniṭṭha realm—for these five, there is finality after passing away from here. Bhikkhus, whoever has unwavering confidence in me, all are stream-enterers. Among those stream-enterers, for these five there is finality here, and for these five there is finality after passing away from here.” The fourth.

5. Paṭhamasukhasuttaṃ

5. The First Discourse on Happiness

65. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā sāriputto magadhesu viharati nālakagāmake. Atha kho sāmaṇḍakāni paribbājako yenāyasmā [P 5.0121] sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho sāmaṇḍakāni paribbājako āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ etadavoca –

65. On one occasion the Venerable Sāriputta was dwelling among the Magadhans in the small village of Nālaka. Then the wanderer Sāmaṇḍakāni approached the Venerable Sāriputta and exchanged joyful greetings with him. When this joyful and memorable talk was concluded, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the wanderer Sāmaṇḍakāni said this to the Venerable Sāriputta:

“Kiṃ nu kho, āvuso sāriputta, sukhaṃ, kiṃ dukkha”nti? “Abhinibbatti kho, āvuso[T 5.0130], dukkhā, anabhinibbatti sukhā. Abhinibbattiyā, āvuso, sati idaṃ dukkhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – sītaṃ uṇhaṃ jighacchā pipāsā uccāro passāvo aggisamphasso daṇḍasamphasso satthasamphasso ñātīpi mittāpi saṅgamma samāgamma rosenti. Abhinibbattiyā, āvuso, sati idaṃ dukkhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ. Anabhinibbattiyā, āvuso, sati idaṃ sukhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – na sītaṃ na uṇhaṃ na jighacchā na pipāsā na uccāro na passāvo na aggisamphasso na daṇḍasamphasso na satthasamphasso ñātīpi mittāpi saṅgamma samāgamma na rosenti. Anabhinibbattiyā, āvuso, sati idaṃ sukhaṃ pāṭikaṅkha”nti. Pañcamaṃ.

“What, friend Sāriputta, is happiness, and what is suffering?” “Rebirth, friend, is suffering; non-rebirth is happiness. When there is rebirth, friend, this suffering is to be expected: cold, heat, hunger, thirst, excrement, urine, contact with fire, contact with a stick, contact with a weapon; and relatives and friends, having met and come together, vex. When there is rebirth, friend, this suffering is to be expected. When there is non-rebirth, friend, this happiness is to be expected: no cold, no heat, no hunger, no thirst, no excrement, no urine, no contact with fire, no contact with a stick, no contact with a weapon; and relatives and friends, having met and come together, do not vex. When there is non-rebirth, friend, this happiness is to be expected.” The fifth.

6. Dutiyasukhasuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse on Happiness

66. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā sāriputto magadhesu viharati nālakagāmake. Atha kho sāmaṇḍakāni paribbājako yenāyasmā sāriputto tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā sāriputtena saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho sāmaṇḍakāni paribbājako āyasmantaṃ [P 5.0122] sāriputtaṃ etadavoca –

66. On one occasion the Venerable Sāriputta was dwelling among the Magadhans in the small village of Nālaka. Then the wanderer Sāmaṇḍakāni approached the Venerable Sāriputta and exchanged joyful greetings with him. When this joyful and memorable talk was concluded, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the wanderer Sāmaṇḍakāni said this to the Venerable Sāriputta:

“Kiṃ [V 3.0101] nu kho, āvuso, sāriputta, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye sukhaṃ, kiṃ dukkha”nti? “Anabhirati kho, āvuso, imasmiṃ dhammavinaye dukkhā, abhirati sukhā. Anabhiratiyā, āvuso, sati idaṃ dukkhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – gacchantopi sukhaṃ sātaṃ [M 3.0353] nādhigacchati, ṭhitopi… nisinnopi… sayānopi… gāmagatopi… araññagatopi… rukkhamūlagatopi… suññāgāragatopi… abbhokāsagatopi… bhikkhumajjhagatopi sukhaṃ sātaṃ nādhigacchati. Anabhiratiyā, āvuso, sati [T 5.0131] idaṃ dukkhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ.

“What, friend Sāriputta, is happiness in this Dhamma and Discipline, and what is suffering?” “Friend, non-delight is suffering in this Dhamma and Discipline; delight is happiness. When there is non-delight, friend, this suffering is to be expected: one does not obtain happiness and mental pleasure when walking, standing, sitting, or lying down; when one has gone to a village, to the forest, to the foot of a tree, to an empty dwelling, to the open air, or into the midst of the bhikkhus, one does not obtain happiness and mental pleasure. When there is non-delight, friend, this suffering is to be expected.

“Abhiratiyā, āvuso, sati idaṃ sukhaṃ pāṭikaṅkhaṃ – gacchantopi sukhaṃ sātaṃ adhigacchati, ṭhitopi… nisinnopi… sayānopi… gāmagatopi… araññagatopi… rukkhamūlagatopi… suññāgāragatopi… abbhokāsagatopi… bhikkhumajjhagatopi sukhaṃ sātaṃ adhigacchati. Abhiratiyā, āvuso, sati idaṃ sukhaṃ pāṭikaṅkha”nti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“When there is delight, friend, this happiness is to be expected: one obtains happiness and mental pleasure when walking, standing, sitting, or lying down; when one has gone to a village, to the forest, to the foot of a tree, to an empty dwelling, to the open air, or into the midst of the bhikkhus, one obtains happiness and mental pleasure. When there is delight, friend, this happiness is to be expected.” Sixth.

7. Paṭhamanaḷakapānasuttaṃ

7. The First Discourse at Naḷakapāna

67. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā kosalesu cārikaṃ caramāno mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṃ yena naḷakapānaṃ nāma kosalānaṃ nigamo tadavasari. Tatra sudaṃ bhagavā naḷakapāne viharati palāsavane. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā tadahuposathe bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto nisinno hoti. Atha kho bhagavā bahudeva rattiṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā tuṇhībhūtaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ anuviloketvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ āmantesi –

67. On one occasion the Blessed One was wandering on tour in the Kosalan country with a large Saṅgha of bhikkhus when he arrived at a Kosalan market town named Naḷakapāna. There the Blessed One was dwelling in the Palāsa Grove. Now on that occasion, it being the Uposatha day, the Blessed One was sitting surrounded by the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. Then, after instructing, urging, rousing, and delighting the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk for a great part of the night, the Blessed One surveyed the utterly silent Saṅgha of bhikkhus and addressed the Venerable Sāriputta:

“Vigatathinamiddho vigatathīnamiddho (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) kho, sāriputta, bhikkhusaṅgho. Paṭibhātu taṃ, sāriputta[P 5.0123], bhikkhūnaṃ dhammī kathā. Piṭṭhi me āgilāyati; tamahaṃ āyamissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavato paccassosi.

“Sāriputta, this Saṅgha of bhikkhus is free from sloth and torpor. Let a Dhamma talk for the bhikkhus occur to you, Sāriputta. My back is aching; I will stretch it.” “Very well, venerable sir,” the Venerable Sāriputta replied to the Blessed One.

Atha kho bhagavā catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññāpetvā dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṃ kappesi pāde pādaṃ accādhāya sato sampajāno uṭṭhānasaññaṃ manasi karitvā. Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto [V 3.0102] bhikkhū āmantesi – “āvuso bhikkhave”ti. “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca –

Then the Blessed One, having folded his outer robe into four, lay down on his right side in the lion’s posture, with one foot placed slightly upon the other, mindful and clearly comprehending, having established in his mind the perception of rising. Then the Venerable Sāriputta addressed the bhikkhus: “Friends, bhikkhus.” “Friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Sāriputta. The Venerable Sāriputta said this:

“Yassa [M 3.0354] kassaci, āvuso, saddhā natthi kusalesu dhammesu, hirī hiri (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) natthi… ottappaṃ natthi [T 5.0132]… vīriyaṃ viriyaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) natthi… paññā natthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no vuddhi. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, kāḷapakkhe candassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāyateva vaṇṇena hāyati maṇḍalena hāyati ābhāya hāyati ārohapariṇāhena; evamevaṃ kho, āvuso, yassa kassaci saddhā natthi kusalesu dhammesu, hirī natthi… ottappaṃ natthi… vīriyaṃ natthi… paññā natthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no vuddhi.

“Friends, for anyone who lacks faith in wholesome qualities, who lacks moral shame… who lacks moral dread… who lacks energy… who lacks wisdom in wholesome qualities, as night and day pass, only decline in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not growth. Just as, friends, during the dark fortnight, as night and day pass, the moon wanes in its beauty, wanes in its circumference, wanes in its radiance, and wanes in its height and breadth; so too, for anyone who lacks faith in wholesome qualities, who lacks moral shame… who lacks moral dread… who lacks energy… who lacks wisdom in wholesome qualities, as night and day pass, only decline in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not growth.

“Assaddho purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, parihānametaṃ; ‘ahiriko purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, parihānametaṃ; ‘anottappī purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, parihānametaṃ; ‘kusīto purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, parihānametaṃ; ‘duppañño purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, parihānametaṃ; ‘kodhano purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, parihānametaṃ; ‘upanāhī purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, parihānametaṃ; ‘pāpiccho purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, parihānametaṃ; ‘pāpamitto purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, parihānametaṃ; ‘micchādiṭṭhiko purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, parihānametaṃ.

“Friends, ‘a faithless person’—this is decline. ‘A shameless person’—this is decline. ‘A person with no moral dread’—this is decline. ‘A lazy person’—this is decline. ‘An unwise person’—this is decline. ‘An angry person’—this is decline. ‘A hostile person’—this is decline. ‘A person of evil wishes’—this is decline. ‘A person with bad friends’—this is decline. ‘A person of wrong view’—this is decline.

“Yassa kassaci, āvuso, saddhā atthi kusalesu dhammesu, hirī atthi… ottappaṃ atthi… paññā [P 5.0124] atthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no parihāni. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, juṇhapakkhe candassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vaḍḍhateva vaṇṇena [T 5.0133] vaḍḍhati maṇḍalena vaḍḍhati ābhāya vaḍḍhati ārohapariṇāhena; evamevaṃ kho, āvuso, yassa kassaci saddhā atthi kusalesu dhammesu, hirī atthi… ottappaṃ atthi… vīriyaṃ atthi… paññā atthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no parihāni.

“Friends, for anyone who has faith in wholesome qualities, who has moral shame… who has moral dread… who has energy… who has wisdom in wholesome qualities, as night and day pass, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline. Just as, friends, during the bright fortnight, as night and day pass, the moon waxes in its beauty, waxes in its circumference, waxes in its radiance, and waxes in its height and breadth; so too, for anyone who has faith in wholesome qualities, who has moral shame… who has moral dread… who has energy… who has wisdom in wholesome qualities, as night and day pass, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline.”

“‘Saddho [V 3.0103][M 3.0355] purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, aparihānametaṃ; ‘hirīmā purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, aparihānametaṃ; ‘ottappī purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, aparihānametaṃ; ‘āraddhavīriyo purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, aparihānametaṃ; ‘paññavā purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, aparihānametaṃ; ‘akkodhano purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, aparihānametaṃ; ‘anupanāhī purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, aparihānametaṃ; ‘appiccho purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, aparihānametaṃ; ‘kalyāṇamitto purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, aparihānametaṃ; ‘sammādiṭṭhiko purisapuggalo’ti, āvuso, aparihānameta”nti.

“Friends, ‘a person who is faithful’—this is a state of non-decline. ‘A person who has moral shame’—this is a state of non-decline. ‘A person who has moral dread’—this is a state of non-decline. ‘A person whose energy is aroused’—this is a state of non-decline. ‘A person who is wise’—this is a state of non-decline. ‘A person who is not given to anger’—this is a state of non-decline. ‘A person who does not bear grudges’—this is a state of non-decline. ‘A person of few wishes’—this is a state of non-decline. ‘A person who has good friends’—this is a state of non-decline. ‘A person who has right view’—this is a state of non-decline.”

Atha kho bhagavā paccuṭṭhāya āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ āmantesi – “sādhu sādhu, sāriputta! Yassa kassaci, sāriputta, saddhā natthi kusalesu dhammesu, hirī natthi… ottappaṃ natthi… vīriyaṃ natthi… paññā natthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no vuddhi. Seyyathāpi, sāriputta, kāḷapakkhe candassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāyateva vaṇṇena hāyati maṇḍalena hāyati ābhāya hāyati ārohapariṇāhena; evamevaṃ kho, sāriputta, yassa kassaci saddhā natthi kusalesu [T 5.0134] dhammesu…pe… paññā natthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā [P 5.0125]…pe… no vuddhi.

Then the Blessed One, having risen early, addressed the Venerable Sāriputta: “Good, good, Sāriputta! For anyone, Sāriputta, who has no faith in wholesome qualities, has no moral shame… has no moral dread… has no energy… has no wisdom in wholesome qualities, for them, as night or day comes, only decline in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not growth. Just as, Sāriputta, for the moon in the waning fortnight, as night or day comes, it wanes in beauty, wanes in circumference, wanes in radiance, wanes in height and breadth; even so, Sāriputta, for anyone who has no faith in wholesome qualities… has no wisdom in wholesome qualities, for them, as night or day comes… not growth.”

“‘Assaddho purisapuggalo’ti, sāriputta, parihānametaṃ; ahiriko… anottappī… kusīto… duppañño… kodhano… upanāhī… pāpiccho… pāpamitto… ‘micchādiṭṭhiko purisapuggalo’ti, sāriputta, parihānametaṃ.

“Sāriputta, ‘a person who is faithless’—this is a state of decline. ‘A person who is shameless’… ‘a person who has no moral dread’… ‘a person who is lazy’… ‘a person of little wisdom’… ‘a person who is given to anger’… ‘a person who bears grudges’… ‘a person of evil wishes’… ‘a person who has bad friends’… ‘a person who has wrong view’—this is a state of decline.

“Yassa kassaci, sāriputta, saddhā atthi kusalesu dhammesu, hirī atthi… ottappaṃ atthi… vīriyaṃ atthi… paññā atthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no parihāni. Seyyathāpi, sāriputta, juṇhapakkhe candassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vaḍḍhateva vaṇṇena vaḍḍhati maṇḍalena vaḍḍhati ābhāya vaḍḍhati ārohapariṇāhena; evamevaṃ kho, sāriputta, yassa kassaci saddhā atthi kusalesu dhammesu, hirī atthi… ottappaṃ atthi… vīriyaṃ atthi… paññā atthi kusalesu [V 3.0104] dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no parihāni.

“Sāriputta, for anyone who has faith in wholesome qualities, has moral shame… has moral dread… has energy… has wisdom in wholesome qualities, for them, as night or day comes, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline. Just as, Sāriputta, for the moon in the waxing fortnight, as night or day comes, it waxes in beauty, waxes in circumference, waxes in radiance, waxes in height and breadth; even so, Sāriputta, for anyone who has faith in wholesome qualities, has moral shame… has moral dread… has energy… has wisdom in wholesome qualities, for them, as night or day comes, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline.”

“‘Saddho [M 3.0356] purisapuggalo’ti, sāriputta, aparihānametaṃ; hirīmā… ottappī… āraddhavīriyo… paññavā… akkodhano… anupanāhī… appiccho… kalyāṇamitto… ‘sammādiṭṭhiko purisapuggalo’ti, sāriputta, aparihānameta”nti. Sattamaṃ.

“Sāriputta, ‘a person who is faithful’—this is a state of non-decline. ‘A person who has moral shame’… ‘a person who has moral dread’… ‘a person whose energy is aroused’… ‘a person who is wise’… ‘a person who is not given to anger’… ‘a person who does not bear grudges’… ‘a person of few wishes’… ‘a person who has good friends’… ‘a person who has right view’—this is a state of non-decline.” The Seventh Sutta.

8. Dutiyanaḷakapānasuttaṃ

8. The Second Discourse at Naḷakapāna

68. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā naḷakapāne viharati palāsavane. Tena kho pana samayena bhagavā tadahuposathe bhikkhusaṅghaparivuto nisinno hoti. Atha kho bhagavā bahudeva rattiṃ bhikkhūnaṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā [T 5.0135] samuttejetvā sampahaṃsetvā tuṇhībhūtaṃ tuṇhībhūtaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ anuviloketvā āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ āmantesi –

68. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Naḷakapāna in the Palāsa Grove. On that occasion, it being the Uposatha day, the Blessed One was seated surrounded by the Saṅgha of bhikkhus. Then the Blessed One, having instructed, urged, roused, and gladdened the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk for a great part of the night, surveyed the silent Saṅgha of bhikkhus and addressed the Venerable Sāriputta:

“Vigatathinamiddho kho, sāriputta, bhikkhusaṅgho. Paṭibhātu taṃ, sāriputta, bhikkhūnaṃ [P 5.0126] dhammī kathā. Piṭṭhi me āgilāyati; tamahaṃ āyamissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho āyasmā sāriputto bhagavato paccassosi.

“Sāriputta, the Saṅgha of bhikkhus is free from sloth and torpor. Let a Dhamma talk for the bhikkhus occur to you, Sāriputta. My back is aching; I will stretch it.” “Yes, venerable sir,” the Venerable Sāriputta replied to the Blessed One.

Atha kho bhagavā catugguṇaṃ saṅghāṭiṃ paññāpetvā dakkhiṇena passena sīhaseyyaṃ kappesi pāde pādaṃ accādhāya sato sampajāno uṭṭhānasaññaṃ manasi karitvā. Tatra kho āyasmā sāriputto bhikkhū āmantesi – “āvuso, bhikkhave”ti! “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato sāriputtassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā sāriputto etadavoca –

Then the Blessed One, having folded his outer robe in four, lay down on his right side in the lion’s posture, with one foot overlapping the other, mindful and clearly comprehending, having established in his mind the perception of rising. Then the Venerable Sāriputta addressed the bhikkhus: “Friends, bhikkhus!” “Friend,” those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Sāriputta. The Venerable Sāriputta said this:

“Yassa kassaci, āvuso, saddhā natthi kusalesu dhammesu, hirī natthi… ottappaṃ natthi… vīriyaṃ natthi… paññā natthi… sotāvadhānaṃ natthi… dhammadhāraṇā natthi… atthūpaparikkhā natthi… dhammānudhammappaṭipatti natthi… appamādo natthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no vuddhi. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, kāḷapakkhe candassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāyateva vaṇṇena [V 3.0105] hāyati maṇḍalena hāyati ābhāya hāyati ārohapariṇāhena; evamevaṃ kho, āvuso, yassa kassaci saddhā natthi kusalesu dhammesu, hirī natthi… ottappaṃ natthi… vīriyaṃ natthi… paññā natthi… sotāvadhānaṃ natthi… dhammadhāraṇā natthi… atthūpaparikkhā natthi… dhammānudhammappaṭipatti [T 5.0136] natthi… appamādo natthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā [M 3.0357] divaso vā āgacchati, hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no vuddhi.

“Friends, for anyone who has no faith in wholesome qualities, no moral shame, no moral dread, no energy, no wisdom, no attentiveness in listening, no retention of the Dhamma, no examination of the meaning, no practice in accordance with the Dhamma, and no diligence regarding wholesome qualities, as night and day pass, only a decline in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not growth. Just as, friends, during the dark fortnight, as night and day pass, the moon wanes in beauty, in its orb, in radiance, and in height and circumference; so too, friends, for anyone who has no faith in wholesome qualities, no moral shame, no moral dread, no energy, no wisdom, no attentiveness in listening, no retention of the Dhamma, no examination of the meaning, no practice in accordance with the Dhamma, and no diligence regarding wholesome qualities, as night and day pass, only a decline in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not growth.”

“Yassa kassaci, āvuso, saddhā atthi kusalesu dhammesu, hirī atthi… ottappaṃ atthi… vīriyaṃ atthi… paññā atthi… sotāvadhānaṃ atthi… dhammadhāraṇā atthi… atthūpaparikkhā atthi… dhammānudhammappaṭipatti atthi… appamādo atthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no parihāni. Seyyathāpi, āvuso, juṇhapakkhe [P 5.0127] candassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vaḍḍhateva vaṇṇena vaḍḍhati maṇḍalena vaḍḍhati ābhāya vaḍḍhati ārohapariṇāhena; evamevaṃ kho, āvuso, yassa kassaci saddhā atthi kusalesu dhammesu…pe… appamādo atthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no parihānī”ti.

“Friends, for anyone who has faith in wholesome qualities, has moral shame, has moral dread, has energy, has wisdom, has attentiveness in listening, has retention of the Dhamma, has examination of the meaning, has practice in accordance with the Dhamma, and has diligence regarding wholesome qualities, as night and day pass, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline. Just as, friends, during the bright fortnight, as night and day pass, the moon waxes in beauty, in its orb, in radiance, and in height and circumference; so too, friends, for anyone who has faith in wholesome qualities ... and has diligence regarding wholesome qualities, as night and day pass, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline.”

Atha kho bhagavā paccuṭṭhāya āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ āmantesi – “sādhu sādhu, sāriputta! Yassa kassaci, sāriputta, saddhā natthi kusalesu dhammesu hirī natthi… ottappaṃ natthi… paññā natthi… vīriyaṃ natthi… sotāvadhānaṃ natthi… dhammadhāraṇā natthi… atthūpaparikkhā natthi… dhammānudhammappaṭipatti natthi… appamādo natthi kusalesu dhammesu tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no vuddhi. Seyyathāpi, sāriputta, kāḷapakkhe candassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāyateva vaṇṇena hāyati maṇḍalena hāyati ābhāya hāyati ārohapariṇāhena; evamevaṃ kho, sāriputta, yassa kassaci saddhā natthi kusalesu dhammesu…pe… appamādo [T 5.0137] natthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, hāniyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no vuddhi.

Then the Blessed One rose and addressed the Venerable Sāriputta: “Good, good, Sāriputta! For anyone who has no faith in wholesome qualities, no moral shame, no moral dread, no wisdom, no energy, no attentiveness in listening, no retention of the Dhamma, no examination of the meaning, no practice in accordance with the Dhamma, and no diligence regarding wholesome qualities, as night and day pass, only a decline in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not growth. Just as, Sāriputta, during the dark fortnight, as night and day pass, the moon wanes in beauty, in its orb, in radiance, and in height and circumference; so too, Sāriputta, for anyone who has no faith in wholesome qualities ... and no diligence regarding wholesome qualities, as night and day pass, only a decline in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not growth.”

“Yassa kassaci, sāriputta, saddhā atthi kusalesu dhammesu hirī atthi… ottappaṃ atthi… vīriyaṃ atthi… paññā atthi… sotāvadhānaṃ atthi… dhammadhāraṇā atthi… atthūpaparikkhā [V 3.0106] atthi… dhammānudhammappaṭipatti atthi… appamādo atthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no parihāni. Seyyathāpi, sāriputta, juṇhapakkhe candassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vaḍḍhateva vaṇṇena [P 5.0128] vaḍḍhati maṇḍalena vaḍḍhati ābhāya vaḍḍhati [M 3.0358] ārohapariṇāhena; evamevaṃ kho, sāriputta, yassa kassaci saddhā atthi kusalesu dhammesu…pe… appamādo atthi kusalesu dhammesu, tassa yā ratti vā divaso vā āgacchati, vuddhiyeva pāṭikaṅkhā kusalesu dhammesu no parihānī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Sāriputta, for anyone who has faith in wholesome qualities, has moral shame, has moral dread, has energy, has wisdom, has attentiveness in listening, has retention of the Dhamma, has examination of the meaning, has practice in accordance with the Dhamma, and has diligence regarding wholesome qualities, as night and day pass, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline. Just as, Sāriputta, during the bright fortnight, as night and day pass, the moon waxes in beauty, in its orb, in radiance, and in height and circumference; so too, Sāriputta, for anyone who has faith in wholesome qualities ... and has diligence regarding wholesome qualities, as night and day pass, only growth in wholesome qualities is to be expected, not decline.” The eighth.

9. Paṭhamakathāvatthusuttaṃ

9. The First Discourse on Topics of Conversation

69. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā [T 5.0138] upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannisinnā sannipatitā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ anuyuttā viharanti, seyyathidaṃ – dī. ni. 1.17; ma. ni. 2.223; saṃ. ni. 5.1080; pāci. 508 rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ mahāmattakathaṃ senākathaṃ bhayakathaṃ yuddhakathaṃ annakathaṃ pānakathaṃ vatthakathaṃ sayanakathaṃ mālākathaṃ gandhakathaṃ ñātikathaṃ yānakathaṃ gāmakathaṃ nigamakathaṃ nagarakathaṃ janapadakathaṃ itthikathaṃ itthikathaṃ purisakathaṃ (ka.) ma. ni. aṭṭha. 2.223 passitabbaṃ sūrakathaṃ visikhākathaṃ kumbhaṭṭhānakathaṃ pubbapetakathaṃ nānattakathaṃ lokakkhāyikaṃ samuddakkhāyikaṃ itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vāti.

69. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now on that occasion, a number of bhikkhus, after their meal, on returning from their alms-round, had gathered and were sitting together in the assembly hall, engaged in various kinds of worldly talk, that is: talk about kings, robbers, great ministers, armies, dangers, and battles; talk about food, drink, clothing, beds, garlands, and perfumes; talk about relatives, vehicles, villages, market towns, cities, and districts; talk about women and heroes; talk at crossroads; talk at water-fetching places; talk about the departed; talk on miscellaneous matters; speculation about the world, speculation about the ocean, and talk about existence and non-existence.

Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṃ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yena upaṭṭhānasālā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Nisajja kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “kāya nuttha, bhikkhave, etarahi kathāya sannisinnā sannipatitā, kā ca pana vo antarākathā vippakatā”ti?

Then, in the evening, the Blessed One emerged from seclusion and approached the assembly hall. Having approached, he sat down on the seat that had been prepared. Seated, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “For what discussion are you gathered together here now, bhikkhus? And what was the talk that you left unfinished?”

“Idha mayaṃ, bhante, pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannisinnā sannipatitā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ anuyuttā viharāma, seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ…pe… itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vā”ti. “Na kho panetaṃ, bhikkhave, tumhākaṃ patirūpaṃ kulaputtānaṃ [P 5.0129] saddhāya agārasmā anagāriyaṃ pabbajitānaṃ, yaṃ tumhe anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ anuyuttā vihareyyātha, seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ mahāmattakathaṃ senākathaṃ bhayakathaṃ yuddhakathaṃ annakathaṃ pānakathaṃ vatthakathaṃ sayanakathaṃ mālākathaṃ gandhakathaṃ ñātikathaṃ yānakathaṃ gāmakathaṃ [V 3.0107] nigamakathaṃ nagarakathaṃ janapadakathaṃ itthikathaṃ sūrakathaṃ visikhākathaṃ kumbhaṭṭhānakathaṃ pubbapetakathaṃ nānattakathaṃ lokakkhāyikaṃ samuddakkhāyikaṃ itibhavābhavakathaṃ iti vāti.

“Here, venerable sir, after our meal, on returning from our alms-round, we had gathered and were sitting together in the assembly hall, engaged in various kinds of worldly talk, that is: talk about kings, robbers …pe… and talk about existence and non-existence.” “Bhikkhus, it is not fitting for you, sons of good family who have gone forth from the household life into homelessness out of faith, that you should engage in various kinds of worldly talk, that is: talk about kings, robbers, great ministers, armies, dangers, and battles; talk about food, drink, clothing, beds, garlands, and perfumes; talk about relatives, vehicles, villages, market towns, cities, and districts; talk about women and heroes; talk at crossroads; talk at water-fetching places; talk about the departed; talk on miscellaneous matters; speculation about the world, speculation about the ocean, and talk about existence and non-existence.”

“Dasayimāni[M 3.0359], bhikkhave, kathāvatthūni. Katamāni dasa? Appicchakathā, santuṭṭhikathā, pavivekakathā[T 5.0139], asaṃsaggakathā, vīriyārambhakathā, sīlakathā, samādhikathā, paññākathā, vimuttikathā, vimuttiñāṇadassanakathāti – imāni kho, bhikkhave, dasa kathāvatthūni.

“Bhikkhus, there are these ten subjects for discussion. What ten? Talk on fewness of wishes, talk on contentment, talk on seclusion, talk on non-entanglement, talk on arousing energy, talk on virtue, talk on concentration, talk on wisdom, talk on liberation, and talk on the knowledge and vision of liberation. These, bhikkhus, are the ten subjects for discussion.”

“Imesaṃ ce tumhe, bhikkhave, dasannaṃ kathāvatthūnaṃ upādāyupādāya kathaṃ katheyyātha, imesampi candimasūriyānaṃ evaṃmahiddhikānaṃ evaṃmahānubhāvānaṃ tejasā tejaṃ pariyādiyeyyātha, ko pana vādo aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakāna”nti! Navamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if you were to engage again and again in talk based on these ten subjects for discussion, you would outshine in splendor even the sun and moon, so mighty and powerful are they—to say nothing of the wanderers of other sects!” Ninth.

10. Dutiyakathāvatthusuttaṃ

10. The Second Discourse on Subjects of Talk

70. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā bhikkhū pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkantā upaṭṭhānasālāyaṃ sannisinnā sannipatitā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ anuyuttā viharanti, seyyathidaṃ – rājakathaṃ corakathaṃ mahāmattakathaṃ…pe… itibhavābhavakathaṃ [T 5.0140] iti vāti.

70. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. Now at that time, a number of bhikkhus, after their meal, having returned from their alms round, had sat down together and assembled in the assembly hall, and were engaged in various kinds of worldly talk, that is to say: talk about kings, talk about thieves, talk about great ministers... talk about worldly gain and loss, and so on.

“Dasayimāni, bhikkhave, pāsaṃsāni ṭhānāni. Katamāni dasa? Idha[P 5.0130], bhikkhave, bhikkhu attanā ca appiccho hoti, appicchakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā hoti. ‘Appiccho bhikkhu appicchakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā’ti pāsaṃsametaṃ ṭhānaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, there are these ten grounds for praise. What ten? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is himself of few wishes and speaks to the other bhikkhus on fewness of wishes. ‘A bhikkhu is of few wishes and speaks to the other bhikkhus on fewness of wishes’: this is a ground for praise.

“Attanā ca santuṭṭho hoti, santuṭṭhikathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā hoti. ‘Santuṭṭho bhikkhu santuṭṭhikathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā’ti pāsaṃsametaṃ ṭhānaṃ.

“He is himself content and speaks to the other bhikkhus on contentment. ‘A bhikkhu is content and speaks to the other bhikkhus on contentment’: this is a ground for praise.

“Attanā ca pavivitto hoti, pavivekakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā hoti. ‘Pavivitto bhikkhu pavivekakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā’ti pāsaṃsametaṃ ṭhānaṃ.

“He is himself secluded and speaks to the other bhikkhus on seclusion. ‘A bhikkhu is secluded and speaks to the other bhikkhus on seclusion’: this is a ground for praise.

“Attanā [V 3.0108] ca asaṃsaṭṭho hoti, asaṃsaṭṭhakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā hoti. ‘Asaṃsaṭṭho bhikkhu asaṃsaṭṭhakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā’ti pāsaṃsametaṃ ṭhānaṃ.

“He is himself unassociated and speaks to the other bhikkhus on non-association. ‘A bhikkhu is unassociated and speaks to the other bhikkhus on non-association’: this is a ground for praise.

“Attanā ca āraddhavīriyo hoti, vīriyārambhakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā hoti. ‘Āraddhavīriyo bhikkhu vīriyārambhakathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā’ti pāsaṃsametaṃ ṭhānaṃ.

“He has himself aroused his energy and speaks to the other bhikkhus on arousing energy. ‘A bhikkhu has aroused his energy and speaks to the other bhikkhus on arousing energy’: this is a ground for praise.

“Attanā [M 3.0360] ca sīlasampanno hoti, sīlasampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā hoti. ‘Sīlasampanno bhikkhu sīlasampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā’ti pāsaṃsametaṃ ṭhānaṃ.

“He is himself accomplished in virtue and speaks to the other bhikkhus on the accomplishment of virtue. ‘A bhikkhu is accomplished in virtue and speaks to the other bhikkhus on the accomplishment of virtue’: this is a ground for praise.

“Attanā ca samādhisampanno hoti, samādhisampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā hoti. ‘Samādhisampanno bhikkhu samādhisampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā’ti pāsaṃsametaṃ ṭhānaṃ.

“He is himself accomplished in concentration and speaks to the other bhikkhus on the accomplishment of concentration. ‘A bhikkhu is accomplished in concentration and speaks to the other bhikkhus on the accomplishment of concentration’: this is a ground for praise.

“Attanā ca paññāsampanno hoti, paññāsampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā hoti. ‘Paññāsampanno bhikkhu paññāsampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā’ti pāsaṃsametaṃ ṭhānaṃ.

“He is himself accomplished in wisdom and speaks to the other bhikkhus on the accomplishment of wisdom. ‘A bhikkhu is accomplished in wisdom and speaks to the other bhikkhus on the accomplishment of wisdom’: this is a ground for praise.

“Attanā ca vimuttisampanno hoti, vimuttisampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā hoti. ‘Vimuttisampanno bhikkhu vimuttisampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā’ti pāsaṃsametaṃ ṭhānaṃ.

“He is himself accomplished in liberation and speaks to the other bhikkhus on the accomplishment of liberation. ‘A bhikkhu is accomplished in liberation and speaks to the other bhikkhus on the accomplishment of liberation’: this is a ground for praise.

“Attanā ca vimuttiñāṇadassanasampanno hoti, vimuttiñāṇadassanasampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ [T 5.0141] kattā hoti. ‘Vimuttiñāṇadassanasampanno bhikkhu vimuttiñāṇadassanasampadākathañca bhikkhūnaṃ kattā’ti pāsaṃsametaṃ ṭhānaṃ. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, dasa pāsaṃsāni ṭhānānī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“He is himself accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation and speaks to the other bhikkhus on the accomplishment of the knowledge and vision of liberation. ‘A bhikkhu is accomplished in the knowledge and vision of liberation and speaks to the other bhikkhus on the accomplishment of the knowledge and vision of liberation’: this is a ground for praise. These, bhikkhus, are the ten grounds for praise.” Tenth.

Yamakavaggo dutiyo.

The Chapter on Pairs, the Second.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Avijjā [P 5.0131] taṇhā niṭṭhā ca, avecca dve sukhāni ca;

Naḷakapāne dve vuttā, kathāvatthūpare duveti.

Ignorance, craving, and conclusion, two on unwavering confidence, and happiness; two taught at Naḷakapāna, and two more on subjects of talk.

(8) 3. Ākaṅkhavaggo

(8) 3. The Chapter on Aspirations

1. Ākaṅkhasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Aspirations

71. a. ni. 4.12; itivu. 111 Ekaṃ [V 3.0109] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

71. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s Park. There the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus.” “Venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied. The Blessed One said this:

“Sampannasīlā[M 3.0361], bhikkhave, viharatha sampannapātimokkhā, pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvutā viharatha ācāragocarasampannā aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvino, samādāya sikkhatha sikkhāpadesu.

“Bhikkhus, dwell accomplished in virtue and accomplished in the Pātimokkha; dwell restrained by the restraint of the Pātimokkha, possessed of good conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults; having undertaken them, train in the training rules.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘sabrahmacārīnaṃ piyo cassaṃ manāpo ca garu ca bhāvanīyo cā’ti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto [T 5.0142] anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu should wish: ‘May I be dear and agreeable to my companions in the holy life, respected and esteemed by them,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues, is devoted to internal serenity of mind, does not neglect jhāna, is endowed with insight, and is one who frequents empty dwellings.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘lābhī assaṃ cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārāna’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu should wish: ‘May I be a recipient of robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues, is devoted to internal serenity of mind, does not neglect jhāna, is endowed with insight, and is one who frequents empty dwellings.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘yesāhaṃ paribhuñjāmi cīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārānaṃ tesaṃ te kārā mahapphalā assu mahānisaṃsā’ti, sīlesvevassa…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu should wish: ‘May the deeds of those whose robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick I use be of great fruit and great benefit,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues... and is one who frequents empty dwellings.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave[P 5.0132], bhikkhu ‘ye me ye maṃ (ma. ni. 1.65) petā ñātī sālohitā kālaṅkatā kālakatā (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) pasannacittā anussaranti tesaṃ taṃ mahapphalaṃ assa mahānisaṃsa’nti, sīlesvevassa…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu should wish: ‘When my departed kinsmen and blood relatives recollect me with confident minds, may that act be of great fruit and great benefit for them,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues... and is one who frequents empty dwellings.

“Ākaṅkheyya [V 3.0110] ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘santuṭṭho assaṃ itarītaracīvarapiṇḍapātasenāsanagilānapaccayabhesajjaparikkhārenā’ti, sīlesvevassa…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu should wish: ‘May I be content with whatever robes, almsfood, lodging, and medicinal requisites for the sick I may receive,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues... and is one who cultivates seclusion in empty dwellings.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘khamo assaṃ sītassa uṇhassa jighacchāya pipāsāya ḍaṃsamakasavātātapasarīsapasamphassānaṃ, duruttānaṃ durāgatānaṃ vacanapathānaṃ uppannānaṃ sārīrikānaṃ vedanānaṃ dukkhānaṃ tibbānaṃ tippānaṃ (sī. syā. kaṃ. pī.) kharānaṃ kaṭukānaṃ asātānaṃ amanāpānaṃ pāṇaharānaṃ adhivāsakajātiko assa’nti, sīlesvevassa…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu should wish: ‘May I be patient with cold and heat, hunger and thirst; with the touch of gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, and crawling creatures; with ill-spoken, unwelcome paths of speech; may I be of a nature to endure arisen bodily feelings that are painful, sharp, harsh, piercing, disagreeable, unpleasant, and life-threatening,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues... and is one who cultivates seclusion in empty dwellings.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘aratiratisaho assaṃ, na ca maṃ aratirati saheyya, uppannaṃ aratiratiṃ abhibhuyya [T 5.0143] abhibhuyya vihareyya’nti, sīlesvevassa…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu should wish: ‘May I be a conqueror of discontent and delight, and may discontent and delight not conquer me. May I dwell having repeatedly conquered any discontent and delight that has arisen,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues... and is one who cultivates seclusion in empty dwellings.

“Ākaṅkheyya [M 3.0362] ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘bhayabheravasaho assaṃ, na ca maṃ bhayabheravo saheyya, uppannaṃ bhayabheravaṃ abhibhuyya abhibhuyya vihareyya’nti, sīlesvevassa…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu should wish: ‘May I be a conqueror of fear and dread, and may fear and dread not conquer me. May I dwell having repeatedly conquered any fear and dread that has arisen,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues... and is one who cultivates seclusion in empty dwellings.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘catunnaṃ jhānānaṃ ābhicetasikānaṃ diṭṭhadhammasukhavihārānaṃ nikāmalābhī assaṃ akicchalābhī akasiralābhī’ti, sīlesvevassa…pe… brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu should wish: ‘May I be an attainer at will, without trouble or difficulty, of the four jhānas that pertain to the higher mind and are pleasant dwellings in this very life,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues... and is one who cultivates seclusion in empty dwellings.

“Ākaṅkheyya ce, bhikkhave, bhikkhu ‘āsavānaṃ khayā anāsavaṃ cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ diṭṭheva dhamme [P 5.0133] sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā upasampajja vihareyya’nti, sīlesvevassa paripūrakārī ajjhattaṃ cetosamathamanuyutto anirākatajjhāno vipassanāya samannāgato brūhetā suññāgārānaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, if a bhikkhu should wish: ‘By the destruction of the taints, may I, in this very life, realize for myself with direct knowledge the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, and having attained it, dwell therein,’ he should be one who fulfills the virtues, is devoted to internal serenity of mind, does not neglect jhāna, is endowed with insight, and is one who cultivates seclusion in empty dwellings.

“‘Sampannasīlā, bhikkhave, viharatha sampannapātimokkhā, pātimokkhasaṃvarasaṃvutā viharatha ācāragocarasampannā aṇumattesu vajjesu bhayadassāvino, samādāya sikkhatha sikkhāpadesū’ti, iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vutta”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“That which was spoken—‘Bhikkhus, dwell accomplished in virtue and accomplished in the Pātimokkha; dwell restrained by the restraint of the Pātimokkha, possessed of good conduct and resort, seeing danger in the slightest faults; having undertaken them, train in the training rules’—was spoken in reference to this.” First.

2. Kaṇṭakasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Thorns

72. Ekaṃ [V 3.0111] samayaṃ bhagavā vesāliyaṃ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṃ sambahulehi abhiññātehi abhiññātehi therehi sāvakehi saddhiṃ – āyasmatā ca cālena pālena (syā.), āyasmatā ca upacālena uppālena (syā.), āyasmatā ca kukkuṭena kakkaṭena (sī. syā.), āyasmatā ca kaḷimbhena kavimbhena (sī.), āyasmatā ca nikaṭena kaṭena (sī.), āyasmatā ca kaṭissahena; aññehi ca abhiññātehi abhiññātehi therehi sāvakehi saddhiṃ.

72. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesālī in the Great Wood at the Gabled Hall, together with a number of very well-known elder disciples: the Venerable Cāla, the Venerable Upacāla, the Venerable Kukkuṭa, the Venerable Kaḷimbha, the Venerable Nikaṭa, and the Venerable Kaṭissaha, and with other very well-known elder disciples.

Tena kho pana samayena sambahulā abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī bhadrehi [T 5.0144] bhadrehi yānehi parapurāya paraṃpurāya (syā. aṭṭha.) uccāsaddā mahāsaddā mahāvanaṃ ajjhogāhanti bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Atha kho tesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ etadahosi – “ime kho sambahulā abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī bhadrehi bhadrehi yānehi parapurāya uccāsaddā mahāsaddā mahāvanaṃ ajjhogāhanti [M 3.0363] bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. ‘Saddakaṇṭakā kho pana jhānā’ vuttā bhagavatā. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yena gosiṅgasālavanadāyo tenupasaṅkameyyāma[P 5.0134]. Tattha mayaṃ appasaddā appākiṇṇā phāsuṃ phāsu (syā. ka.) vihareyyāmā”ti. Atha kho te āyasmanto yena gosiṅgasālavanadāyo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; tattha te āyasmanto appasaddā appākiṇṇā phāsuṃ viharanti.

Now at that time, a number of very well-known Licchavis in a fleet of splendid carriages were entering the Great Wood with loud and great noise to see the Blessed One. Then it occurred to those venerable ones: ‘These very well-known Licchavis in a fleet of splendid carriages are entering the Great Wood with loud and great noise to see the Blessed One. The Blessed One has said: “Sound is a thorn to the jhānas.” It would be good if we were to go to the Gosiṅga Sāla-wood. There we would dwell comfortably, with little noise and not crowded.’ Then those venerable ones went to the Gosiṅga Sāla-wood. There they dwell comfortably, with little noise and not crowded.

Atha kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “kahaṃ nu kho, bhikkhave, cālo, kahaṃ upacālo, kahaṃ kukkuṭo, kahaṃ kaḷimbho, kahaṃ nikaṭo, kahaṃ kaṭissaho; kahaṃ nu kho te, bhikkhave, therā sāvakā gatā”ti?

Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, where is Cāla? Where is Upacāla? Where is Kukkuṭa? Where is Kaḷimbha? Where is Nikaṭa? Where is Kaṭissaha? Where have those elder disciples gone?”

“Idha, bhante, tesaṃ āyasmantānaṃ etadahosi – ‘ime kho sambahulā abhiññātā abhiññātā licchavī bhadrehi bhadrehi yānehi parapurāya uccāsaddā mahāsaddā mahāvanaṃ ajjhogāhanti bhagavantaṃ dassanāya ‘saddakaṇṭakā kho pana jhānāvuttā bhagavatā yaṃnūna mayaṃ yena gosiṅgasālavanadāyo tenupasaṅkameyyāma tattha mayaṃ appasaddā appākiṇṇā phāsuṃ vihareyyāmā’ti. Atha kho te, bhante, āyasmanto yena gosiṅgasālavanadāyo tenupasaṅkamiṃsu. Tattha te āyasmanto appasaddā appākiṇṇā phāsuṃ viharantī”ti[T 5.0145].

“Venerable sir, here it occurred to those venerable ones: ‘These very well-known Licchavis in a fleet of splendid carriages are entering the Great Wood with loud and great noise to see the Blessed One. The Blessed One has said: “Sound is a thorn to the jhānas.” It would be good if we were to go to the Gosiṅga Sāla-wood. There we would dwell comfortably, with little noise and not crowded.’ Then, venerable sir, those venerable ones went to the Gosiṅga Sāla-wood. There they are dwelling comfortably, with little noise and not crowded.”

“Sādhu [V 3.0112] sādhu, bhikkhave, yathā te mahāsāvakā sammā byākaramānā byākareyyuṃ, ‘saddakaṇṭakā hi, bhikkhave, jhānā’ vuttā mayā.

“Good, good, bhikkhus! Those great disciples have explained it correctly. For, bhikkhus, I have said that sound is a thorn to the jhānas.”

“Dasayime, bhikkhave, kaṇṭakā. Katame dasa? Pavivekārāmassa saṅgaṇikārāmatā kaṇṭako, asubhanimittānuyogaṃ anuyuttassa subhanimittānuyogo kaṇṭako, indriyesu guttadvārassa visūkadassanaṃ kaṇṭako, brahmacariyassa mātugāmūpacāro mātugāmopavicāro (sī.), mātugāmūpavicaro (ka.) kaṇṭako, kathā. 333 paṭhamassa [P 5.0135] jhānassa saddo kaṇṭako, dutiyassa jhānassa vitakkavicārā kaṇṭakā, tatiyassa jhānassa pīti kaṇṭako, catutthassa jhānassa assāsapassāso kaṇṭako, saññāvedayitanirodhasamāpattiyā saññā ca vedanā ca kaṇṭako rāgo kaṇṭako doso kaṇṭako moho kaṇṭako.

“Bhikkhus, there are these ten thorns. What ten? For one who delights in seclusion, delight in company is a thorn. For one devoted to the practice of the sign of the foul, the practice of the sign of the beautiful is a thorn. For one who guards the doors of the sense faculties, the seeing of shows is a thorn. For the holy life, close contact with women is a thorn. For the first jhāna, sound is a thorn. For the second jhāna, thought and examination are thorns. For the third jhāna, rapture is a thorn. For the fourth jhāna, in-and-out breathing is a thorn. For the attainment of the cessation of perception and feeling, perception and feeling are thorns. Lust is a thorn; hatred is a thorn; delusion is a thorn.”

“Akaṇṭakā[M 3.0364], bhikkhave, viharatha. Nikkaṇṭakā, bhikkhave, viharatha. Akaṇṭakanikkaṇṭakā, bhikkhave, viharatha. Akaṇṭakā, bhikkhave, arahanto; nikkaṇṭakā, bhikkhave, arahanto; akaṇṭakanikkaṇṭakā, bhikkhave, arahanto”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, dwell thornless. Bhikkhus, dwell free of thorns. Bhikkhus, dwell thornless and free of thorns. The Arahants, bhikkhus, are thornless. The Arahants are free of thorns. The Arahants are thornless and free of thorns.” Second.

3. Iṭṭhadhammasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on Desirable Things

73. “Dasayime, bhikkhave, dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dullabhā lokasmiṃ. Katame dasa? Bhogā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dullabhā lokasmiṃ; vaṇṇo iṭṭho kanto manāpo dullabho lokasmiṃ; ārogyaṃ iṭṭhaṃ kantaṃ manāpaṃ dullabhaṃ lokasmiṃ; sīlaṃ iṭṭhaṃ kantaṃ manāpaṃ dullabhaṃ lokasmiṃ; brahmacariyaṃ iṭṭhaṃ kantaṃ manāpaṃ dullabhaṃ lokasmiṃ; mittā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dullabhā lokasmiṃ; bāhusaccaṃ iṭṭhaṃ kantaṃ manāpaṃ dullabhaṃ lokasmiṃ; paññā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dullabhā lokasmiṃ; dhammā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dullabhā lokasmiṃ[T 5.0146]; saggā iṭṭhā kantā manāpā dullabhā lokasmiṃ.

73. “Bhikkhus, these ten things are desirable, lovely, pleasing, and hard to find in the world. What ten? Wealth is desirable, lovely, pleasing, and hard to find in the world; beauty is desirable, lovely, pleasing, and hard to find in the world; health is desirable, lovely, pleasing, and hard to find in the world; virtuous conduct is desirable, lovely, pleasing, and hard to find in the world; the holy life is desirable, lovely, pleasing, and hard to find in the world; friends are desirable, lovely, pleasing, and hard to find in the world; extensive learning is desirable, lovely, pleasing, and hard to find in the world; wisdom is desirable, lovely, pleasing, and hard to find in the world; qualities are desirable, lovely, pleasing, and hard to find in the world; heavens are desirable, lovely, pleasing, and hard to find in the world.”

“Imesaṃ [P 5.0136] kho, bhikkhave, dasannaṃ dhammānaṃ iṭṭhānaṃ kantānaṃ manāpānaṃ dullabhānaṃ lokasmiṃ dasa dhammā paripanthā paribandhā (ka.) – ālasyaṃ anuṭṭhānaṃ bhogānaṃ paripantho, amaṇḍanā avibhūsanā vaṇṇassa paripantho, asappāyakiriyā ārogyassa paripantho, pāpamittatā sīlānaṃ paripantho, indriyaasaṃvaro brahmacariyassa paripantho, visaṃvādanā mittānaṃ paripantho, asajjhāyakiriyā bāhusaccassa [V 3.0113] paripantho, asussūsā aparipucchā paññāya paripantho, ananuyogo apaccavekkhaṇā dhammānaṃ paripantho, micchāpaṭipatti saggānaṃ paripantho. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, dasannaṃ iṭṭhānaṃ kantānaṃ manāpānaṃ dullabhānaṃ lokasmiṃ ime dasa dhammā paripanthā.

“Bhikkhus, for these ten things that are desirable, lovely, pleasing, and hard to find in the world, there are ten obstacles. Laziness and lack of exertion are an obstacle to wealth; lack of adornment and embellishment is an obstacle to beauty; unsuitable actions are an obstacle to health; bad friendship is an obstacle to virtuous conduct; lack of sense restraint is an obstacle to the holy life; deception is an obstacle to friends; neglect of recitation is an obstacle to extensive learning; unwillingness to listen and failure to inquire are an obstacle to wisdom; lack of application and review are an obstacle to qualities; and wrong practice is an obstacle to the heavens. For these ten things that are desirable, lovely, pleasing, and hard to find in the world, these are the ten obstacles.”

“Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, dasannaṃ dhammānaṃ iṭṭhānaṃ kantānaṃ manāpānaṃ dullabhānaṃ lokasmiṃ dasa dhammā āhārā – uṭṭhānaṃ anālasyaṃ bhogānaṃ āhāro, maṇḍanā vibhūsanā vaṇṇassa āhāro, sappāyakiriyā ārogyassa āhāro, kalyāṇamittatā sīlānaṃ āhāro, indriyasaṃvaro brahmacariyassa āhāro, avisaṃvādanā mittānaṃ āhāro, sajjhāyakiriyā bāhusaccassa āhāro, sussūsā paripucchā paññāya āhāro, anuyogo paccavekkhaṇā dhammānaṃ āhāro, sammāpaṭipatti saggānaṃ āhāro[M 3.0365]. Imesaṃ kho, bhikkhave, dasannaṃ dhammānaṃ iṭṭhānaṃ kantānaṃ manāpānaṃ dullabhānaṃ lokasmiṃ ime dasa dhammā āhārā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, for these ten things that are desirable, lovely, pleasing, and hard to find in the world, there are ten supports. Exertion and diligence are the support for wealth; adornment and embellishment are the support for beauty; suitable actions are the support for health; good friendship is the support for virtuous conduct; sense restraint is the support for the holy life; non-deception is the support for friends; recitation is the support for extensive learning; willingness to listen and inquiry are the support for wisdom; application and review are the support for qualities; and right practice is the support for the heavens. For these ten things that are desirable, lovely, pleasing, and hard to find in the world, these are the ten supports.” Third.

4. Vaḍḍhisuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on Growth

74. “Dasahi[T 5.0147][P 5.0137], bhikkhave, vaḍḍhīhi vaḍḍhamāno ariyasāvako ariyāya vaḍḍhiyā vaḍḍhati, sārādāyī ca hoti varādāyī kāyassa. Katamehi dasahi? Khettavatthūhi vaḍḍhati, dhanadhaññena vaḍḍhati, puttadārehi vaḍḍhati, dāsakammakaraporisehi vaḍḍhati, catuppadehi vaḍḍhati, saddhāya vaḍḍhati, sīlena vaḍḍhati, sutena vaḍḍhati, cāgena vaḍḍhati, paññāya vaḍḍhati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi vaḍḍhīhi vaḍḍhamāno ariyasāvako ariyāya vaḍḍhiyā vaḍḍhati, sārādāyī ca hoti varādāyī kāyassāti.

74. “Bhikkhus, growing with ten kinds of growth, a noble disciple grows with the noble growth; he becomes one who takes the essence of the body and one who takes what is excellent of the body. With which ten? He grows with fields and land, he grows with wealth and grain, he grows with sons and wife, he grows with slaves, workers, and men, he grows with quadrupeds, he grows in faith, he grows in virtue, he grows in learning, he grows in generosity, he grows in wisdom. Indeed, bhikkhus, growing with these ten kinds of growth, a noble disciple grows with the noble growth; he becomes one who takes the essence of the body and one who takes what is excellent of the body.”

“Dhanena dhaññena ca yodha vaḍḍhati,

Puttehi dārehi catuppadehi ca;

Sa bhogavā hoti yasassi pūjito,

Ñātīhi mittehi athopi rājubhi.

“One who in this world grows with wealth and grain, with children, wife, and quadrupeds, that person becomes wealthy, famous, and honored by kinsmen, friends, and also by kings.

“Saddhāya sīlena ca yodha vaḍḍhati,

Paññāya cāgena sutena cūbhayaṃ;

So [V 3.0114] tādiso sappuriso vicakkhaṇo,

Diṭṭheva dhamme ubhayena vaḍḍhatī”ti. catutthaṃ;

“One who in this world grows with faith, virtue, wisdom, generosity, and learning—that good person of such a kind, who is discerning, grows in both ways in this very life.” The fourth.

5. Migasālāsuttaṃ

5. The Discourse with Migasālā

75. Ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho āyasmā ānando pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena migasālāya upāsikāya nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdi. Atha kho migasālā upāsikā yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā [T 5.0148] kho migasālā upāsikā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavoca –

75. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery. Then, in the morning, the Venerable Ānanda, having dressed and taken his bowl and outer robe, approached the residence of the female lay follower Migasālā. Having approached, he sat down on the prepared seat. Then the female lay follower Migasālā approached the Venerable Ānanda. Having approached, she paid homage to the Venerable Ānanda and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the female lay follower Migasālā said this to the Venerable Ānanda:

“Kathaṃ kathaṃ nāmāyaṃ, bhante ānanda, bhagavatā dhammo [P 5.0138] desito aññeyyo, yatra hi nāma brahmacārī ca abrahmacārī ca ubho samasamagatikā bhavissanti abhisamparāyaṃ. Pitā me, bhante, purāṇo brahmacārī hoti [M 3.0366] ārācārī anācārī (ka.) virato methunā gāmadhammā. So kālaṅkato bhagavatā byākato – ‘sakadāgāmī satto sakadāgāmisatto (sī. syā. pī.) tusitaṃ kāyaṃ upapanno’ti. Pitāmaho me pettāpi yo me (sī.), pita piyo me (syā.) a. ni. 6.44, bhante, isidatto abrahmacārī ahosi sadārasantuṭṭho. Sopi kālaṅkato bhagavatā byākato – ‘sakadāgāmī satto tusitaṃ kāyaṃ upapanno’ti.

“Venerable Ānanda, how is this Dhamma taught by the Blessed One to be understood, wherein both one who lives the holy life and one who does not live the holy life will have the very same destiny in the next life? My father, venerable sir, Purāṇa, lived the holy life, was of remote conduct, and abstained from sexual intercourse, the practice of villagers. When he passed away, he was declared by the Blessed One thus: ‘Having become a once-returner, he has been reborn in the Tusita celestial realm.’ My grandfather, venerable sir, Isidatta, did not live the holy life; he was content with his own wife. When he passed away, he too was declared by the Blessed One thus: ‘Having become a once-returner, he has been reborn in the Tusita celestial realm.’

“Kathaṃ kathaṃ nāmāyaṃ, bhante ānanda, bhagavatā dhammo desito aññeyyo, yatra hi nāma brahmacārī ca abrahmacārī ca ubho samasamagatikā bhavissanti abhisamparāya”nti? “Evaṃ kho panetaṃ, bhagini, bhagavatā byākata”nti.

“Venerable Ānanda, how is this Dhamma taught by the Blessed One to be understood, wherein both one who lives the holy life and one who does not live the holy life will have the very same destiny in the next life?” “Indeed, sister, it was declared thus by the Blessed One.”

Atha kho āyasmā ānando migasālāya upāsikāya nivesane piṇḍapātaṃ gahetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi. Atha kho āyasmā ānando pacchābhattaṃ piṇḍapātapaṭikkanto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

Then the Venerable Ānanda, having received almsfood at the residence of the female lay follower Migasālā, rose from his seat and departed. Then, after the meal, having returned from the alms-round, the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda said this to the Blessed One:

“Idhāhaṃ[V 3.0115], bhante, pubbaṇhasamayaṃ nivāsetvā pattacīvaramādāya yena migasālāya upāsikāya nivesanaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā paññatte āsane nisīdiṃ. Atha kho, bhante, migasālā upāsikā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho, bhante, migasālā upāsikā maṃ etadavoca [T 5.0149] –

“Venerable sir, this morning, having adjusted my lower robe and taken my bowl and outer robe, I approached the residence of the female lay follower Migasālā. Having approached, I sat down on the prepared seat. Then, venerable sir, the female lay follower Migasālā approached me. Having approached, she paid homage to me and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, venerable sir, the female lay follower Migasālā said this to me:

‘Kathaṃ kathaṃ nāmāyaṃ, bhante ānanda, bhagavatā dhammo desito [P 5.0139] aññeyyo, yatra hi nāma brahmacārī ca abrahmacārī ca ubho samasamagatikā bhavissanti abhisamparāyaṃ. Pitā me, bhante, purāṇo brahmacārī ahosi ārācārī virato methunā gāmadhammā. So kālaṅkato bhagavatā byākato sakadāgāmī satto tusitaṃ kāyaṃ upapannoti. Pitāmaho me, bhante, isidatto abrahmacārī ahosi sadārasantuṭṭho. Sopi kālaṅkato bhagavatā byākato – sakadāgāmī satto tusitaṃ kāyaṃ upapannoti.

‘Venerable Ānanda, how is this Dhamma taught by the Blessed One to be understood, wherein both one who lives the holy life and one who does not live the holy life will have the very same destiny in the next life? My father, venerable sir, Purāṇa, lived the holy life, was of remote conduct, and abstained from sexual intercourse, the practice of villagers. When he passed away, he was declared by the Blessed One thus: “Having become a once-returner, he has been reborn in the Tusita celestial realm.” My grandfather, venerable sir, Isidatta, did not live the holy life; he was content with his own wife. When he passed away, he too was declared by the Blessed One thus: “Having become a once-returner, he has been reborn in the Tusita celestial realm.”’

Kathaṃ [M 3.0367] kathaṃ nāmāyaṃ, bhante ānanda, bhagavatā dhammo desito aññeyyo, yatra hi nāma brahmacārī ca abrahmacārī ca ubho samasamagatikā bhavissanti abhisamparāya’nti? Evaṃ vutte ahaṃ, bhante, migasālaṃ upāsikaṃ etadavocaṃ – ‘evaṃ kho panetaṃ, bhagini, bhagavatā byākata’”nti.

‘Venerable Ānanda, how is this Dhamma taught by the Blessed One to be understood, wherein both one who lives the holy life and one who does not live the holy life will have the very same destiny in the next life?’ When this was said, venerable sir, I said this to the female lay follower Migasālā: ‘Indeed, sister, it was declared thus by the Blessed One.’”

“Kā cānanda, migasālā upāsikā bālā abyattā ammakā ammakapaññā ambakā ambakapaññā (sī. pī.), andhakā andhakapaññā (syā.), ke ca purisapuggalaparopariye ñāṇe?

“And what, Ānanda, is this female lay follower Migasālā—foolish, incompetent, a woman with a woman's wisdom? And what are the Perfectly Enlightened Ones in regard to the knowledge of the diversity in the faculties of individuals?

“Dasayime, ānanda, puggalā santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ. Katame dasa? Idhānanda, ekacco puggalo dussīlo hoti. Tañca cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti, yatthassa taṃ dussīlyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati. Tassa savanenapi akataṃ hoti, bāhusaccenapi akataṃ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi appaṭividdhaṃ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṃ na labhati. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā hānāya pareti, no visesāya; hānagāmīyeva hoti, no visesagāmī.

“Ānanda, these ten persons are found existing in the world. What ten? Here, Ānanda, a certain person is immoral. He does not understand as it truly is that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein his immorality ceases without remainder. For him, what should be accomplished by hearing has not been accomplished, what should be accomplished by extensive learning has not been accomplished, and what should be penetrated by view has not been penetrated; and he does not obtain temporary liberation. With the breaking up of the body, after death, he goes to decline, not to a superior state; he is one who goes to decline, not one who goes to a superior state.

“Idha panānanda, ekacco puggalo dussīlo hoti. Tañca cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ yathābhūtaṃ [T 5.0150][V 3.0116] pajānāti yatthassa [P 5.0140] taṃ dussīlyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati. Tassa savanenapi kataṃ hoti, bāhusaccenapi kataṃ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi paṭividdhaṃ suppaṭividdhaṃ (syā.) hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṃ labhati. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā visesāya pareti, no hānāya; visesagāmīyeva hoti, no hānagāmī.

“Furthermore, Ānanda, a certain person is immoral. But he understands as it truly is that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein his immorality ceases without remainder. For him, what should be accomplished by hearing has been accomplished; what should be accomplished by extensive learning has been accomplished; what should be penetrated by view has been penetrated; and he obtains a temporary liberation. With the breaking up of the body, after death, he proceeds to a superior state, not to decline; he is one who goes only to a superior state, not one who goes to decline.

“Tatrānanda, pamāṇikā pamiṇanti – ‘imassapi teva dhammā, aparassapi teva dhammā. Kasmā nesaṃ eko hīno eko paṇīto’ti? Tañhi tesaṃ, ānanda, hoti dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya.

“In this case, Ānanda, those who take to measuring, measure thus: ‘This person has these same qualities, and the other person has these same qualities. Why among them is one inferior and one superior?’ Indeed, Ānanda, that leads to their long-term harm and suffering.

“Tatrānanda, yvāyaṃ puggalo dussīlo hoti. Tañca cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti yatthassa taṃ dussīlyaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati. Tassa savanenapi kataṃ hoti, bāhusaccenapi kataṃ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi paṭividdhaṃ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṃ labhati. Ayaṃ, ānanda, puggalo amunā purimena puggalena abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca. Taṃ kissa hetu? Imaṃ hānanda, puggalaṃ dhammasoto nibbahati. Tadantaraṃ ko jāneyya, aññatra tathāgatena! Tasmātihānanda, mā puggalesu pamāṇikā ahuvattha[M 3.0368], mā puggalesu pamāṇaṃ gaṇhittha. Khaññati hānanda, puggalesu pamāṇaṃ gaṇhanto. Ahaṃ vā, ānanda ahañcānanda (sī. syā. ka.) a. ni. 6.44 passitabbaṃ, puggalesu pamāṇaṃ gaṇheyyaṃ yo vā panassa mādiso.

“In this case, Ānanda, as for the person who is immoral but understands as it truly is that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein his immorality ceases without remainder; for whom what should be accomplished by hearing has been accomplished; what should be accomplished by extensive learning has been accomplished; what should be penetrated by view has been penetrated; and who obtains a temporary liberation: this person, Ānanda, is more excellent and more sublime than that former person. For what reason? Because, Ānanda, the stream of the Dhamma carries this person. Who could know that distinction, other than the Tathāgata? Therefore, Ānanda, do not be ones who take the measure of persons; do not take the measure of persons. One who takes the measure of persons, Ānanda, harms himself. I, Ānanda, might take the measure of persons, or one who is like me.

“Idha [P 5.0141] panānanda, ekacco puggalo sīlavā hoti. Tañca cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti yatthassa taṃ sīlaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati. Tassa savanenapi akataṃ hoti, bāhusaccenapi akataṃ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi appaṭividdhaṃ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṃ [T 5.0151] na labhati. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā hānāya pareti, no visesāya; hānagāmīyeva hoti, no visesagāmī.

“Furthermore, Ānanda, a certain person is virtuous. But he does not understand as it truly is that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein his virtue ceases without remainder. For him, what should be accomplished by hearing has not been accomplished; what should be accomplished by extensive learning has not been accomplished; what should be penetrated by view has not been penetrated; and he does not obtain a temporary liberation. With the breaking up of the body, after death, he proceeds to decline, not to a superior state; he is one who goes only to decline, not one who goes to a superior state.

“Idha panānanda, ekacco puggalo sīlavā hoti. Tañca cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti yatthassa taṃ sīlaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati. Tassa savanenapi kataṃ hoti, bāhusaccenapi kataṃ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi paṭividdhaṃ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṃ labhati. So kāyassa [V 3.0117] bhedā paraṃ maraṇā visesāya pareti, no hānāya; visesagāmīyeva hoti, no hānagāmī.

“Furthermore, Ānanda, a certain person is virtuous. And he understands as it truly is that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein his virtue ceases without remainder. For him, what should be accomplished by hearing has been accomplished; what should be accomplished by extensive learning has been accomplished; what should be penetrated by view has been penetrated; and he obtains a temporary liberation. With the breaking up of the body, after death, he proceeds to a superior state, not to decline; he is one who goes only to a superior state, not one who goes to decline.

“Tatrānanda, pamāṇikā pamiṇanti…pe… ahaṃ vā, ānanda, puggalesu pamāṇaṃ gaṇheyyaṃ yo vā panassa mādiso.

“In this case, Ānanda, those who take to measuring, measure thus… I, Ānanda, might take the measure of persons, or one who is like me.

“Idha panānanda, ekacco puggalo tibbarāgo hoti. Tañca cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti yatthassa so rāgo apariseso nirujjhati. Tassa savanenapi akataṃ hoti, bāhusaccenapi akataṃ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi appaṭividdhaṃ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṃ na labhati. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā hānāya pareti, no visesāya; hānagāmīyeva hoti, no visesagāmī.

Furthermore, Ānanda, a certain person is one of intense passion. But he does not understand as it truly is that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein that passion of his ceases without remainder. For him, what should be accomplished by hearing has not been accomplished; what should be accomplished by extensive learning has not been accomplished; what should be penetrated by view has not been penetrated; and he does not obtain a temporary liberation. With the breaking up of the body, after death, he proceeds to decline, not to a superior state; he is one who goes only to decline, not one who goes to a superior state.

“Idha panānanda, ekacco puggalo tibbarāgo hoti. Tañca cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti yatthassa so rāgo apariseso nirujjhati. Tassa savanenapi kataṃ hoti, bāhusaccenapi kataṃ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi paṭividdhaṃ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṃ labhati. So kāyassa [P 5.0142] bhedā paraṃ maraṇā visesāya pareti, no hānāya; visesagāmīyeva hoti, no hānagāmī.

Furthermore, Ānanda, a certain person is one of intense passion. And he understands as it truly is that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein that passion of his ceases without remainder. For him, what should be accomplished by hearing has been accomplished; what should be accomplished by extensive learning has been accomplished; what should be penetrated by view has been penetrated; and he obtains a temporary liberation. With the breaking up of the body, after death, he proceeds to a superior state, not to decline; he is one who goes only to a superior state, not one who goes to decline.

“Tatrānanda[M 3.0369], pamāṇikā pamiṇanti…pe… ahaṃ vā, ānanda, puggalesu pamāṇaṃ gaṇheyyaṃ yo vā [T 5.0152] panassa mādiso.

In this case, Ānanda, those who take to measuring, measure thus... I, Ānanda, might take the measure of persons, or one who is like me.

“Idha panānanda, ekacco puggalo kodhano hoti. Tañca cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti yatthassa so kodho apariseso nirujjhati. Tassa savanenapi akataṃ hoti, bāhusaccenapi akataṃ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi appaṭividdhaṃ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṃ na labhati. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā hānāya pareti, no visesāya; hānagāmīyeva hoti, no visesagāmī.

Furthermore, Ānanda, a certain person is irascible. But he does not understand as it truly is that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein that anger of his ceases without remainder. For him, what should be accomplished by hearing has not been accomplished; what should be accomplished by extensive learning has not been accomplished; what should be penetrated by view has not been penetrated; and he does not obtain a temporary liberation. With the breaking up of the body, after death, he proceeds to decline, not to a superior state; he is one who goes only to decline, not one who goes to a superior state.

“Idha panānanda, ekacco puggalo kodhano hoti. Tañca cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ yathābhūtaṃ [V 3.0118] pajānāti yatthassa so kodho apariseso nirujjhati. Tassa savanenapi kataṃ hoti, bāhusaccenapi kataṃ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi paṭividdhaṃ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṃ labhati. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā visesāya pareti, no hānāya; visesagāmīyeva hoti, no hānagāmī.

Furthermore, Ānanda, a certain person is irascible. And he understands as it truly is that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein that anger of his ceases without remainder. For him, what should be accomplished by hearing has been accomplished; what should be accomplished by extensive learning has been accomplished; what should be penetrated by view has been penetrated; and he obtains a temporary liberation. With the breaking up of the body, after death, he proceeds to a superior state, not to decline; he is one who goes only to a superior state, not one who goes to decline.

“Tatrānanda, pamāṇikā pamiṇanti…pe… ahaṃ vā, ānanda, puggalesu pamāṇaṃ gaṇheyyaṃ yo vā panassa mādiso.

In this case, Ānanda, those who take to measuring, measure thus... I, Ānanda, might take the measure of persons, or one who is like me.

“Idha panānanda, ekacco puggalo uddhato hoti. Tañca cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ yathābhūtaṃ nappajānāti yatthassa taṃ uddhaccaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati. Tassa savanenapi akataṃ hoti, bāhusaccenapi akataṃ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi appaṭividdhaṃ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṃ na labhati. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā hānāya pareti, no visesāya; hānagāmīyeva hoti, no visesagāmī.

Furthermore, Ānanda, a certain person is restless. But he does not understand as it truly is that liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein that restlessness of his ceases without remainder. For him, what should be accomplished by hearing has not been accomplished; what should be accomplished by extensive learning has not been accomplished; what should be penetrated by view has not been penetrated; and he does not obtain a temporary liberation. With the breaking up of the body, after death, he proceeds to decline, not to a superior state; he is one who goes only to decline, not one who goes to a superior state.

“Idha panānanda, ekacco puggalo uddhato hoti. Tañca cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti yatthassa taṃ uddhaccaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati. Tassa savanenapi [T 5.0153] kataṃ hoti, bāhusaccenapi kataṃ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi [P 5.0143] paṭividdhaṃ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṃ labhati. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā visesāya pareti, no hānāya; visesagāmīyeva hoti, no hānagāmī.

Furthermore, Ānanda, a certain person is restless. And he understands as it truly is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein that restlessness of his ceases without remainder. For him, what should be accomplished by hearing has been accomplished; what should be accomplished by extensive learning has been accomplished; what should be penetrated by view has been penetrated; and he obtains a temporary liberation. With the breaking up of the body, after death, he proceeds to a superior state, not to decline; he is one who goes only to a superior state, not one who goes to decline.

“Tatrānanda[M 3.0370], pamāṇikā pamiṇanti – ‘imassapi teva dhammā, aparassapi teva dhammā. Kasmā nesaṃ eko hīno eko paṇīto’ti? Tañhi tesaṃ, ānanda, hoti dīgharattaṃ ahitāya dukkhāya.

In that connection, Ānanda, those who take measure, measure thus: ‘This person has these qualities, and the other person also has these qualities. Why among them is one inferior and one superior?’ That, Ānanda, is for their long-term harm and suffering.

“Tatrānanda, yvāyaṃ puggalo uddhato hoti tañca cetovimuttiṃ paññāvimuttiṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāti yatthassa taṃ uddhaccaṃ aparisesaṃ nirujjhati, tassa savanenapi kataṃ hoti, bāhusaccenapi kataṃ hoti, diṭṭhiyāpi paṭividdhaṃ hoti, sāmāyikampi vimuttiṃ labhati. Ayaṃ, ānanda, puggalo amunā purimena puggalena abhikkantataro ca paṇītataro ca. Taṃ kissa hetu[V 3.0119]? Imaṃ hānanda, puggalaṃ dhammasoto nibbahati. Tadantaraṃ ko jāneyya aññatra tathāgatena! Tasmātihānanda, mā puggalesu pamāṇikā ahuvattha; mā puggalesu pamāṇaṃ gaṇhittha. Khaññati hānanda, puggalesu pamāṇaṃ gaṇhanto. Ahaṃ vā, ānanda, puggalesu pamāṇaṃ gaṇheyyaṃ yo vā panassa mādiso.

In that connection, Ānanda, the person who is restless and understands as it truly is the liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom wherein that restlessness of his ceases without remainder; for whom what should be accomplished by hearing has been accomplished, what should be accomplished by extensive learning has been accomplished, what should be penetrated by view has been penetrated, and who obtains a temporary liberation—this person, Ānanda, is more excellent and more sublime than the former person. For what reason? Because, Ānanda, the stream of the Dhamma carries this person along. Who could know that distinction apart from the Tathāgata? Therefore, Ānanda, do not be ones who take the measure of persons; do not take the measure of persons. For, Ānanda, one who takes the measure of persons is undermined. I, Ānanda, might take the measure of persons, or one who is like me.

“Kā cānanda, migasālā upāsikā bālā abyattā ammakā ammakapaññā, ke ca purisapuggalaparopariye ñāṇe! Ime kho, ānanda, dasa puggalā santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ.

And what, Ānanda, is the laywoman Migasālā—foolish, incompetent, a woman with a woman's wisdom—and what are those with the knowledge of the diversity in the faculties of individuals! These, Ānanda, are the ten persons found existing in the world.

“Yathārūpena, ānanda, sīlena purāṇo samannāgato ahosi tathārūpena sīlena isidatto samannāgato abhavissa, nayidha purāṇo isidattassa [T 5.0154] gatimpi aññassa. Yathārūpāya [P 5.0144] cānanda, paññāya isidatto samannāgato ahosi tathārūpāya paññāya purāṇo samannāgato abhavissa, nayidha isidatto purāṇassa gatimpi aññassa. Iti kho, ānanda, ime puggalā ubho ekaṅgahīnā”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

Ānanda, if Isidatta had been endowed with the same kind of virtue with which Purāṇa was endowed, Purāṇa would not have known even the disposition of Isidatta. And Ānanda, if Purāṇa had been endowed with the same kind of wisdom with which Isidatta was endowed, Isidatta would not have known even the disposition of Purāṇa. Thus, Ānanda, these two persons were each lacking in one respect.” Fifth.

6. Tayodhammasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Three Qualities

76. “Tayome, bhikkhave, dhammā loke na saṃvijjeyyuṃ, na tathāgato loke uppajjeyya arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, na tathāgatappavedito dhammavinayo loke dibbeyya. Katame tayo? Jāti ca, jarā ca, maraṇañca – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhammā loke na saṃvijjeyyuṃ, na tathāgato loke uppajjeyya arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, na tathāgatappavedito dhammavinayo loke dibbeyya. Yasmā ca kho, bhikkhave, ime tayo dhammā loke saṃvijjanti tasmā tathāgato loke uppajjati arahaṃ sammāsambuddho, tasmā tathāgatappavedito dhammavinayo loke dibbati.

76. Bhikkhus, if these three phenomena did not exist in the world, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, would not arise in the world, nor would the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata shine in the world. What three? Birth, aging, and death. Indeed, bhikkhus, if these three phenomena did not exist in the world, the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, would not arise in the world, nor would the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata shine in the world. And because, bhikkhus, these three phenomena exist in the world, therefore the Tathāgata, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, arises in the world; therefore the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata shines in the world.

“Tayome[M 3.0371], bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo jātiṃ pahātuṃ jaraṃ pahātuṃ maraṇaṃ pahātuṃ. Katame tayo? Rāgaṃ appahāya, dosaṃ appahāya, mohaṃ appahāya – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme appahāya abhabbo jātiṃ pahātuṃ jaraṃ pahātuṃ maraṇaṃ pahātuṃ.

Bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning birth, abandoning aging, and abandoning death. What three?
