Without having abandoned lust, without having abandoned aversion, without having abandoned delusion. Indeed, bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning birth, abandoning aging, and abandoning death.

“Tayome bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo rāgaṃ pahātuṃ dosaṃ pahātuṃ mohaṃ pahātuṃ. Katame [V 3.0120] tayo? Sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ appahāya, vicikicchaṃ appahāya, sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ appahāya – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme appahāya abhabbo rāgaṃ pahātuṃ dosaṃ pahātuṃ mohaṃ pahātuṃ.

Bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning lust, abandoning aversion, and abandoning delusion. What three? Without having abandoned identity-view, without having abandoned doubt, without having abandoned clinging to rites and rituals. Indeed, bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning lust, abandoning aversion, and abandoning delusion.

“Tayome[P 5.0145], bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ [T 5.0155] pahātuṃ vicikicchaṃ pahātuṃ sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ pahātuṃ. Katame tayo? Ayonisomanasikāraṃ appahāya, kummaggasevanaṃ appahāya, cetaso līnattaṃ appahāya – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme appahāya abhabbo sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ pahātuṃ vicikicchaṃ pahātuṃ sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ pahātuṃ.

Bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning identity-view, abandoning doubt, and abandoning clinging to rites and rituals. What three? Without having abandoned improper attention, without having abandoned resorting to the wrong path, without having abandoned mental sluggishness. Indeed, bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning identity-view, abandoning doubt, and abandoning clinging to rites and rituals.

“Tayome, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo ayoniso manasikāraṃ pahātuṃ kummaggasevanaṃ pahātuṃ cetaso līnattaṃ pahātuṃ. Katame tayo? Muṭṭhasaccaṃ appahāya, asampajaññaṃ appahāya, cetaso vikkhepaṃ appahāya – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme appahāya abhabbo ayonisomanasikāraṃ pahātuṃ kummaggasevanaṃ pahātuṃ cetaso līnattaṃ pahātuṃ.

Bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning improper attention, abandoning resorting to the wrong path, and abandoning mental sluggishness. What three? Without having abandoned lapsed mindfulness, without having abandoned lack of clear comprehension, without having abandoned mental distraction. Indeed, bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning improper attention, abandoning resorting to the wrong path, and abandoning mental sluggishness.

“Tayome, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo muṭṭhasaccaṃ pahātuṃ asampajaññaṃ pahātuṃ cetaso vikkhepaṃ pahātuṃ. Katame tayo? Ariyānaṃ adassanakamyataṃ appahāya, ariyadhammassa ariyadhammaṃ (syā.) asotukamyataṃ appahāya, upārambhacittataṃ appahāya – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme appahāya abhabbo muṭṭhasaccaṃ pahātuṃ asampajaññaṃ pahātuṃ cetaso vikkhepaṃ pahātuṃ.

Bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning lapsed mindfulness, abandoning lack of clear comprehension, and abandoning mental distraction. What three? Without having abandoned unwillingness to see the noble ones, without having abandoned unwillingness to hear the noble Dhamma, without having abandoned a censorious mind. Indeed, bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning lapsed mindfulness, abandoning lack of clear comprehension, and abandoning mental distraction.

“Tayome, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo ariyānaṃ adassanakamyataṃ pahātuṃ ariyadhammassa asotukamyataṃ pahātuṃ upārambhacittataṃ pahātuṃ. Katame tayo? Uddhaccaṃ appahāya, asaṃvaraṃ appahāya, dussīlyaṃ appahāya [M 3.0372] – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme appahāya abhabbo ariyānaṃ adassanakamyataṃ pahātuṃ ariyadhammassa asotukamyataṃ pahātuṃ upārambhacittataṃ pahātuṃ.

Bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning unwillingness to see the noble ones, abandoning unwillingness to hear the noble Dhamma, and abandoning a censorious mind. What three? Without having abandoned restlessness, without having abandoned lack of restraint, without having abandoned immorality. Indeed, bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning unwillingness to see the noble ones, abandoning unwillingness to hear the noble Dhamma, and abandoning a censorious mind.

“Tayome[P 5.0146], bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo uddhaccaṃ pahātuṃ asaṃvaraṃ pahātuṃ dussīlyaṃ pahātuṃ. Katame tayo[T 5.0156]? Assaddhiyaṃ appahāya, avadaññutaṃ appahāya, kosajjaṃ appahāya – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme appahāya abhabbo uddhaccaṃ pahātuṃ asaṃvaraṃ pahātuṃ dussīlyaṃ pahātuṃ.

Bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning restlessness, abandoning lack of restraint, and abandoning immorality. What three? Without having abandoned faithlessness, without having abandoned ingratitude, without having abandoned laziness. Indeed, bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning restlessness, abandoning lack of restraint, and abandoning immorality.

“Tayome[V 3.0121], bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo assaddhiyaṃ pahātuṃ avadaññutaṃ pahātuṃ kosajjaṃ pahātuṃ. Katame tayo? Anādariyaṃ appahāya, dovacassataṃ appahāya, pāpamittataṃ appahāya – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme appahāya abhabbo assaddhiyaṃ pahātuṃ avadaññutaṃ pahātuṃ kosajjaṃ pahātuṃ.

Bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning faithlessness, abandoning ingratitude, and abandoning laziness. What three? Without having abandoned disrespect, without having abandoned being difficult to admonish, without having abandoned friendship with the wicked. Indeed, bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning faithlessness, abandoning ingratitude, and abandoning laziness.

“Tayome, bhikkhave, dhamme appahāya abhabbo anādariyaṃ pahātuṃ dovacassataṃ pahātuṃ pāpamittataṃ pahātuṃ. Katame tayo? Ahirikaṃ appahāya, anottappaṃ appahāya, pamādaṃ appahāya – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme appahāya abhabbo anādariyaṃ pahātuṃ dovacassataṃ pahātuṃ pāpamittataṃ pahātuṃ.

Bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning disrespect, abandoning being difficult to admonish, and abandoning friendship with the wicked. What three? Without having abandoned lack of moral shame, without having abandoned lack of moral dread, without having abandoned heedlessness. Indeed, bhikkhus, without having abandoned these three phenomena, one is incapable of abandoning disrespect, abandoning being difficult to admonish, and abandoning friendship with the wicked.

“Ahirikoyaṃ, bhikkhave, anottāpī pamatto hoti. So pamatto samāno abhabbo anādariyaṃ pahātuṃ dovacassataṃ pahātuṃ pāpamittataṃ pahātuṃ. So pāpamitto samāno abhabbo assaddhiyaṃ pahātuṃ avadaññutaṃ pahātuṃ kosajjaṃ pahātuṃ. So kusīto samāno abhabbo uddhaccaṃ pahātuṃ asaṃvaraṃ pahātuṃ dussīlyaṃ pahātuṃ. So dussīlo samāno abhabbo ariyānaṃ adassanakamyataṃ pahātuṃ ariyadhammassa asotukamyataṃ pahātuṃ upārambhacittataṃ pahātuṃ. So upārambhacitto samāno abhabbo muṭṭhasaccaṃ pahātuṃ asampajaññaṃ pahātuṃ cetaso vikkhepaṃ pahātuṃ. So vikkhittacitto [P 5.0147] samāno abhabbo ayonisomanasikāraṃ pahātuṃ kummaggasevanaṃ pahātuṃ cetaso līnattaṃ pahātuṃ. So līnacitto samāno [T 5.0157] abhabbo sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ pahātuṃ vicikicchaṃ pahātuṃ sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ pahātuṃ. So vicikiccho samāno abhabbo rāgaṃ pahātuṃ dosaṃ [M 3.0373] pahātuṃ mohaṃ pahātuṃ. So rāgaṃ appahāya dosaṃ appahāya mohaṃ appahāya abhabbo jātiṃ pahātuṃ jaraṃ pahātuṃ maraṇaṃ pahātuṃ.

Monks, this one is shameless, without moral dread, and heedless. Being heedless, one is incapable of abandoning disrespect, resistance to correction, and having evil friends. Having evil friends, one is incapable of abandoning faithlessness, stinginess, and laziness. Being lazy, one is incapable of abandoning restlessness, lack of restraint, and immorality. Being immoral, one is incapable of abandoning unwillingness to see the noble ones, unwillingness to hear the noble Dhamma, and a censorious mind. Having a censorious mind, one is incapable of abandoning lapsed mindfulness, lack of clear comprehension, and mental distraction. With a distracted mind, one is incapable of abandoning unwise attention, following the wrong path, and mental sluggishness. With a sluggish mind, one is incapable of abandoning identity view, doubt, and grasping at rites and rituals. Being doubtful, one is incapable of abandoning lust, hatred, and delusion. Without abandoning lust, hatred, and delusion, one is incapable of abandoning birth, aging, and death.

“Tayome, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo jātiṃ pahātuṃ jaraṃ pahātuṃ maraṇaṃ pahātuṃ. Katame tayo? Rāgaṃ pahāya, dosaṃ pahāya, mohaṃ pahāya – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme pahāya bhabbo jātiṃ pahātuṃ jaraṃ pahātuṃ maraṇaṃ pahātuṃ.

Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning birth, aging, and death. What three? By abandoning lust, hatred, and delusion. Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning birth, aging, and death.

“Tayome, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo rāgaṃ pahātuṃ dosaṃ pahātuṃ mohaṃ pahātuṃ. Katame tayo[V 3.0122]? Sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ pahāya, vicikicchaṃ pahāya, sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ pahāya – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme pahāya bhabbo rāgaṃ pahātuṃ dosaṃ pahātuṃ mohaṃ pahātuṃ.

Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning lust, hatred, and delusion. What three? By abandoning identity view, doubt, and grasping at rites and rituals. Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning lust, hatred, and delusion.

“Tayome, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ pahātuṃ vicikicchaṃ pahātuṃ sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ pahātuṃ. Katame tayo? Ayonisomanasikāraṃ pahāya, kummaggasevanaṃ pahāya, cetaso līnattaṃ pahāya – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme pahāya bhabbo sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ pahātuṃ vicikicchaṃ pahātuṃ sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ pahātuṃ.

Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning identity view, doubt, and grasping at rites and rituals. What three? By abandoning unwise attention, following the wrong path, and mental sluggishness. Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning identity view, doubt, and grasping at rites and rituals.

“Tayome, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo ayonisomanasikāraṃ pahātuṃ kummaggasevanaṃ pahātuṃ cetaso līnattaṃ pahātuṃ. Katame tayo? Muṭṭhasaccaṃ pahāya, asampajaññaṃ pahāya, cetaso vikkhepaṃ pahāya – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme pahāya bhabbo ayonisomanasikāraṃ pahātuṃ kummaggasevanaṃ pahātuṃ [T 5.0158] cetaso līnattaṃ pahātuṃ.

Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning unwise attention, following the wrong path, and mental sluggishness. What three? By abandoning lapsed mindfulness, lack of clear comprehension, and mental distraction. Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning unwise attention, following the wrong path, and mental sluggishness.

“Tayome[P 5.0148], bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo muṭṭhasaccaṃ pahātuṃ asampajaññaṃ pahātuṃ cetaso vikkhepaṃ pahātuṃ. Katame tayo? Ariyānaṃ adassanakamyataṃ pahāya, ariyadhammassa asotukamyataṃ pahāya, upārambhacittataṃ pahāya – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme pahāya bhabbo muṭṭhassaccaṃ pahātuṃ asampajaññaṃ pahātuṃ cetaso vikkhepaṃ pahātuṃ.

Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning lapsed mindfulness, lack of clear comprehension, and mental distraction. What three? By abandoning unwillingness to see the noble ones, unwillingness to hear the noble Dhamma, and a censorious mind. Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning lapsed mindfulness, lack of clear comprehension, and mental distraction.

“Tayome, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo ariyānaṃ adassanakamyataṃ pahātuṃ ariyadhammassa asotukamyataṃ pahātuṃ upārambhacittataṃ pahātuṃ. Katame tayo? Uddhaccaṃ pahāya, asaṃvaraṃ pahāya, dussīlyaṃ pahāya – ime [M 3.0374] kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme pahāya bhabbo ariyānaṃ adassanakamyataṃ pahātuṃ ariyadhammassa asotukamyataṃ pahātuṃ upārambhacittataṃ pahātuṃ.

Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning unwillingness to see the noble ones, unwillingness to hear the noble Dhamma, and a censorious mind. What three? By abandoning restlessness, lack of restraint, and immorality. Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning unwillingness to see the noble ones, unwillingness to hear the noble Dhamma, and a censorious mind.

“Tayome, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo uddhaccaṃ pahātuṃ asaṃvaraṃ pahātuṃ dussīlyaṃ pahātuṃ. Katame tayo? Assaddhiyaṃ pahāya, avadaññutaṃ pahāya, kosajjaṃ pahāya – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme pahāya bhabbo uddhaccaṃ pahātuṃ asaṃvaraṃ pahātuṃ dussīlyaṃ pahātuṃ.

Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning restlessness, lack of restraint, and immorality. What three? By abandoning faithlessness, stinginess, and laziness. Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning restlessness, lack of restraint, and immorality.

“Tayome, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo assaddhiyaṃ pahātuṃ avadaññutaṃ pahātuṃ kosajjaṃ [V 3.0123] pahātuṃ. Katame tayo? Anādariyaṃ pahāya, dovacassataṃ pahāya, pāpamittataṃ pahāya – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme [T 5.0159] pahāya bhabbo assaddhiyaṃ pahātuṃ avadaññutaṃ pahātuṃ kosajjaṃ pahātuṃ.

Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning faithlessness, stinginess, and laziness. What three? By abandoning disrespect, resistance to correction, and having evil friends. Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning faithlessness, stinginess, and laziness.

“Tayome, bhikkhave, dhamme pahāya bhabbo anādariyaṃ pahātuṃ dovacassataṃ pahātuṃ pāpamittataṃ pahātuṃ. Katame tayo? Ahirikaṃ pahāya, anottappaṃ pahāya, pamādaṃ pahāya – ime kho, bhikkhave, tayo dhamme pahāya bhabbo anādariyaṃ pahātuṃ dovacassataṃ pahātuṃ pāpamittataṃ pahātuṃ.

Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning disrespect, resistance to correction, and having evil friends. What three? By abandoning shamelessness, lack of moral dread, and heedlessness. Monks, by abandoning these three things, one is capable of abandoning disrespect, resistance to correction, and having evil friends.

“Hirīmāyaṃ, bhikkhave, ottāpī appamatto hoti. So appamatto samāno bhabbo anādariyaṃ pahātuṃ dovacassataṃ pahātuṃ pāpamittataṃ pahātuṃ. So kalyāṇamitto samāno [P 5.0149] bhabbo assaddhiyaṃ pahātuṃ avadaññutaṃ pahātuṃ kosajjaṃ pahātuṃ. So āraddhavīriyo samāno bhabbo uddhaccaṃ pahātuṃ asaṃvaraṃ pahātuṃ dussīlyaṃ pahātuṃ. So sīlavā samāno bhabbo ariyānaṃ adassanakamyataṃ pahātuṃ ariyadhammassa asotukamyataṃ pahātuṃ upārambhacittataṃ pahātuṃ. So anupārambhacitto samāno bhabbo muṭṭhassaccaṃ pahātuṃ asampajaññaṃ pahātuṃ cetaso vikkhepaṃ pahātuṃ. So avikkhittacitto samāno bhabbo ayonisomanasikāraṃ pahātuṃ kummaggasevanaṃ pahātuṃ cetaso līnattaṃ pahātuṃ. So alīnacitto samāno bhabbo sakkāyadiṭṭhiṃ pahātuṃ vicikicchaṃ pahātuṃ sīlabbataparāmāsaṃ pahātuṃ. So avicikiccho samāno bhabbo rāgaṃ pahātuṃ dosaṃ pahātuṃ mohaṃ pahātuṃ. So rāgaṃ pahāya [M 3.0375] dosaṃ pahāya mohaṃ pahāya bhabbo jātiṃ pahātuṃ jaraṃ pahātuṃ maraṇaṃ pahātu”nti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, one who has a sense of shame and moral dread is heedful. Being heedful, one is capable of abandoning disrespect, intractability, and bad friendship. Having good friends, one is capable of abandoning lack of faith, unreceptiveness, and laziness. Having aroused energy, one is capable of abandoning restlessness, non-restraint, and bad conduct. Being virtuous, one is capable of abandoning unwillingness to see the noble ones, unwillingness to hear the noble Dhamma, and a critical mind. With an uncritical mind, one is capable of abandoning lapsed mindfulness, lack of clear comprehension, and mental distraction. With an undistracted mind, one is capable of abandoning unwise attention, resorting to a wrong path, and mental sluggishness. With an unsluggish mind, one is capable of abandoning identity view, doubt, and clinging to rites and observances. Being free from doubt, one is capable of abandoning lust, hatred, and delusion. Having abandoned lust, hatred, and delusion, one is capable of abandoning birth, aging, and death.” Sixth.

7. Kākasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Crow

77. “Dasahi, bhikkhave, asaddhammehi samannāgato kāko. Katamehi dasahi? Dhaṃsī ca, pagabbho ca, tintiṇo nillajjo (ka.) tintiṇoti tintiṇaṃ vuccati taṇhā… (sī. syā. aṭṭha.) abhidhamme khuddakavatthuvibhaṅge tintiṇapadaniddese passitabbaṃ ca, mahagghaso ca, luddo ca, akāruṇiko ca, dubbalo ca, oravitā ca, muṭṭhassati ca, necayiko nerasiko (sī.) tadaṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana “necayiko” tveva dissati ca – imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi asaddhammehi samannāgato kāko. Evamevaṃ kho[T 5.0160], bhikkhave, dasahi asaddhammehi samannāgato pāpabhikkhu. Katamehi dasahi? Dhaṃsī ca, pagabbho ca, tintiṇo ca, mahagghaso ca, luddo ca, akāruṇiko [V 3.0124] ca, dubbalo ca, oravitā ca, muṭṭhassati ca, necayiko ca – imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi asaddhammehi samannāgato pāpabhikkhū”ti. Sattamaṃ.

77. “Bhikkhus, a crow is endowed with ten qualities of an untrue person. What ten? It is destructive, bold, greedy, gluttonous, cruel, uncompassionate, weak, clamorous, of lapsed mindfulness, and one who does not store things up. These, bhikkhus, are the ten qualities of an untrue person with which a crow is endowed. In the same way, bhikkhus, a wicked bhikkhu is endowed with ten qualities of an untrue person. What ten? He is destructive, bold, greedy, gluttonous, cruel, uncompassionate, weak, clamorous, of lapsed mindfulness, and one who does not store things up. These, bhikkhus, are the ten qualities of an untrue person with which a wicked bhikkhu is endowed.” Seventh.

8. Nigaṇṭhasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Nigaṇṭhas

78. “Dasahi[P 5.0150], bhikkhave, asaddhammehi samannāgatā nigaṇṭhā. Katamehi dasahi? Assaddhā, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā; dussīlā, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā; ahirikā, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā; anottappino, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā; asappurisasambhattino, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā; attukkaṃsakaparavambhakā, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā; sandiṭṭhiparāmāsā ādhānaggāhī duppaṭinissaggino, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā; kuhakā, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā; pāpicchā, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā; pāpamittā, bhikkhave, nigaṇṭhā – imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi asaddhammehi samannāgatā nigaṇṭhā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

78. “Bhikkhus, the Nigaṇṭhas are endowed with ten qualities of an untrue person. What ten? Bhikkhus, the Nigaṇṭhas are faithless; bhikkhus, the Nigaṇṭhas are immoral; bhikkhus, the Nigaṇṭhas are shameless; bhikkhus, the Nigaṇṭhas are without moral dread; bhikkhus, the Nigaṇṭhas associate with untrue persons; bhikkhus, the Nigaṇṭhas praise themselves and disparage others; bhikkhus, the Nigaṇṭhas wrongly grasp their own views, hold to them firmly, and abandon them with difficulty; bhikkhus, the Nigaṇṭhas are deceitful; bhikkhus, the Nigaṇṭhas have evil desires; bhikkhus, the Nigaṇṭhas have bad friends. These, bhikkhus, are the ten qualities of an untrue person with which the Nigaṇṭhas are endowed.” Eighth.

9. Āghātavatthusuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Grounds for Resentment

79. a. ni. 9.29 “Dasayimāni, bhikkhave, āghātavatthūni. Katamāni dasa? ‘Anatthaṃ me acarī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati; ‘anatthaṃ me caratī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati; ‘anatthaṃ me carissatī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati; ‘piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acarī’ti…pe… ‘anatthaṃ caratī’ti…pe… ‘anatthaṃ carissatī’ti āghātaṃ bandhati, ‘appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acarī’ti…pe… ‘atthaṃ caratī’ti…pe… ‘atthaṃ carissatī’ti [M 3.0376] āghātaṃ bandhati; aṭṭhāne ca kuppati – imāni kho, bhikkhave, dasa āghātavatthūnī”ti. Navamaṃ.

79. “Bhikkhus, there are these ten grounds for harboring resentment. What ten? Thinking, ‘This person has acted to my detriment,’ one harbors resentment. Thinking, ‘This person is acting to my detriment,’ one harbors resentment. Thinking, ‘This person will act to my detriment,’ one harbors resentment. Thinking, ‘This person has acted to the detriment of one who is dear and agreeable to me’ … ‘is acting to the detriment’ … ‘will act to the detriment,’ one harbors resentment. Thinking, ‘This person has acted for the welfare of one who is not dear and is disagreeable to me’ … ‘is acting for the welfare’ … ‘will act for the welfare,’ one harbors resentment. And one becomes angry without cause. These, bhikkhus, are the ten grounds for harboring resentment.” Ninth.

10. Āghātapaṭivinayasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Dispelling Resentment

80. “Dasayime[T 5.0161], bhikkhave, āghātapaṭivinayā. Katame dasa? ‘Anatthaṃ me acari, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṃ paṭivineti[P 5.0151], ‘anatthaṃ me carati, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṃ paṭivineti, ‘anatthaṃ me carissati, taṃ kutettha labbhā’ti āghātaṃ paṭivineti, piyassa me manāpassa anatthaṃ acari…pe… carati…pe… carissati, taṃ kutettha labbhāti āghātaṃ paṭivineti[V 3.0125], appiyassa me amanāpassa atthaṃ acari…pe… atthaṃ carati…pe… atthaṃ carissati, taṃ kutettha labbhāti āghātaṃ paṭivineti, aṭṭhāne ca na kuppati – ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa āghātapaṭivinayā”ti. Dasamaṃ.

80. “Bhikkhus, there are these ten ways of dispelling resentment. What ten? Thinking, ‘This person has acted to my detriment, but what is to be gained from that?’ one dispels resentment. Thinking, ‘This person is acting to my detriment, but what is to be gained from that?’ one dispels resentment. Thinking, ‘This person will act to my detriment, but what is to be gained from that?’ one dispels resentment. Thinking, ‘This person has acted to the detriment of one who is dear and pleasing to me’ … ‘is acting’ … ‘will act, but what is to be gained from that?’ one dispels resentment. Thinking, ‘This person has acted for the welfare of one who is not dear or pleasing to me’ … ‘is acting for the welfare’ … ‘will act for the welfare, but what is to be gained from that?’ one dispels resentment. And one does not get angry without cause. These, bhikkhus, are the ten ways of dispelling resentment.” Tenth.

Ākaṅkhavaggo tatiyo.

The Third Chapter on Wishes.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Ākaṅkho kaṇṭako iṭṭhā, vaḍḍhi ca migasālāya;

Tayo dhammā ca kāko ca, nigaṇṭhā dve ca āghātāti.

Wish, Thorn, and Desired, Growth and Migasālā; Three Dhammas and the Crow, Nigaṇṭhas, and two on Resentment.

(9) 4. Theravaggo

4. The Chapter on the Elders

1. Vāhanasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Vāhana

81. Ekaṃ [V 3.0126] samayaṃ bhagavā campāyaṃ viharati gaggarāya pokkharaṇiyā tīre. Atha kho āyasmā vāhano yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā vāhano bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “katihi nu kho, bhante, dhammehi tathāgato nissaṭo visaṃyutto vippamutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā [T 5.0162] viharatī”ti?

81. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Campā on the bank of the Gaggarā lotus pond. Then the Venerable Vāhana approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the Venerable Vāhana said to the Blessed One: “Venerable Sir, from how many things is the Tathāgata departed, disjoined, and released, dwelling with a mind made limitless?”

“Dasahi [P 5.0152] kho, vāhana, dhammehi tathāgato nissaṭo visaṃyutto vippamutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharati. Katamehi dasahi? Rūpena kho, vāhana, tathāgato nissaṭo visaṃyutto vippamutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā [M 3.0377] viharati, vedanāya kho, vāhana…pe… saññāya kho, vāhana… saṅkhārehi kho, vāhana… viññāṇena kho, vāhana… jātiyā kho, vāhana… jarāya kho, vāhana… maraṇena kho, vāhana… dukkhehi kho, vāhana… kilesehi kho, vāhana, tathāgato nissaṭo visaṃyutto vippamutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharati. Seyyathāpi, vāhana, uppalaṃ vā padumaṃ vā puṇḍarīkaṃ vā udake jātaṃ udake saṃvaḍḍhaṃ udakā paccuggamma ṭhitaṃ anupalittaṃ udakena; evamevaṃ kho, vāhana, imehi dasahi dhammehi tathāgato nissaṭo visaṃyutto vippamutto vimariyādīkatena cetasā viharatī”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Vāhana, it is from ten dhammas that the Tathāgata is departed, disjoined, and released, dwelling with a mind made limitless. What ten? From form, Vāhana, the Tathāgata is departed, disjoined, and released, dwelling with a mind made limitless. From feeling… from perception… from formations… from consciousness… from birth… from aging… from death… from sufferings… from defilements, Vāhana, the Tathāgata is departed, disjoined, and released, dwelling with a mind made limitless. Just as, Vāhana, a blue lotus, a red lotus, or a white lotus is born in the water and grows up in the water, but stands risen above the water, unsoiled by the water; so too, Vāhana, from these ten dhammas, the Tathāgata is departed, disjoined, and released, dwelling with a mind made limitless.” First.

2. Ānandasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse concerning Ānanda

82. Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ bhagavā etadavoca –

82. Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. The Blessed One said this to the Venerable Ānanda as he was sitting to one side:

“So [V 3.0127] vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘assaddho samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu who is faithless might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is not possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘dussīlo samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu who is immoral might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is not possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘appassuto samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu who has learned little might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is not possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘dubbaco samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ [P 5.0153] virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti [T 5.0163] netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu who is difficult to admonish might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is not possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘pāpamitto samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu with bad friends might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is not possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘kusīto samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu who is lazy might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is not possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘muṭṭhassati samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu who is unmindful might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is not possible.

“So [M 3.0378] vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘asantuṭṭho samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu who is discontented might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is not possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘pāpiccho samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu of evil wishes might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is not possible.

“So [V 3.0128] vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘micchādiṭṭhiko samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu of wrong view might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is not possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘imehi dasahi dhammehi samannāgato imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu endowed with these ten qualities might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is not possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘saddho samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu who is faithful might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘sīlavā samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu who is virtuous might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘bahussuto sutadharo samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu who is very learned and retains what he has learned might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘suvaco samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu who is easy to admonish might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘kalyāṇamitto samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye [T 5.0164] vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu with good friends might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘āraddhavīriyo samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu with aroused energy might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘upaṭṭhitassati samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti [P 5.0154] ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu with established mindfulness might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is possible.

“So [V 3.0129] vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘santuṭṭho samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu who is content might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘appiccho samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu of few wishes might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is possible.

“So [M 3.0379] vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘sammādiṭṭhiko samāno imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṃ vijjati.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu of right view might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is possible.

“So vatānanda, bhikkhu ‘imehi dasahi dhammehi samannāgato imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Ānanda, that a bhikkhu endowed with these ten qualities might achieve growth, increase, and fullness in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is possible.” Second.

3. Puṇṇiyasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse concerning Puṇṇiya

83. Atha kho āyasmā puṇṇiyo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho āyasmā puṇṇiyo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bhante, hetu ko paccayo yena appekadā tathāgataṃ dhammadesanā paṭibhāti appekadā nappaṭibhātī”ti?

83. Then the Venerable Puṇṇiya went to the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the Venerable Puṇṇiya said to the Blessed One: 'Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason why sometimes a Dhamma discourse occurs to the Tathāgata and sometimes it does not occur?'

“Saddho ca, puṇṇiya, bhikkhu hoti, no ca upasaṅkamitā; neva tāva tathāgataṃ dhammadesanā paṭibhāti. Yato ca kho, puṇṇiya, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti upasaṅkamitā ca, evaṃ tathāgataṃ [T 5.0165] dhammadesanā paṭibhāti.

“Puṇṇiya, a bhikkhu is faithful, but he is not one who approaches; to that extent, a Dhamma discourse does not occur to the Tathāgata. But when, Puṇṇiya, a bhikkhu is both faithful and one who approaches, in that case a Dhamma discourse occurs to the Tathāgata.

“Saddho ca, puṇṇiya, bhikkhu hoti upasaṅkamitā ca, no ca payirupāsitā…pe… payirupāsitā ca, no ca paripucchitā… paripucchitā ca, no ca ohitasoto dhammaṃ suṇāti… ohitasoto ca dhammaṃ suṇāti, no ca sutvā dhammaṃ dhāreti… sutvā ca dhammaṃ dhāreti, no ca dhātānaṃ dhammānaṃ atthaṃ upaparikkhati… dhātānañca dhammānaṃ atthaṃ upaparikkhati no ca atthamaññāya [P 5.0155] dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammappaṭipanno hoti… atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammappaṭipanno [V 3.0130] ca hoti, no ca kalyāṇavāco hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagaḷāya atthassa viññāpaniyā… kalyāṇavāco ca hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagaḷāya atthassa viññāpaniyā, no ca sandassako hoti samādapako samuttejako sampahaṃsako sabrahmacārīnaṃ, neva tāva tathāgataṃ dhammadesanā paṭibhāti.

“Puṇṇiya, a bhikkhu is faithful and one who approaches, but is not one who attends upon him… he attends upon him, but is not one who questions… he questions, but does not listen to the Dhamma with an attentive ear… he listens to the Dhamma with an attentive ear, but having heard the Dhamma, does not retain it… having heard the Dhamma, he retains it, but does not investigate the meaning of the teachings he has retained… he investigates the meaning of the teachings he has retained, but having understood the meaning and the Dhamma, he does not practice in accordance with the Dhamma… having understood the meaning and the Dhamma, he practices in accordance with the Dhamma, but he is not of good speech, of good elocution, endowed with urbane, clear, and flawless speech that makes the meaning known… he is of good speech, of good elocution, endowed with urbane, clear, and flawless speech that makes the meaning known, but he is not one who instructs, establishes, incites, and gladdens his companions in the holy life; to that extent, a Dhamma discourse does not occur to the Tathāgata.

“Yato ca kho, puṇṇiya, bhikkhu saddho ca hoti, upasaṅkamitā ca, payirupāsitā ca, paripucchitā ca, ohitasoto ca dhammaṃ suṇāti, sutvā ca dhammaṃ dhāreti, dhātānañca dhammānaṃ atthaṃ upaparikkhati, atthamaññāya dhammamaññāya dhammānudhammappaṭipanno [M 3.0380] ca hoti, kalyāṇavāco ca hoti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo poriyā vācāya samannāgato vissaṭṭhāya anelagaḷāya atthassa viññāpaniyā, sandassako ca hoti samādapako samuttejako sampahaṃsako sabrahmacārīnaṃ – evaṃ tathāgataṃ dhammadesanā paṭibhāti. Imehi kho, puṇṇiya[T 5.0166], dasahi dhammehi samannāgatā samannāgato (ka.) ekantaṃ tathāgataṃ dhammadesanā paṭibhātīti (syā.) ekantapaṭibhānā ekantapaṭibhānaṃ (sī.) tathāgataṃ dhammadesanā hotī”ti ekantaṃ tathāgataṃ dhammadesanā paṭibhātīti (syā.). Tatiyaṃ.

“But when, Puṇṇiya, a bhikkhu is faithful, one who approaches, one who attends upon him, one who questions, one who listens to the Dhamma with an attentive ear, one who having heard the Dhamma retains it, one who investigates the meaning of the teachings he has retained, one who having understood the meaning and the Dhamma practices in accordance with the Dhamma, one who is of good speech, of good elocution, endowed with urbane, clear, and flawless speech that makes the meaning known, and one who instructs, establishes, incites, and gladdens his companions in the holy life—in that case a Dhamma discourse occurs to the Tathāgata. Puṇṇiya, when one is endowed with these ten qualities, a Dhamma discourse occurs to the Tathāgata with certainty.” Third.

4. Byākaraṇasuttaṃ

4. The Sutta on Declaration

84. Tatra kho āyasmā mahāmoggallāno bhikkhū āmantesi – “āvuso bhikkhave”ti. “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahāmoggallānassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā mahāmoggallāno etadavoca –

84. There, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna addressed the bhikkhus: 'Friends, bhikkhus!' 'Yes, friend,' those bhikkhus replied. The Venerable Mahāmoggallāna said this:

“Idhāvuso, bhikkhu aññaṃ byākaroti – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti. Tamenaṃ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako [P 5.0156] vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo samanuyuñjati samanuggāhati samanubhāsati. So tathāgatena vā tathāgatasāvakena vā jhāyinā samāpattikusalena paracittakusalena paracittapariyāyakusalena samanuyuñjiyamāno samanuggāhiyamāno samanubhāsiyamāno irīṇaṃ āpajjati vicinaṃ visinaṃ (sī. aṭṭha.) āpajjati anayaṃ āpajjati byasanaṃ āpajjati anayabyasanaṃ āpajjati.

“Here, friends, a bhikkhu makes a declaration of final knowledge: ‘I understand: “Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.”’ The Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata—one who attains jhāna, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, skilled in the courses of the minds of others—cross-questions, interrogates, and questions him thoroughly. Being cross-questioned, interrogated, and questioned thoroughly by the Tathāgata or his disciple, he is reduced to a barren state, comes to perplexity, and falls into misfortune and disaster.

“Tamenaṃ [V 3.0131] tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṃ cetasā ceto paricca manasi karoti – ‘kiṃ nu kho ayamāyasmā aññaṃ byākaroti – khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti?

“The Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata—one who attains jhāna, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, skilled in the courses of the minds of others—encompasses that bhikkhu’s mind with his own and gives attention: ‘Why does this venerable one make a declaration of final knowledge: “I understand: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being’”?’

“Tamenaṃ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti –

“The Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata—one who attains jhāna, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, skilled in the courses of the minds of others—having encompassed that bhikkhu’s mind with his own, understands thus:

‘Kodhano [M 3.0381] kho ayamāyasmā; kodhapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā bahulaṃ viharati. Kodhapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye [T 5.0167] parihānametaṃ.

‘Indeed, this venerable one is prone to anger; he often dwells with a mind obsessed by anger. And for a mind to be obsessed by anger is a decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Upanāhī kho pana ayamāyasmā; upanāhapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā bahulaṃ viharati. Upanāhapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘Indeed, this venerable one is resentful; he often dwells with a mind obsessed by resentment. And for a mind to be obsessed by resentment is a decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Makkhī kho pana ayamāyasmā; makkhapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā bahulaṃ viharati. Makkhapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘Indeed, this venerable one is contemptuous; he often dwells with a mind obsessed by contempt. And for a mind to be obsessed by contempt is a decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Paḷāsī kho pana ayamāyasmā; paḷāsapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā bahulaṃ viharati. Paḷāsapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘Indeed, this venerable one is competitive; he often dwells with a mind obsessed by competitiveness. And for a mind to be obsessed by competitiveness is a decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Issukī kho pana ayamāyasmā; issāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā bahulaṃ viharati. Issāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘Indeed, this venerable one is envious; he often dwells with a mind obsessed by envy. And for a mind to be obsessed by envy is a decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Maccharī kho pana ayamāyasmā; maccherapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā bahulaṃ viharati. Maccherapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kho [P 5.0157] pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘Indeed, this venerable one is miserly; he often dwells with a mind obsessed by miserliness. And for a mind to be obsessed by miserliness is a decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Saṭho kho pana ayamāyasmā; sāṭheyyapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā bahulaṃ viharati. Sāṭheyyapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘Indeed, this venerable one is fraudulent; he often dwells with a mind obsessed by fraud. And this obsession with fraud is a cause of decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Māyāvī [V 3.0132] kho pana ayamāyasmā; māyāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā bahulaṃ viharati. Māyāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘Indeed, this venerable one is deceitful; he often dwells with a mind obsessed by deceit. And this obsession with deceit is a cause of decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Pāpiccho kho pana ayamāyasmā; icchāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā bahulaṃ viharati. Icchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘Indeed, this venerable one has evil wishes; he often dwells with a mind obsessed by wishes. And this obsession with wishes is a cause of decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Sati [M 3.0382] muṭṭhassati (sī. syā.) kho pana ayamāyasmā uttari karaṇīye oramattakena visesādhigamena antarā vosānaṃ āpanno. Antarā vosānagamanaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ’.

‘When there is still something further to be done, this venerable one has stopped halfway, having gained some minor distinction. And to stop halfway is a cause of decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.’

“So vatāvuso, bhikkhu ‘ime dasa dhamme appahāya [T 5.0168] imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. So vatāvuso, bhikkhu ‘ime dasa dhamme pahāya imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“Friends, that a monk who has not abandoned these ten qualities should attain growth, development, and abundance in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is impossible. But that a monk who has abandoned these ten qualities should attain growth, development, and abundance in this Dhamma and Discipline—this is possible.” Fourth.

5. Katthīsuttaṃ

5. Discourse on the Boaster

85. Ekaṃ samayaṃ āyasmā mahācundo cetīsu viharati sahajātiyaṃ. Tatra kho āyasmā mahācundo bhikkhū āmantesi – “āvuso bhikkhave”ti. “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahācundassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā mahācundo etadavoca –

85. At one time the Venerable Mahācunda was dwelling among the Cetis at Sahajāti. There the Venerable Mahācunda addressed the monks: “Friends, monks!” “Friend,” those monks replied to the Venerable Mahācunda. The Venerable Mahācunda said this:

“Idhāvuso, bhikkhu katthī hoti vikatthī adhigamesu – ‘ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṃ tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṃ ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ [P 5.0158] samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṃ ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipī’ti.

“Here, friends, a monk is a boaster and a braggart in regard to his attainments, claiming: ‘I enter and emerge from the first jhāna; I enter and emerge from the second jhāna; I enter and emerge from the third jhāna; I enter and emerge from the fourth jhāna; I enter and emerge from the base of infinite space; I enter and emerge from the base of infinite consciousness; I enter and emerge from the base of nothingness; I enter and emerge from the base of neither perception nor non-perception; I enter and emerge from the cessation of perception and feeling.’”

“Tamenaṃ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo [V 3.0133] samanuyuñjati samanuggāhati samanubhāsati. So tathāgatena vā tathāgatasāvakena vā jhāyinā samāpattikusalena paracittakusalena paracittapariyāyakusalena samanuyuñjiyamāno samanuggāhiyamāno samanubhāsiyamāno irīṇaṃ āpajjati vicinaṃ āpajjati anayaṃ āpajjati byasanaṃ āpajjati anayabyasanaṃ āpajjati.

“Then the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata—a meditator, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, skilled in the courses of the minds of others—cross-examines, investigates, and questions him thoroughly. When he is being cross-examined, investigated, and questioned thoroughly by the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata who is a meditator, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, and skilled in the courses of the minds of others, he falls into a barren state, falls into perplexity, falls into misfortune, falls into ruin, falls into misfortune and ruin.”

“Tamenaṃ [T 5.0169][M 3.0383] tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṃ cetasā ceto paricca manasi karoti – ‘kiṃ nu kho ayamāyasmā katthī hoti vikatthī adhigamesu – ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi…pe… ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipī’ti.

“Then the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata—a meditator, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, skilled in the courses of the minds of others—having encompassed that monk’s mind with his own, gives attention thus: ‘For what reason is this venerable one a boaster and a braggart in regard to his attainments, claiming: “I enter and emerge from the first jhāna … I enter and emerge from the cessation of perception and feeling”?’”

“Tamenaṃ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti –

“Then the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata—a meditator, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, skilled in the courses of the minds of others—having encompassed that monk’s mind with his own, understands thus:

‘Dīgharattaṃ kho ayamāyasmā khaṇḍakārī chiddakārī sabalakārī kammāsakārī na santatakārī na santatavutti sīlesu. Dussīlo kho ayamāyasmā. Dussilyaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

“‘For a long time this venerable one has been one who breaks his virtue, makes it holey, spotted, and blotchy; he has not been one who acts consistently and comports himself consistently in regard to the rules of moral conduct. This venerable one is immoral. And immorality is a cause of decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Assaddho kho pana ayamāyasmā; assaddhiyaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

“‘This venerable one is faithless. And faithlessness is a cause of decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Appassuto kho pana ayamāyasmā anācāro; appasaccaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ[P 5.0159].

“‘This venerable one is unlearned and of bad conduct. And being unlearned is a cause of decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Dubbaco kho pana ayamāyasmā; dovacassatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

“‘This venerable one is difficult to correct. And difficulty in being corrected is a cause of decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Pāpamitto kho pana ayamāyasmā; pāpamittatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

“‘This venerable one has bad friends. And having bad friends is a cause of decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Kusīto [V 3.0134] kho pana ayamāyasmā; kosajjaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

“‘This venerable one is lazy. And laziness is a cause of decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Muṭṭhassati kho pana ayamāyasmā; muṭṭhassaccaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

“‘This venerable one is unmindful. And unmindfulness is a cause of decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Kuhako kho pana ayamāyasmā; kohaññaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

“‘This venerable one is deceitful. And deceit is a cause of decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Dubbharo kho pana ayamāyasmā; dubbharatā kho [T 5.0170] pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

“‘This venerable one is difficult to support. And being difficult to support is a cause of decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Duppañño [M 3.0384] kho pana ayamāyasmā; duppaññatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ’.

“‘This venerable one is unwise. And unwisdom is a cause of decline in the Dhamma and Discipline proclaimed by the Tathāgata.’

“Seyyathāpi, āvuso, sahāyako sahāyakaṃ evaṃ vadeyya – ‘yadā te, samma, dhanena bandho (ka.) dhanakaraṇīyaṃ assa, yāceyyāsi maṃ yācissasi maṃ (sī.), pavedeyyāsi maṃ (syā.), parājeyyāpi maṃ (ka.) dhanaṃ. Dassāmi te dhana’nti. So kiñcideva dhanakaraṇīye samuppanne sahāyako sahāyakaṃ evaṃ vadeyya – ‘attho me, samma, dhanena. Dehi me dhana’nti. So evaṃ vadeyya – ‘tena hi, samma, idha khanāhī’ti. So tatra khananto nādhigaccheyya. So evaṃ vadeyya – ‘alikaṃ maṃ, samma, avaca; tucchakaṃ maṃ, samma, avaca – idha khanāhī’ti. So evaṃ vadeyya – ‘nāhaṃ taṃ, samma, alikaṃ avacaṃ, tucchakaṃ avacaṃ. Tena hi, samma, idha khanāhī’ti. So tatrapi khananto nādhigaccheyya. So evaṃ vadeyya – ‘alikaṃ maṃ, samma, avaca, tucchakaṃ maṃ, samma, avaca – idha khanāhī’ti. So evaṃ vadeyya – ‘nāhaṃ taṃ, samma, alikaṃ avacaṃ, tucchakaṃ avacaṃ[P 5.0160]. Tena hi, samma, idha khanāhī’ti. So tatrapi khananto nādhigaccheyya. So evaṃ vadeyya – ‘alikaṃ maṃ, samma, avaca, tucchakaṃ maṃ, samma, avaca – idha khanāhī’ti. So evaṃ vadeyya – ‘nāhaṃ taṃ, samma, alikaṃ avacaṃ, tucchakaṃ avacaṃ. Api ca ahameva ummādaṃ pāpuṇiṃ cetaso vipariyāya’nti.

Friends, it is just as if a friend were to say to another friend: ‘Friend, whenever you have a need for wealth, you should ask me for wealth. I will give you wealth.’ Then, when some need for wealth arises, that friend says to the other: ‘Friend, I have a need for wealth. Give me wealth.’ The other replies: ‘In that case, friend, dig here.’ But digging there, he does not find it. He says: ‘Friend, you spoke falsely to me; you spoke emptily to me: ‘Dig here.’’ The other replies: ‘Friend, I did not speak falsely to you, nor did I speak emptily. In that case, friend, dig here.’ But digging there too, he does not find it. He says: ‘Friend, you spoke falsely to me; you spoke emptily to me: ‘Dig here.’’ The other replies: ‘Friend, I did not speak falsely to you, nor did I speak emptily. In that case, friend, dig here.’ But digging there too, he does not find it. He says: ‘Friend, you spoke falsely to me; you spoke emptily to me: ‘Dig here.’’ The other replies: ‘Friend, I did not speak falsely to you, nor did I speak emptily. But I myself have gone mad; I have reached a derangement of mind.’

“Evamevaṃ [V 3.0135] kho, āvuso, bhikkhu katthī hoti vikatthī adhigamesu – ‘ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṃ dutiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṃ tatiyaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṃ catutthaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmipi [T 5.0171] vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṃ ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṃ viññāṇañcāyatanaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṃ ākiñcaññāyatanaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṃ nevasaññānāsaññāyatanaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipi, ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipī’ti.

In this very way, friends, a monk is a boaster and a braggart regarding his attainments, saying: ‘I enter upon and emerge from the first jhāna; I enter upon and emerge from the second jhāna; I enter upon and emerge from the third jhāna; I enter upon and emerge from the fourth jhāna; I enter upon and emerge from the base of infinite space; I enter upon and emerge from the base of infinite consciousness; I enter upon and emerge from the base of nothingness; I enter upon and emerge from the base of neither perception nor non-perception; I enter upon and emerge from the cessation of perception and feeling.’

“Tamenaṃ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo samanuyuñjati samanuggāhati samanubhāsati. So tathāgatena vā tathāgatasāvakena vā jhāyinā samāpattikusalena paracittakusalena paracittapariyāyakusalena samanuyuñjiyamāno samanuggāhiyamāno samanubhāsiyamāno irīṇaṃ [M 3.0385] āpajjati vicinaṃ āpajjati anayaṃ āpajjati byasanaṃ āpajjati anayabyasanaṃ āpajjati.

Then the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata—one who is a meditator, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, skilled in the course of the minds of others—questions, interrogates, and admonishes him. When he is being questioned, interrogated, and admonished by the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata who is a meditator, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, and skilled in the course of the minds of others, he falls into a barren state, falls into a state of being found wanting, falls into misfortune, falls into ruin, and falls into misfortune and ruin.

“Tamenaṃ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṃ cetasā ceto paricca manasi karoti – ‘kiṃ nu kho ayamāyasmā katthī hoti vikatthī adhigamesu – ahaṃ paṭhamaṃ jhānaṃ samāpajjāmipi…pe… ahaṃ saññāvedayitanirodhaṃ samāpajjāmipi vuṭṭhahāmipī’ti.

Then the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata—one who is a meditator, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, skilled in the course of the minds of others—having encompassed that monk’s mind with his own, gives attention thus: ‘For what reason, I wonder, is this venerable one a boaster and a braggart in regard to his attainments, saying: “I enter upon and emerge from the first jhāna … I enter upon and emerge from the cessation of perception and feeling”?’

“Tamenaṃ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti –

Then the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata—one who is a meditator, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, skilled in the course of the minds of others—having encompassed that monk’s mind with his own, knows distinctly:

‘Dīgharattaṃ [P 5.0161] kho ayamāyasmā khaṇḍakārī chiddakārī sabalakārī kammāsakārī, na santatakārī na santatavutti sīlesu. Dussīlo kho ayamāyasmā; dussilyaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘For a long time, indeed, this venerable one has been one who breaks his virtue, makes it holey, spotted, and blotchy; he has not been one who acts continuously nor has he been of continuous practice in regard to the precepts. Indeed, this venerable one is immoral. And this immorality, in the Dhamma and Vinaya declared by the Tathāgata, is a cause of decline.

‘Assaddho kho pana ayamāyasmā; assaddhiyaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ[T 5.0172].

‘Indeed, this venerable one is faithless. And this faithlessness, in the Dhamma and Vinaya declared by the Tathāgata, is a cause of decline.

‘Appassuto [V 3.0136] kho pana ayamāyasmā anācāro; appasaccaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘Indeed, this venerable one has little learning and has improper conduct. And this state of having little learning, in the Dhamma and Vinaya declared by the Tathāgata, is a cause of decline.

‘Dubbaco kho pana ayamāyasmā; dovacassatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘Indeed, this venerable one is difficult to admonish. And this state of being difficult to admonish, in the Dhamma and Vinaya declared by the Tathāgata, is a cause of decline.

‘Pāpamitto kho pana ayamāyasmā; pāpamittatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘Indeed, this venerable one has evil friends. And this state of having evil friends, in the Dhamma and Vinaya declared by the Tathāgata, is a cause of decline.

‘Kusīto kho pana ayamāyasmā; kosajjaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘Indeed, this venerable one is lazy. And this laziness, in the Dhamma and Vinaya declared by the Tathāgata, is a cause of decline.

‘Muṭṭhassati kho pana ayamāyasmā; muṭṭhassaccaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘Indeed, this venerable one is of lapsed mindfulness. And this state of having lapsed mindfulness, in the Dhamma and Vinaya declared by the Tathāgata, is a cause of decline.

‘Kuhako kho pana ayamāyasmā; kohaññaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘Indeed, this venerable one is a charlatan. And this charlatanry, in the Dhamma and Vinaya declared by the Tathāgata, is a cause of decline.

‘Dubbharo [M 3.0386] kho pana ayamāyasmā; dubbharatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘Indeed, this venerable one is difficult to support. And this state of being difficult to support, in the Dhamma and Vinaya declared by the Tathāgata, is a cause of decline.

‘Duppañño kho pana ayamāyasmā; duppaññatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ’.

‘Indeed, this venerable one is unwise. And this unwisdom is a decline in the Dhamma and Vinaya declared by the Tathāgata.’

“So vatāvuso, bhikkhu ‘ime dasa dhamme appahāya imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. So vatāvuso, bhikkhu ‘ime dasa dhamme pahāya imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

Indeed, friends, that a monk, without having abandoned these ten qualities, will attain growth, development, and abundance in this Dhamma and Vinaya—this is not possible. Indeed, friends, that a monk, having abandoned these ten qualities, will attain growth, development, and abundance in this Dhamma and Vinaya—this is possible. The fifth.

6. Adhimānasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on Conceit

86. Ekaṃ [V 3.0137] samayaṃ āyasmā mahākassapo rājagahe viharati veḷuvane kalandakanivāpe. Tatra kho āyasmā mahākassapo [P 5.0162] bhikkhū āmantesi – “āvuso bhikkhave”ti. “Āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahākassapassa paccassosuṃ. Āyasmā mahākassapo etadavoca –

86. At one time the Venerable Mahākassapa was dwelling at Rājagaha, in the Bamboo Grove, the Squirrels’ Sanctuary. There the Venerable Mahākassapa addressed the bhikkhus: ‘Friends, bhikkhus.’ ‘Friend,’ those bhikkhus replied to the Venerable Mahākassapa. The Venerable Mahākassapa said this:

“Idhāvuso, bhikkhu aññaṃ [T 5.0173] byākaroti – ‘khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti. Tamenaṃ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo samanuyuñjati samanuggāhati samanubhāsati. So tathāgatena vā tathāgatasāvakena vā jhāyinā samāpattikusalena paracittakusalena paracittapariyāyakusalena samanuyuñjiyamāno samanuggāhiyamāno samanubhāsiyamāno irīṇaṃ āpajjati vicinaṃ āpajjati anayaṃ āpajjati byasanaṃ āpajjati anayabyasanaṃ āpajjati.

Here, friends, a bhikkhu makes a declaration of final knowledge: ‘Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being, I understand.’ Then the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata—one accomplished in jhāna, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, skilled in the ways of others’ minds—questions him, presses him, and cross-examines him. Being questioned, pressed, and cross-examined by the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata—one accomplished in jhāna, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, skilled in the ways of others’ minds—he falls into a barren state, falls into worthlessness, falls into misfortune, falls into ruin, falls into misfortune and ruin.

“Tamenaṃ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṃ cetasā ceto paricca manasi karoti – ‘kiṃ nu kho ayamāyasmā aññaṃ byākaroti – khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.

Then the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata—one accomplished in jhāna, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, skilled in the ways of others’ minds—having encompassed that person’s mind with his own mind, gives attention thus: ‘Why now does this venerable one make a declaration of final knowledge: “Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being, I understand”?’

“Tamenaṃ [M 3.0387] tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti –

Then the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata—one accomplished in jhāna, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, skilled in the ways of others’ minds—having encompassed that person’s mind with his own mind, understands thus:

‘Adhimāniko kho ayamāyasmā adhimānasacco, appatte pattasaññī, akate katasaññī, anadhigate adhigatasaññī. Adhimānena aññaṃ byākaroti – khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.

‘This venerable one is conceited, one whose assertion is based on conceit; he perceives the unattained as attained, the undone as done, the unrealized as realized. Through conceit he makes a declaration of final knowledge: “Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being, I understand.”’

“Tamenaṃ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo [V 3.0138] evaṃ cetasā ceto paricca manasi karoti – ‘kiṃ nu kho ayamāyasmā nissāya adhimāniko adhimānasacco, appatte pattasaññī, akate katasaññī, anadhigate adhigatasaññī. Adhimānena [T 5.0174] aññaṃ byākaroti – khīṇā jāti[P 5.0163], vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.

Then the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata—one accomplished in jhāna, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, skilled in the ways of others’ minds—having encompassed that person’s mind with his own mind, gives attention thus: ‘Relying on what is this venerable one conceited, holding conceit as truth, perceiving the unattained as attained, the undone as done, the unrealized as realized? Through conceit he makes a declaration of final knowledge: “Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being, I understand.”’

“Tamenaṃ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti –

Then the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata—one accomplished in jhāna, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, skilled in the ways of others’ minds—having encompassed that person’s mind with his own mind, understands thus:

‘Bahussuto kho pana ayamāyasmā sutadharo sutasannicayo, ye te dhammā ādikalyāṇā majjhekalyāṇā pariyosānakalyāṇā sātthaṃ sabyañjanaṃ kevalaparipuṇṇaṃ parisuddhaṃ brahmacariyaṃ abhivadanti, tathārūpāssa dhammā bahussutā honti dhātā vacasā paricitā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhā. Tasmā ayamāyasmā adhimāniko adhimānasacco, appatte pattasaññī, akate katasaññī, anadhigate adhigatasaññī. Adhimānena aññaṃ byākaroti – khīṇā jāti, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, kataṃ karaṇīyaṃ, nāparaṃ itthattāyāti pajānāmī’ti.

‘This venerable one is learned, a bearer of what has been heard, a treasurer of what has been heard. Those teachings that are good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, with the right meaning and phrasing, which proclaim the perfectly complete and pure holy life—such teachings have been much heard by him, retained, recited, mentally examined, and well penetrated by view. It is for this reason that this venerable one is conceited, one whose assertion is based on conceit, perceiving the unattained as attained, the undone as done, the unrealized as realized. Through conceit he makes a declaration of final knowledge: “Birth is destroyed, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more of this state of being, I understand.”’

“Tamenaṃ tathāgato vā tathāgatasāvako vā jhāyī samāpattikusalo paracittakusalo paracittapariyāyakusalo evaṃ cetasā ceto paricca pajānāti –

Then the Tathāgata or a disciple of the Tathāgata—one accomplished in jhāna, skilled in the attainments, skilled in the minds of others, skilled in the ways of others’ minds—having encompassed that person’s mind with his own mind, understands thus:

‘Abhijjhālu kho pana ayamāyasmā; abhijjhāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā bahulaṃ viharati. Abhijjhāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘This venerable one is covetous; he often dwells with a mind obsessed by covetousness. And being obsessed by covetousness is a decline in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Byāpanno [M 3.0388] kho pana ayamāyasmā; byāpādapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā bahulaṃ viharati. Byāpādapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘This venerable one is malevolent; he often dwells with a mind obsessed by ill will. And being obsessed by ill will is a decline in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Thinamiddho kho pana ayamāyasmā; thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhitena cetasā bahulaṃ viharati. Thinamiddhapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘This venerable one is subject to sloth and torpor; he often dwells with a mind obsessed by sloth and torpor. And being obsessed by sloth and torpor is a decline in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Uddhato [V 3.0139] kho pana ayamāyasmā; uddhaccapariyuṭṭhitena [T 5.0175] cetasā bahulaṃ viharati. Uddhaccapariyuṭṭhānaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘This venerable one is restless; he often dwells with a mind obsessed by restlessness. And being obsessed by restlessness is a decline in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Vicikiccho kho pana ayamāyasmā; vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhitena cetasā bahulaṃ viharati. Vicikicchāpariyuṭṭhānaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘This venerable one is doubtful; he often dwells with a mind obsessed by doubt. And being obsessed by doubt is a decline in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Kammārāmo kho pana ayamāyasmā kammarato kammārāmataṃ anuyutto. Kammārāmatā [P 5.0164] kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘This venerable one delights in work, is fond of work, and is devoted to delighting in work. And delight in work is a decline in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Bhassārāmo kho pana ayamāyasmā bhassarato bhassārāmataṃ anuyutto. Bhassārāmatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘This venerable one delights in talk, is fond of talk, and is devoted to delighting in talk. And delight in talk is a decline in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Niddārāmo kho pana ayamāyasmā niddārato niddārāmataṃ anuyutto. Niddārāmatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘This venerable one delights in sleep, is fond of sleep, and is devoted to delighting in sleep. And delight in sleep is a decline in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Saṅgaṇikārāmo kho pana ayamāyasmā saṅgaṇikarato saṅgaṇikārāmataṃ anuyutto. Saṅgaṇikārāmatā kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ.

‘This venerable one delights in company, is fond of company, and is devoted to delighting in company. And delight in company is a decline in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.

‘Sati kho pana ayamāyasmā uttari karaṇīye oramattakena visesādhigamena antarā vosānaṃ āpanno. Antarā vosānagamanaṃ kho pana tathāgatappavedite dhammavinaye parihānametaṃ’.

‘This venerable one, while there was a further duty to be done, has reached a standstill in the interim through the attainment of a minor distinction. And this reaching a standstill in the interim is a decline in the Dhamma and Vinaya proclaimed by the Tathāgata.’

“So vatāvuso, bhikkhu ‘ime dasa dhamme appahāya imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. So vatāvuso, bhikkhu [M 3.0389] ‘ime dasa dhamme pahāya imasmiṃ dhammavinaye vuddhiṃ virūḷhiṃ vepullaṃ āpajjissatī’ti ṭhānametaṃ vijjatī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

Indeed, friend, that a bhikkhu, without having abandoned these ten states, will attain growth, development, and abundance in this Dhamma-Vinaya—this is not a possibility. Indeed, friend, that a bhikkhu, having abandoned these ten states, will attain growth, development, and abundance in this Dhamma-Vinaya—this is a possibility. The Sixth.

7. Nappiyasuttaṃ

7. The Sutta on Not Being Dear

87. Tatra [T 5.0176][V 3.0140] kho bhagavā kālaṅkataṃ bhikkhuṃ kalandakaṃ bhikkhuṃ (sī.), kāḷakabhikkhuṃ (syā.) ārabbha bhikkhū āmantesi – “bhikkhavo”ti. “Bhadante”ti te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

87. There, the Blessed One, concerning a bhikkhu who had passed away, addressed the bhikkhus, 'Bhikkhus!' 'Venerable Sir,' those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Idha, bhikkhave, bhikkhu adhikaraṇiko hoti, adhikaraṇasamathassa na vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu adhikaraṇiko hoti adhikaraṇasamathassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Here, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is one who creates disputes and does not speak in praise of the settling of disputes. Bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu is one who creates disputes and does not speak in praise of the settling of disputes—this state also does not conduce to being dear, to being respected, to development, to the state of a recluse, or to unity.

“Puna [P 5.0165] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na sikkhākāmo hoti, sikkhāsamādānassa sikkhākāmassa (ka.) na vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na sikkhākāmo hoti sikkhāsamādānassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not desirous of the training and does not speak in praise of undertaking the training. Bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu is not desirous of the training and does not speak in praise of undertaking the training—this state also does not conduce to being dear, to being respected, to development, to the state of a recluse, or to unity.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pāpiccho hoti, icchāvinayassa na vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu pāpiccho hoti icchāvinayassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu has evil desires and does not speak in praise of the removal of desire. Bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu has evil desires and does not speak in praise of the removal of desire—this state also does not conduce to being dear, to being respected, to development, to the state of a recluse, or to unity.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kodhano hoti, kodhavinayassa na vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu kodhano hoti kodhavinayassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is angry and does not speak in praise of the removal of anger. Bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu is angry and does not speak in praise of the removal of anger—this state also does not conduce to being dear, to being respected, to development, to the state of a recluse, or to unity.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu makkhī hoti, makkhavinayassa na vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu makkhī hoti makkhavinayassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is denigrating and does not speak in praise of the removal of denigration. Bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu is denigrating and does not speak in praise of the removal of denigration—this state also does not conduce to being dear, to being respected, to development, to the state of a recluse, or to unity.

“Puna [M 3.0390] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu saṭho hoti[T 5.0177], sāṭheyyavinayassa na vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave[V 3.0141], bhikkhu saṭho hoti sāṭheyyavinayassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is fraudulent and does not speak in praise of the removal of fraud. Bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu is fraudulent and does not speak in praise of the removal of fraud—this state also does not conduce to being dear, to being respected, to development, to the state of a recluse, or to unity.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu māyāvī hoti, māyāvinayassa na vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu māyāvī hoti māyāvinayassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is deceitful and does not speak in praise of the removal of deceit. Bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu is deceitful and does not speak in praise of the removal of deceit—this state also does not conduce to being dear, to being respected, to development, to the state of a recluse, or to unity.

“Puna [P 5.0166] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammānaṃ na nisāmakajātiko hoti, dhammanisantiyā na vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammānaṃ na nisāmakajātiko hoti dhammanisantiyā na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not of a nature to be attentive to the Dhammas and does not speak in praise of attentiveness to the Dhamma. Bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu is not of a nature to be attentive to the Dhammas and does not speak in praise of attentiveness to the Dhamma—this state also does not conduce to being dear, to being respected, to development, to the state of a recluse, or to unity.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na paṭisallīno hoti, paṭisallānassa na vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na paṭisallīno hoti paṭisallānassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not given to seclusion and does not speak in praise of seclusion. Bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu is not given to seclusion and does not speak in praise of seclusion—this state also does not conduce to being dear, to being respected, to development, to the state of a recluse, or to unity.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṃ na paṭisanthārako paṭisandhārako (ka.) hoti, paṭisanthārakassa na vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṃ na paṭisanthārako hoti paṭisanthārakassa na vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo na piyatāya na garutāya na bhāvanāya na sāmaññāya na ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Furthermore, Bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not welcoming towards his companions in the holy life and does not speak in praise of one who is welcoming. Bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu is not welcoming towards his companions in the holy life and does not speak in praise of one who is welcoming—this state also does not conduce to being dear, to being respected, to development, to the state of a recluse, or to unity.

“Evarūpassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno kiñcāpi evaṃ icchā uppajjeyya – ‘aho vata [T 5.0178] maṃ sabrahmacārī sakkareyyuṃ garuṃ kareyyuṃ garukareyyuṃ (sī. syā.) māneyyuṃ pūjeyyu’nti, atha kho naṃ sabrahmacārī na ceva sakkaronti na garuṃ karonti garukaronti (sī. syā.) na mānenti na pūjenti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathāhissa, bhikkhave, viññū sabrahmacārī te pāpake akusale dhamme appahīne samanupassanti.

For a bhikkhu of such a kind, Bhikkhus, even if this wish should arise: ‘Oh, may my companions in the holy life honor me, respect me, esteem me, and revere me!’—nevertheless, his companions in the holy life do not honor him, do not respect him, do not esteem him, and do not revere him. For what reason? Because, Bhikkhus, his wise companions in the holy life see in him those evil, unwholesome states that have not been abandoned.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, assakhaḷuṅkassa kiñcāpi evaṃ icchā uppajjeyya – ‘aho vata maṃ [V 3.0142] manussā ājānīyaṭṭhāne ṭhapeyyuṃ, ājānīyabhojanañca bhojeyyuṃ, ājānīyaparimajjanañca parimajjeyyu’nti, atha kho naṃ manussā na [M 3.0391] ceva ājānīyaṭṭhāne ṭhapenti na ca ājānīyabhojanaṃ bhojenti na ca ājānīyaparimajjanaṃ parimajjanti. Taṃ [P 5.0167] kissa hetu? Tathāhissa, bhikkhave, viññū manussā tāni sāṭheyyāni kūṭeyyāni jimheyyāni vaṅkeyyāni appahīnāni samanupassanti. Evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, evarūpassa bhikkhuno kiñcāpi evaṃ icchā uppajjeyya – ‘aho vata maṃ sabrahmacārī sakkareyyuṃ garuṃ kareyyuṃ māneyyuṃ pūjeyyu’nti, atha kho naṃ sabrahmacārī na ceva sakkaronti na garuṃ karonti na mānenti na pūjenti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathāhissa, bhikkhave, viññū sabrahmacārī te pāpake akusale dhamme appahīne samanupassanti.

Suppose, monks, a worthless horse might have this wish: ‘Oh, that people would place me in the rank of a thoroughbred, feed me a thoroughbred’s food, and groom me with a thoroughbred’s grooming!’—still, people do not place him in the rank of a thoroughbred, feed him a thoroughbred’s food, or groom him with a thoroughbred’s grooming. For what reason? Because, monks, wise people see that its deceitful, fraudulent, crooked, and devious qualities have not been abandoned. So too, monks, for a monk of such a kind, even if this wish should arise: ‘Oh, that my companions in the holy life would respect me, hold me in high esteem, cherish me, and revere me!’—still, his companions in the holy life do not respect him, hold him in high esteem, cherish him, or revere him. For what reason? Because, monks, his wise companions in the holy life see that those evil, unwholesome states have not been abandoned in him.

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na adhikaraṇiko hoti, adhikaraṇasamathassa vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu na adhikaraṇiko hoti adhikaraṇasamathassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo piyatāya garutāya bhāvanāya sāmaññāya ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Here, monks, a monk is not one who creates disputes, and he speaks in praise of the settling of disputes. The fact that a monk is not one who creates disputes and speaks in praise of the settling of disputes—this quality, too, leads to being dear, to respect, to development, to the state of a recluse, and to unity.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sikkhākāmo hoti, sikkhāsamādānassa vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sikkhākāmo hoti [T 5.0179] sikkhāsamādānassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo piyatāya garutāya bhāvanāya sāmaññāya ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Furthermore, monks, a monk is desirous of the training and speaks in praise of undertaking the training. The fact that a monk is desirous of the training and speaks in praise of undertaking the training—this quality, too, leads to being dear, to respect, to development, to the state of a recluse, and to unity.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appiccho hoti, icchāvinayassa vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu appiccho hoti icchāvinayassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo…pe… ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.
