Furthermore, monks, a monk has few desires and speaks in praise of the removal of desire. The fact that a monk has few desires and speaks in praise of the removal of desire—this quality, too, leads to… unity.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akkodhano hoti, kodhavinayassa vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akkodhano hoti kodhavinayassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo…pe… ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Furthermore, monks, a monk is not angry and speaks in praise of the removal of anger. The fact that a monk is not angry and speaks in praise of the removal of anger—this quality, too, leads to… unity.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu amakkhī hoti, makkhavinayassa vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave[V 3.0143], bhikkhu amakkhī hoti makkhavinayassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo…pe… ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Furthermore, monks, a monk is not contemptuous and speaks in praise of the removal of contempt. The fact that a monk is not contemptuous and speaks in praise of the removal of contempt—this quality, too, leads to… unity.

“Puna [P 5.0168] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asaṭho hoti, sāṭheyyavinayassa vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu asaṭho hoti sāṭheyyavinayassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo…pe… ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Furthermore, monks, a monk is not deceitful and speaks in praise of the removal of deceit. The fact that a monk is not deceitful and speaks in praise of the removal of deceit—this quality, too, leads to… unity.

“Puna [M 3.0392] caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu amāyāvī hoti, māyāvinayassa vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu amāyāvī hoti māyāvinayassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo…pe… ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Furthermore, monks, a monk is not tricky and speaks in praise of the removal of trickery. The fact that a monk is not tricky and speaks in praise of the removal of trickery—this quality, too, leads to… unity.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammānaṃ nisāmakajātiko hoti, dhammanisantiyā vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu dhammānaṃ nisāmakajātiko hoti dhammanisantiyā vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo…pe… ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Furthermore, monks, a monk is of a nature that carefully considers the Dhamma, and he speaks in praise of carefully considering the Dhamma. The fact that a monk is of a nature that carefully considers the Dhamma and speaks in praise of carefully considering the Dhamma—this quality, too, leads to… unity.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisallīno hoti, paṭisallānassa vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu paṭisallīno hoti paṭisallānassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo…pe… ekībhāvāya [T 5.0180] saṃvattati.

Furthermore, monks, a monk dwells in seclusion and speaks in praise of seclusion. The fact that a monk dwells in seclusion and speaks in praise of seclusion—this quality, too, leads to… unity.

“Puna caparaṃ, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṃ paṭisanthārako hoti, paṭisanthārakassa vaṇṇavādī. Yampi, bhikkhave, bhikkhu sabrahmacārīnaṃ paṭisanthārako hoti paṭisanthārakassa vaṇṇavādī, ayampi dhammo piyatāya garutāya bhāvanāya sāmaññāya ekībhāvāya saṃvattati.

Furthermore, monks, a monk is friendly and courteous toward his companions in the holy life and speaks in praise of one who is friendly and courteous. The fact that a monk is friendly and courteous toward his companions in the holy life and speaks in praise of one who is friendly and courteous—this quality, too, leads to being dear, to respect, to development, to the state of a recluse, and to unity.

“Evarūpassa, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno kiñcāpi na evaṃ icchā uppajjeyya – ‘aho vata maṃ sabrahmacārī sakkareyyuṃ garuṃ kareyyuṃ māneyyuṃ pūjeyyu’nti, atha kho naṃ sabrahmacārī sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathāhissa, bhikkhave, viññū sabrahmacārī te pāpake akusale dhamme pahīne samanupassanti.

For a monk of such a kind, monks, even if the wish should not arise, ‘Oh, may my companions in the holy life respect me, hold me in high esteem, cherish me, and revere me,’ still his companions in the holy life respect him, hold him in high esteem, cherish him, and revere him. For what reason? Because, monks, his wise companions in the holy life see that those evil, unwholesome states have been abandoned in him.

“Seyyathāpi[V 3.0144], bhikkhave, bhaddassa assājānīyassa kiñcāpi na evaṃ icchā uppajjeyya – ‘aho vata maṃ manussā ājānīyaṭṭhāne ṭhapeyyuṃ, ājānīyabhojanañca bhojeyyuṃ, ājānīyaparimajjanañca parimajjeyyu’nti, atha kho naṃ manussā ājānīyaṭṭhāne ca ṭhapenti ājānīyabhojanañca bhojenti [P 5.0169] ājānīyaparimajjanañca parimajjanti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathāhissa, bhikkhave, viññū manussā tāni sāṭheyyāni kūṭeyyāni jimheyyāni vaṅkeyyāni pahīnāni samanupassanti.

Suppose, monks, a fine thoroughbred horse might not have this wish: ‘Oh, that people would place me in the rank of a thoroughbred, feed me a thoroughbred’s food, and groom me with a thoroughbred’s grooming!’ Yet people do place him in the rank of a thoroughbred, feed him a thoroughbred’s food, and groom him with a thoroughbred’s grooming. For what reason? Because, monks, wise people see that its deceitful, fraudulent, crooked, and devious qualities have been abandoned.

“Evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, evarūpassa bhikkhuno kiñcāpi na evaṃ icchā uppajjeyya – ‘aho vata maṃ sabrahmacārī sakkareyyuṃ garuṃ kareyyuṃ māneyyuṃ pūjeyyu’nti, atha kho naṃ sabrahmacārī sakkaronti garuṃ karonti mānenti pūjenti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Tathāhissa, bhikkhave, viññū sabrahmacārī te pāpake akusale dhamme pahīne samanupassantī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

So too, monks, for a monk of such a kind, even if the wish should not arise: ‘Oh, may my companions in the holy life respect me, hold me in high esteem, cherish me, and revere me!’—nevertheless, his companions in the holy life respect him, hold him in high esteem, cherish him, and revere him. For what reason? Because, monks, his wise companions in the holy life see that those evil, unwholesome states have been abandoned in him.” Seventh.

8. Akkosakasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Abuser

88. “Yo [T 5.0181][M 3.0393] so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akkosakaparibhāsako ariyūpavādī sabrahmacārīnaṃ ṭhānametaṃ avakāso aṭṭhānametaṃ anavakāso (sī. syā. pī.) yaṃ so dasannaṃ byasanānaṃ aññataraṃ byasanaṃ nigaccheyya na nigaccheyya (sī. syā. pī.). Katamesaṃ dasannaṃ? Anadhigataṃ nādhigacchati, adhigatā parihāyati, saddhammassa na vodāyanti, saddhammesu vā adhimāniko hoti anabhirato vā brahmacariyaṃ carati, aññataraṃ vā saṃkiliṭṭhaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjati, gāḷhaṃ vā rogātaṅkaṃ phusati, ummādaṃ vā pāpuṇāti cittakkhepaṃ, sammūḷho kālaṃ karoti, kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati. Yo so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu akkosakaparibhāsako ariyūpavādī sabrahmacārīnaṃ, ṭhānametaṃ avakāso yaṃ so imesaṃ dasannaṃ byasanānaṃ aññataraṃ byasanaṃ nigaccheyyā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

88. “Bhikkhus, whatever bhikkhu is an insulter and reviler of his companions in the holy life and a slanderer of noble ones, it is a possibility, it is an opportunity, that he may come to one of ten calamities. What ten? (1) He does not attain the unattained. (2) He declines from what has been attained. (3) For him, the good Dhamma does not become pure. (4) Or he becomes conceited in the good Dhamma. (5) Or he practices the holy life without delight. (6) Or he commits some defiled offense. (7) Or he contracts a severe illness. (8) Or he attains madness or mental distraction. (9) He dies confused. (10) With the breaking up of the body, after death, he is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of downfall, in hell. Bhikkhus, whatever bhikkhu is an insulter and reviler of his companions in the holy life and a slanderer of noble ones, it is a possibility, it is an opportunity, that he may come to one of these ten calamities.” Eighth.

9. Kokālikasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Kokālika

89. saṃ. ni. 1.181; su. ni. kokālikasutta Atha [P 5.0170] kho kokāliko bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho kokāliko bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “pāpicchā, bhante, sāriputtamoggallānā, pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gatā”ti. “Mā [V 3.0145] hevaṃ, kokālika, mā hevaṃ, kokālika! Pasādehi, kokālika, sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṃ. Pesalā sāriputtamoggallānā”ti.

89. Then the bhikkhu Kokālika approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the bhikkhu Kokālika said this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, Sāriputta and Moggallāna have evil desires; they have fallen under the sway of evil desires.’ ‘Do not speak thus, Kokālika! Do not speak thus, Kokālika! Clarify your mind, Kokālika, towards Sāriputta and Moggallāna. Sāriputta and Moggallāna are of lovely virtue.’

Dutiyampi kho kokāliko bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kiñcāpi me, bhante, bhagavā saddhāyiko paccayiko, atha kho pāpicchāva sāriputtamoggallānā, pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gatā”ti. “Mā hevaṃ, kokālika, mā hevaṃ, kokālika! Pasādehi, kokālika, sāriputtamoggallānesu [T 5.0182] cittaṃ. Pesalā sāriputtamoggallānā”ti.

For a second time, the bhikkhu Kokālika said this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, although the Blessed One is credible and trustworthy to me, nevertheless Sāriputta and Moggallāna indeed have evil desires; they have indeed fallen under the sway of evil desires.’ ‘Do not speak thus, Kokālika! Do not speak thus, Kokālika! Clarify your mind, Kokālika, towards Sāriputta and Moggallāna. Sāriputta and Moggallāna are of lovely virtue.’

Tatiyampi kho kokāliko bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kiñcāpi me, bhante, bhagavā saddhāyiko paccayiko, atha kho pāpicchāva sāriputtamoggallānā, pāpikānaṃ icchānaṃ vasaṃ gatā”ti. “Mā hevaṃ, kokālika, mā hevaṃ, kokālika! Pasādehi, kokālika[M 3.0394], sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṃ. Pesalā sāriputtamoggallānā”ti.

For a third time, the bhikkhu Kokālika said this to the Blessed One: ‘Venerable sir, although the Blessed One is credible and trustworthy to me, nevertheless Sāriputta and Moggallāna indeed have evil desires; they have indeed fallen under the sway of evil desires.’ ‘Do not speak thus, Kokālika! Do not speak thus, Kokālika! Clarify your mind, Kokālika, towards Sāriputta and Moggallāna. Sāriputta and Moggallāna are of lovely virtue.’

Atha kho kokāliko bhikkhu uṭṭhāyāsanā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi. Acirapakkantassa ca kokālikassa bhikkhuno sāsapamattīhi pīḷakāhi sabbo kāyo phuṭo ahosi. Sāsapamattiyo hutvā muggamattiyo ahesuṃ, muggamattiyo hutvā kalāyamattiyo ahesuṃ, kalāyamattiyo hutvā kolaṭṭhimattiyo ahesuṃ, kolaṭṭhimattiyo hutvā kolamattiyo ahesuṃ, kolamattiyo hutvā āmalakamattiyo ahesuṃ, āmalakamattiyo hutvā (tiṇḍukamattiyo ahesuṃ, tiṇḍukamattiyo hutvā,) saṃ. ni. 1.181; su. ni. kokālikasutta natthi beḷuvasalāṭukamattiyo ahesuṃ, beḷuvasalāṭukamattiyo hutvā billamattiyo ahesuṃ, billamattiyo hutvā pabhijjiṃsu, pubbañca [P 5.0171] lohitañca pagghariṃsu. So sudaṃ kadalipattesu seti macchova visagilito.

Then the bhikkhu Kokālika rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, and, circumambulating him to the right, departed. Not long after the bhikkhu Kokālika had departed, his entire body was covered with boils the size of mustard seeds. Having become the size of mustard seeds, they became the size of mung beans; having become the size of mung beans, they became the size of chickpeas; having become the size of chickpeas, they became the size of jujube stones; having become the size of jujube stones, they became the size of jujube fruits; having become the size of jujube fruits, they became the size of myrobalan fruits; having become the size of myrobalan fruits, they became the size of persimmon fruits; having become the size of persimmon fruits, they became the size of unripe bael fruits; having become the size of unripe bael fruits, they became the size of bael fruits. Having become the size of bael fruits, they burst, and pus and blood discharged. He indeed lay on banana leaves like a fish that has swallowed poison.

Atha kho turū paccekabrahmā tuduppaccekabrahmā (sī. pī.), tudi paccekabrahmā (syā.), turi paccekabrahmā (ka.) saṃ. ni. 1.180 yena kokāliko bhikkhu tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā vehāse ṭhatvā kokālikaṃ bhikkhuṃ etadavoca – “pasādehi, kokālika, sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṃ. Pesalā sāriputtamoggallānā”ti. “Kosi tvaṃ, āvuso”ti? “Ahaṃ turū paccekabrahmā”ti. “Nanu tvaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā anāgāmī byākato, atha kiñcarahi idhāgato? Passa yāvañca te idaṃ aparaddha”nti.

Then the Paccekabrahmā Turū approached the bhikkhu Kokālika; having approached, he stood in the air and said this to the bhikkhu Kokālika: ‘Clarify your mind, Kokālika, towards Sāriputta and Moggallāna. Sāriputta and Moggallāna are of lovely virtue.’ ‘Who are you, friend?’ ‘I am the Paccekabrahmā Turū.’ ‘Friend, were you not declared a non-returner by the Blessed One? Then why have you come here? Behold how great this offense of yours is!’

Atha [V 3.0146] kho turū [T 5.0183] paccekabrahmā kokālikaṃ bhikkhuṃ gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi –

Then the Paccekabrahmā Turū addressed the bhikkhu Kokālika with verses:

“Purisassa hi jātassa, kuṭhārī jāyate mukhe;

Yāya chindati attānaṃ, bālo dubbhāsitaṃ bhaṇaṃ.

“An axe is born in the mouth of a person, with which the fool cuts himself when speaking ill-spoken words.

“Yo nindiyaṃ pasaṃsati, taṃ vā nindati yo pasaṃsiyo;

Vicināti mukhena so kaliṃ, kalinā tena sukhaṃ na vindati.

“He who praises one who is blameworthy, or blames one who is praiseworthy, gathers demerit with his mouth; because of that demerit he finds no happiness.

“Appamattako ayaṃ kali, yo akkhesu dhanaparājayo;

Sabbassāpi sahāpi attanā, ayameva mahattaro kali;

Yo sugatesu manaṃ padūsaye.

“A small demerit is this: the loss of wealth at dice, together with all one’s possessions and oneself. This indeed is the far greater demerit: to corrupt one’s mind towards the Well-Gone Ones.

“Sataṃ [M 3.0395] sahassānaṃ nirabbudānaṃ, chattiṃsati pañca ca abbudāni;

Yamariyagarahī nirayaṃ upeti, vācaṃ manañca paṇidhāya pāpaka”nti.

“For one hundred thousand nirabbudas, and for thirty-six and five abbudas, he who reviles the noble ones goes to hell, having directed evil speech and mind.”

Atha [P 5.0172] kho kokāliko bhikkhu teneva ābādhena kālamakāsi. Kālaṅkato ca kokāliko bhikkhu padumaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṃ āghātetvā.

Then the bhikkhu Kokālika died of that very illness. And having died, the bhikkhu Kokālika was reborn in the Paduma hell for having corrupted his mind towards Sāriputta and Moggallāna.

Atha kho brahmā sahampati abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito kho brahmā sahampati bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kokāliko, bhante[T 5.0184], bhikkhu kālaṅkato. Kālaṅkato ca, bhante, kokāliko bhikkhu padumaṃ nirayaṃ upapanno sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṃ āghātetvā”ti. Idamavoca brahmā sahampati. Idaṃ vatvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyi.

Then, when the night was advanced, the Brahmā Sahampati, with surpassing beauty, having illuminated the entire Jeta’s Grove, approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and stood to one side. Standing to one side, the Brahmā Sahampati said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, the bhikkhu Kokālika has died. And having died, venerable sir, the bhikkhu Kokālika has been reborn in the Paduma hell for having corrupted his mind towards Sāriputta and Moggallāna.” This is what the Brahmā Sahampati said. Having said this, he paid homage to the Blessed One, and, circumambulating him to the right, he vanished right there.

Atha kho bhagavā tassā rattiyā accayena bhikkhū āmantesi – “imaṃ, bhikkhave, rattiṃ brahmā sahampati abhikkantāya rattiyā abhikkantavaṇṇo kevalakappaṃ jetavanaṃ obhāsetvā yenāhaṃ tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā maṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi. Ekamantaṃ ṭhito [V 3.0147] kho, bhikkhave, brahmā sahampati maṃ etadavoca – ‘kokāliko, bhante, bhikkhu kālaṅkato; kālaṅkato ca, bhante, kokāliko bhikkhu padumaṃ nirayaṃ upapanno sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṃ āghātetvā’ti. Idamavoca, bhikkhave, brahmā sahampati. Idaṃ vatvā maṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā tatthevantaradhāyī”ti.

Then, when the night had passed, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: “Bhikkhus, this night, when the night was advanced, the Brahmā Sahampati, having illuminated the entire Jeta’s Grove with his surpassing radiance, approached me. Having approached, he paid homage to me and stood to one side. Standing to one side, bhikkhus, the Brahmā Sahampati said this to me: ‘Venerable sir, the bhikkhu Kokālika has passed away. And having passed away, venerable sir, the bhikkhu Kokālika has been reborn in the Paduma hell for having developed a mind of ill will toward Sāriputta and Moggallāna.’ This is what the Brahmā Sahampati said, bhikkhus. Having said this, he paid homage to me, and, circumambulating me to the right, he vanished right there.”

Evaṃ vutte aññataro bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kīva dīghaṃ nu kho, bhante, padume niraye āyuppamāṇa”nti? “Dīghaṃ kho, bhikkhu, padume niraye āyuppamāṇaṃ. Na taṃ sukaraṃ saṅkhātuṃ – ‘ettakāni vassānīti [P 5.0173] vā ettakāni vassasatānīti vā ettakāni vassasahassānīti vā ettakāni vassasatasahassānīti vā’”ti.

When this was said, a certain bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One: “Venerable sir, how long is the lifespan in the Paduma hell?” “The lifespan in the Paduma hell is long, bhikkhu. It is not easy to count it as ‘so many years,’ or ‘so many hundreds of years,’ or ‘so many thousands of years,’ or ‘so many hundreds of thousands of years.’”

“Sakkā pana, bhante, upamaṃ kātu”nti? “Sakkā, bhikkhū,”ti bhagavā avoca – “seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsatikhāriko kosalako tilavāho tato puriso vassasatassa vassasatassa accayena ekamekaṃ tilaṃ uddhareyya[M 3.0396]. Khippataraṃ kho so, bhikkhu, vīsatikhāriko kosalako tilavāho iminā [T 5.0185] upakkamena parikkhayaṃ pariyādānaṃ gaccheyya, na tveva eko abbudo nirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati abbudā nirayā, evameko nirabbudo nirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati nirabbudā nirayā, evameko ababo nirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati ababā nirayā, evameko aṭaṭo nirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati aṭaṭā nirayā, evameko ahaho nirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati ahahā nirayā, evameko kumudo nirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati kumudā nirayā, evameko sogandhiko nirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati sogandhikā nirayā, evameko uppalako nirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati uppalakā nirayā, evameko puṇḍarīko nirayo. Seyyathāpi, bhikkhu, vīsati puṇḍarīkā nirayā, evameko padumo nirayo. Padumaṃ kho pana, bhikkhu, nirayaṃ kokāliko bhikkhu upapanno sāriputtamoggallānesu cittaṃ āghātetvā”ti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato athāparaṃ etadavoca satthā –

“But, venerable sir, is it possible to make a comparison?” “It is possible, bhikkhu,” the Blessed One said. “Suppose, bhikkhu, there were a Kosalan cartload of twenty khārikas of sesame seeds. From that, a man would remove one sesame seed at the passing of every hundred years. Sooner, bhikkhu, would that Kosalan cartload of twenty khārikas of sesame seeds be exhausted and depleted by this endeavor than would one Abbuda hell. Just as there are twenty Abbuda hells, bhikkhu, so is one Nirabbuda hell. Just as there are twenty Nirabbuda hells, so is one Ababa hell. Just as there are twenty Ababa hells, so is one Aṭaṭa hell. Just as there are twenty Aṭaṭa hells, so is one Ahaha hell. Just as there are twenty Ahaha hells, so is one Kumuda hell. Just as there are twenty Kumuda hells, so is one Sogandhika hell. Just as there are twenty Sogandhika hells, so is one Uppalaka hell. Just as there are twenty Uppalaka hells, so is one Puṇḍarīka hell. Just as there are twenty Puṇḍarīka hells, so is one Paduma hell. It is to the Paduma hell, bhikkhu, that the bhikkhu Kokālika has been reborn for having developed a mind of ill will toward Sāriputta and Moggallāna.” This is what the Blessed One said. Having said this, the Well-farer, the Teacher, further said this:

“Purisassa [P 5.0174] hi jātassa, kuṭhārī jāyate mukhe;

Yāya chindati attānaṃ, bālo dubbhāsitaṃ bhaṇaṃ.

“For a person who is born, an axe is born in his mouth, with which the fool, speaking ill-spoken words, cuts himself.”

“Yo [T 5.0186][V 3.0148] nindiyaṃ pasaṃsati, taṃ vā nindati yo pasaṃsiyo;

Vicināti mukhena so kaliṃ, kalinā tena sukhaṃ na vindati.

“He who praises one worthy of blame, or who blames one worthy of praise, gathers demerit with his mouth; through that demerit, he finds no happiness.”

“Appamattako ayaṃ kali, yo akkhesu dhanaparājayo;

Sabbassāpi sahāpi attanā, ayameva mahattaro kali;

Yo sugatesu manaṃ padūsaye.

“Trifling is this demerit—the loss of wealth at dice, together with all one’s possessions and oneself. This indeed is the greater demerit: that one should corrupt one’s mind against the Well-gone Ones.”

“Sataṃ sahassānaṃ nirabbudānaṃ, chattiṃsati pañca ca abbudāni;

Yamariyagarahī nirayaṃ upeti, vācaṃ manañca paṇidhāya pāpaka”nti. navamaṃ;

“For one hundred thousand nirabbudas, and for thirty-six and five abbudas, the reviler of noble ones goes to hell, having directed evil speech and mind.”

10. Khīṇāsavabalasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Powers of One Whose Taints Are Destroyed

90. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho āyasmantaṃ sāriputtaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “kati nu kho, sāriputta, khīṇāsavassa [M 3.0397] bhikkhuno balāni, yehi balehi samannāgato khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayaṃ paṭijānāti – ‘khīṇā me āsavā’”ti?

90. Then the Venerable Sāriputta approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. As he was sitting there, the Blessed One said to him: “Sāriputta, how many powers does a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed possess, endowed with which a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declares the destruction of the taints thus: ‘My taints are destroyed’?”

“Dasa, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balāni, yehi balehi samannāgato khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayaṃ paṭijānāti – ‘khīṇā me āsavā’ti. Katamāni dasa? a. ni. 8.28; paṭi. ma. 2.44 Idha, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno aniccato sabbe saṅkhārā yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhā honti. Yampi[P 5.0175], bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno aniccato sabbe saṅkhārā yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhā honti, idampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayaṃ paṭijānāti – ‘khīṇā me āsavā’ti.

“Venerable sir, there are ten powers of a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, endowed with which a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declares the destruction of the taints thus: ‘My taints are destroyed.’ What ten? Here, venerable sir, for a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, all formations have been well seen as they really are with right wisdom as impermanent. And since, venerable sir, for a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, all formations have been well seen as they really are with right wisdom as impermanent, this too is a power of a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, relying on which a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declares the destruction of the taints: ‘My taints are destroyed.’

“Puna caparaṃ, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno aṅgārakāsūpamā kāmā yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhā honti. Yampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno aṅgārakāsūpamā kāmā yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhā [T 5.0187] honti, idampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayaṃ paṭijānāti – ‘khīṇā me āsavā’ti.

“Furthermore, venerable sir, for a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, sensual pleasures have been well seen as they really are with right wisdom as being like a pit of embers. And since, venerable sir, for a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, sensual pleasures have been well seen as they really are with right wisdom as being like a pit of embers, this too is a power of a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, relying on which a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declares the destruction of the taints: ‘My taints are destroyed.’

“Puna [V 3.0149] caparaṃ, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno vivekaninnaṃ cittaṃ hoti vivekapoṇaṃ vivekapabbhāraṃ vivekaṭṭhaṃ nekkhammābhirataṃ byantībhūtaṃ sabbaso āsavaṭṭhāniyehi dhammehi. Yampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno vivekaninnaṃ cittaṃ hoti vivekapoṇaṃ vivekapabbhāraṃ vivekaṭṭhaṃ nekkhammābhirataṃ byantībhūtaṃ sabbaso āsavaṭṭhāniyehi dhammehi, idampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayaṃ paṭijānāti – ‘khīṇā me āsavā’ti.

“Furthermore, venerable sir, the mind of a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed is inclined to seclusion, sloping towards seclusion, bent on seclusion, established in seclusion, delighting in renunciation, and has become free from all things that are grounds for the taints. And since, venerable sir, the mind of a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed is inclined to seclusion, sloping towards seclusion, bent on seclusion, established in seclusion, delighting in renunciation, and has become free from all things that are grounds for the taints, this too is a power of a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, relying on which a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declares the destruction of the taints: ‘My taints are destroyed.’

“Puna caparaṃ, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā honti subhāvitā. Yampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno cattāro satipaṭṭhānā bhāvitā honti subhāvitā, idampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayaṃ paṭijānāti – ‘khīṇā me āsavā’ti.

“Furthermore, venerable sir, for a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, the four establishments of mindfulness have been developed and well developed. And since, venerable sir, for a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, the four establishments of mindfulness have been developed and well developed, this too is a power of a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, relying on which a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declares the destruction of the taints: ‘My taints are destroyed.’

“Puna caparaṃ, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno cattāro sammappadhānā bhāvitā honti subhāvitā…pe… cattāro iddhipādā bhāvitā honti subhāvitā [M 3.0398] …pe… pañcindriyāni… pañca balāni bhāvitāni [P 5.0176] honti subhāvitāni… satta bojjhaṅgā bhāvitā honti subhāvitā… ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvito hoti subhāvito. Yampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno ariyo aṭṭhaṅgiko maggo bhāvito hoti subhāvito, idampi, bhante, khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balaṃ hoti, yaṃ balaṃ āgamma khīṇāsavo bhikkhu [T 5.0188] āsavānaṃ khayaṃ paṭijānāti – ‘khīṇā me āsavā’ti.

“Furthermore, venerable sir, for a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, the four right strivings have been developed and well developed … the four bases for spiritual power have been developed and well developed … the five spiritual faculties … the five powers have been developed and well developed … the seven factors of enlightenment have been developed and well developed … the Noble Eightfold Path has been developed and well developed. And since, venerable sir, for a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, the Noble Eightfold Path has been developed and well developed, this too is a power of the bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, relying on which a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declares the destruction of the taints: ‘My taints are destroyed.’

“Imāni kho, bhante, dasa khīṇāsavassa bhikkhuno balāni, yehi balehi samannāgato khīṇāsavo bhikkhu āsavānaṃ khayaṃ paṭijānāti – ‘khīṇā me āsavā’”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“These, venerable sir, are the ten powers of a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed, endowed with which a bhikkhu whose taints are destroyed declares the destruction of the taints: ‘My taints are destroyed.’” Tenth.

Theravaggo catuttho.

The Chapter on the Elders—the Fourth.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Vāhanānando puṇṇiyo, byākaraṃ katthimāniko;

Napiyakkosakokāli, khīṇāsavabalena cāti.

Vāhana, Ānanda, Puṇṇiya, Declaration, Katthī, Mānika; Nappiya, Akkosa, Kokālika, and with the Power of One Whose Taints Are Destroyed.

(10) 5. Upālivaggo

(10) 5. The Chapter on Upāli

1. Kāmabhogīsuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on Enjoyers of Sensual Pleasures

91. Ekaṃ [V 3.0150] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ bhagavā etadavoca –

91. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling in Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika approached the Blessed One; having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, he sat down to one side. The Blessed One said this to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika who was sitting to one side:

“Dasayime[P 5.0177], gahapati, kāmabhogī santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ. Katame dasa? Idha, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena; adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena na attānaṃ sukheti na pīṇeti na attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti (sī. syā. pī.) evamuparipi na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karoti.

“Householder, these ten enjoyers of sensual pleasures exist and are found in the world. What ten? Here, householder, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth unrighteously and by force; having sought wealth unrighteously and by force, he does not make himself happy, does not gratify himself, does not share, and does not perform meritorious deeds.

“Idha [M 3.0399] pana, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena; adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti, na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karoti.

“Furthermore, householder, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth unrighteously and by force; having sought wealth unrighteously and by force, he makes himself happy and gratifies himself; he does not share and does not perform meritorious deeds.

“Idha pana[T 5.0189], gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena; adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti.

“Furthermore, householder, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth unrighteously and by force; having sought wealth unrighteously and by force, he makes himself happy, gratifies himself, shares, and performs meritorious deeds.

“Idha pana, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi; dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi na attānaṃ sukheti na pīṇeti na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karoti.

“Furthermore, householder, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both by force and not by force; having sought wealth both righteously and unrighteously, and both by force and not by force, he does not make himself happy, does not gratify himself, does not share, and does not perform meritorious deeds.

“Idha pana, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi[V 3.0151]; dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti, na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karoti.

“Furthermore, householder, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both by force and not by force; having sought wealth both righteously and unrighteously, and both by force and not by force, he makes himself happy and gratifies himself; he does not share and does not perform meritorious deeds.

“Idha pana, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi; dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti.

“Furthermore, householder, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both by force and not by force; having sought wealth both righteously and unrighteously, and both by force and not by force, he makes himself happy, gratifies himself, shares, and performs meritorious deeds.

“Idha pana, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena; dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena na attānaṃ sukheti na pīṇeti na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karoti.

“Furthermore, householder, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth righteously and not by force; having sought wealth righteously and not by force, he does not make himself happy, does not gratify himself, does not share, and does not perform meritorious deeds.

“Idha pana, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena; dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena [P 5.0178] attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti, na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karoti.

“Furthermore, householder, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth righteously and not by force; having sought wealth righteously and not by force, he makes himself happy and gratifies himself; he does not share and does not perform meritorious deeds.

“Idha pana, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena; dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti. Te ca bhoge gathito gadhito (ka.) a. ni. 3.124 passitabbaṃ mucchito [M 3.0400] ajjhosanno ajjhāpanno (sabbattha) a. ni. 3.124 suttavaṇṇanā ṭīkā oloketabbā anādīnavadassāvī anissaraṇapañño [T 5.0190] paribhuñjati.

“Furthermore, householder, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth righteously and not by force; having sought wealth righteously and not by force, he makes himself happy, gratifies himself, shares, and performs meritorious deeds. And he enjoys that wealth while being greedy for it, infatuated with it, and attached to it, not seeing the danger and without the wisdom of escape.

“Idha pana, gahapati, ekacco kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena; dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti. Te ca bhoge agathito amucchito anajjhosanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati.

“Furthermore, householder, a certain enjoyer of sensual pleasures seeks wealth righteously and not by force; having sought wealth righteously and not by force, he makes himself happy, gratifies himself, shares, and performs meritorious deeds. And he enjoys that wealth without being greedy for it, not infatuated with it, and unattached to it, seeing the danger and possessing the wisdom of escape.”

“Tatra, gahapati, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena, adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena na attānaṃ sukheti na pīṇeti na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karoti, ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī tīhi ṭhānehi gārayho. ‘Adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenā’ti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena gārayho. ‘Na attānaṃ sukheti na pīṇetī’ti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena [V 3.0152] gārayho. ‘Na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karotī’ti, iminā tatiyena ṭhānena gārayho. Ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī imehi tīhi ṭhānehi gārayho.

“Among these, householder, as to that enjoyer of sensual pleasures who seeks wealth unrighteously and by force, and having sought wealth unrighteously and by force, does not make himself happy, does not gratify himself, does not share, and does not perform meritorious deeds—this enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is blameworthy on three grounds. Because ‘he seeks wealth unrighteously and by force,’ on this first ground he is blameworthy. Because ‘he does not make himself happy and does not gratify himself,’ on this second ground he is blameworthy. Because ‘he does not share and does not perform meritorious deeds,’ on this third ground he is blameworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is blameworthy on these three grounds.

“Tatra, gahapati, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena, adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karoti, ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenā’ti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena gārayho. ‘Attānaṃ sukheti pīṇetī’ti, iminā ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karotī’ti iminā dutiyena ṭhānena gārayho. Ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī imehi dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho iminā ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso.

“Among these, householder, as to that enjoyer of sensual pleasures who seeks wealth unrighteously and by force, and having sought wealth unrighteously and by force, makes himself happy and gratifies himself, but does not share and does not perform meritorious deeds—this enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is blameworthy on two grounds and praiseworthy on one ground. Because ‘he seeks wealth unrighteously and by force,’ on this first ground he is blameworthy. Because ‘he makes himself happy and gratifies himself,’ on this one ground he is praiseworthy. Because ‘he does not share and does not perform meritorious deeds,’ on this second ground he is blameworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is blameworthy on these two grounds and praiseworthy on this one ground.

“Tatra[P 5.0179], gahapati, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasena[T 5.0191], adhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti, ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī ekena ṭhānena gārayho dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso. ‘Adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenā’ti, iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho. ‘Attānaṃ sukheti [M 3.0401] pīṇetī’ti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Saṃvibhajati puññāni karotī’ti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho, imehi dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso.

“Among these, householder, as to that enjoyer of sensual pleasures who seeks wealth unrighteously and by force, and having sought wealth unrighteously and by force, makes himself happy, gratifies himself, shares, and performs meritorious deeds—this enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is blameworthy on one ground and praiseworthy on two grounds. Because ‘he seeks wealth unrighteously and by force,’ on this one ground he is blameworthy. Because ‘he makes himself happy and gratifies himself,’ on this first ground he is praiseworthy. Because ‘he shares and performs meritorious deeds,’ on this second ground he is praiseworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is blameworthy on this one ground and praiseworthy on these two grounds.

“Tatra, gahapati, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi, dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi na attānaṃ sukheti na pīṇeti na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karoti, ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso tīhi ṭhānehi gārayho. ‘Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenā’ti, iminā ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenā’ti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena gārayho. ‘Na attānaṃ sukheti na pīṇetī’ti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena gārayho. ‘Na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karotī’ti, iminā tatiyena ṭhānena gārayho. Ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī iminā ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso imehi tīhi ṭhānehi gārayho.

“Among these, householder, as to that enjoyer of sensual pleasures who seeks wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both with force and without force; and having sought wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both with force and without force, does not make himself happy, does not gratify himself, does not share, and does not perform meritorious deeds—this enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is praiseworthy on one ground and blameworthy on three grounds. Because ‘he seeks wealth righteously and without force,’ on this one ground he is praiseworthy. Because ‘he seeks wealth unrighteously and with force,’ on this first ground he is blameworthy. Because ‘he does not make himself happy and does not gratify himself,’ on this second ground he is blameworthy. Because ‘he does not share and does not perform meritorious deeds,’ on this third ground he is blameworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is praiseworthy on this one ground and blameworthy on these three grounds.

“Tatra[V 3.0153], gahapati, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi, dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karoti, ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho[T 5.0192]. ‘Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenā’ti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenā’ti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena gārayho. ‘Attānaṃ sukheti pīṇetī’ti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karotī’ti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena gārayho. Ayaṃ[P 5.0180], gahapati, kāmabhogī imehi dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso imehi dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho.

“Among these, householder, as to that enjoyer of sensual pleasures who seeks wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both with force and without force; and having sought wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both with force and without force, makes himself happy and gratifies himself, but does not share and does not perform meritorious deeds—this enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is praiseworthy on two grounds and blameworthy on two grounds. Because ‘he seeks wealth righteously and without force,’ on this first ground he is praiseworthy. Because ‘he seeks wealth unrighteously and with force,’ on this first ground he is blameworthy. Because ‘he makes himself happy and gratifies himself,’ on this second ground he is praiseworthy. Because ‘he does not share and does not perform meritorious deeds,’ on this second ground he is blameworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is praiseworthy on these two grounds and blameworthy on these two grounds.

“Tatra, gahapati, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenapi asāhasenapi, dhammādhammena bhoge pariyesitvā sāhasenapi asāhasenapi attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti, ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso ekena [M 3.0402] ṭhānena gārayho. ‘Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenā’ti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Adhammena bhoge pariyesati sāhasenā’ti, iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho. ‘Attānaṃ sukheti pīṇetī’ti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Saṃvibhajati puññāni karotī’ti, iminā tatiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī imehi tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho.

“Among these, householder, as to that enjoyer of sensual pleasures who seeks wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both with force and without force; and having sought wealth both righteously and unrighteously, both with force and without force, makes himself happy, gratifies himself, shares, and performs meritorious deeds—this enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is praiseworthy on three grounds and blameworthy on one ground. Because ‘he seeks wealth righteously and without force,’ on this first ground he is praiseworthy. Because ‘he seeks wealth unrighteously and with force,’ on this one ground he is blameworthy. Because ‘he makes himself happy and gratifies himself,’ on this second ground he is praiseworthy. Because ‘he shares and performs meritorious deeds,’ on this third ground he is praiseworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is praiseworthy on these three grounds and blameworthy on this one ground.

“Tatra, gahapati, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena, dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena na attānaṃ sukheti na pīṇeti na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karoti, ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho. Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenā’ti, iminā ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Na attānaṃ sukheti na pīṇetī’ti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena gārayho. ‘Na saṃvibhajati [T 5.0193] na puññāni karotī’ti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena gārayho. Ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī iminā ekena ṭhānena pāsaṃso imehi dvīhi ṭhānehi gārayho.

“Among these, householder, as to that enjoyer of sensual pleasures who seeks wealth righteously and without force; and having sought wealth righteously and without force, does not make himself happy, does not gratify himself, does not share, and does not perform meritorious deeds—this enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is praiseworthy on one ground and blameworthy on two grounds. Because ‘he seeks wealth righteously and without force,’ on this one ground he is praiseworthy. Because ‘he does not make himself happy and does not gratify himself,’ on this first ground he is blameworthy. Because ‘he does not share and does not perform meritorious deeds,’ on this second ground he is blameworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is praiseworthy on this one ground and blameworthy on these two grounds.

“Tatra, gahapati, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena, dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karoti, ayaṃ, gahapati[V 3.0154], kāmabhogī dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso ekena ṭhānena gārayho. ‘Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenā’ti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Attānaṃ sukheti pīṇetī’ti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Na saṃvibhajati na puññāni karotī’ti iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho. Ayaṃ[P 5.0181], gahapati, kāmabhogī imehi dvīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho.

“Herein, householder, there is the enjoyer of sensual pleasures who seeks wealth righteously and without force; and having sought wealth righteously and without force, he makes himself happy and gratified, but does not share it and does not perform meritorious deeds. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is praiseworthy on two grounds and blameworthy on one ground. ‘He seeks wealth righteously and without force’—on this first ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He makes himself happy and gratified’—on this second ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He does not share it and does not perform meritorious deeds’—on this one ground he is blameworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is praiseworthy on these two grounds and blameworthy on this one ground.

“Tatra, gahapati yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena, dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti, te ca bhoge gathito mucchito ajjhosanno anādīnavadassāvī anissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati, ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso ekena ṭhānena gārayho. ‘Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenā’ti, iminā paṭhamena [M 3.0403] ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Attānaṃ sukheti pīṇetī’ti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Saṃvibhajati puññāni karotī’ti, iminā tatiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Te ca bhoge gathito mucchito ajjhosanno anādīnavadassāvī anissaraṇapañño paribhuñjatī’ti[T 5.0194], iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho. Ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī imehi tīhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso iminā ekena ṭhānena gārayho.

“Herein, householder, there is the enjoyer of sensual pleasures who seeks wealth righteously and without force; and having sought wealth righteously and without force, he makes himself happy and gratified, shares it, and performs meritorious deeds, but he enjoys that wealth being greedy for it, infatuated with it, and attached to it, not seeing the danger and being without wisdom regarding the escape. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is praiseworthy on three grounds and blameworthy on one ground. ‘He seeks wealth righteously and without force’—on this first ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He makes himself happy and gratified’—on this second ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He shares it and performs meritorious deeds’—on this third ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He enjoys that wealth being greedy for it, infatuated with it, and attached to it, not seeing the danger and being without wisdom regarding the escape’—on this one ground he is blameworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is praiseworthy on these three grounds and blameworthy on this one ground.

“Tatra, gahapati, yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena, dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti, te ca bhoge agathito amucchito anajjhosanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati, ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī catūhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso. ‘Dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasenā’ti, iminā paṭhamena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Attānaṃ sukheti pīṇetī’ti, iminā dutiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Saṃvibhajati puññāni karotī’ti, iminā tatiyena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. ‘Te ca bhoge agathito amucchito anajjhosanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjatī’ti, iminā catutthena ṭhānena pāsaṃso. Ayaṃ, gahapati, kāmabhogī imehi catūhi ṭhānehi pāsaṃso.

“Herein, householder, there is an enjoyer of sensual pleasures who seeks wealth by rightful means, without violence; having sought wealth by rightful means and without violence, he makes himself happy and gratifies himself, shares it, and performs meritorious deeds; and he enjoys that wealth without being greedy for it, infatuated with it, or attached to it, seeing the danger in it and discerning the escape from it. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is praiseworthy on four grounds. ‘He seeks wealth by rightful means, without violence’—on this first ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He makes himself happy and gratifies himself’—on this second ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He shares it and performs meritorious deeds’—on this third ground he is praiseworthy. ‘He enjoys that wealth without being greedy for it, infatuated with it, or attached to it, seeing the danger in it and discerning the escape from it’—on this fourth ground he is praiseworthy. This enjoyer of sensual pleasures, householder, is praiseworthy on these four grounds.

“Ime kho, gahapati, dasa kāmabhogī santo saṃvijjamānā lokasmiṃ. Imesaṃ kho, gahapati, dasannaṃ kāmabhogīnaṃ yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena, dhammena [P 5.0182] bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati puññāni karoti, te ca bhoge [V 3.0155] agathito amucchito anajjhosanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati, ayaṃ imesaṃ dasannaṃ kāmabhogīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca pāmokkho mokkho (ka. sī.) a. ni. 4.95; 5.181; saṃ. ni. 3.662 ca uttamo ca pavaro ca. Seyyathāpi, gahapati, gavā khīraṃ, khīramhā dadhi, dadhimhā navanītaṃ, navanītamhā sappi, sappimhā sappimaṇḍo. Sappimaṇḍo tattha aggamakkhāyati.

“These, householder, are the ten enjoyers of sensual pleasures who are found existing in the world. Among these ten enjoyers of sensual pleasures, the one who seeks wealth by rightful means, without violence; having sought wealth by rightful means and without violence, makes himself happy and gratifies himself, shares it, and performs meritorious deeds; and enjoys that wealth without being greedy for it, infatuated with it, or attached to it, seeing the danger in it and discerning the escape from it—this one is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent among these ten enjoyers of sensual pleasures. Just as, householder, from a cow comes milk, from milk comes curd, from curd comes fresh butter, from fresh butter comes ghee, and from ghee comes the cream of ghee; the cream of ghee is declared the best among them.

Evamevaṃ kho[T 5.0195], gahapati, imesaṃ dasannaṃ kāmabhogīnaṃ yvāyaṃ kāmabhogī dhammena bhoge pariyesati asāhasena, dhammena bhoge pariyesitvā asāhasena attānaṃ sukheti pīṇeti saṃvibhajati [M 3.0404] puññāni karoti, te ca bhoge agathito amucchito anajjhosanno ādīnavadassāvī nissaraṇapañño paribhuñjati, ayaṃ imesaṃ dasannaṃ kāmabhogīnaṃ aggo ca seṭṭho ca pāmokkho mokkho (ka. sī.) a. ni. 5.181 ca uttamo ca pavaro cā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“In the same way, householder, among these ten enjoyers of sensual pleasures, the one who seeks wealth by rightful means, without violence; having sought wealth by rightful means and without violence, makes himself happy and gratifies himself, shares it, and performs meritorious deeds; and enjoys that wealth without being greedy for it, infatuated with it, or attached to it, seeing the danger in it and discerning the escape from it—this one is the foremost, the best, the chief, the highest, and the most excellent among these ten enjoyers of sensual pleasures.” First.

2. Bhayasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on Fear

92. a. ni. 9.27; saṃ. ni. 5.1024 Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ bhagavā etadavoca –

92. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika went to the Blessed One, approached, paid homage to the Blessed One, and sat down to one side. As he was sitting to one side, the Blessed One said this to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika:

“Yato, kho, gahapati, ariyasāvakassa pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti, catūhi ca sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, ariyo cassa ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho, so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto. Sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo’ti.

“Householder, when five fears and enmities have been pacified for a noble disciple, and he is endowed with the four factors of stream-entry, and the noble method has been well seen and well penetrated by him with wisdom, if he so wishes, he may declare of himself: ‘I am one for whom hell is destroyed, the animal realm is destroyed, the realm of ghosts is destroyed, the plane of misery, the bad destinations, and the lower worlds are destroyed. I am a stream-enterer, no longer subject to falling into the lower realms, certain, and destined for enlightenment.’”

“Katamāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti? Yaṃ[P 5.0183], gahapati, pāṇātipātī pāṇātipātapaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṃ veraṃ pasavati samparāyikampi bhayaṃ veraṃ pasavati cetasikampi dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti, pāṇātipātā paṭivirato neva diṭṭhadhammikampi neva diṭṭhadhammikaṃ bhayaṃ veraṃ pasavati na samparāyikampi na samparāyikaṃ bhayaṃ veraṃ pasavati na cetasikampi na cetasikaṃ (sī. syā. pī.) dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti. Pāṇātipātā paṭiviratassa evaṃ taṃ bhayaṃ veraṃ vūpasantaṃ hoti[T 5.0196].

“What five fears and enmities have been pacified? Householder, one who destroys life, on account of destroying life, generates fear and enmity in the present life and fear and enmity in future lives, and he experiences mental suffering and displeasure. For one who abstains from destroying life, he does not generate fear and enmity in the present life, nor does he generate fear and enmity in future lives, nor does he experience mental suffering and displeasure. For one who abstains from destroying life, that fear and enmity is thus pacified.

“Yaṃ[V 3.0156], gahapati, adinnādāyī…pe… kāmesumicchācārī… musāvādī… surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhāyī surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānapaccayā diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṃ veraṃ pasavati samparāyikampi bhayaṃ veraṃ pasavati cetasikampi dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti, surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭivirato neva diṭṭhadhammikampi bhayaṃ veraṃ pasavati na samparāyikampi bhayaṃ veraṃ pasavati na cetasikampi dukkhaṃ domanassaṃ paṭisaṃvedeti. Surāmerayamajjapamādaṭṭhānā paṭiviratassa evaṃ [M 3.0405] taṃ bhayaṃ veraṃ vūpasantaṃ hoti. Imāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti.

“Householder, one who takes what is not given… one who engages in sexual misconduct… one who speaks falsely… one who partakes of liquor, wine, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence, on account of partaking of liquor, wine, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence, generates fear and enmity in the present life and fear and enmity in future lives, and experiences mental suffering and displeasure. One who abstains from liquor, wine, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence generates neither fear and enmity in the present life, nor fear and enmity in future lives, nor does one experience mental suffering and displeasure. For one who abstains from liquor, wine, and intoxicants which are the basis for negligence, that fear and enmity is thus pacified. These five fears and enmities are pacified.

“Katamehi catūhi sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti? Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako buddhe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘itipi so bhagavā…pe… buddho bhagavā’ti; dhamme aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘svākkhāto bhagavatā dhammo sandiṭṭhiko akāliko ehipassiko opaneyyiko paccattaṃ veditabbo viññūhī’ti; saṅghe aveccappasādena samannāgato hoti – ‘suppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ujuppaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, ñāyappaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, sāmīcippaṭipanno bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho, yadidaṃ cattāri purisayugāni aṭṭha purisapuggalā, esa bhagavato sāvakasaṅgho āhuneyyo pāhuneyyo dakkhiṇeyyo añjalikaraṇīyo anuttaraṃ puññakkhettaṃ lokassā’ti; ariyakantehi sīlehi samannāgato hoti [P 5.0184] ‘akhaṇḍehi acchiddehi asabalehi akammāsehi bhujissehi viññuppasatthehi aparāmaṭṭhehi [T 5.0197] samādhisaṃvattanikehi’. Imehi catūhi sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti.

With which four factors of stream-entry is one endowed? Here, householder, a noble disciple is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Buddha thus: ‘Indeed, the Blessed One is an Arahant... the Buddha, the Blessed One.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Dhamma thus: ‘The Dhamma is well-proclaimed by the Blessed One, directly visible, immediate, inviting one to come and see, leading onward, to be personally experienced by the wise.’ He is endowed with unwavering confidence in the Sangha thus: ‘The Sangha of the Blessed One’s disciples is practicing the good way, practicing the straight way, practicing the true way, practicing the proper way; that is, the four pairs of persons, the eight types of individuals—this Sangha of the Blessed One’s disciples is worthy of gifts, worthy of hospitality, worthy of offerings, worthy of reverential salutation, the unsurpassed field of merit for the world.’ He is endowed with virtues dear to the noble ones, unbroken, unperforated, unspotted, unblemished, liberating, praised by the wise, unsullied, conducive to concentration. With these four factors of stream-entry he is endowed.

“Katamo cassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho? Idha, gahapati, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘iti imasmiṃ sati idaṃ hoti; imassuppādā idaṃ uppajjati; imasmiṃ asati idaṃ na hoti; imassa nirodhā idaṃ nirujjhati, yadidaṃ – avijjāpaccayā saṅkhārā, saṅkhārapaccayā viññāṇaṃ, viññāṇapaccayā nāmarūpaṃ, nāmarūpapaccayā saḷāyatanaṃ, saḷāyatanapaccayā phasso, phassapaccayā vedanā, vedanāpaccayā taṇhā, taṇhāpaccayā upādānaṃ, upādānapaccayā bhavo, bhavapaccayā jāti, jātipaccayā jarāmaraṇaṃ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā sambhavanti, evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa samudayo hoti; avijjāya tveva asesavirāganirodhā saṅkhāranirodho…pe… evametassa kevalassa dukkhakkhandhassa [V 3.0157] nirodho hotī’ti. Ayañcassa ariyo ñāyo paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho.

And what is the noble method that is well seen and well penetrated with wisdom? Here, householder, a noble disciple reflects thus: ‘When this exists, that comes to be; with the arising of this, that arises. When this does not exist, that does not come to be; with the cessation of this, that ceases. That is to say: with ignorance as condition, formations come to be; with formations as condition, consciousness comes to be; with consciousness as condition, name-and-form comes to be; with name-and-form as condition, the six sense bases come to be; with the six sense bases as condition, contact comes to be; with contact as condition, feeling comes to be; with feeling as condition, craving comes to be; with craving as condition, clinging comes to be; with clinging as condition, becoming comes to be; with becoming as condition, birth comes to be; with birth as condition, aging-and-death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair come to be. Such is the origin of this whole mass of suffering. But with the remainderless fading away and cessation of that very ignorance, formations cease… and so forth… such is the cessation of this whole mass of suffering.’ This is the noble method that is well seen and well penetrated with wisdom.

“Yato kho, gahapati, ariyasāvakassa imāni pañca bhayāni verāni vūpasantāni honti, imehi ca catūhi sotāpattiyaṅgehi samannāgato hoti, ayañcassa ariyo ñāyo [T 5.0198] paññāya sudiṭṭho hoti suppaṭividdho[M 3.0406], so ākaṅkhamāno attanāva attānaṃ byākareyya – ‘khīṇanirayomhi khīṇatiracchānayoni khīṇapettivisayo khīṇāpāyaduggativinipāto; sotāpannohamasmi avinipātadhammo niyato sambodhiparāyaṇo”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

When, householder, these five fears and enmities have been pacified for a noble disciple, and he is endowed with these four factors of stream-entry, and this noble method has been well seen and well penetrated with wisdom, then, if he so wishes, he may declare of himself: ‘I am one for whom hell is destroyed, the animal realm is destroyed, the realm of ghosts is destroyed, the plane of misery, the bad destinations, and the lower worlds are destroyed. I am a stream-enterer, no longer subject to falling into states of woe, certain, and destined for supreme enlightenment.’ The second.

3. Kiṃdiṭṭhikasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on What View

93. Ekaṃ [P 5.0185] samayaṃ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṃ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati divā divassa sāvatthiyā nikkhami bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍikassa gahapatissa etadahosi – “akālo kho tāva bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Paṭisallīno bhagavā. Manobhāvanīyānampi bhikkhūnaṃ akālo dassanāya. Paṭisallīnā manobhāvanīyā bhikkhū. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ ārāmo tenupasaṅkameyya”nti.

93. On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī, in Jeta's Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika's monastery. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, in the middle of the day, left Sāvatthī to see the Blessed One. Then it occurred to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika: “It is not the right time to see the Blessed One. The Blessed One is in seclusion. It is also not the right time to see the monks who are developing their minds. The monks who are developing their minds are in seclusion. Suppose I were to approach the monastery of the wanderers of other sects?”

Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ ārāmo tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho pana samayena aññatitthiyā paribbājakā saṅgamma samāgamma unnādino uccāsaddamahāsaddā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ kathentā nisinnā honti. Addasaṃsu kho te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna aññamaññaṃ saṇṭhāpesuṃ – “appasaddā bhonto hontu, mā bhonto saddamakattha. Ayaṃ anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati ārāmaṃ āgacchati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvako. Yāvatā kho pana samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakā gihī odātavasanā sāvatthiyaṃ paṭivasanti, ayaṃ tesaṃ aññataro anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati. Appasaddakāmā [T 5.0199] kho pana te āyasmanto appasaddavinītā appasaddassa vaṇṇavādino. Appeva nāma appasaddaṃ parisaṃ viditvā upasaṅkamitabbaṃ maññeyyā”ti.

Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika approached the monastery of the wanderers of other sects. At that time, those wanderers of other sects had gathered together and were sitting, making a great clamor and loud noise, engaged in various kinds of worldly talk. Those wanderers of other sects saw the householder Anāthapiṇḍika coming from afar. Upon seeing him, they quieted one another: “Sirs, be quiet; sirs, do not make a sound. This householder Anāthapiṇḍika, a disciple of the ascetic Gotama, is approaching the monastery. Of all the white-clad lay disciples of the ascetic Gotama who reside in Sāvatthī, this householder Anāthapiṇḍika is one. Those venerables desire quiet, are trained in quiet, and speak in praise of quiet. Perhaps, upon seeing a quiet assembly, he might think it worth approaching.”

Atha [V 3.0158] kho te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yena te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ [P 5.0186] vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā [M 3.0407] etadavocuṃ – “vadehi, gahapati, kiṃdiṭṭhiko samaṇo gotamo”ti? “Na kho ahaṃ, bhante, bhagavato sabbaṃ diṭṭhiṃ jānāmī”ti.

Then those wanderers of other sects became silent. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika approached those wanderers of other sects. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with them. After concluding this courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. As the householder Anāthapiṇḍika was sitting to one side, those wanderers of other sects said this to him: “Tell us, householder, what is the view of the ascetic Gotama?” “Venerable sirs, I do not know all of the Blessed One's views.”

“Iti kira tvaṃ, gahapati, na samaṇassa gotamassa sabbaṃ diṭṭhiṃ jānāsi; vadehi, gahapati, kiṃdiṭṭhikā bhikkhū”ti? “Bhikkhūnampi kho ahaṃ, bhante, na sabbaṃ diṭṭhiṃ jānāmī”ti.

“So, householder, you do not know all the views of the ascetic Gotama? Then tell us, householder, what is the view of the monks?” “Venerable sirs, I do not know all the views of the monks either.”

“Iti kira tvaṃ, gahapati, na samaṇassa gotamassa sabbaṃ diṭṭhiṃ jānāsi napi bhikkhūnaṃ sabbaṃ diṭṭhiṃ jānāsi; vadehi, gahapati, kiṃdiṭṭhikosi tuva”nti? “Etaṃ kho, bhante, amhehi na dukkaraṃ byākātuṃ yaṃdiṭṭhikā mayaṃ. Iṅgha tāva āyasmanto yathāsakāni diṭṭhigatāni byākarontu, pacchāpetaṃ amhehi na dukkaraṃ bhavissati byākātuṃ yaṃdiṭṭhikā maya”nti.

“So, householder, it seems you do not know all the views of the ascetic Gotama, nor do you know all the views of the monks. Tell us, householder, what is your view?” “Venerable sirs, it is not difficult for us to declare what our view is. Come now, let the venerable ones first declare their own respective views. Afterwards, it will not be difficult for us to declare what our view is.”

Evaṃ vutte aññataro paribbājako anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “sassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhiko ahaṃ, gahapatī”ti.

When this was said, a certain wanderer said this to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika: “The world is eternal; this alone is true, anything else is futile—this, householder, is my view.”

Aññataropi kho [T 5.0200] paribbājako anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “asassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhiko ahaṃ, gahapatī”ti.

Another wanderer also said this to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika: “The world is not eternal; this alone is true, anything else is futile—this, householder, is my view.”

Aññataropi kho paribbājako anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavoca – “antavā loko…pe… anantavā loko… taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ… aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ… hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā… na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā… hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhiko ahaṃ, gahapatī”ti.

Another wanderer also said this to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika: 'The world is finite... the world is infinite... the life-principle is the same as the body... the life-principle is different from the body... a being exists after death... a being does not exist after death... a being both exists and does not exist after death... a being neither exists nor does not exist after death. This alone is true; anything else is futile. I am of such a view, householder.'

Evaṃ [V 3.0159] vutte anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati te paribbājake etadavoca – “yvāyaṃ, bhante, āyasmā evamāha – ‘sassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhiko ahaṃ, gahapatī’ti[P 5.0187], imassa ayamāyasmato diṭṭhi attano vā ayonisomanasikārahetu uppannā paratoghosapaccayā vā. Sā kho panesā diṭṭhi bhūtā saṅkhatā cetayitā paṭiccasamuppannā. Yaṃ kho pana kiñci bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ cetayitaṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ tadaniccaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ. Yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadeveso āyasmā allīno, tadeveso āyasmā ajjhupagato.

When this was said, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika said to those wanderers: 'Venerable sirs, regarding the venerable one who speaks thus: "The world is eternal. This alone is true; anything else is futile. I am of such a view, householder," this view of that venerable one has arisen either from his own unwise attention or from the utterance of another as a condition. Indeed, that view has come to be, is conditioned, is volitionally formed, and is dependently arisen. And whatever has come to be, is conditioned, is volitionally formed, and is dependently arisen, that is impermanent. What is impermanent, that is suffering. It is to that which is suffering that this venerable one is attached; it is to that very thing that this venerable one adheres.'

“Yopāyaṃ[M 3.0408], bhante, āyasmā evamāha – ‘asassato loko, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhiko ahaṃ, gahapatī’ti, imassāpi ayamāyasmato diṭṭhi attano vā ayonisomanasikārahetu uppannā paratoghosapaccayā vā. Sā kho panesā diṭṭhi bhūtā saṅkhatā cetayitā paṭiccasamuppannā. Yaṃ kho pana kiñci bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ cetayitaṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ tadaniccaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ. Yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadeveso āyasmā allīno, tadeveso āyasmā ajjhupagato.

Venerable sirs, regarding the venerable one who speaks thus: 'The world is not eternal. This alone is true; anything else is futile. I am of such a view, householder,' this view of that venerable one has also arisen either from his own unwise attention or from the utterance of another as a condition. Indeed, that view has come to be, is conditioned, is volitionally formed, and is dependently arisen. And whatever has come to be, is conditioned, is volitionally formed, and is dependently arisen, that is impermanent. What is impermanent, that is suffering. It is to that which is suffering that this venerable one is attached; it is to that very thing that this venerable one adheres.'

“Yopāyaṃ, bhante, āyasmā evamāha – ‘antavā loko [T 5.0201] …pe… anantavā loko… taṃ jīvaṃ taṃ sarīraṃ… aññaṃ jīvaṃ aññaṃ sarīraṃ… hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā… na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā… hoti ca na ca hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā… neva hoti na na hoti tathāgato paraṃ maraṇā, idameva saccaṃ moghamaññanti – evaṃdiṭṭhiko ahaṃ, gahapatī’ti, imassāpi ayamāyasmato diṭṭhi attano vā ayonisomanasikārahetu uppannā paratoghosapaccayā vā. Sā kho panesā diṭṭhi bhūtā saṅkhatā cetayitā paṭiccasamuppannā. Yaṃ kho pana kiñci bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ cetayitaṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ tadaniccaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ. Yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadeveso āyasmā allīno, tadeveso āyasmā ajjhupagato”ti.

Venerable sirs, regarding the venerable one who speaks thus: 'The world is finite... the world is infinite... the life-principle is the same as the body... the life-principle is different from the body... a being exists after death... a being does not exist after death... a being both exists and does not exist after death... a being neither exists nor does not exist after death. This alone is true; anything else is futile. I am of such a view, householder,' this view of that venerable one has also arisen either from his own unwise attention or from the utterance of another as a condition. Indeed, that view has come to be, is conditioned, is volitionally formed, and is dependently arisen. And whatever has come to be, is conditioned, is volitionally formed, and is dependently arisen, that is impermanent. What is impermanent, that is suffering. It is to that which is suffering that this venerable one is attached; it is to that very thing that this venerable one adheres.'

Evaṃ [P 5.0188] vutte te paribbājakā anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ etadavocuṃ – “byākatāni kho, gahapati, amhehi sabbeheva yathāsakāni diṭṭhigatāni. Vadehi, gahapati, kiṃdiṭṭhikosi tuva”nti? “Yaṃ kho, bhante, kiñci bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ cetayitaṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ tadaniccaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ. ‘Yaṃ dukkhaṃ taṃ netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, na meso attā’ti – evaṃdiṭṭhiko ahaṃ, bhante”ti.

When this was said, those wanderers said to the householder Anāthapiṇḍika: 'Householder, we have all indeed declared our respective views. Tell us, householder, of what view are you?' 'Venerable sirs, whatever has come to be, is conditioned, is volitionally formed, and is dependently arisen, that is impermanent. What is impermanent, that is suffering. Regarding that which is suffering, I hold the view: "This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self." Such is my view, venerable sirs.'

“Yaṃ [V 3.0160] kho, gahapati, kiñci bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ cetayitaṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ tadaniccaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ. Yaṃ dukkhaṃ tadeva tvaṃ, gahapati, allīno, tadeva tvaṃ, gahapati, ajjhupagato”ti.

Householder, whatever has come to be, is conditioned, is volitionally formed, and is dependently arisen, that is impermanent. What is impermanent, that is suffering. It is to that which is suffering that you, householder, are attached; it is to that very thing that you, householder, adhere.

“Yaṃ kho, bhante, kiñci bhūtaṃ saṅkhataṃ cetayitaṃ paṭiccasamuppannaṃ tadaniccaṃ. Yadaniccaṃ taṃ dukkhaṃ. ‘Yaṃ dukkhaṃ taṃ netaṃ mama, nesohamasmi, nameso attā’ti – evametaṃ yathābhūtaṃ sammappaññāya sudiṭṭhaṃ[T 5.0202]. Tassa ca uttari nissaraṇaṃ yathābhūtaṃ pajānāmī”ti.

Venerable sirs, whatever has come to be, is conditioned, is volitionally formed, and is dependently arisen, that is impermanent. What is impermanent, that is suffering. That which is suffering, I have well seen as it actually is with right wisdom thus: 'This is not mine, this I am not, this is not my self.' And I know as it actually is the further escape beyond it.

Evaṃ [M 3.0409] vutte te paribbājakā tuṇhībhūtā maṅkubhūtā pattakkhandhā adhomukhā pajjhāyantā appaṭibhānā nisīdiṃsu. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati te paribbājake tuṇhībhūte maṅkubhūte pattakkhandhe adhomukhe pajjhāyante appaṭibhāne viditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati yāvatako ahosi tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṃ kathāsallāpo taṃ sabbaṃ bhagavato ārocesi. “Sādhu sādhu, gahapati! Evaṃ kho te, gahapati, moghapurisā kālena kālaṃ sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggahetabbā”ti.

When this was said, those wanderers were silent, dismayed, with shoulders drooping, downcast, brooding, unable to reply. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, knowing that those wanderers were silent, dismayed, with shoulders drooping, downcast, brooding, and unable to reply, rose from his seat, approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the householder Anāthapiṇḍika reported to the Blessed One the entire conversation he had had with those wanderers of other sects. 'Excellent, excellent, householder! In just this way, householder, those foolish men should from time to time be thoroughly rebuked in accordance with the Dhamma.'

Atha kho bhagavā anāthapiṇḍikaṃ gahapatiṃ dhammiyā kathāya sandassesi samādapesi samuttejesi sampahaṃsesi. Atha kho anāthapiṇḍiko gahapati bhagavatā dhammiyā kathāya sandassito samādapito samuttejito sampahaṃsito uṭṭhāyāsanā [P 5.0189] bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā padakkhiṇaṃ katvā pakkāmi.

Then the Blessed One instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened the householder Anāthapiṇḍika with a talk on the Dhamma. Then the householder Anāthapiṇḍika, having been instructed, encouraged, inspired, and gladdened by the Blessed One with a talk on the Dhamma, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Blessed One, circumambulated him keeping his right side toward him, and departed.

Atha kho bhagavā acirapakkante anāthapiṇḍike gahapatimhi bhikkhū āmantesi – “yopi so, bhikkhave, bhikkhu vassasatupasampanno bhikkhu dīgharattaṃ avedhi dhammo (syā.) imasmiṃ dhammavinaye, sopi evamevaṃ aññatitthiye paribbājake sahadhammena suniggahitaṃ niggaṇheyya yathā taṃ anāthapiṇḍikena gahapatinā niggahitā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

Then, not long after the householder Anāthapiṇḍika had departed, the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus: 'Bhikkhus, even a bhikkhu in this Dhamma and Discipline who has been ordained for a hundred years should thoroughly rebuke wanderers of other sects in accordance with the Dhamma in the very same way that they were rebuked by the householder Anāthapiṇḍika.' The third.

4. Vajjiyamāhitasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse to Vajjiyamāhita

94. Ekaṃ [V 3.0161] samayaṃ bhagavā campāyaṃ viharati gaggarāya pokkharaṇiyā tīre. Atha kho vajjiyamāhito gahapati divā divassa campāya nikkhami bhagavantaṃ [T 5.0203] dassanāya. Atha kho vajjiyamāhitassa gahapatissa etadahosi – “akālo kho tāva bhagavantaṃ dassanāya. Paṭisallīno bhagavā. Manobhāvanīyānampi bhikkhūnaṃ akālo dassanāya. Paṭisallīnā manobhāvanīyāpi bhikkhū. Yaṃnūnāhaṃ yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ ārāmo tenupasaṅkameyya”nti.

94. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Campā on the bank of the Gaggarā lotus pond. Then, in the middle of the day, the householder Vajjiyamāhita left Campā to see the Blessed One. Then it occurred to the householder Vajjiyamāhita: “It is not yet the time to see the Blessed One. The Blessed One is in seclusion. It is also not the time to see the bhikkhus who develop the mind. The bhikkhus who develop the mind are also in seclusion. What if I were to go to the park of the wanderers of other sects?”

Atha [M 3.0410] kho vajjiyamāhito gahapati yena aññatitthiyānaṃ paribbājakānaṃ ārāmo tenupasaṅkami. Tena kho pana samayena te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā saṅgamma samāgamma unnādino uccāsaddamahāsaddā anekavihitaṃ tiracchānakathaṃ kathentā nisinnā honti.

Then the householder Vajjiyamāhita approached the park of the wanderers of other sects. Now at that time, those wanderers of other sects were seated, having gathered together, making a noisy din, with high voices and great noise, speaking on many kinds of worldly talk.

Addasaṃsu kho te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā vajjiyamāhitaṃ gahapatiṃ dūratova āgacchantaṃ. Disvāna aññamaññaṃ saṇṭhāpesuṃ – “appasaddā bhonto hontu. Mā bhonto saddamakattha. Ayaṃ vajjiyamāhito gahapati āgacchati samaṇassa gotamassa sāvako. Yāvatā kho pana [P 5.0190] samaṇassa gotamassa sāvakā gihī odātavasanā campāyaṃ paṭivasanti, ayaṃ tesaṃ aññataro vajjiyamāhito gahapati. Appasaddakāmā kho pana te āyasmanto appasaddavinītā appasaddassa vaṇṇavādino. Appeva nāma appasaddaṃ parisaṃ viditvā upasaṅkamitabbaṃ maññeyyā”ti.

Those wanderers of other sects saw the householder Vajjiyamāhita coming from afar. Seeing him, they settled each other down, saying: “Sirs, be quiet! Sirs, do not make a sound! This householder Vajjiyamāhita, a disciple of the ascetic Gotama, is coming. Of all the lay disciples of the ascetic Gotama dressed in white who dwell in Campā, this householder Vajjiyamāhita is one of them. Those venerable ones are fond of quiet, trained in quiet, and speak in praise of quiet. Perhaps, knowing the assembly to be quiet, he might think it fit to approach.”

Atha kho te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā tuṇhī ahesuṃ. Atha kho vajjiyamāhito gahapati yena te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā tehi aññatitthiyehi paribbājakehi saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinnaṃ kho vajjiyamāhitaṃ gahapatiṃ te aññatitthiyā paribbājakā etadavocuṃ – “saccaṃ [T 5.0204] kira, gahapati, samaṇo gotamo sabbaṃ tapaṃ garahati, sabbaṃ tapassiṃ lūkhājīviṃ ekaṃsena upakkosati upavadatī”ti? “Na kho, bhante, bhagavā sabbaṃ tapaṃ garahati napi sabbaṃ tapassiṃ lūkhājīviṃ ekaṃsena upakkosati upavadati. Gārayhaṃ kho, bhante, bhagavā garahati[V 3.0162], pasaṃsitabbaṃ pasaṃsati. Gārayhaṃ kho pana, bhante, bhagavā garahanto pasaṃsitabbaṃ pasaṃsanto vibhajjavādo bhagavā. Na so bhagavā ettha ekaṃsavādo”ti.

Then those wanderers of other sects became silent. Then the householder Vajjiyamāhita approached those wanderers of other sects. Having approached, he exchanged greetings with them. After concluding the pleasant and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. To the householder Vajjiyamāhita, who was seated to one side, those wanderers of other sects said this: “Is it true, householder, as is said, that the ascetic Gotama criticizes all asceticism, and that he categorically reviles and disparages every ascetic who lives a harsh life?” “No, venerable sirs, the Blessed One does not criticize all asceticism, nor does he categorically revile and disparage every ascetic who lives a harsh life. Venerable sirs, the Blessed One criticizes what is blameworthy and praises what is praiseworthy.
