“Sammāsaṅkappassa, bhikkhave, micchāsaṅkappo nijjiṇṇo hoti; ye ca micchāsaṅkappapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā [T 5.0230] sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti; sammāsaṅkappapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti.

“Monks, for one with right thought, wrong thought is eradicated; and for him, the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong thought are also eradicated; and conditioned by right thought, many wholesome states reach fulfillment through development.

“Sammāvācassa, bhikkhave, micchāvācā nijjiṇṇā hoti; ye ca micchāvācāpaccayā aneke [V 3.0183] pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti; sammāvācāpaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti.

“Monks, for one with right speech, wrong speech is eradicated; and for him, the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong speech are also eradicated; and conditioned by right speech, many wholesome states reach fulfillment through development.

“Sammākammantassa, bhikkhave, micchākammanto nijjiṇṇo hoti; ye ca micchākammantapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti; sammākammantapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti.

“Monks, for one with right action, wrong action is eradicated; and for him, the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong action are also eradicated; and conditioned by right action, many wholesome states reach fulfillment through development.

“Sammāājīvassa[M 3.0431], bhikkhave, micchāājīvo nijjiṇṇo hoti; ye ca micchāājīvapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti; sammāājīvapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti.

“Monks, for one with right livelihood, wrong livelihood is eradicated; and for him, the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong livelihood are also eradicated; and conditioned by right livelihood, many wholesome states reach fulfillment through development.

“Sammāvāyāmassa, bhikkhave, micchāvāyāmo nijjiṇṇo hoti; ye ca micchāvāyāmapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti; sammāvāyāmapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti.

“Monks, for one with right effort, wrong effort is eradicated; and for him, the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong effort are also eradicated; and conditioned by right effort, many wholesome states reach fulfillment through development.

“Sammāsatissa, bhikkhave, micchāsati nijjiṇṇā hoti; ye ca micchāsatipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti; sammāsatipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti.

“Monks, for one with right mindfulness, wrong mindfulness is eradicated; and for him, the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong mindfulness are also eradicated; and conditioned by right mindfulness, many wholesome states reach fulfillment through development.

“Sammāsamādhissa, bhikkhave, micchāsamādhi nijjiṇṇo hoti; ye ca micchāsamādhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti [T 5.0231] te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti; sammāsamādhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā [P 5.0216] dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti.

“Monks, for one with right concentration, wrong concentration is eradicated; and for him, the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong concentration are also eradicated; and conditioned by right concentration, many wholesome states reach fulfillment through development.

“Sammāñāṇissa, bhikkhave, micchāñāṇaṃ nijjiṇṇaṃ hoti; ye ca micchāñāṇapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti; sammāñāṇapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti.

Bhikkhus, for one with right knowledge, wrong knowledge is worn out; and for him, the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong knowledge are also worn out; and conditioned by right knowledge, many wholesome states reach fulfillment through development.

“Sammāvimuttissa, bhikkhave, micchāvimutti nijjiṇṇā hoti; ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā [V 3.0184] aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa nijjiṇṇā honti; sammāvimuttipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti. Imāni kho, bhikkhave, dasa nijjaravatthūnī”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

Bhikkhus, for one with right liberation, wrong liberation is worn out; and for him, the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong liberation are also worn out; and conditioned by right liberation, many wholesome states reach fulfillment through development. Indeed, Bhikkhus, these are the ten grounds for wearing out. The sixth.

7. Dhovanasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on Washing

107. “Atthi, bhikkhave, dakkhiṇesu janapadesu dhovanaṃ nāma. Tattha hoti annampi pānampi khajjampi bhojjampi leyyampi peyyampi naccampi gītampi vāditampi. Atthetaṃ, bhikkhave, dhovanaṃ; ‘netaṃ natthī’ti vadāmi. Tañca kho etaṃ, bhikkhave, dhovanaṃ hīnaṃ gammaṃ pothujjanikaṃ anariyaṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ na nibbidāya na virāgāya [M 3.0432] na nirodhāya na upasamāya na abhiññāya na sambodhāya na nibbānāya saṃvattati.

107. “Bhikkhus, in the southern districts there is a custom called ‘bone-washing.’ There, there is food and drink, hard and soft food, things to be licked and drunk, dancing, singing, and instrumental music. That washing exists, bhikkhus; I do not say, ‘It does not exist.’ But that very washing, bhikkhus, is inferior, rustic, of the common folk, ignoble, not connected with benefit; it does not lead to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, or to Nibbāna.”

“Ahañca kho, bhikkhave, ariyaṃ dhovanaṃ desessāmi, yaṃ dhovanaṃ ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati, yaṃ dhovanaṃ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti, jarādhammā sattā jarāya parimuccanti, maraṇadhammā sattā maraṇena parimuccanti, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā [T 5.0232] sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccanti. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

“And I, bhikkhus, will teach the noble washing, a washing that leads exclusively to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, and to Nibbāna; a washing by means of which beings whose nature is to be born are freed from birth; beings whose nature is to age are freed from aging; beings whose nature is to die are freed from death; beings whose nature is sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are freed from sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. Listen to it, pay close attention; I will speak.” “Very well, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus responded to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Katamañca taṃ, bhikkhave, ariyaṃ dhovanaṃ, (yaṃ dhovanaṃ) ( ) natthi syāmapotthake ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya [P 5.0217] sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati, yaṃ dhovanaṃ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti, jarādhammā sattā jarāya parimuccanti, maraṇadhammā sattā maraṇena parimuccanti, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccanti?

“And what, bhikkhus, is that noble washing which leads exclusively to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, and to Nibbāna; a washing by means of which beings whose nature is to be born are freed from birth; beings whose nature is to age are freed from aging; beings whose nature is to die are freed from death; beings whose nature is sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are freed from sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair?”

“Sammādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, micchādiṭṭhi niddhotā hoti; ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke [V 3.0185] pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa niddhotā honti; sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti.

“Bhikkhus, for one with right view, wrong view is washed away; and for him, the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong view are also washed away; and conditioned by right view, many wholesome states reach fulfillment through development.

“Sammāsaṅkappassa, bhikkhave, micchāsaṅkappo niddhoto hoti…pe… sammāvācassa, bhikkhave, micchāvācā niddhotā hoti… sammākammantassa, bhikkhave, micchākammanto niddhoto hoti… sammāājīvassa, bhikkhave, micchāājīvo niddhoto hoti… sammāvāyāmassa, bhikkhave, micchāvāyāmo niddhoto hoti… sammāsatissa, bhikkhave, micchāsati niddhotā hoti… sammāsamādhissa, bhikkhave, micchāsamādhi niddhoto hoti… sammāñāṇissa, bhikkhave, micchāñāṇaṃ niddhotaṃ hoti…pe….

“Bhikkhus, for one with right intention, wrong intention is washed away… for one with right speech, wrong speech is washed away… for one with right action, wrong action is washed away… for one with right livelihood, wrong livelihood is washed away… for one with right effort, wrong effort is washed away… for one with right mindfulness, wrong mindfulness is washed away… for one with right concentration, wrong concentration is washed away… for one with right knowledge, wrong knowledge is washed away….”

“Sammāvimuttissa[M 3.0433], bhikkhave, micchāvimutti niddhotā hoti; ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa niddhotā honti; sammāvimuttipaccayā [T 5.0233] ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti. Idaṃ kho taṃ, bhikkhave, ariyaṃ dhovanaṃ ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattati, yaṃ dhovanaṃ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti, jarādhammā sattā jarāya parimuccanti, maraṇadhammā sattā maraṇena parimuccanti, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccantī”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, for one with right liberation, wrong liberation is washed away; and for him, the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong liberation are also washed away; and conditioned by right liberation, many wholesome states reach fulfillment through development. This, bhikkhus, is that noble washing which leads exclusively to disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, and to Nibbāna; a washing by means of which beings whose nature is to be born are freed from birth; beings whose nature is to age are freed from aging; beings whose nature is to die are freed from death; and beings whose nature is sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are freed from sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair.” The seventh.

8. Tikicchakasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Physician

108. “Tikicchakā[P 5.0218], bhikkhave, virecanaṃ denti pittasamuṭṭhānānampi ābādhānaṃ paṭighātāya, semhasamuṭṭhānānampi ābādhānaṃ paṭighātāya, vātasamuṭṭhānānampi ābādhānaṃ paṭighātāya. Atthetaṃ, bhikkhave, virecanaṃ; ‘netaṃ natthī’ti vadāmi. Tañca kho etaṃ, bhikkhave, virecanaṃ sampajjatipi vipajjatipi.

108. “Bhikkhus, physicians give a purgative to counteract illnesses arising from bile, to counteract illnesses arising from phlegm, and to counteract illnesses arising from wind. This purgative exists, bhikkhus; I do not say that it does not exist. But this purgative, bhikkhus, sometimes succeeds and sometimes fails.”

“Ahañca kho, bhikkhave, ariyaṃ virecanaṃ desessāmi, yaṃ virecanaṃ sampajjatiyeva no vipajjati, yaṃ virecanaṃ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti, jarādhammā sattā jarāya parimuccanti, maraṇadhammā sattā maraṇena parimuccanti, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā [V 3.0186] sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccanti. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

“But I, bhikkhus, will teach the noble purgative, which only succeeds and does not fail; a purgative by means of which beings whose nature is to be born are freed from birth, beings whose nature is to age are freed from aging, beings whose nature is to die are freed from death, and beings whose nature is sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair are freed from sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair. Listen to it, pay close attention; I will speak.” “Very well, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus responded to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Katamañca taṃ, bhikkhave, ariyaṃ virecanaṃ, yaṃ virecanaṃ sampajjatiyeva no vipajjati, yaṃ virecanaṃ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti, jarādhammā sattā jarāya parimuccanti, maraṇadhammā sattā maraṇena parimuccanti[T 5.0234], sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccanti?

And what, bhikkhus, is that noble purgative which always succeeds and does not fail, by relying on which beings subject to the nature of birth are freed from birth, beings subject to the nature of aging are freed from aging, beings subject to the nature of death are freed from death, and beings subject to the nature of sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair are freed from sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair?

“Sammādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, micchādiṭṭhi virittā hoti; ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa virittā honti; sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti.

Bhikkhus, for one with right view, wrong view is purged; and the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong view are also purged for them; and conditioned by right view, many wholesome states go to the fulfillment of development.

“Sammāsaṅkappassa[M 3.0434], bhikkhave, micchāsaṅkappo viritto hoti…pe… sammāvācassa, bhikkhave, micchāvācā virittā hoti… sammākammantassa, bhikkhave, micchākammanto viritto hoti… sammāājīvassa, bhikkhave, micchāājīvo viritto hoti… sammāvāyāmassa, bhikkhave, micchāvāyāmo viritto hoti… sammāsatissa, bhikkhave, micchāsati virittā hoti… sammāsamādhissa[P 5.0219], bhikkhave, micchāsamādhi viritto hoti… sammāñāṇissa, bhikkhave, micchāñāṇaṃ virittaṃ hoti…pe….

Bhikkhus, for one with right intention, wrong intention is purged… for one with right speech, wrong speech is purged… for one with right action, wrong action is purged… for one with right livelihood, wrong livelihood is purged… for one with right effort, wrong effort is purged… for one with right mindfulness, wrong mindfulness is purged… for one with right concentration, wrong concentration is purged… for one with right knowledge, wrong knowledge is purged….

“Sammāvimuttissa, bhikkhave, micchāvimutti virittā hoti; ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa virittā honti; sammāvimuttipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti. Idaṃ kho taṃ, bhikkhave, ariyaṃ virecanaṃ yaṃ virecanaṃ sampajjatiyeva no vipajjati, yaṃ virecanaṃ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti…pe… sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccantī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

Bhikkhus, for one with right liberation, wrong liberation is purged; and the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong liberation are also purged for them; and conditioned by right liberation, many wholesome states go to the fulfillment of development. This, bhikkhus, is that noble purgative which always succeeds and does not fail, by relying on which beings subject to the nature of birth are freed from birth… are freed from sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair.” Eighth.

9. Vamanasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Emetic

109. “Tikicchakā[V 3.0187], bhikkhave, vamanaṃ denti pittasamuṭṭhānānampi ābādhānaṃ [T 5.0235] paṭighātāya, semhasamuṭṭhānānampi ābādhānaṃ paṭighātāya, vātasamuṭṭhānānampi ābādhānaṃ paṭighātāya. Atthetaṃ, bhikkhave, vamanaṃ; ‘netaṃ natthī’ti vadāmi. Tañca kho etaṃ, bhikkhave, vamanaṃ sampajjatipi vipajjatipi.

109. Bhikkhus, physicians administer emetics to counteract illnesses arising from bile, phlegm, and wind. This emetic does exist, bhikkhus; I do not say it does not. But this emetic, bhikkhus, sometimes succeeds and sometimes fails.

“Ahañca kho, bhikkhave, ariyaṃ vamanaṃ desessāmi, yaṃ vamanaṃ sampajjatiyeva no vipajjati, yaṃ vamanaṃ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti, jarādhammā sattā jarāya parimuccanti, maraṇadhammā sattā maraṇena parimuccanti, sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccanti. Taṃ suṇātha…pe….

But I, bhikkhus, shall teach the noble emetic, which only succeeds and does not fail, by relying on which beings subject to birth are freed from birth, beings subject to aging are freed from aging, beings subject to death are freed from death, and beings subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair are freed from sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair. Listen to it….

“Katamañca taṃ, bhikkhave, ariyaṃ vamanaṃ, yaṃ vamanaṃ sampajjatiyeva no vipajjati, yaṃ vamanaṃ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti…pe… sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsadhammā [P 5.0220] sattā sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccanti?

And what, bhikkhus, is that noble emetic which only succeeds and does not fail, by relying on which beings subject to birth are freed from birth… beings subject to sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair are freed from sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair?

“Sammādiṭṭhikassa[M 3.0435], bhikkhave, micchādiṭṭhi vantā hoti; ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa vantā honti; sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti.

Bhikkhus, for one with right view, wrong view is vomited out; and the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong view are also vomited out for him; and conditioned by right view, many wholesome states go to the fulfillment of development.

“Sammāsaṅkappassa, bhikkhave, micchāsaṅkappo vanto hoti…pe… sammāvācassa, bhikkhave, micchāvācā vantā hoti… sammākammantassa, bhikkhave, micchākammanto vanto hoti… sammāājīvassa bhikkhave, micchāājīvo vanto hoti… sammāvāyāmassa, bhikkhave, micchāvāyāmo vanto hoti… sammāsatissa, bhikkhave, micchāsati vantā hoti… sammāsamādhissa, bhikkhave, micchāsamādhi vanto hoti… sammāñāṇissa, bhikkhave, micchāñāṇaṃ vantaṃ hoti [T 5.0236] …pe….

Bhikkhus, for one with right intention, wrong intention is vomited out… for one with right speech, wrong speech is vomited out… for one with right action, wrong action is vomited out… for one with right livelihood, wrong livelihood is vomited out… for one with right effort, wrong effort is vomited out… for one with right mindfulness, wrong mindfulness is vomited out… for one with right concentration, wrong concentration is vomited out… for one with right knowledge, wrong knowledge is vomited out….

“Sammāvimuttissa[V 3.0188], bhikkhave, micchāvimutti vantā hoti; ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa vantā honti; sammāvimuttipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti. Idaṃ kho taṃ, bhikkhave, ariyaṃ vamanaṃ yaṃ vamanaṃ sampajjatiyeva no vipajjati, yaṃ vamanaṃ āgamma jātidhammā sattā jātiyā parimuccanti…pe… sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsehi parimuccantī”ti. Navamaṃ.

Bhikkhus, for one with right liberation, wrong liberation is vomited out; and the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong liberation are also vomited out for him; and conditioned by right liberation, many wholesome states go to the fulfillment of development. This, bhikkhus, is that noble emetic which only succeeds and does not fail, by relying on which beings subject to birth are freed from birth… are freed from sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair.” Ninth.

10. Niddhamanīyasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Dispelling

110. “Dasayime, bhikkhave, niddhamanīyā dhammā. Katame dasa? Sammādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, micchādiṭṭhi niddhantā hoti; ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti te cassa niddhantā honti; sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti[P 5.0221].

110. Bhikkhus, there are these ten qualities to be dispelled. What ten? For one with right view, bhikkhus, wrong view is dispelled. And whatever many evil, unwholesome states arise on account of wrong view, they too are dispelled for him. And on account of right view, many wholesome states go to fulfillment by development.

“Sammāsaṅkappassa, bhikkhave, micchāsaṅkappo niddhanto hoti…pe… sammāvācassa bhikkhave, micchāvācā niddhantā hoti… sammākammantassa, bhikkhave, micchākammanto niddhanto hoti… sammāājīvassa, bhikkhave, micchāājīvo niddhanto hoti… sammāvāyāmassa, bhikkhave, micchāvāyāmo niddhanto hoti… sammāsatissa, bhikkhave, micchāsati niddhantā hoti… sammāsamādhissa, bhikkhave, micchāsamādhi niddhanto hoti… sammāñāṇissa, bhikkhave, micchāñāṇaṃ niddhantaṃ hoti….

“For one with right thought, bhikkhus, wrong thought is dispelled… For one with right speech, bhikkhus, wrong speech is dispelled… For one with right action, bhikkhus, wrong action is dispelled… For one with right livelihood, bhikkhus, wrong livelihood is dispelled… For one with right effort, bhikkhus, wrong effort is dispelled… For one with right mindfulness, bhikkhus, wrong mindfulness is dispelled… For one with right concentration, bhikkhus, wrong concentration is dispelled… For one with right knowledge, bhikkhus, wrong knowledge is dispelled….

“Sammāvimuttissa[M 3.0436], bhikkhave, micchāvimutti niddhantā hoti; ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā [T 5.0237] dhammā sambhavanti te cassa niddhantā honti; sammāvimuttipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti. Ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa niddhamanīyā dhammā”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“For one with right liberation, bhikkhus, wrong liberation is dispelled. And whatever many evil, unwholesome states arise on account of wrong liberation, they too are dispelled for him. And on account of right liberation, many wholesome states go to fulfillment by development. These, indeed, bhikkhus, are the ten qualities to be dispelled.” The tenth.

11. Paṭhamaasekhasuttaṃ

11. The First Discourse on the Adept

111. Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

111. Then a certain bhikkhu approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:

“‘Asekho [V 3.0189] asekho’ti, bhante, vuccati. Kittāvatā bhante, bhikkhu asekho hotī”ti? “Idha, bhikkhu, bhikkhu asekhāya sammādiṭṭhiyā samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāsaṅkappena samannāgato hoti, asekhāya sammāvācāya samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammākammantena samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāājīvena samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāvāyāmena samannāgato hoti, asekhāya sammāsatiyā samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāsamādhinā samannāgato hoti, asekhena sammāñāṇena samannāgato hoti, asekhāya sammāvimuttiyā samannāgato hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhu, bhikkhu asekho hotī”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

“‘Adept, adept,’ venerable sir, it is said. To what extent, venerable sir, is a bhikkhu an adept?” “Here, bhikkhu, a bhikkhu is endowed with the adept’s right view, is endowed with the adept’s right thought, is endowed with the adept’s right speech, is endowed with the adept’s right action, is endowed with the adept’s right livelihood, is endowed with the adept’s right effort, is endowed with the adept’s right mindfulness, is endowed with the adept’s right concentration, is endowed with the adept’s right knowledge, and is endowed with the adept’s right liberation. It is in this way, bhikkhu, that a bhikkhu is an adept.” The eleventh.

12. Dutiyaasekhasuttaṃ

12. The Second Discourse on the Adept

112. “Dasayime[P 5.0222], bhikkhave, asekhiyā dhammā. Katame dasa? Asekhā sammādiṭṭhi, asekho sammāsaṅkappo, asekhā sammāvācā, asekho sammākammanto, asekho sammāājīvo, asekho sammāvāyāmo, asekhā sammāsati, asekho sammāsamādhi, asekhaṃ sammāñāṇaṃ, asekhā sammāvimutti – ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa asekhiyā dhammā”ti. Dvādasamaṃ.

112. “Bhikkhus, there are these ten qualities of an adept. Which ten? The adept’s right view, the adept’s right thought, the adept’s right speech, the adept’s right action, the adept’s right livelihood, the adept’s right effort, the adept’s right mindfulness, the adept’s right concentration, the adept’s right knowledge, and the adept’s right liberation. These, bhikkhus, are the ten qualities of an adept.” The twelfth.

Samaṇasaññāvaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on the Perceptions of an Ascetic.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary verse:

Saññā [T 5.0238] bojjhaṅgā micchattaṃ, bījaṃ vijjāya nijjaraṃ;

Dhovanaṃ tikicchā vamanaṃ niddhamanaṃ dve asekhāti.

Perception, enlightenment factors, wrongness; seed, knowledge, wearing away; washing, treatment, vomiting, expulsion, and two on the adept.

(12) 2. Paccorohaṇivaggo

(12) 2. The Chapter on Descending

1. Paṭhamaadhammasuttaṃ

1. The First Discourse on the Non-Dhamma

113. a. ni. 10.171 “Adhammo [V 3.0190][M 3.0437] ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo anattho ca; dhammo ca veditabbo attho ca. Adhammañca viditvā anatthañca, dhammañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabbaṃ.

113. “Bhikkhus, the non-Dhamma should be understood, and what is not beneficial; the Dhamma should be understood, and what is beneficial. Having understood the non-Dhamma and what is not beneficial, and the Dhamma and what is beneficial, one should practice in accordance with the Dhamma and in accordance with what is beneficial.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, adhammo ca anattho ca? Micchādiṭṭhi, micchāsaṅkappo, micchāvācā, micchākammanto, micchāājīvo, micchāvāyāmo, micchāsati, micchāsamādhi, micchāñāṇaṃ, micchāvimutti – ayaṃ [P 5.0223] vuccati, bhikkhave, adhammo ca anattho ca.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the non-Dhamma and what is not beneficial? Wrong view, wrong thought, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong concentration, wrong knowledge, and wrong liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the non-Dhamma and what is not beneficial.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, dhammo ca attho ca? Sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi, sammāñāṇaṃ, sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammo ca attho ca.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma and what is beneficial? Right view, right thought, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration, right knowledge, and right liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma and what is beneficial.”

“‘Adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo anattho ca; dhammo ca veditabbo attho ca. Adhammañca viditvā anatthañca, dhammañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabba’nti, iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vutta”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“‘Bhikkhus, the non-Dhamma should be understood, and what is not beneficial; the Dhamma should be understood, and what is beneficial. Having understood the non-Dhamma and what is not beneficial, and the Dhamma and what is beneficial, one should practice in accordance with the Dhamma and in accordance with what is beneficial.’ Thus was it said, and it was said in reference to this.” The first.

2. Dutiyaadhammasuttaṃ

2. The Second Discourse on the Non-Dhamma

114. “Adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo dhammo ca; anattho ca veditabbo attho ca. Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā [T 5.0239] atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabbaṃ.

114. “Bhikkhus, the non-Dhamma should be understood and the Dhamma should be understood; what is not beneficial should be understood and what is beneficial should be understood. Having understood the non-Dhamma and the Dhamma, and having understood what is not beneficial and what is beneficial, one should practice in accordance with the Dhamma and in accordance with what is beneficial.”

“Katamo [V 3.0191] ca, bhikkhave, adhammo, katamo ca dhammo, katamo ca anattho, katamo ca attho?

“And what, bhikkhus, is the non-Dhamma, what is the Dhamma, what is not beneficial, and what is beneficial?”

“Micchādiṭṭhi, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammādiṭṭhi dhammo; ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Wrong view, bhikkhus, is the non-Dhamma; right view is the Dhamma. The many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong view: this is what is not beneficial. And conditioned by right view, many wholesome states go to the perfection of development: this is what is beneficial.”

“Micchāsaṅkappo[M 3.0438], bhikkhave, adhammo; sammāsaṅkappo dhammo; ye ca micchāsaṅkappapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; sammāsaṅkappapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Wrong thought, bhikkhus, is the non-Dhamma; right thought is the Dhamma. The many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong thought: this is what is not beneficial. And conditioned by right thought, many wholesome states go to the perfection of development: this is what is beneficial.”

“Micchāvācā, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammāvācā dhammo; ye ca micchāvācāpaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; sammāvācāpaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Wrong speech, bhikkhus, is the non-Dhamma; right speech is the Dhamma. The many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong speech: this is what is not beneficial. And conditioned by right speech, many wholesome states go to the perfection of development: this is what is beneficial.”

“Micchākammanto, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammākammanto dhammo; ye ca micchākammantapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ [P 5.0224] anattho; sammākammantapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Monks, wrong action is not the Dhamma; right action is the Dhamma. And because of wrong action, many evil, unwholesome states come into being—this is what is harmful. And because of right action, many wholesome states reach the culmination of development—this is what is beneficial.”

“Micchāājīvo, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammāājīvo dhammo; ye ca micchāājīvapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; sammāājīvapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Monks, wrong livelihood is not the Dhamma; right livelihood is the Dhamma. And because of wrong livelihood, many evil, unwholesome states come into being—this is what is harmful. And because of right livelihood, many wholesome states reach the culmination of development—this is what is beneficial.”

“Micchāvāyāmo, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammāvāyāmo dhammo; ye ca micchāvāyāmapaccayā [T 5.0240] aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; sammāvāyāmapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Monks, wrong effort is not the Dhamma; right effort is the Dhamma. And because of wrong effort, many evil, unwholesome states come into being—this is what is harmful. And because of right effort, many wholesome states reach the culmination of development—this is what is beneficial.”

“Micchāsati, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammāsati dhammo; ye ca micchāsatipaccayā aneke pāpakā [V 3.0192] akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; sammāsatipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Monks, wrong mindfulness is not the Dhamma; right mindfulness is the Dhamma. And because of wrong mindfulness, many evil, unwholesome states come into being—this is what is harmful. And because of right mindfulness, many wholesome states reach the culmination of development—this is what is beneficial.”

“Micchāsamādhi, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammāsamādhi dhammo; ye ca micchāsamādhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; sammāsamādhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Monks, wrong concentration is not the Dhamma; right concentration is the Dhamma. And because of wrong concentration, many evil, unwholesome states come into being—this is what is harmful. And because of right concentration, many wholesome states reach the culmination of development—this is what is beneficial.”

“Micchāñāṇaṃ, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammāñāṇaṃ dhammo; ye ca micchāñāṇapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; sammāñāṇapaccayā [M 3.0439] ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Monks, wrong knowledge is not the Dhamma; right knowledge is the Dhamma. And because of wrong knowledge, many evil, unwholesome states come into being—this is what is harmful. And because of right knowledge, many wholesome states reach the culmination of development—this is what is beneficial.”

“Micchāvimutti, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammāvimutti dhammo; ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; sammāvimuttipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Monks, wrong liberation is not the Dhamma; right liberation is the Dhamma. And because of wrong liberation, many evil, unwholesome states come into being—this is what is harmful. And because of right liberation, many wholesome states reach the culmination of development—this is what is beneficial.”

“‘Adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo dhammo ca; anattho ca veditabbo attho ca. Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabba’nti, iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vutta”nti. Dutiyaṃ.

“‘Monks, what is not the Dhamma should be understood, and the Dhamma should be understood; what is harmful should be understood, and what is beneficial should be understood. Having understood what is not the Dhamma and the Dhamma, and having understood what is harmful and what is beneficial, one should practice in accordance with the Dhamma and in accordance with what is beneficial.’ That which was spoken thus, was spoken in reference to this.” Second Sutta.

3. Tatiyaadhammasuttaṃ

3. The Third Discourse on What is Not the Dhamma

115. “Adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo dhammo ca; anattho ca [T 5.0241] veditabbo attho ca. Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā [P 5.0225] paṭipajjitabba”nti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisi.

115. “Monks, what is not the Dhamma should be understood, and the Dhamma should be understood; what is harmful should be understood, and what is beneficial should be understood. Having understood what is not the Dhamma and the Dhamma, and having understood what is harmful and what is beneficial, one should practice in accordance with the Dhamma and in accordance with what is beneficial.” The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Well-Farer rose from his seat and entered the monastery.

Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi – “idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo dhammo ca; anattho ca veditabbo attho ca[V 3.0193]. Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabba’nti. Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyā”ti?

Then, not long after the Blessed One had departed, this thought occurred to those monks: “Friends, the Blessed One, having set forth this summary in brief without analyzing the meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered the monastery, saying: ‘Monks, what is not the Dhamma should be understood, and the Dhamma should be understood; what is harmful should be understood, and what is beneficial should be understood. Having understood what is not the Dhamma and the Dhamma, and having understood what is harmful and what is beneficial, one should practice in accordance with the Dhamma and in accordance with what is beneficial.’ Now who could analyze in detail the meaning of this summary that was set forth in brief by the Blessed One, but whose meaning was not analyzed in detail?”

Atha kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāma puccheyyāma (sī. syā. pī.) ma. ni. 1.202 passitabbaṃ. Yathā no āyasmā ānando byākarissati tathā naṃ dhāressāmā”ti.

Then this thought occurred to those monks: “This Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. Venerable Ānanda is capable of analyzing in detail the meaning of this summary that was set forth in brief by the Blessed One, but whose meaning was not analyzed in detail. It would be good if we were to approach Venerable Ānanda; having approached, we could ask Venerable Ānanda about this matter. As Venerable Ānanda explains it to us, so shall we bear it in mind.”

Atha [M 3.0440] kho te bhikkhū yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā ānandena saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā [T 5.0242] kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavocuṃ –

Then those monks approached the Venerable Ānanda. Having approached, they exchanged greetings with the Venerable Ānanda. Having concluded their courteous and memorable conversation, they sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those monks said this to the Venerable Ānanda:

“Idaṃ kho no, āvuso ānanda, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘adhammo ca…pe… tathā paṭipajjitabba’nti.

“Friend Ānanda, the Blessed One, having set forth this summary in brief without analyzing the meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered the monastery, saying: ‘What is not the Dhamma… and so on… one should practice accordingly.’”

“Tesaṃ no, āvuso, amhākaṃ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi – ‘idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavatā saṃkhittena [P 5.0226] uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – adhammo ca…pe… tathā paṭipajjitabbanti. Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyā’ti?

“Friend, for us, not long after the Blessed One had departed, this thought occurred: ‘Friends, the Blessed One, having set forth this summary in brief without analyzing the meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered the monastery, saying: “What is not the Dhamma… and so on… one should practice accordingly.” Now who could analyze in detail the meaning of this summary that was set forth in brief by the Blessed One, but whose meaning was not analyzed in detail?’”

“Tesaṃ no, āvuso, amhākaṃ etadahosi – ‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāma. Yathā no āyasmā ānando byākarissati tathā naṃ [T 5.0243] dhāressāmā’ti. Vibhajatu āyasmā ānando”ti.

“For us, friend, this thought occurred: ‘This Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. The Venerable Ānanda is capable of analyzing in detail the meaning of this summary that was pointed out in brief by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail. It would be good if we were to approach the Venerable Ānanda; having approached, we could ask the Venerable Ānanda about this matter. As the Venerable Ānanda explains it to us, so we will bear it in mind.’ May the Venerable Ānanda please analyze it.”

“Seyyathāpi[V 3.0194], āvuso, puriso sāratthiko sāragavesī sārapariyesanaṃ caramāno mahato rukkhassa tiṭṭhato sāravato atikkammeva mūlaṃ atikkamma khandhaṃ sākhāpalāse sāraṃ pariyesitabbaṃ maññeyya; evaṃsampadamidaṃ āyasmantānaṃ satthari sammukhībhūte taṃ bhagavantaṃ atisitvā amhe etamatthaṃ paṭipucchitabbaṃ maññatha. So hāvuso, bhagavā jānaṃ jānāti passaṃ passati, cakkhubhūto ñāṇabhūto dhammabhūto brahmabhūto vattā pavattā atthassa ninnetā amatassa dātā dhammassāmī tathāgato. So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi yaṃ tumhe bhagavantaṃyeva [M 3.0441] upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ [P 5.0227] paṭipuccheyyātha. Yathā vo bhagavā byākareyya tathā naṃ dhāreyyāthā”ti.

“Friends, it is as if a man in need of heartwood, seeking heartwood, wandering in search of heartwood, were to pass over the root and the trunk of a great, standing, pithy tree, and think that heartwood should be sought among the branches and leaves. Such is the case with you venerable ones who, with the Teacher present before you, have passed over that Blessed One and think that we should be questioned about this matter. For, friends, that Blessed One knows what should be known, sees what should be seen; he has become the eye, become the knowledge, become the Dhamma, become the Brahma; he is the speaker, the proclaimer, the one who leads to the meaning, the giver of the Deathless, the lord of the Dhamma, the Tathāgata. That was the very time for you to approach the Blessed One himself and question him about this matter. As the Blessed One would have explained it to you, so you should have borne it in mind.”

“Addhāvuso ānanda, bhagavā jānaṃ jānāti passaṃ passati cakkhubhūto ñāṇabhūto dhammabhūto brahmabhūto vattā pavattā atthassa ninnetā amatassa dātā dhammassāmī tathāgato. So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi yaṃ mayaṃ bhagavantaṃyeva upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāma, yathā no bhagavā byākareyya tathā naṃ dhāreyyāma. Api cāyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Vibhajatāyasmā ānando agaruṃ katvā”ti.

“Certainly, friend Ānanda, the Blessed One knows what should be known, sees what should be seen; he has become the eye, become the knowledge, become the Dhamma, become the Brahma; he is the speaker, the proclaimer, the one who leads to the meaning, the giver of the Deathless, the lord of the Dhamma, the Tathāgata. That was indeed the very time for us to approach the Blessed One himself and question him about this matter; as the Blessed One would have explained it to us, so we would have borne it in mind. However, the Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. The Venerable Ānanda is capable of analyzing in detail the meaning of this summary that was pointed out in brief by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail. May the Venerable Ānanda analyze it, without finding it burdensome.”

“Tenahāvuso, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa [T 5.0244] paccassosuṃ. Athāyasmā ānando etadavoca –

“In that case, friends, listen and pay close attention; I will speak.” “Yes, friend,” those monks replied to the Venerable Ānanda. Then the Venerable Ānanda said this:

“Yaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo dhammo ca; anattho ca veditabbo attho ca. Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabba’nti.

“Friends, the Blessed One, having stated a summary in brief without analyzing the meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered his dwelling, saying: ‘Monks, what is not-Dhamma should be understood, and what is Dhamma should be understood; what is not-benefit should be understood, and what is benefit should be understood. Having understood what is not-Dhamma and what is Dhamma, and having understood what is not-benefit and what is benefit, one should practice in accordance with the Dhamma and in accordance with the benefit.’”

Katamo cāvuso, adhammo, katamo ca dhammo, katamo ca anattho, katamo ca attho?

“And what, friends, is not-Dhamma, and what is Dhamma? What is not-benefit, and what is benefit?”

“Micchādiṭṭhi, āvuso, adhammo; sammādiṭṭhi dhammo; ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā [V 3.0195] akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Friends, wrong view is not-Dhamma; right view is Dhamma. And the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong view—this is not-benefit. And the many wholesome states that reach fulfillment by development conditioned by right view—this is benefit.”

“Micchāsaṅkappo, āvuso, adhammo; sammāsaṅkappo dhammo… micchāvācā, āvuso, adhammo; sammāvācā dhammo [P 5.0228] … micchākammanto, āvuso, adhammo; sammākammanto dhammo… micchāājīvo, āvuso, adhammo; sammāājīvo [M 3.0442] dhammo… micchāvāyāmo, āvuso, adhammo; sammāvāyāmo dhammo… micchāsati, āvuso, adhammo; sammāsati dhammo… micchāsamādhi, āvuso, adhammo; sammāsamādhi dhammo… micchāñāṇaṃ, āvuso, adhammo; sammāñāṇaṃ dhammo….

“Friends, wrong intention is not-Dhamma; right intention is Dhamma… Friends, wrong speech is not-Dhamma; right speech is Dhamma… Friends, wrong action is not-Dhamma; right action is Dhamma… Friends, wrong livelihood is not-Dhamma; right livelihood is Dhamma… Friends, wrong effort is not-Dhamma; right effort is Dhamma… Friends, wrong mindfulness is not-Dhamma; right mindfulness is Dhamma… Friends, wrong concentration is not-Dhamma; right concentration is Dhamma… Friends, wrong knowledge is not-Dhamma; right knowledge is Dhamma….

Micchāvimutti, āvuso, adhammo; sammāvimutti dhammo; ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; sammāvimuttipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Friends, wrong liberation is not-Dhamma; right liberation is Dhamma. And the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong liberation—this is not-benefit. And the many wholesome states that reach fulfillment by development conditioned by right liberation—this is benefit.”

“Ayaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena [T 5.0245] atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo dhammo ca…pe… tathā paṭipajjitabba’nti, imassa kho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi. Ākaṅkhamānā ca pana tumhe, āvuso, bhagavantaṃyeva upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyātha. Yathā vo bhagavā byākaroti byākareyya (syā.) tathā naṃ dhāreyyāthā”ti.

“This, friends, is the summary that the Blessed One stated in brief without analyzing the meaning in detail before rising from his seat and entering his dwelling: ‘Monks, what is not-Dhamma should be understood, and what is Dhamma should be understood…pe… and one should practice accordingly.’ Friends, this is how I understand in detail the meaning of this summary stated in brief by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail. However, friends, if you wish, you may approach the Blessed One himself and ask him about this matter. As the Blessed One explains it to you, so you should bear it in mind.”

“Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato ānandassa bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ –

“Yes, friend,” those monks said, and having rejoiced and approved of the Venerable Ānanda’s words, they rose from their seats and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, they paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those monks said this to the Blessed One:

“Yaṃ kho no bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo…pe… tathā paṭijjitabba’nti.

“The Blessed One stated a summary for us in brief without analyzing the meaning in detail, and having risen from his seat, entered his dwelling, saying: ‘Monks, what is not-Dhamma should be understood…pe… and one should practice accordingly.’”

“Tesaṃ [V 3.0196] no, bhante, amhākaṃ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi – ‘idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena [P 5.0229] atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo…pe… [T 5.0246] tathā paṭipajjitabbanti. Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyā’ti?

“Venerable Sir, soon after the Blessed One had departed, this thought occurred to us: ‘Friends, the Blessed One stated this summary for us in brief without analyzing the meaning in detail, and having risen from his seat, entered his dwelling, saying: “Monks, what is not-Dhamma should be understood… and one should practice accordingly.” Who, now, could analyze in detail the meaning of this summary stated in brief by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail?’”

“Tesaṃ [M 3.0443] no, bhante, amhākaṃ etadahosi – ‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā ānando satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā ānando imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāma. Yathā no āyasmā ānando byākarissati tathā naṃ dhāressāmā’ti.

“Venerable Sir, this thought occurred to us: ‘The Venerable Ānanda is praised by the Teacher and held in high esteem by his wise companions in the holy life. The Venerable Ānanda is capable of analyzing in detail the meaning of this summary stated in brief by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail. It would be good if we were to approach the Venerable Ānanda and ask him about this matter. As the Venerable Ānanda explains it to us, so we will bear it in mind.’”

“Atha kho mayaṃ, bhante, yenāyasmā ānando tenupasaṅkamimhā; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etamatthaṃ apucchimhā. Tesaṃ no, bhante, āyasmatā ānandena imehi ākārehi imehi padehi imehi byañjanehi attho suvibhatto”ti vibhattoti (?) evameva hi aññesu īdisasuttesu dissati.

“So, Venerable Sir, we approached the Venerable Ānanda; having approached, we asked the Venerable Ānanda about this matter. And, Venerable Sir, the meaning was well analyzed for us by the Venerable Ānanda with these methods, these phrases, and these expressions.”

“Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhave! Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, ānando. Mahāpañño, bhikkhave, ānando. Maṃ cepi tumhe, bhikkhave, upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyātha, ahampi cetaṃ evamevaṃ ahampi taṃ evamevaṃ (ma. ni. 1.205) byākareyyaṃ yathā taṃ ānandena byākataṃ. Eso ceva tassa eso cevetassa (ma. ni. 1.205) attho evañca naṃ dhāreyyāthā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Good, good, monks! Ānanda is wise, monks. Ānanda is of great wisdom, monks. If you, monks, were to approach me and ask about this matter, I too would explain it in exactly the same way as Ānanda has explained it. This is indeed its meaning, and you should bear it in mind thus.” The Third Sutta.

4. Ajitasuttaṃ

4. The Ajita Sutta

116. Atha kho ajito paribbājako yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā [T 5.0247] ekamantaṃ nisīdi[P 5.0230]. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho ajito paribbājako bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

116. Then the wanderer Ajita approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged joyful greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded a conversation that was joyful and memorable, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the wanderer Ajita said this to the Blessed One:

“Amhākaṃ[V 3.0197], bho gotama, paṇḍito nāma sabrahmacārī. Tena pañcamattāni cittaṭṭhānasatāni cintitāni, yehi aññatitthiyā upāraddhāva jānanti upāraddhā pajānanti (sī.) upāraddhasmā”ti upāraddhamhāti (sī. pī.).

“Venerable Gotama, we have a fellow practitioner named Paṇḍita. He has thought of five hundred states of mind by which sectarians of other beliefs know that they have been assailed.”

Atha [M 3.0444] kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi – “dhāretha no tumhe, bhikkhave, paṇḍitavatthūnī”ti? “Etassa, bhagavā, kālo etassa, sugata, kālo yaṃ bhagavā bhāseyya, bhagavato sutvā bhikkhū dhāressantī”ti.

Then the Blessed One addressed the monks: “Monks, bear in mind the grounds for being a wise person.” “Now is the time, Blessed One! Now is the time, Sugata, for the Blessed One to speak. Having heard it from the Blessed One, the monks will bear it in mind.”

“Tena hi, bhikkhave, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

“In that case, monks, listen and apply your mind well; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those monks assented to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco adhammikena vādena adhammikaṃ vādaṃ abhiniggaṇhāti abhinippīḷeti, tena ca adhammikaṃ parisaṃ rañjeti. Tena sā adhammikā parisā uccāsaddamahāsaddā hoti – ‘paṇḍito vata, bho, paṇḍito vata, bho’ti.

“Here, monks, a certain person with an unrighteous argument refutes and crushes an unrighteous argument, and thereby pleases an unrighteous assembly. By this, that unrighteous assembly becomes loud and uproarious, saying: ‘Indeed, sirs, what a wise person! Indeed, sirs, what a wise person!’”

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco adhammikena vādena dhammikaṃ vādaṃ abhiniggaṇhāti abhinippīḷeti, tena ca adhammikaṃ parisaṃ rañjeti. Tena sā adhammikā parisā uccāsaddamahāsaddā hoti – ‘paṇḍito vata, bho, paṇḍito vata, bho’ti.

“Furthermore, monks, here a certain person with an unrighteous argument refutes and crushes a righteous argument, and thereby pleases an unrighteous assembly. By this, that unrighteous assembly becomes loud and uproarious, saying: ‘Indeed, sirs, what a wise person! Indeed, sirs, what a wise person!’”

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco adhammikena vādena dhammikañca vādaṃ adhammikañca vādaṃ abhiniggaṇhāti abhinippīḷeti, tena ca adhammikaṃ parisaṃ rañjeti. Tena sā adhammikā parisā uccāsaddamahāsaddā hoti – ‘paṇḍito vata, bho, paṇḍito vata, bho’ti.

“Furthermore, monks, here a certain person with an unrighteous argument refutes and crushes both a righteous argument and an unrighteous argument, and thereby pleases an unrighteous assembly. By this, that unrighteous assembly becomes loud and uproarious, saying: ‘Indeed, sirs, what a wise person! Indeed, sirs, what a wise person!’”

“Adhammo [T 5.0248][P 5.0231] ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo dhammo ca; anattho ca veditabbo attho ca. Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabbaṃ.

“Monks, the unrighteous should be known and the righteous should be known; the unbeneficial should be known and the beneficial should be known. Having known the unrighteous and the righteous, and having known the unbeneficial and the beneficial, one should practice in accordance with what is righteous and in accordance with what is beneficial.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, adhammo, katamo ca dhammo, katamo ca anattho, katamo ca attho? Micchādiṭṭhi, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammādiṭṭhi dhammo; ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā [V 3.0198] akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“And what, monks, is the unrighteous, and what is the righteous? What is the unbeneficial, and what is the beneficial? Wrong view, monks, is unrighteous; right view is righteous. And the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong view—this is the unbeneficial. And the many wholesome states that, conditioned by right view, go to the fulfillment of development—this is the beneficial.”

“Micchāsaṅkappo, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammāsaṅkappo dhammo… micchāvācā, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammāvācā dhammo… micchākammanto, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammākammanto dhammo… micchāājīvo, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammāājīvo dhammo [M 3.0445]… micchāvāyāmo, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammāvāyāmo dhammo… micchāsati, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammāsati dhammo… micchāsamādhi, bhikkhave adhammo; sammāsamādhi dhammo… micchāñāṇaṃ, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammāñāṇaṃ dhammo[T 5.0249].

“Wrong intention, monks, is unrighteous; right intention is righteous… Wrong speech, monks, is unrighteous; right speech is righteous… Wrong action, monks, is unrighteous; right action is righteous… Wrong livelihood, monks, is unrighteous; right livelihood is righteous… Wrong effort, monks, is unrighteous; right effort is righteous… Wrong mindfulness, monks, is unrighteous; right mindfulness is righteous… Wrong concentration, monks, is unrighteous; right concentration is righteous… Wrong knowledge, monks, is unrighteous; right knowledge is righteous.”

“Micchāvimutti, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammāvimutti dhammo; ye ca micchāvimuttipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; sammāvimuttipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Wrong liberation, monks, is unrighteous; right liberation is righteous. And the many evil, unwholesome states that arise conditioned by wrong liberation—this is the unbeneficial. And the many wholesome states that, conditioned by right liberation, go to the fulfillment of development—this is the beneficial.”

“‘Adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo dhammo ca; anattho ca veditabbo attho ca. Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca[P 5.0232], anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabba’nti, iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vutta”nti. Catutthaṃ.

“‘Monks, the unrighteous should be known and the righteous should be known; the unbeneficial should be known and the beneficial should be known. Having known the unrighteous and the righteous, and having known the unbeneficial and the beneficial, one should practice in accordance with what is righteous and in accordance with what is beneficial.’ When this was said, it was said in reference to this.” Fourth.

5. Saṅgāravasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse with Saṅgārava

117. a. ni. 10.169 Atha kho saṅgāravo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho saṅgāravo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, orimaṃ tīraṃ, kiṃ pārimaṃ tīra”nti? “Micchādiṭṭhi kho, brāhmaṇa, orimaṃ tīraṃ, sammādiṭṭhi pārimaṃ tīraṃ; micchāsaṅkappo orimaṃ tīraṃ, sammāsaṅkappo pārimaṃ tīraṃ; micchāvācā orimaṃ tīraṃ, sammāvācā pārimaṃ tīraṃ; micchākammanto orimaṃ tīraṃ, sammākammanto pārimaṃ tīraṃ; micchāājīvo orimaṃ tīraṃ, sammāājīvo pārimaṃ tīraṃ; micchāvāyāmo orimaṃ tīraṃ, sammāvāyāmo pārimaṃ tīraṃ; micchāsati orimaṃ tīraṃ, sammāsati pārimaṃ tīraṃ; micchāsamādhi orimaṃ [V 3.0199] tīraṃ, sammāsamādhi pārimaṃ tīraṃ; micchāñāṇaṃ orimaṃ tīraṃ, sammāñāṇaṃ pārimaṃ tīraṃ; micchāvimutti orimaṃ tīraṃ, sammāvimutti pārimaṃ tīranti. Idaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, orimaṃ tīraṃ, idaṃ [T 5.0250] pārimaṃ tīranti.

117. Then the brahmin Saṅgārava approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged greetings with the Blessed One. Having concluded the courteous and memorable talk, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, the brahmin Saṅgārava said to the Blessed One: “What, Master Gotama, is the near shore, and what is the far shore?” “Wrong view, brahmin, is the near shore, and right view is the far shore; wrong intention is the near shore, and right intention is the far shore; wrong speech is the near shore, and right speech is the far shore; wrong action is the near shore, and right action is the far shore; wrong livelihood is the near shore, and right livelihood is the far shore; wrong effort is the near shore, and right effort is the far shore; wrong mindfulness is the near shore, and right mindfulness is the far shore; wrong concentration is the near shore, and right concentration is the far shore; wrong knowledge is the near shore, and right knowledge is the far shore; wrong liberation is the near shore, and right liberation is the far shore. This, brahmin, is the near shore, and this is the far shore.”

“Appakā te manussesu, ye janā pāragāmino;

Athāyaṃ itarā pajā, tīramevānudhāvati.

“Few are those among humans who go to the far shore; but this other populace runs along this very shore.”

“Ye ca kho sammadakkhāte, dhamme dhammānuvattino;

Te janā pāramessanti, maccudheyyaṃ suduttaraṃ.

“But those who practice in accordance with the Dhamma, so well-expounded—those people will go to the far shore, having crossed the realm of Death, so very hard to traverse.”

“Kaṇhaṃ [M 3.0446] dhammaṃ vippahāya, sukkaṃ bhāvetha paṇḍito;

Okā anokamāgamma, viveke yattha dūramaṃ.

“A wise person should abandon dark states and cultivate bright ones. Having gone from home to homelessness, into that seclusion where it is hard to find delight.”

“Tatrābhiratimiccheyya, hitvā kāme akiñcano;

Pariyodapeyya attānaṃ, cittaklesehi paṇḍito.

“There one should desire delight, having abandoned sensual pleasures, owning nothing. A wise person should purify oneself from the defilements of the mind.”

“Yesaṃ [P 5.0233] sambodhiyaṅgesu, sammā cittaṃ subhāvitaṃ;

Ādānapaṭinissagge, anupādāya ye ratā;

Khīṇāsavā jutimanto jutīmanto (sī.), te loke parinibbutā”ti. pañcamaṃ;

“Those whose minds are well-developed in the factors of enlightenment, who, without grasping, delight in the relinquishing of clinging; with taints destroyed, radiant, they are fully extinguished in the world.” Fifth.

6. Orimatīrasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Near Shore

118. “Orimañca, bhikkhave, tīraṃ desessāmi pārimañca tīraṃ. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

118. “Monks, I will teach the near shore and the far shore. Listen to it and pay close attention; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, orimaṃ tīraṃ, katamañca pārimaṃ tīraṃ? Micchādiṭṭhi orimaṃ tīraṃ[V 3.0200], sammādiṭṭhi pārimaṃ tīraṃ…pe… micchāvimutti orimaṃ tīraṃ, sammāvimutti pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, orimaṃ tīraṃ, idaṃ pārimaṃ tīranti.

“And what, monks, is the near shore, and what is the far shore? Wrong view is the near shore, and right view is the far shore… wrong liberation is the near shore, and right liberation is the far shore. This, monks, is the near shore, and this is the far shore.”

“Appakā te manussesu, ye janā pāragāmino;

Athāyaṃ itarā pajā, tīramevānudhāvati.

“Few are those among humans who go to the far shore; but this other populace runs along this very shore.”

“Ye [T 5.0251] ca kho sammadakkhāte, dhamme dhammānuvattino;

Te janā pāramessanti, maccudheyyaṃ suduttaraṃ.

“But those who practice in accordance with the Dhamma, so well-expounded—those people will go to the far shore, having crossed the realm of Death, so very hard to traverse.”

“Kaṇhaṃ dhammaṃ vippahāya, sukkaṃ bhāvetha paṇḍito;

Okā anoka māgamma, viveke yattha dūramaṃ.

“A wise person should abandon dark states and cultivate bright ones. Having gone from home to homelessness, into that seclusion where it is hard to find delight.”

“Tatrābhiratimiccheyya, hitvā kāme akiñcano;

Pariyodapeyya attānaṃ, cittaklesehi paṇḍito.

“There one should desire delight, having abandoned sensual pleasures, owning nothing. A wise person should purify oneself from the defilements of the mind.”

“Yesaṃ sambodhiyaṅgesu, sammā cittaṃ subhāvitaṃ;

Ādānapaṭinissagge, anupādāya ye ratā;

Khīṇāsavā jutimanto, te loke parinibbutā”ti. chaṭṭhaṃ;

“Those whose minds are well-developed in the factors of enlightenment, who, without grasping, delight in the relinquishing of clinging; with taints destroyed, radiant, they are fully extinguished in the world.” Sixth.

7. Paṭhamapaccorohaṇīsuttaṃ

7. The First Discourse on the ‘Descending’

119. Tena [M 3.0447] kho pana samayena jāṇussoṇi jānussoni (ka. sī.), jānussoṇi (ka. sī.), jāṇusoṇi (ka.) brāhmaṇo tadahuposathe sīsaṃnhāto sīsaṃnahāto (sī. pī.), sīsanhāto (syā.) navaṃ khomayugaṃ nivattho allakusamuṭṭhiṃ [P 5.0234] ādāya bhagavato avidūre ekamantaṃ ṭhito hoti.

119. At that time, the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi, having bathed his head on that Uposatha day, clad in a new pair of linen garments, and taking a handful of fresh kusa grass, was standing to one side, not far from the Blessed One.

Addasā kho bhagavā jāṇussoṇiṃ brāhmaṇaṃ tadahuposathe sīsaṃnhātaṃ navaṃ khomayugaṃ nivatthaṃ allakusamuṭṭhiṃ ādāya ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ. Disvāna jāṇussoṇiṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, tadahuposathe sīsaṃnhāto navaṃ khomayugaṃ nivattho allakusamuṭṭhiṃ ādāya ekamantaṃ ṭhito[V 3.0201]? Kiṃ nvajja kiṃ nu ajja (syā.), kiṃ nu kho ajja (pī.), kiṃ nu khvajja (ka.) brāhmaṇakulassā”ti brāhmaṇa brahmakusalassāti (ka.)? “Paccorohaṇī, bho gotama, ajja brāhmaṇakulassā”ti brahmakusalassāti (ka.).

The Blessed One saw the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi, who on that Uposatha day had bathed his head, was clad in a new pair of linen garments, and, taking a handful of fresh kusa grass, was standing to one side. Having seen him, the Blessed One said this to the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi: 'Brahmin, why is it that on this Uposatha day, having bathed your head, clad in a new pair of linen garments, and taking a handful of fresh kusa grass, you are standing to one side? Brahmin, what is the business of the brahmin clan today?' 'Master Gotama, today is the ‘descending’ for the brahmin clan.'

“Yathā kathaṃ pana, brāhmaṇa, brāhmaṇānaṃ paccorohaṇī hotī”ti? “Idha, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā tadahuposathe sīsaṃnhātā navaṃ khomayugaṃ nivatthā allena gomayena pathaviṃ opuñjitvā haritehi kusehi pattharitvā pavitthāretvā (ka.) antarā ca velaṃ [T 5.0252] antarā ca agyāgāraṃ seyyaṃ kappenti. Te taṃ rattiṃ tikkhattuṃ paccuṭṭhāya pañjalikā aggiṃ namassanti – ‘paccorohāma bhavantaṃ, paccorohāma bhavanta’nti. Bahukena ca sappitelanavanītena aggiṃ santappenti. Tassā ca rattiyā accayena paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena brāhmaṇe santappenti. Evaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇānaṃ paccorohaṇī hotī”ti.

'Brahmin, in what way is the brahmins’ ‘descending’?' 'Here, Master Gotama, on the Uposatha day, brahmins, having bathed their heads and put on a new pair of linen garments, smear the ground with wet cow dung, spread it with green kusa grass, and make their bed between the sand heap and the fire-hut. That night, they rise three times and, with hands joined in reverence, pay homage to the fire, saying: “We descend to you, venerable one; we descend to you, venerable one.” They satisfy the fire with abundant ghee, oil, and fresh butter. Then, at the end of that night, they satisfy the brahmins with fine hard and soft food. In this way, Master Gotama, is the brahmins’ ‘descending’.'

“Aññathā kho, brāhmaṇa, brāhmaṇānaṃ paccorohaṇī hoti, aññathā ca pana ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hotī”ti. “Yathā kathaṃ pana, bho gotama, ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hoti? Sādhu me bhavaṃ gotamo tathā dhammaṃ desetu yathā ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hotī”ti.

'Brahmin, the ‘descending’ of the brahmins is one way, and the ‘descending’ in the discipline of the Noble One is another.' 'Master Gotama, in what way is the ‘descending’ in the discipline of the Noble One? May the venerable Gotama be pleased to teach me the Dhamma about how the ‘descending’ is in the discipline of the Noble One.'

“Tena [M 3.0448] hi, brāhmaṇa, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –

“In that case, brahmin, listen and pay close attention; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi responded to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Idha[P 5.0235], brāhmaṇa, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘micchādiṭṭhiyā kho pāpako vipāko diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcā’ ti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya micchādiṭṭhiṃ pajahati; micchādiṭṭhiyā paccorohati.

“Here, brahmin, a noble disciple reflects thus: ‘Wrong view indeed has an evil result both in the present life and in the future.’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons wrong view; he descends from wrong view.

… Micchāsaṅkappassa kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya micchāsaṅkappaṃ pajahati; micchāsaṅkappā paccorohati.

‘Wrong intention indeed has an evil result both in the present life and in the future.’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons wrong intention; he descends from wrong intention.

… Micchāvācāya kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya micchāvācaṃ pajahati; micchāvācāya paccorohati.

‘Wrong speech indeed has an evil result both in the present life and in the future.’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons wrong speech; he descends from wrong speech.

…Micchākammantassa [V 3.0202] kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya micchākammantaṃ pajahati; micchākammantā [T 5.0253] paccorohati.

‘Wrong action indeed has an evil result both in the present life and in the future.’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons wrong action; he descends from wrong action.

…Micchāājīvassa kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya micchāājīvaṃ pajahati; micchāājīvā paccorohati.

‘Wrong livelihood indeed has an evil result both in the present life and in the future.’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons wrong livelihood; he descends from wrong livelihood.

…Micchāvāyāmassa kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya micchāvāyāmaṃ pajahati; micchāvāyāmā paccorohati.

‘Wrong effort indeed has an evil result both in the present life and in the future.’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons wrong effort; he descends from wrong effort.

…Micchāsatiyā kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya micchāsatiṃ pajahati; micchāsatiyā paccorohati.

‘Wrong mindfulness indeed has an evil result both in the present life and in the future.’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons wrong mindfulness; he descends from wrong mindfulness.

…Micchāsamādhissa kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya micchāsamādhiṃ pajahati; micchāsamādhimhā paccorohati.

‘Wrong concentration indeed has an evil result both in the present life and in the future.’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons wrong concentration; he descends from wrong concentration.

…Micchāñāṇassa [M 3.0449] kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya micchāñāṇaṃ pajahati; micchāñāṇamhā paccorohati.

‘Wrong knowledge indeed has an evil result both in the present life and in the future.’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons wrong knowledge; he descends from wrong knowledge.

‘Micchāvimuttiyā kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcā’ti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya micchāvimuttiṃ pajahati; micchāvimuttiyā paccorohati. Evaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hotī”ti.

‘Wrong liberation indeed has an evil result both in the present life and in the future.’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons wrong liberation; he descends from wrong liberation. In this way, brahmin, is the descending in the discipline of the Noble One.”

“Aññathā, bho gotama, brāhmaṇānaṃ paccorohaṇī, aññathā ca pana ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hoti. Imissā ca, bho gotama, ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇiyā brāhmaṇānaṃ paccorohaṇī kalaṃ nāgghati soḷasiṃ. Abhikkantaṃ[P 5.0236], bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Sattamaṃ.

“Venerable Gotama, the brahmins’ descending is one way, and the descending in the discipline of the Noble One is another. The brahmins’ descending is not worth a sixteenth part of this descending in the discipline of the Noble One. Excellent, Venerable Gotama! … May the Venerable Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life from this day forward.” Seventh.

8. Dutiyapaccorohaṇīsuttaṃ

8. The Second Discourse on Descending

120. “Ariyaṃ [V 3.0203] vo, bhikkhave, paccorohaṇiṃ desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha… katamā ca, bhikkhave, ariyā paccorohaṇī? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti [T 5.0254] paṭisañcikkhati – ‘micchādiṭṭhiyā kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcā’ti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya micchādiṭṭhiṃ pajahati; micchādiṭṭhiyā paccorohati. Micchāsaṅkappassa kho pāpako vipāko… micchāvācāya kho… micchākammantassa kho… micchāājīvassa kho… micchāvāyāmassa kho… micchāsatiyā kho… micchāsamādhissa kho… micchāñāṇassa kho… micchāvimuttiyā kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya micchāvimuttiṃ pajahati; micchāvimuttiyā paccorohati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyā paccorohaṇī”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

120. “Monks, I will teach you the noble descending. Listen to it… And what, monks, is the noble descending? Here, monks, a noble disciple reflects thus: ‘Wrong view has an evil result, both in this present life and in the life to come.’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons wrong view; he descends from wrong view. ‘Wrong intention has an evil result… wrong speech… wrong action… wrong livelihood… wrong effort… wrong mindfulness… wrong concentration… wrong knowledge… wrong liberation has an evil result, both in this present life and in the life to come.’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons wrong liberation; he descends from wrong liberation. This, monks, is called the noble descending.” Eighth.

9. Pubbaṅgamasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Forerunner

121. “Sūriyassa, bhikkhave, udayato etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ – aruṇuggaṃ. Evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ etaṃ pubbaṅgamaṃ etaṃ pubbanimittaṃ, yadidaṃ – sammādiṭṭhi. Sammādiṭṭhikassa, bhikkhave, sammāsaṅkappo pahoti, sammāsaṅkappassa sammāvācā pahoti, sammākammanto [M 3.0450] pahoti, sammākammantassa sammāājīvo pahoti, sammāājīvassa sammāvāyāmo pahoti, sammāvāyāmassa sammāsati pahoti, sammāsatissa sammāsamādhi pahoti[P 5.0237], sammāsamādhissa sammāñāṇaṃ pahoti, sammāñāṇissa sammāvimutti pahotī”ti. Navamaṃ.

121. “Monks, the forerunner and precursor of the sunrise is the dawn. In the same way, monks, the forerunner and precursor of wholesome states is right view. For one with right view, monks, right intention arises. For one with right intention, right speech arises. For one with right speech, right action arises. For one with right action, right livelihood arises. For one with right livelihood, right effort arises. For one with right effort, right mindfulness arises. For one with right mindfulness, right concentration arises. For one with right concentration, right knowledge arises. For one with right knowledge, right liberation arises.” Ninth.

10. Āsavakkhayasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on the Destruction of the Taints

122. “Dasayime, bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā āsavānaṃ khayāya saṃvattanti. Katame dasa? Sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi, sammāñāṇaṃ[T 5.0255], sammāvimutti – ime kho[V 3.0204], bhikkhave, dasa dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā āsavānaṃ khayāya saṃvattantī”ti. Dasamaṃ.

122. “Monks, these ten states, when developed and cultivated, lead to the destruction of the taints. What are the ten? Right view, right intention, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration, right knowledge, and right liberation. These, monks, are the ten states that, when developed and cultivated, lead to the destruction of the taints.” Tenth.

Paccorohaṇivaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter on Descending.

Tassuddānaṃ –

The summary:

Tayo adhammā ajito, saṅgāravo ca orimaṃ;

Dve ceva paccorohaṇī, pubbaṅgamaṃ āsavakkhayoti.

The three on unrighteousness, Ajita, Saṅgārava, and This Shore; the two on descending, The Forerunner, and The Destruction of the Taints.

(13) 3. Parisuddhavaggo

(13) 3. The Chapter on Purity

1. Paṭhamasuttaṃ

1. The First Discourse

123. “Dasayime[V 3.0205], bhikkhave, dhammā parisuddhā pariyodātā, nāññatra sugatavinayā. Katame dasa? Sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi, sammāñāṇaṃ, sammāvimutti – ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa dhammā parisuddhā pariyodātā, nāññatra sugatavinayā”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

123. “Monks, these ten states are pure and exceedingly bright; they are not found apart from the discipline of the Sugata. Which ten? Right view, right thought, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration, right knowledge, and right liberation. Monks, these ten states are indeed pure and exceedingly bright; they are not found apart from the discipline of the Sugata.” First.

2. Dutiyasuttaṃ

2. The Second Discourse

124. “Dasayime, bhikkhave, dhammā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā. Katame dasa? Sammādiṭṭhi [P 5.0238]…pe… sammāvimutti – ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa dhammā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

124. “Monks, these ten states, not having arisen before, do not arise apart from the discipline of the Sugata. Which ten? Right view... and so on... right liberation. Monks, these ten states, not having arisen before, indeed do not arise apart from the discipline of the Sugata.” Second.

3. Tatiyasuttaṃ

3. The Third Discourse

125. “Dasayime[M 3.0451], bhikkhave, dhammā mahapphalā mahānisaṃsā, nāññatra sugatavinayā. Katame dasa? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ime kho[T 5.0256], bhikkhave, dasa dhammā mahapphalā mahānisaṃsā, nāññatra sugatavinayā”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

125. “Monks, these ten states are of great fruit and great benefit; they are not found apart from the discipline of the Sugata. Which ten? Right view... and so on... right liberation. Monks, these ten states are indeed of great fruit and great benefit; they are not found apart from the discipline of the Sugata.” Third.

4. Catutthasuttaṃ

4. The Fourth Discourse

126. “Dasayime, bhikkhave, dhammā rāgavinayapariyosānā honti dosavinayapariyosānā honti mohavinayapariyosānā honti, nāññatra sugatavinayā. Katame dasa? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa dhammā rāgavinayapariyosānā [V 3.0206] honti dosavinayapariyosānā honti mohavinayapariyosānā honti, nāññatra sugatavinayā”ti. Catutthaṃ.

126. “Monks, these ten states culminate in the removal of lust, hatred, and delusion; they are not found apart from the discipline of the Sugata. Which ten? Right view... and so on... right liberation. Monks, these ten states indeed culminate in the removal of lust, hatred, and delusion; they are not found apart from the discipline of the Sugata.” Fourth.

5. Pañcamasuttaṃ

5. The Fifth Discourse

127. “Dasayime, bhikkhave, dhammā ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā. Katame dasa? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa dhammā ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

127. “Monks, these ten states lead to utter disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to higher knowledge, to awakening, and to Nibbāna, but not apart from the discipline of the Sugata. Which ten? Right view... and so on... right liberation. Monks, these ten states indeed lead to utter disenchantment, to dispassion, to cessation, to peace, to higher knowledge, to awakening, and to Nibbāna, but not apart from the discipline of the Sugata.” Fifth.

6. Chaṭṭhasuttaṃ

6. The Sixth Discourse
