128. “Dasayime, bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā. Katame dasa? Sammādiṭṭhi [P 5.0239]…pe… sammāvimutti – ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā anuppannā uppajjanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

128. “Monks, these ten states, when developed and cultivated, arise where they have not arisen before, and nowhere else than in the discipline of the Sugata. Which ten? Right view... and so on... right liberation. These, monks, are the ten states that, when developed and cultivated, indeed arise where they have not arisen before, and nowhere else than in the discipline of the Sugata.” Sixth.

7. Sattamasuttaṃ

7. The Seventh Discourse

129. “Dasayime, bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā honti mahānisaṃsā, nāññatra sugatavinayā. Katame dasa? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā mahapphalā honti mahānisaṃsā, nāññatra sugatavinayā”ti. Sattamaṃ.

129. “Monks, these ten states, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit and great benefit, and nowhere else than in the discipline of the Sugata. Which ten? Right view... and so on... right liberation. These, monks, are the ten states that, when developed and cultivated, are indeed of great fruit and great benefit, and nowhere else than in the discipline of the Sugata.” Seventh.

8. Aṭṭhamasuttaṃ

8. The Eighth Discourse

130. “Dasayime[T 5.0257][M 3.0452], bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā rāgavinayapariyosānā honti dosavinayapariyosānā honti mohavinayapariyosānā honti, nāññatra sugatavinayā. Katame dasa? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā [V 3.0207] rāgavinayapariyosānā honti dosavinayapariyosānā honti mohavinayapariyosānā honti, nāññatra sugatavinayā”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

130. “Monks, these ten states, when developed and cultivated, culminate in the removal of lust, hatred, and delusion, and nowhere else than in the discipline of the Sugata. Which ten? Right view... and so on... right liberation. These, monks, are the ten states that, when developed and cultivated, indeed culminate in the removal of lust, hatred, and delusion, and nowhere else than in the discipline of the Sugata.” Eighth.

9. Navamasuttaṃ

9. The Ninth Discourse

131. “Dasayime, bhikkhave, dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā. Katame dasa? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa dhammā bhāvitā bahulīkatā ekantanibbidāya virāgāya nirodhāya upasamāya abhiññāya sambodhāya nibbānāya saṃvattanti, nāññatra sugatavinayā”ti. Navamaṃ.

131. “Monks, these ten states, when developed and cultivated, lead solely to disenchantment, dispassion, cessation, peace, higher knowledge, awakening, and Nibbāna, and nowhere else than in the discipline of the Sugata. Which ten? Right view... and so on... right liberation. These, monks, are the ten states that, when developed and cultivated, indeed lead solely to disenchantment, dispassion, cessation, peace, higher knowledge, awakening, and Nibbāna, and nowhere else than in the discipline of the Sugata.” Ninth.

10. Dasamasuttaṃ

10. The Tenth Discourse

132. “Dasayime[P 5.0240], bhikkhave, micchattā. Katame dasa? Micchādiṭṭhi, micchāsaṅkappo, micchāvācā, micchākammanto, micchāājīvo, micchāvāyāmo, micchāsati, micchāsamādhi, micchāñāṇaṃ, micchāvimutti – ime kho, bhikkhave, dasa micchattā”ti. Dasamaṃ.

132. “Monks, these are the ten states of wrongness. Which ten? Wrong view, wrong thought, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong concentration, wrong knowledge, and wrong liberation. These, monks, are indeed the ten states of wrongness.” Tenth.

11. Ekādasamasuttaṃ

11. The Eleventh Discourse

133. “Dasayime, bhikkhave, sammattā. Katame dasa? Sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi, sammāñāṇaṃ, sammāvimutti – ime kho[T 5.0258], bhikkhave, dasa sammattā”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

133. “Monks, these are the ten states of rightness. Which ten? Right view, right thought, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration, right knowledge, and right liberation. These, monks, are indeed the ten states of rightness.” Eleventh.

Parisuddhavaggo tatiyo.

The Chapter on Purity, the Third.

(14) 4. Sādhuvaggo

(14) 4. The Chapter on the Good

1. Sādhusuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Good

134. a. ni. 10.178 “Sādhuñca [M 3.0453][V 3.0208] vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi asādhuñca. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

134. “Monks, I will teach you the good and the bad. Listen to it and attend carefully; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, asādhu? Micchādiṭṭhi, micchāsaṅkappo, micchāvācā, micchākammanto, micchāājīvo, micchāvāyāmo, micchāsati, micchāsamādhi, micchāñāṇaṃ, micchāvimutti – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, asādhu. Katamañca, bhikkhave, sādhu? Sammādiṭṭhi[P 5.0241], sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi, sammāñāṇaṃ, sammāvimutti – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sādhū”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the bad? Wrong view, wrong thought, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong concentration, wrong knowledge, and wrong liberation. This, monks, is called the bad. And what, monks, is the good? Right view, right thought, right speech, right action, right livelihood, right effort, right mindfulness, right concentration, right knowledge, and right liberation. This, monks, is called the good.” First.

2. Ariyadhammasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Noble Dhamma

135. “Ariyadhammañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi anariyadhammañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, anariyo dhammo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, anariyo dhammo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, ariyo dhammo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyo dhammo”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

135. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the noble Dhamma and the ignoble Dhamma. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the ignoble Dhamma? Wrong view… wrong liberation. This, bhikkhus, is called the ignoble Dhamma. And what, bhikkhus, is the noble Dhamma? Right view… right liberation. This, bhikkhus, is called the noble Dhamma.” Second.

3. Akusalasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Unwholesome

136. “Akusalañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi kusalañca. Taṃ suṇātha [T 5.0259] …pe… katamañca, bhikkhave, akusalaṃ? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave[V 3.0209], akusalaṃ. Katamañca, bhikkhave, kusalaṃ? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, kusala”nti. Tatiyaṃ.

136. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the unwholesome and the wholesome. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the unwholesome? Wrong view… wrong liberation. This, bhikkhus, is called the unwholesome. And what, bhikkhus, is the wholesome? Right view… right liberation. This, bhikkhus, is called the wholesome.” Third.

4. Atthasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Beneficial

137. “Atthañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi anatthañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, anattho? Micchādiṭṭhi [P 5.0242]…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, anattho. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, attho? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, attho”ti. Catutthaṃ.

137. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you what is beneficial and what is unbeneficial. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the unbeneficial? Wrong view… wrong liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the unbeneficial. And what, bhikkhus, is the beneficial? Right view… right liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the beneficial.” Fourth.

5. Dhammasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Dhamma

138. “Dhammañca [M 3.0454] vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi adhammañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, adhammo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhammo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, dhammo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammo”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

138. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma and what is not the Dhamma. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is not the Dhamma? Wrong view… wrong liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called what is not the Dhamma. And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma? Right view… right liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma.” Fifth.

6. Sāsavasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Tainted

139. “Sāsavañca vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi anāsavañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, sāsavo [T 5.0260] dhammo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sāsavo dhammo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, anāsavo dhammo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, anāsavo dhammo”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

139. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the tainted Dhamma and the untainted Dhamma. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the tainted Dhamma? Wrong view… wrong liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the tainted Dhamma. And what, bhikkhus, is the untainted Dhamma? Right view… right liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the untainted Dhamma.” Sixth.

7. Sāvajjasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Blameworthy

140. “Sāvajjañca vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi anavajjañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, sāvajjo dhammo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti [V 3.0210] – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sāvajjo dhammo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, anavajjo dhammo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, anavajjo dhammo”ti. Sattamaṃ.

140. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the blameworthy Dhamma and the blameless Dhamma. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the blameworthy Dhamma? Wrong view… wrong liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the blameworthy Dhamma. And what, bhikkhus, is the blameless Dhamma? Right view… right liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the blameless Dhamma.” Seventh.

8. Tapanīyasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Tormenting

141. “Tapanīyañca [P 5.0243] vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi atapanīyañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, tapanīyo dhammo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, tapanīyo dhammo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, atapanīyo dhammo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, atapanīyo dhammo”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

141. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the tormenting Dhamma and the non-tormenting Dhamma. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the tormenting Dhamma? Wrong view… wrong liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the tormenting Dhamma. And what, bhikkhus, is the non-tormenting Dhamma? Right view… right liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the non-tormenting Dhamma.” Eighth.

9. Ācayagāmisuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Accumulation

142. “Ācayagāmiñca vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi apacayagāmiñca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave[T 5.0261], ācayagāmī dhammo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ācayagāmī dhammo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave[M 3.0455], apacayagāmī dhammo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, apacayagāmī dhammo”ti. Navamaṃ.

142. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma that leads to rebirth and the Dhamma that leads to Nibbāna. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that leads to rebirth? Wrong view… wrong liberation. This, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that leads to rebirth. And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that leads to Nibbāna? Right view… right liberation. This, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that leads to Nibbāna.” Ninth.

10. Dukkhudrayasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Suffering as an Outcome

143. “Dukkhudrayañca vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi sukhudrayañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, dukkhudrayo dhammo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhudrayo dhammo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sukhudrayo dhammo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sukhudrayo dhammo”ti. Dasamaṃ.

143. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma that has suffering as its outcome and the Dhamma that has happiness as its outcome. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that has suffering as its outcome? Wrong view… wrong liberation. This, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that has suffering as its outcome. And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that has happiness as its outcome? Right view… right liberation. This, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that has happiness as its outcome.” Tenth.

11. Dukkhavipākasuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on Painful Results

144. “Dukkhavipākañca [V 3.0211][P 5.0244] vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi sukhavipākañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, dukkhavipāko dhammo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhavipāko dhammo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sukhavipāko dhammo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sukhavipāko dhammo”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

144. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma that has painful results and the Dhamma that has pleasant results. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that has painful results? Wrong view… wrong liberation. This, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that has painful results. And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that has pleasant results? Right view… right liberation. This, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that has pleasant results.” Eleventh.

Sādhuvaggo catuttho.

The Sādhu Chapter, the Fourth.

(15) 5. Ariyavaggo

(15) 5. The Noble Chapter

1. Ariyamaggasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Noble Path

145. “Ariyamaggañca [T 5.0262][V 3.0212] vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi anariyamaggañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, anariyo maggo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, anariyo maggo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, ariyo maggo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyo maggo”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

145. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma that is the noble path and the Dhamma that is the ignoble path. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the ignoble path? Wrong view… wrong liberation. This, bhikkhus, is called the ignoble path. And what, bhikkhus, is the noble path? Right view… right liberation. This, bhikkhus, is called the noble path.” First.

2. Kaṇhamaggasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Dark Path

146. “Kaṇhamaggañca vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi sukkamaggañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo [P 5.0245] ca, bhikkhave, kaṇhamaggo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ [M 3.0456] vuccati, bhikkhave, kaṇhamaggo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sukkamaggo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sukkamaggo”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

146. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma that is the dark path and the Dhamma that is the bright path. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the dark path? Wrong view… wrong liberation. This, bhikkhus, is called the dark path. And what, bhikkhus, is the bright path? Right view… right liberation. This, bhikkhus, is called the bright path.” Second.

3. Saddhammasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the True Dhamma

147. “Saddhammañca vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi asaddhammañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, asaddhammo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, asaddhammo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, saddhammo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, saddhammo”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

147. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the true Dhamma and the untrue Dhamma. Listen to that... And what, bhikkhus, is the untrue Dhamma? Wrong view... wrong liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the untrue Dhamma. And what, bhikkhus, is the true Dhamma? Right view... right liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the true Dhamma.” The Third.

4. Sappurisadhammasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Dhamma of a True Person

148. “Sappurisadhammañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi asappurisadhammañca. Taṃ [T 5.0263] suṇātha [V 3.0213] …pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, asappurisadhammo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, asappurisadhammo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sappurisadhammo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sappurisadhammo”ti. Catutthaṃ.

148. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma of a true person and the Dhamma of an untrue person. Listen to that... And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma of an untrue person? Wrong view... wrong liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma of an untrue person. And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma of a true person? Right view... right liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma of a true person.” The Fourth.

5. Uppādetabbasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on What Should Be Brought into Being

149. “Uppādetabbañca vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi na uppādetabbañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, na uppādetabbo dhammo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, na uppādetabbo dhammo. Katamo [P 5.0246] ca, bhikkhave, uppādetabbo dhammo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, uppādetabbo dhammo”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

149. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma that should be brought into being and the Dhamma that should not be brought into being. Listen to that... And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that should not be brought into being? Wrong view... wrong liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that should not be brought into being. And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that should be brought into being? Right view... right liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that should be brought into being.” The Fifth.

6. Āsevitabbasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on What Should Be Practiced

150. “Āsevitabbañca vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi na āsevitabbañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, na āsevitabbo dhammo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, na āsevitabbo dhammo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, āsevitabbo dhammo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, āsevitabbo dhammo”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

150. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma that should be practiced and the Dhamma that should not be practiced. Listen to that... And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that should not be practiced? Wrong view... wrong liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that should not be practiced. And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that should be practiced? Right view... right liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that should be practiced.” The Sixth.

7. Bhāvetabbasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on What Should Be Developed

151. “Bhāvetabbañca [M 3.0457] vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi na bhāvetabbañca[T 5.0264]. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, na bhāvetabbo dhammo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, na bhāvetabbo dhammo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, bhāvetabbo dhammo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhāvetabbo dhammo”ti. Sattamaṃ.

151. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma that should be developed and the Dhamma that should not be developed. Listen to that... And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that should not be developed? Wrong view... wrong liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that should not be developed. And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that should be developed? Right view... right liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that should be developed.” The Seventh.

8. Bahulīkātabbasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on What Should Be Cultivated

152. “Bahulīkātabbañca [V 3.0214] vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi na bahulīkātabbañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, na bahulīkātabbo dhammo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, na bahulīkātabbo dhammo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, bahulīkātabbo dhammo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bahulīkātabbo dhammo”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

152. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma that should be cultivated and the Dhamma that should not be cultivated. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that should not be cultivated? Wrong view… wrong liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that should not be cultivated. And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that should be cultivated? Right view… right liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that should be cultivated.” The Eighth.

9. Anussaritabbasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on What Should Be Recollected

153. “Anussaritabbañca [P 5.0247] vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi na anussaritabbañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, na anussaritabbo dhammo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, na anussaritabbo dhammo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, anussaritabbo dhammo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, anussaritabbo dhammo”ti. Navamaṃ.

153. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma that should be recollected and the Dhamma that should not be recollected. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that should not be recollected? Wrong view… wrong liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that should not be recollected. And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that should be recollected? Right view… right liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that should be recollected.” The Ninth.

10. Sacchikātabbasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on What Should Be Realized

154. “Sacchikātabbañca [T 5.0265] vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi na sacchikātabbañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, na sacchikātabbo dhammo? Micchādiṭṭhi…pe… micchāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, na sacchikātabbo dhammo. Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sacchikātabbo dhammo? Sammādiṭṭhi…pe… sammāvimutti – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sacchikātabbo dhammo”ti. Dasamaṃ.

154. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma that should be realized and the Dhamma that should not be realized. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that should not be realized? Wrong view… wrong liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that should not be realized. And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma that should be realized? Right view… right liberation—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma that should be realized.” The Tenth.

Ariyavaggo pañcamo.

The Noble Chapter, the Fifth.

Tatiyapaṇṇāsakaṃ samattaṃ.

The Third Fifty is Concluded.

4. Catutthapaṇṇāsakaṃ

4. The Fourth Fifty

(16) 1. Puggalavaggo

(16) 1. The Chapter on Individuals

1. Sevitabbasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on One to Be Associated With

155. “Dasahi[T 5.0266][V 3.0215][M 3.0458], bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato puggalo na sevitabbo. Katamehi dasahi? Micchādiṭṭhiko [P 5.0248] hoti, micchāsaṅkappo hoti, micchāvāco hoti, micchākammanto hoti, micchāājīvo hoti, micchāvāyāmo hoti, micchāsati hoti, micchāsamādhi hoti, micchāñāṇī hoti, micchāvimutti hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato puggalo na sevitabbo.

155. “Bhikkhus, a person endowed with ten qualities should not be associated with. What ten? He is of wrong view, of wrong intention, of wrong speech, of wrong action, of wrong livelihood, of wrong effort, of wrong mindfulness, of wrong concentration, of wrong knowledge, and of wrong liberation. Bhikkhus, a person endowed with these ten qualities should not be associated with.

“Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato puggalo sevitabbo. Katamehi dasahi? Sammādiṭṭhiko hoti, sammāsaṅkappo hoti, sammāvāco hoti, sammākammanto hoti, sammāājīvo hoti, sammāvāyāmo hoti, sammāsati hoti, sammāsamādhi hoti, sammāñāṇī hoti, sammāvimutti hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato puggalo sevitabbo”ti.

“Bhikkhus, a person endowed with ten qualities should be associated with. What ten? He is of right view, of right intention, of right speech, of right action, of right livelihood, of right effort, of right mindfulness, of right concentration, of right knowledge, and of right liberation. Bhikkhus, a person endowed with these ten qualities should be associated with.”

2-12. Bhajitabbādisuttāni

2-12. Discourses beginning with 'To Be Associated With'

156-166. “Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato puggalo na bhajitabbo…pe… bhajitabbo…pe… na payirupāsitabbo… payirupāsitabbo…pe… na pujjo hoti… pujjo hoti…pe… na pāsaṃso hoti… pāsaṃso hoti…pe… agāravo hoti… sagāravo hoti…pe… appatisso hoti… sappatisso hoti…pe… na ārādhako hoti [V 3.0216] … ārādhako hoti…pe… na visujjhati… visujjhati…pe… mānaṃ nādhibhoti… mānaṃ adhibhoti…pe. [P 5.0249]… paññāya na vaḍḍhati… paññāya vaḍḍhati…pe….

“Monks, a person endowed with ten qualities should not be associated with... should be associated with... should not be attended upon... should be attended upon... is not to be venerated... is to be venerated... is not praiseworthy... is praiseworthy... is disrespectful... is respectful... is without deference... is with deference... is not one who pleases... is one who pleases... is not purified... is purified... does not overcome conceit... overcomes conceit... does not grow in wisdom... grows in wisdom...”

“Bahuṃ apuññaṃ [T 5.0267] pasavati… bahuṃ puññaṃ pasavati. Katamehi dasahi? Sammādiṭṭhiko hoti, sammāsaṅkappo hoti, sammāvāco hoti, sammākammanto hoti, sammāājīvo hoti, sammāvāyāmo hoti[M 3.0459], sammāsati hoti, sammāsamādhi hoti, sammāñāṇī hoti, sammāvimutti hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato puggalo bahuṃ puññaṃ pasavatī”ti.

“A person generates much demerit... a person generates much merit. With which ten? One is of right view, of right intention, of right speech, of right action, of right livelihood, of right effort, of right mindfulness, of right concentration, of right knowledge, and of right liberation. Monks, a person endowed with these ten qualities generates much merit.”

Puggalavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Chapter on Persons.

(17) 2. Jāṇussoṇivaggo

(17) 2. The Jāṇussoṇi Section

1. Brāhmaṇapaccorohaṇīsuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Brahmin’s Descent

167. Tena [V 3.0217] kho pana samayena jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo tadahuposathe sīsaṃnhāto navaṃ khomayugaṃ nivattho allakusamuṭṭhiṃ ādāya bhagavato avidūre ekamantaṃ ṭhito hoti.

167. Now at that time, the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi, having bathed his head on the uposatha day, dressed in a new pair of linen garments, and holding a handful of wet kusa grass, was standing to one side not far from the Blessed One.

Addasā kho bhagavā jāṇussoṇiṃ brāhmaṇaṃ tadahuposathe sīsaṃnhātaṃ navaṃ khomayugaṃ nivatthaṃ allakusamuṭṭhiṃ ādāya ekamantaṃ ṭhitaṃ. Disvāna jāṇussoṇiṃ brāhmaṇaṃ etadavoca – “kiṃ nu tvaṃ, brāhmaṇa, tadahuposathe sīsaṃnhāto navaṃ khomayugaṃ nivattho allakusamuṭṭhiṃ ādāya ekamantaṃ ṭhito? Kiṃ nvajja brāhmaṇakulassā”ti? “Paccorohaṇī, bho gotama, ajja brāhmaṇakulassā”ti[P 5.0250].

The Blessed One saw the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi standing to one side, his head bathed on the uposatha day, dressed in a new pair of linen garments, and holding a handful of wet kusa grass. Seeing him, the Blessed One said to him: “Why, brahmin, are you standing to one side, your head bathed on the uposatha day, dressed in a new pair of linen garments, and holding a handful of wet kusa grass? What observance is there for the brahmins today?” “Today, Master Gotama, is the Paccorohaṇī observance for the brahmins.”

“Yathā kathaṃ pana, brāhmaṇa, brāhmaṇānaṃ paccorohaṇī hotī”ti? “Idha, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā tadahuposathe sīsaṃnhātā navaṃ khomayugaṃ nivatthā allena gomayena pathaviṃ opuñjitvā haritehi kusehi pattharitvā antarā ca velaṃ antarā ca agyāgāraṃ seyyaṃ kappenti. Te taṃ rattiṃ tikkhattuṃ [T 5.0268] paccuṭṭhāya pañjalikā aggiṃ namassanti – ‘paccorohāma bhavantaṃ, paccorohāma bhavanta’nti. Bahukena ca sappitelanavanītena aggiṃ santappenti. Tassā ca rattiyā accayena paṇītena khādanīyena bhojanīyena brāhmaṇe santappenti. Evaṃ, bho gotama, brāhmaṇānaṃ paccorohaṇī hotī”ti.

“But how, brahmin, is the Paccorohaṇī observance of the brahmins?” “Here, Master Gotama, on the uposatha day, the brahmins bathe their heads, dress in new linen garments, smear the ground with wet cow dung, spread it with green kusa grass, and between the sand pile and the fire-hut, they prepare a bed. That night, they rise three times and, with hands reverently joined, pay homage to the fire, saying: ‘We descend to you, O venerable one; we descend to you, O venerable one.’ And they satisfy the fire with abundant ghee, oil, and fresh butter. At the end of that night, they satisfy the brahmins with choice hard and soft foods. Thus, Master Gotama, is the Paccorohaṇī observance of the brahmins.”

“Aññathā kho, brāhmaṇa, brāhmaṇānaṃ paccorohaṇī hoti, aññathā ca pana ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hotī”ti. “Yathā kathaṃ [M 3.0460] pana, bho gotama, ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hoti? Sādhu me bhavaṃ gotamo tathā dhammaṃ desetu yathā ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hotī”ti.

“The Paccorohaṇī observance of the brahmins is one way, brahmin, and the Paccorohaṇī observance in the Noble One’s Discipline is another.” “But how, Master Gotama, is there a Paccorohaṇī observance in the Noble One’s Discipline? It would be good if Master Gotama would teach me the Dhamma as to how the Paccorohaṇī observance occurs in the Noble One’s Discipline.”

“Tena [V 3.0218] hi, brāhmaṇa, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –

“Well then, brahmin, listen and attend carefully; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Idha, brāhmaṇa, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘pāṇātipātassa kho pāpako vipāko diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcā’ ti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya pāṇātipātaṃ pajahati; pāṇātipātā paccorohati.

“Here, brahmin, a noble disciple reflects thus: ‘The taking of life has an evil result both in this very life and in the life to come.’ Having reflected thus, he abandons the taking of life; he descends from the taking of life.

…Adinnādānassa kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya adinnādānaṃ pajahati; adinnādānā paccorohati.

‘...Taking what is not given has an evil result both in this very life and in the life to come.’ Having reflected thus, he abandons taking what is not given; he descends from taking what is not given.

…Kāmesumicchācārassa kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya kāmesumicchācāraṃ pajahati; kāmesumicchācārā paccorohati.

‘...Sexual misconduct has an evil result both in this very life and in the life to come.’ Having reflected thus, he abandons sexual misconduct; he descends from sexual misconduct.

…Musāvādassa kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya [P 5.0251] musāvādaṃ pajahati; musāvādā paccorohati.

‘...False speech has an evil result both in this very life and in the life to come.’ Having reflected thus, he abandons false speech; he descends from false speech.

…Pisuṇāya vācāya kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme [T 5.0269] abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya pisuṇaṃ vācaṃ pajahati; pisuṇāya vācāya paccorohati.

‘...Divisive speech has an evil result both in this very life and in the life to come.’ Having reflected thus, he abandons divisive speech; he descends from divisive speech.

…Pharusāya vācāya kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya pharusaṃ vācaṃ pajahati; pharusāya vācāya paccorohati.

‘...Harsh speech has an evil result both in this very life and in the life to come.’ Having reflected thus, he abandons harsh speech; he descends from harsh speech.

…Samphappalāpassa kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya samphappalāpaṃ pajahati; samphappalāpā paccorohati.

‘...Frivolous speech has an evil result both in this very life and in the life to come.’ Having reflected thus, he abandons frivolous speech; he descends from frivolous speech.

…Abhijjhāya [M 3.0461] kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya abhijjhaṃ pajahati; abhijjhāya paccorohati.

‘...Covetousness has an evil result both in this very life and in the life to come.’ Having reflected thus, he abandons covetousness; he descends from covetousness.

…Byāpādassa [V 3.0219] kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcāti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya byāpādaṃ pajahati; byāpādā paccorohati.

‘...Ill will has an evil result both in this very life and in the life to come.’ Having reflected thus, he abandons ill will; he descends from ill will.

…Micchādiṭṭhiyā kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcā’ti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya micchādiṭṭhiṃ pajahati; micchādiṭṭhiyā paccorohati. Evaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hotī”ti.

‘...Wrong view has an evil result both in this very life and in the life to come.’ Having reflected thus, he abandons wrong view; he descends from wrong view. This, brahmin, is how the Paccorohaṇī observance occurs in the Noble One’s Discipline.”

“Aññathā kho, bho gotama, brāhmaṇānaṃ paccorohaṇī hoti, aññathā ca pana ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇī hoti. Imissā, bho gotama, ariyassa vinaye paccorohaṇiyā brāhmaṇānaṃ paccorohaṇī kalaṃ nāgghati soḷasiṃ. Abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“Indeed, Master Gotama, the desisting of the brahmins is of one kind, and the desisting in the Discipline of the Noble One is of another kind. Master Gotama, the desisting of the brahmins is not worth a sixteenth part of this desisting in the Discipline of the Noble One. Excellent, Master Gotama! … From this day forward, may Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life.” First Sutta.

2. Ariyapaccorohaṇīsuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Noble Desisting

168. “Ariyaṃ vo, bhikkhave, paccorohaṇiṃ desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ[T 5.0270]. Bhagavā etadavoca –

168. “Monks, I will teach you the noble desisting. Listen to it, attend closely, and I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those monks replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, ariyā paccorohaṇī? Idha[P 5.0252], bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘pāṇātipātassa kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcā’ti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya pāṇātipātaṃ pajahati; pāṇātipātā paccorohati.

“And what, monks, is the noble desisting? Here, monks, a noble disciple reflects thus: ‘Indeed, the destruction of life has an evil result, both in the present life and in the future.’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons the destruction of life; he desists from the destruction of life.

… ‘Adinnādānassa kho pāpako vipāko – diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcā’ti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya adinnādānaṃ pajahati; adinnādānā paccorohati.

‘Indeed, taking what is not given has an evil result, both in the present life and in the future.’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons taking what is not given; he desists from taking what is not given.

… [V 3.0220] ‘Kāmesumicchācārassa kho pāpako vipāko…pe… kāmesumicchācārā paccorohati.

‘Indeed, sexual misconduct has an evil result…’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons sexual misconduct; he desists from sexual misconduct.

… ‘Musāvādassa [M 3.0462] kho pāpako vipāko…pe… musāvādā paccorohati.

‘Indeed, false speech has an evil result…’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons false speech; he desists from false speech.

… ‘Pisuṇāya vācāya kho pāpako vipāko…pe… pisuṇāya vācāya paccorohati.

‘Indeed, slanderous speech has an evil result…’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons slanderous speech; he desists from slanderous speech.

… ‘Pharusāya vācāya kho pāpako vipāko…pe… pharusāya vācāya paccorohati.

‘Indeed, harsh speech has an evil result…’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons harsh speech; he desists from harsh speech.

… ‘Samphappalāpassa kho pāpako vipāko…pe… samphappalāpā paccorohati.

‘Indeed, frivolous speech has an evil result…’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons frivolous speech; he desists from frivolous speech.

… ‘Abhijjhāya kho pāpako vipāko…pe… abhijjhāya paccorohati.

‘Indeed, covetousness has an evil result…’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons covetousness; he desists from covetousness.

… ‘Byāpādassa kho pāpako vipāko…pe… [T 5.0271] byāpādā paccorohati.

‘Indeed, ill will has an evil result…’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons ill will; he desists from ill will.

“Katamā ca, bhikkhave, ariyā paccorohaṇī? Idha, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako iti paṭisañcikkhati – ‘micchādiṭṭhiyā kho pāpako vipāko diṭṭhe ceva dhamme abhisamparāyañcā’ti. So iti paṭisaṅkhāya micchādiṭṭhiṃ pajahati; micchādiṭṭhiyā paccorohati. Ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyā paccorohaṇī”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

‘Indeed, wrong view has an evil result, both in the present life and in the future.’ Having reflected thus with wisdom, he abandons wrong view; he desists from wrong view. This, monks, is called the noble desisting.” Second Sutta.

3. Saṅgāravasuttaṃ

3. The Saṅgārava Sutta

169. a. ni. 10.117 Atha [V 3.0221] kho saṅgāravo brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho saṅgāravo brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

169. Then the brahmin Saṅgārava approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged joyful greetings with the Blessed One. After concluding the joyful and memorable talk, he sat down at a suitable place. Sitting at a suitable place, the brahmin Saṅgārava said this to the Blessed One:

“Kiṃ nu kho, bho gotama, orimaṃ tīraṃ, kiṃ pārimaṃ tīra”nti? “Pāṇātipāto kho, brāhmaṇa, orimaṃ tīraṃ, pāṇātipātā veramaṇī pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Adinnādānaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, orimaṃ tīraṃ, adinnādānā veramaṇī pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Kāmesumicchācāro orimaṃ tīraṃ, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Musāvādo orimaṃ tīraṃ, musāvādā veramaṇī pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Pisuṇā vācā orimaṃ tīraṃ, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Pharusā vācā orimaṃ tīraṃ, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Samphappalāpo orimaṃ tīraṃ, samphappalāpā veramaṇī pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Abhijjhā orimaṃ tīraṃ, anabhijjhā pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Byāpādo orimaṃ tīraṃ, abyāpādo pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Micchādiṭṭhi orimaṃ tīraṃ, sammādiṭṭhi pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Idaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, orimaṃ tīraṃ, idaṃ pārimaṃ tīranti.

“Venerable Gotama, what is the near shore, and what is the far shore?” “Brahmin, the destruction of life is the near shore; abstention from the destruction of life is the far shore. Taking what is not given is the near shore; abstention from taking what is not given is the far shore. Wrong conduct in sensual pleasures is the near shore; abstention from wrong conduct in sensual pleasures is the far shore. False speech is the near shore; abstention from false speech is the far shore. Slanderous speech is the near shore; abstention from slanderous speech is the far shore. Harsh speech is the near shore; abstention from harsh speech is the far shore. Frivolous talk is the near shore; abstention from frivolous talk is the far shore. Covetousness is the near shore; non-covetousness is the far shore. Ill will is the near shore; non-ill will is the far shore. Wrong view is the near shore; right view is the far shore. This, brahmin, is the near shore, and this is the far shore.

“Appakā [M 3.0463][P 5.0253] te manussesu, ye janā pāragāmino;

Athāyaṃ [T 5.0272] itarā pajā, tīramevānudhāvati.

“Few are those among humans, the people who go to the far shore; this other populace just runs along the shore.

“Ye ca kho sammadakkhāte, dhamme dhammānuvattino;

Te janā pāramessanti, maccudheyyaṃ suduttaraṃ.

But those people who practice in accordance with the Dhamma in the well-expounded Dhamma, having crossed over the realm of Death, which is very difficult to cross, will reach the far shore.

“Kaṇhaṃ dhammaṃ vippahāya, sukkaṃ bhāvetha paṇḍito;

Okā anokamāgamma, viveke yattha dūramaṃ.

A wise person, having abandoned the dark state, should cultivate the bright state. Having come from the home to the homeless state, to that seclusion where it is difficult to delight.

“Tatrābhiratimiccheyya, hitvā kāme akiñcano;

Pariyodapeyya attānaṃ, cittaklesehi paṇḍito.

Therein, a wise person should wish for delight, having abandoned sensual pleasures, being one with no impediments. One should purify oneself from the defilements of the mind.

“Yesaṃ [V 3.0222] sambodhiyaṅgesu, sammā cittaṃ subhāvitaṃ;

Ādānapaṭinissagge, anupādāya ye ratā;

Khīṇāsavā jutimanto, te loke parinibbutā”ti. tatiyaṃ;

Those whose minds are well and thoroughly developed in the factors of enlightenment, who, without clinging, delight in the relinquishing of grasping; those whose taints are destroyed, who are possessed of great radiance, they are fully extinguished in the world.” Third Sutta.

4. Orimasuttaṃ

4. The Near Shore Sutta

170. “Orimañca, bhikkhave, tīraṃ desessāmi pārimañca tīraṃ. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamañca, bhikkhave, orimaṃ tīraṃ, katamañca pārimaṃ tīraṃ? Pāṇātipāto, bhikkhave, orimaṃ tīraṃ, pāṇātipātā veramaṇī pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Adinnādānaṃ orimaṃ tīraṃ, adinnādānā veramaṇī pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Kāmesumicchācāro orimaṃ tīraṃ, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Musāvādo orimaṃ tīraṃ, musāvādā veramaṇī pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Pisuṇā vācā orimaṃ tīraṃ, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Pharusā vācā orimaṃ tīraṃ, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Samphappalāpo orimaṃ tīraṃ, samphappalāpā veramaṇī pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Abhijjhā orimaṃ tīraṃ, anabhijjhā pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Byāpādo orimaṃ tīraṃ, abyāpādo pārimaṃ [T 5.0273] tīraṃ. Micchādiṭṭhi orimaṃ tīraṃ, sammādiṭṭhi pārimaṃ tīraṃ. Idaṃ kho, bhikkhave, orimaṃ tīraṃ, idaṃ pārimaṃ tīranti.

170. “Monks, I will teach the near shore and the far shore. Listen to that… Monks, what is the near shore, and what is the far shore? Monks, the destruction of life is the near shore; abstention from the destruction of life is the far shore. Taking what is not given is the near shore; abstention from taking what is not given is the far shore. Wrong conduct in sensual pleasures is the near shore; abstention from wrong conduct in sensual pleasures is the far shore. False speech is the near shore; abstention from false speech is the far shore. Slanderous speech is the near shore; abstention from slanderous speech is the far shore. Harsh speech is the near shore; abstention from harsh speech is the far shore. Frivolous talk is the near shore; abstention from frivolous talk is the far shore. Covetousness is the near shore; non-covetousness is the far shore. Ill will is the near shore; non-ill will is the far shore. Wrong view is the near shore; right view is the far shore. This, monks, is the near shore, and this is the far shore.”

“Appakā [P 5.0254] te manussesu, ye janā pāragāmino;

Athāyaṃ itarā pajā, tīramevānudhāvati.

Few are those among humans who go to the far shore; this other populace just runs along this shore.

“Ye ca kho sammadakkhāte, dhamme dhammānuvattino;

Te janā pāramessanti, maccudheyyaṃ suduttaraṃ.

But those who practice in accordance with the Dhamma in the well-expounded Dhamma—they will reach the far shore, having crossed over the realm of Death, which is very difficult to cross.

“Kaṇhaṃ [M 3.0464] dhammaṃ vippahāya, sukkaṃ bhāvetha paṇḍito;

Okā anokamāgamma, viveke yattha dūramaṃ.

Having abandoned the dark state, a wise person should cultivate the bright. Having gone from home to homelessness, to that seclusion where it is difficult to delight.

“Tatrābhiratimiccheyya, hitvā kāme akiñcano;

Pariyodapeyya attānaṃ, cittaklesehi paṇḍito.

Therein one should wish for delight. Having abandoned sensual pleasures, possessing nothing, the wise person should purify the self of the mind's defilements.

“Yesaṃ [V 3.0223] sambodhiyaṅgesu, sammā cittaṃ subhāvitaṃ;

Ādānapaṭinissagge, anupādāya ye ratā;

Khīṇāsavā jutimanto, te loke parinibbutā”ti. catutthaṃ;

Those whose minds are well and thoroughly developed in the factors of enlightenment; who, without clinging, delight in the relinquishing of grasping; whose taints are destroyed, who are possessed of great radiance—they are fully extinguished in the world.” Fourth.

5. Paṭhamaadhammasuttaṃ

5. The First Discourse on Unrighteousness

171. a. ni. 10.113 “Adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo anattho ca; dhammo ca veditabbo attho ca. Adhammañca viditvā anatthañca, dhammañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabbaṃ.

171. Bhikkhus, unrighteousness should be understood, and what is harmful; and the Dhamma should be understood, and what is beneficial. Having understood unrighteousness and what is harmful, and having understood the Dhamma and what is beneficial, one should practice in accordance with the Dhamma and in accordance with what is beneficial.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, adhammo ca anattho ca? Pāṇātipāto, adinnādānaṃ, kāmesumicchācāro, musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo, abhijjhā, byāpādo, micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhammo [T 5.0274] ca anattho ca.

And what, bhikkhus, is unrighteousness and what is harmful? The destruction of life, taking what is not given, misconduct in sensual pleasures, false speech, slanderous speech, harsh speech, frivolous talk, covetousness, ill will, and wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called unrighteousness and what is harmful.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, dhammo ca attho ca? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī, musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī, anabhijjhā, abyāpādo, sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammo ca attho ca.

And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma and what is beneficial? Abstinence from the destruction of life, abstinence from taking what is not given, abstinence from misconduct in sensual pleasures, abstinence from false speech, abstinence from slanderous speech, abstinence from harsh speech, abstinence from frivolous talk, non-covetousness, non-ill will, and right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma and what is beneficial.

“‘Adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo anattho ca; dhammo ca veditabbo attho ca. Adhammañca viditvā anatthañca, dhammañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabba’nti, iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vutta”nti. Pañcamaṃ.

‘Bhikkhus, unrighteousness should be understood, and what is harmful; and the Dhamma should be understood, and what is beneficial. Having understood unrighteousness and what is harmful, and having understood the Dhamma and what is beneficial, one should practice in accordance with the Dhamma and in accordance with what is beneficial.’ It was in reference to this that this was said. Fifth.

6. Dutiyaadhammasuttaṃ

6. The Second Discourse on Unrighteousness

172. “Adhammo [P 5.0255] ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo dhammo ca; anattho ca veditabbo attho ca. Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo [M 3.0465] yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabba”nti. Idamavoca bhagavā. Idaṃ vatvāna sugato uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ pāvisi.

172. Bhikkhus, unrighteousness should be understood, and the Dhamma; what is harmful should be understood, and what is beneficial. Having understood unrighteousness and the Dhamma, and having understood what is harmful and what is beneficial, one should practice in accordance with the Dhamma and in accordance with what is beneficial. The Blessed One said this. Having said this, the Sugata rose from his seat and entered the dwelling.

Atha [V 3.0224] kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi – “idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo dhammo ca; anattho ca veditabbo attho ca. Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabba’nti. Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyā”ti?

Then, not long after the Blessed One had departed, this thought occurred to those bhikkhus: “Friends, the Blessed One, having given us this summary in brief without analyzing the meaning in detail, has risen from his seat and entered the dwelling, saying: ‘Bhikkhus, unrighteousness should be understood, and the Dhamma; what is harmful should be understood, and what is beneficial. Having understood unrighteousness and the Dhamma, and having understood what is harmful and what is beneficial, one should practice in accordance with the Dhamma and in accordance with what is beneficial.’ Now, who could analyze in detail the meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail?”

Atha [T 5.0275] kho tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ etadahosi – “ayaṃ kho āyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etamatthaṃ puccheyyāma. Yathā no āyasmā mahākaccāno byākarissati tathā naṃ dhāressāmā”ti.

Then this thought occurred to those bhikkhus: “This Venerable Mahākaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. The Venerable Mahākaccāna is capable of analyzing in detail the meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail. What if we were to approach the Venerable Mahākaccāna and, having approached him, ask about this matter? As the Venerable Mahākaccāna explains it to us, so shall we bear it in mind.”

Atha kho te bhikkhū yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkamiṃsu; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmatā mahākaccānena saddhiṃ sammodiṃsu. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etadavocuṃ –

Then those bhikkhus approached the Venerable Mahākaccāna. Having approached, they exchanged courteous greetings with the Venerable Mahākaccāna. Having concluded their friendly and memorable talk, they sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those bhikkhus said this to the Venerable Mahākaccāna:

“Idaṃ kho no, āvuso kaccāna, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo dhammo ca; anattho ca veditabbo attho ca. Adhammañca [P 5.0256] viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabba’nti.

“Friend Kaccāna, the Blessed One, having given us this summary in brief without analyzing the meaning in detail, has risen from his seat and entered the dwelling, saying: ‘Bhikkhus, unrighteousness should be understood, and the Dhamma; what is harmful should be understood, and what is beneficial. Having understood unrighteousness and the Dhamma, and having understood what is harmful and what is beneficial, one should practice in accordance with the Dhamma and in accordance with what is beneficial.’”

“Tesaṃ no, āvuso, amhākaṃ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi – ‘idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – adhammo ca, bhikkhave…pe… tathā [T 5.0276] paṭipajjitabbanti. Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena [M 3.0466] uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyā’ti?

“Friend, not long after the Blessed One had departed, this thought occurred to us: ‘Friends, the Blessed One, having given us this summary in brief without analyzing the meaning in detail, has risen from his seat and entered the dwelling, saying: “Bhikkhus, unrighteousness… and so on… one should practice accordingly.” Now, who could analyze in detail the meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail?’”

“Tesaṃ [V 3.0225] no, āvuso, amhākaṃ etadahosi – ‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāma. Yathā no āyasmā mahākaccāno byākarissati tathā naṃ dhāressāmā’ti. Vibhajatu āyasmā mahākaccāno”ti.

“Friend, this thought occurred to us: ‘This Venerable Mahākaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise fellow practitioners of the holy life. The Venerable Mahākaccāna is capable of analyzing in detail the meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail. Let us approach the Venerable Mahākaccāna; having approached the Venerable Mahākaccāna, let us ask about this matter. As the Venerable Mahākaccāna explains it to us, so shall we bear it in mind.’ May the Venerable Mahākaccāna analyze it.”

“Seyyathāpi, āvuso, puriso sāratthiko sāraṃ gavesī sārapariyesanaṃ caramāno mahato rukkhassa tiṭṭhato sāravato atikkammeva mūlaṃ atikkamma khandhaṃ sākhāpalāse sāraṃ pariyesitabbaṃ maññeyya. Evaṃsampadamidaṃ āyasmantānaṃ satthari sammukhībhūte taṃ bhagavantaṃ atisitvā amhe etamatthaṃ paṭipucchitabbaṃ maññatha maññetha (sī.), maññeyyātha (ka.). So hāvuso, bhagavā jānaṃ jānāti passaṃ passati cakkhubhūto ñāṇabhūto dhammabhūto brahmabhūto vattā pavattā atthassa ninnetā amatassa dātā dhammassāmī tathāgato. So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi yaṃ tumhe bhagavantaṃyeva [P 5.0257] upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyātha. Yathā vo bhagavā byākareyya tathā naṃ dhāreyyāthā”ti.

“Friends, it is just as if a man needing heartwood, seeking heartwood, wandering in search of heartwood, were to bypass the root and the trunk of a great, standing tree possessing heartwood, and think that heartwood should be sought among the branches and leaves. So it is for you venerable ones: with the Teacher present before you, you bypass that Blessed One and think that we should be asked about this matter. For, friends, that Blessed One knows what is to be known, sees what is to be seen; he has become the eye, has become knowledge, has become the Dhamma, has become the supreme. He is the speaker, the proclaimer, the guide to the meaning, the giver of the deathless, the lord of the Dhamma, the Tathāgata. This was indeed the time for you to approach the Blessed One himself and ask about this matter. As the Blessed One would explain it to you, so you should remember it.”

“Addhā, āvuso kaccāna, bhagavā jānaṃ jānāti passaṃ passati cakkhubhūto ñāṇabhūto dhammabhūto brahmabhūto vattā pavattā atthassa ninnetā amatassa [T 5.0277] dātā dhammassāmī tathāgato. So ceva panetassa kālo ahosi yaṃ mayaṃ bhagavantaṃyeva upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāma. Yathā no bhagavā byākareyya tathā naṃ dhāreyyāma. Api cāyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Vibhajatāyasmā mahākaccāno agaruṃ karitvā”ti.

“Indeed, friend Kaccāna, the Blessed One knows what is to be known, sees what is to be seen; he has become the eye, has become knowledge, has become the Dhamma, has become the supreme. He is the speaker, the proclaimer, the guide to the meaning, the giver of the deathless, the lord of the Dhamma, the Tathāgata. That was indeed the time for us to approach the Blessed One himself and ask about this matter. As the Blessed One would explain it to us, so we would remember it. Moreover, the Venerable Mahākaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise fellow practitioners. The Venerable Mahākaccāna is capable of analyzing in detail the meaning of this summary given in brief by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail. Let the Venerable Mahākaccāna analyze it, without making it a burden.”

“Tena [M 3.0467] hāvuso, suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, āvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahākaccānassa paccassosuṃ. Athāyasmā mahākaccāno etadavoca –

“In that case, friends, listen and pay close attention; I will speak.” “Yes, friend,” those monks replied to the Venerable Mahākaccāna. Then the Venerable Mahākaccāna said this:

“Yaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā [V 3.0226] uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo…pe… tathā paṭipajjitabba’nti.

“Friends, the Blessed One, having pointed out a summary in brief for us without analyzing the meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered the dwelling, saying: ‘Monks, what is not the Dhamma should be known… and one should practice accordingly.’”

“Katamo, cāvuso, adhammo; katamo ca dhammo? Katamo ca anattho, katamo ca attho? “Pāṇātipāto, āvuso, adhammo; pāṇātipātā veramaṇī dhammo; ye ca pāṇātipātapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; pāṇātipātā veramaṇipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“And what, friends, is not the Dhamma? And what is the Dhamma? And what is not the benefit? And what is the benefit? The destruction of life, friends, is not the Dhamma; abstention from the destruction of life is the Dhamma. And whatever many evil, unwholesome states arise on account of the destruction of life, this is not the benefit. And on account of abstention from the destruction of life, many wholesome states go to the fulfillment of development; this is the benefit.

“Adinnādānaṃ, āvuso, adhammo; adinnādānā veramaṇī dhammo; ye ca adinnādānapaccayā aneke [P 5.0258] pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti[T 5.0278], ayaṃ anattho; adinnādānā veramaṇipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Taking what is not given, friends, is not the Dhamma; abstention from taking what is not given is the Dhamma. And whatever many evil, unwholesome states arise on account of taking what is not given, this is not the benefit. And on account of abstention from taking what is not given, many wholesome states go to the fulfillment of development; this is the benefit.

“Kāmesumicchācāro, āvuso, adhammo; kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī dhammo; ye ca kāmesumicchācārapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Sexual misconduct, friends, is not the Dhamma; abstention from sexual misconduct is the Dhamma. And whatever many evil, unwholesome states arise on account of sexual misconduct, this is not the benefit. And on account of abstention from sexual misconduct, many wholesome states go to the fulfillment of development; this is the benefit.

“Musāvādo, āvuso, adhammo; musāvādā veramaṇī dhammo; ye ca musāvādapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; musāvādā veramaṇipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“False speech, friends, is not the Dhamma; abstention from false speech is the Dhamma. And whatever many evil, unwholesome states arise on account of false speech, this is not the benefit. And on account of abstention from false speech, many wholesome states go to the fulfillment of development; this is the benefit.

“Pisuṇā vācā, āvuso, adhammo; pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī dhammo; ye ca pisuṇāvācāpaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Divisive speech, friends, is not the Dhamma; abstention from divisive speech is the Dhamma. And whatever many evil, unwholesome states arise on account of divisive speech, this is not the benefit. And on account of abstention from divisive speech, many wholesome states go to the fulfillment of development; this is the benefit.

“Pharusā [M 3.0468] vācā, āvuso, adhammo; pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī dhammo; ye ca pharusāvācāpaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; pharusāya vācāya veramaṇipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Harsh speech, friends, is not the Dhamma; abstention from harsh speech is the Dhamma. And whatever many evil, unwholesome states arise on account of harsh speech, this is not the benefit. And on account of abstention from harsh speech, many wholesome states go to the fulfillment of development; this is the benefit.

“Samphappalāpo[V 3.0227], āvuso, adhammo; samphappalāpā veramaṇī dhammo; ye ca samphappalāpapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; samphappalāpā veramaṇipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ [T 5.0279] attho.

“Frivolous speech, friends, is not the Dhamma; abstention from frivolous speech is the Dhamma. And whatever many evil, unwholesome states arise on account of frivolous speech, this is not the benefit. And on account of abstention from frivolous speech, many wholesome states go to the fulfillment of development; this is the benefit.

“Abhijjhā, āvuso, adhammo; anabhijjhā dhammo; ye ca abhijjhāpaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; anabhijjhāpaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Covetousness, friends, is not the Dhamma; non-covetousness is the Dhamma. And whatever many evil, unwholesome states arise on account of covetousness, this is not the benefit. And on account of non-covetousness, many wholesome states go to the fulfillment of development; this is the benefit.”

“Byāpādo, āvuso, adhammo; abyāpādo dhammo; ye ca byāpādapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; abyāpādapaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

Friends, ill will is not the Dhamma; non-ill will is the Dhamma. And the many evil, unwholesome states that arise on account of ill will, this is a detriment. And on account of non-ill will, many wholesome states go to the fulfillment of development; this is a benefit.

“Micchādiṭṭhi, āvuso, adhammo; sammādiṭṭhi dhammo; ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

Friends, wrong view is not the Dhamma; right view is the Dhamma. And the many evil, unwholesome states that arise on account of wrong view, this is a detriment. And on account of right view, many wholesome states go to the fulfillment of development; this is a benefit.”

“‘Yaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ [P 5.0259] avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo…pe… tathā paṭipajjitabba’nti. Imassa kho ahaṃ, āvuso, bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa evaṃ vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi. Ākaṅkhamānā ca pana tumhe, āvuso, bhagavantaṃyeva upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyātha. Yathā no bhagavā byākaroti tathā naṃ dhāreyyāthā”ti.

“Friends, the Blessed One, having set forth a summary for us in brief without analyzing the meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered the monastery, saying: ‘Monks, what is not the Dhamma should be known… and one should practice accordingly.’ Friends, of this summary set forth in brief by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail, I understand the meaning in detail. If you wish, friends, you may approach the Blessed One himself and ask about this matter. As the Blessed One explains it to you, so should you bear it in mind.”

“Evamāvuso”ti kho te bhikkhū āyasmato mahākaccānassa bhāsitaṃ abhinanditvā anumoditvā uṭṭhāyāsanā yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṃsu[M 3.0469]; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ [T 5.0280] abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdiṃsu. Ekamantaṃ nisinnā kho te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ –

“Very well, friend.” Having delighted in and rejoiced at the words of the Venerable Mahākaccāna, those monks rose from their seats and approached the Blessed One. Having approached and paid homage to the Blessed One, they sat down to one side. Seated to one side, those monks said this to the Blessed One:

“Yaṃ kho no, bhante, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā [V 3.0228] vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo…pe… tathā paṭipajjitabba’nti.

“Venerable Sir, the Blessed One, having set forth a summary for us in brief without analyzing the meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered the monastery, saying: ‘Monks, what is not the Dhamma should be known… and one should practice accordingly.’”

“Tesaṃ no, bhante, amhākaṃ acirapakkantassa bhagavato etadahosi – ‘idaṃ kho no, āvuso, bhagavā saṃkhittena uddesaṃ uddisitvā vitthārena atthaṃ avibhajitvā uṭṭhāyāsanā vihāraṃ paviṭṭho – ‘adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo…pe… tathā paṭipajjitabba’nti. Ko nu kho imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajeyyā’ti?

“Venerable Sir, not long after the Blessed One had departed, this thought occurred to us: ‘Friends, the Blessed One, having set forth this summary for us in brief without analyzing the meaning in detail, rose from his seat and entered the monastery, saying: “Monks, what is not the Dhamma should be known… and one should practice accordingly.” Who, now, might analyze in detail the meaning of this summary set forth in brief by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail?’”

“Tesaṃ no, bhante, amhākaṃ etadahosi – ‘ayaṃ kho āyasmā mahākaccāno satthu ceva saṃvaṇṇito, sambhāvito ca viññūnaṃ sabrahmacārīnaṃ. Pahoti cāyasmā mahākaccāno imassa bhagavatā saṃkhittena uddesassa uddiṭṭhassa [P 5.0260] vitthārena atthaṃ avibhattassa vitthārena atthaṃ vibhajituṃ. Yaṃnūna mayaṃ yenāyasmā mahākaccāno tenupasaṅkameyyāma; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyāma. Yathā no āyasmā mahākaccāno byākarissati tathā naṃ dhāressāmā’ti.

“Venerable Sir, this thought occurred to us: ‘This Venerable Mahākaccāna is praised by the Teacher and esteemed by his wise companions in the holy life. The Venerable Mahākaccāna is able to analyze in detail the meaning of this summary set forth in brief by the Blessed One, the meaning of which was not analyzed in detail. Let us now go to the Venerable Mahākaccāna and, having approached him, let us ask him about this matter. As the Venerable Mahākaccāna explains it to us, so shall we bear it in mind.’”

“Atha kho mayaṃ, bhante, yenāyasmā mahākaccāno [T 5.0281] tenupasaṅkamimhā; upasaṅkamitvā āyasmantaṃ mahākaccānaṃ etamatthaṃ apucchimhā. Tesaṃ no, bhante, āyasmatā mahākaccānena imehi akkharehi imehi padehi imehi byañjanehi attho suvibhatto”ti.

“Then, Venerable Sir, we went to the Venerable Mahākaccāna and, having approached him, we asked him about this matter. For us, Venerable Sir, the meaning was well analyzed by the Venerable Mahākaccāna with these letters, these words, and these phrases.”

“Sādhu sādhu, bhikkhave! Paṇḍito, bhikkhave, mahākaccāno. Mahāpañño, bhikkhave, mahākaccāno. Maṃ cepi tumhe, bhikkhave, upasaṅkamitvā etamatthaṃ paṭipuccheyyātha, ahampi cetaṃ evamevaṃ byākareyyaṃ yathā taṃ mahākaccānena byākataṃ. Eso ceva tassa attho. Evañca naṃ dhāreyyāthā”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“Excellent, excellent, monks! Monks, Mahākaccāna is wise. Monks, Mahākaccāna is of great wisdom. If you, monks, had approached me and asked about this matter, I too would have explained it in the very same way that it was explained by Mahākaccāna. This is its very meaning. And you should bear it in mind thus.” Sixth.

7. Tatiyaadhammasuttaṃ

7. The Third Discourse on What is Not the Dhamma

173. “Adhammo [M 3.0470] ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo dhammo ca; anattho ca veditabbo attho ca[V 3.0229]. Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabbaṃ.

173. “Monks, what is not the Dhamma should be known, and the Dhamma should be known; what is a detriment should be known, and what is a benefit should be known. Having known what is not the Dhamma and the Dhamma, and having known what is a detriment and what is a benefit, one should practice in accordance with the Dhamma and in accordance with what is a benefit.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, adhammo, katamo ca dhammo; katamo ca anattho, katamo ca attho? Pāṇātipāto, bhikkhave, adhammo; pāṇātipātā veramaṇī dhammo; ye ca pāṇātipātapaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; pāṇātipātā veramaṇipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“And what, monks, is not the Dhamma, and what is the Dhamma? What is a detriment, and what is a benefit? The taking of life, monks, is not the Dhamma; abstaining from the taking of life is the Dhamma. And the many evil, unwholesome states that arise on account of taking life, this is a detriment. And on account of abstaining from taking life, many wholesome states go to the fulfillment of development; this is a benefit.

“Adinnādānaṃ, bhikkhave, adhammo; adinnādānā veramaṇī dhammo… kāmesumicchācāro, bhikkhave[P 5.0261], adhammo; kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī dhammo… musāvādo, bhikkhave, adhammo; musāvādā veramaṇī dhammo… pisuṇā vācā, bhikkhave, adhammo; pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī dhammo… pharusā vācā, bhikkhave, adhammo; pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī dhammo… samphappalāpo, bhikkhave[T 5.0282], adhammo; samphappalāpā veramaṇī dhammo… abhijjhā, bhikkhave, adhammo; anabhijjhā dhammo… byāpādo, bhikkhave, adhammo; abyāpādo dhammo….

“Monks, taking what is not given is not the Dhamma; abstaining from taking what is not given is the Dhamma… Monks, sexual misconduct is not the Dhamma; abstaining from sexual misconduct is the Dhamma… Monks, false speech is not the Dhamma; abstaining from false speech is the Dhamma… Monks, slanderous speech is not the Dhamma; abstaining from slanderous speech is the Dhamma… Monks, harsh speech is not the Dhamma; abstaining from harsh speech is the Dhamma… Monks, frivolous speech is not the Dhamma; abstaining from frivolous speech is the Dhamma… Monks, covetousness is not the Dhamma; non-covetousness is the Dhamma… Monks, ill will is not the Dhamma; non-ill will is the Dhamma….

“Micchādiṭṭhi, bhikkhave, adhammo; sammādiṭṭhi dhammo; ye ca micchādiṭṭhipaccayā aneke pāpakā akusalā dhammā sambhavanti, ayaṃ anattho; sammādiṭṭhipaccayā ca aneke kusalā dhammā bhāvanāpāripūriṃ gacchanti, ayaṃ attho.

“Monks, wrong view is not the Dhamma; right view is the Dhamma. And the many evil, unwholesome states that arise on account of wrong view, this is a detriment. And on account of right view, many wholesome states go to the fulfillment of development; this is a benefit.”

“‘Adhammo ca, bhikkhave, veditabbo dhammo ca; anattho ca veditabbo attho ca. Adhammañca viditvā dhammañca, anatthañca viditvā atthañca yathā dhammo yathā attho tathā paṭipajjitabba’nti, iti yaṃ taṃ vuttaṃ, idametaṃ paṭicca vutta”nti. Sattamaṃ.

“‘Bhikkhus, what is not Dhamma should be understood, and what is Dhamma should be understood; what is unbeneficial should be understood, and what is beneficial should be understood. Having understood what is not Dhamma and what is Dhamma, what is unbeneficial and what is beneficial, one should practice in accordance with the Dhamma and what is beneficial.’ Thus was it said, and it was in reference to this that it was said.” The seventh.

8. Kammanidānasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on the Cause of Kamma

174. “Pāṇātipātampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, tividhaṃ vadāmi – lobhahetukampi, dosahetukampi, mohahetukampi.

174. “Bhikkhus, I declare the destruction of life to be of three kinds: that which has greed as its cause, that which has hatred as its cause, and that which has delusion as its cause.

“Adinnādānampāhaṃ[M 3.0471][V 3.0230], bhikkhave, tividhaṃ vadāmi – lobhahetukampi, dosahetukampi, mohahetukampi.

“Bhikkhus, I declare taking what is not given to be of three kinds: that which has greed as its cause, that which has hatred as its cause, and that which has delusion as its cause.

“Kāmesumicchācārampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, tividhaṃ vadāmi – lobhahetukampi, dosahetukampi, mohahetukampi.

“Bhikkhus, I declare sexual misconduct to be of three kinds: that which has greed as its cause, that which has hatred as its cause, and that which has delusion as its cause.

“Musāvādampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, tividhaṃ vadāmi – lobhahetukampi, dosahetukampi, mohahetukampi.

“Bhikkhus, I declare false speech to be of three kinds: that which has greed as its cause, that which has hatred as its cause, and that which has delusion as its cause.

“Pisuṇavācampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, tividhaṃ vadāmi – lobhahetukampi, dosahetukampi, mohahetukampi.

“Bhikkhus, I declare slanderous speech to be of three kinds: that which has greed as its cause, that which has hatred as its cause, and that which has delusion as its cause.

“Pharusavācampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, tividhaṃ vadāmi – lobhahetukampi, dosahetukampi, mohahetukampi.

“Bhikkhus, I declare harsh speech to be of three kinds: that which has greed as its cause, that which has hatred as its cause, and that which has delusion as its cause.

“Samphappalāpampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, tividhaṃ vadāmi – lobhahetukampi, dosahetukampi, mohahetukampi.

“Bhikkhus, I declare frivolous speech to be of three kinds: that which has greed as its cause, that which has hatred as its cause, and that which has delusion as its cause.

“Abhijjhampāhaṃ[P 5.0262], bhikkhave, tividhaṃ vadāmi – lobhahetukampi, dosahetukampi, mohahetukampi.

“Bhikkhus, I declare covetousness to be of three kinds: that which has greed as its cause, that which has hatred as its cause, and that which has delusion as its cause.

“Byāpādampāhaṃ, bhikkhave, tividhaṃ vadāmi – lobhahetukampi, dosahetukampi, mohahetukampi.

“Bhikkhus, I declare ill will to be of three kinds: that which has greed as its cause, that which has hatred as its cause, and that which has delusion as its cause.

“Micchādiṭṭhimpāhaṃ, bhikkhave[T 5.0283], tividhaṃ vadāmi – lobhahetukampi, dosahetukampi, mohahetukampi. Iti kho, bhikkhave, lobho kammanidānasambhavo, doso kammanidānasambhavo, moho kammanidānasambhavo. Lobhakkhayā kammanidānasaṅkhayo, dosakkhayā kammanidānasaṅkhayo, mohakkhayā kammanidānasaṅkhayo”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, I declare wrong view to be of three kinds: that which has greed as its cause, that which has hatred as its cause, and that which has delusion as its cause. Thus, bhikkhus, greed is a source for the arising of kamma, hatred is a source for the arising of kamma, and delusion is a source for the arising of kamma. With the destruction of greed, the source of kamma is destroyed; with the destruction of hatred, the source of kamma is destroyed; with the destruction of delusion, the source of kamma is destroyed.” The eighth.

9. Parikkamanasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on Abandonment

175. “Saparikkamano [V 3.0231] ayaṃ, bhikkhave, dhammo, nāyaṃ dhammo aparikkamano. Kathañca, bhikkhave, saparikkamano ayaṃ dhammo, nāyaṃ dhammo aparikkamano? Pāṇātipātissa, bhikkhave, pāṇātipātā veramaṇī parikkamanaṃ hoti. Adinnādāyissa, bhikkhave, adinnādānā veramaṇī parikkamanaṃ hoti. Kāmesumicchācārissa, bhikkhave, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī parikkamanaṃ hoti. Musāvādissa, bhikkhave, musāvādā veramaṇī parikkamanaṃ hoti. Pisuṇavācassa[M 3.0472], bhikkhave, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī parikkamanaṃ hoti. Pharusavācassa, bhikkhave, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī parikkamanaṃ hoti. Samphappalāpissa, bhikkhave, samphappalāpā veramaṇī parikkamanaṃ hoti. Abhijjhālussa, bhikkhave, anabhijjhā parikkamanaṃ hoti. Byāpannacittassa byāpādassa (sī. pī. ka.), byāpannassa (syā.), bhikkhave, abyāpādo parikkamanaṃ hoti. Micchādiṭṭhissa, bhikkhave, sammādiṭṭhi parikkamanaṃ hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, saparikkamano ayaṃ dhammo, nāyaṃ dhammo aparikkamano”ti. Navamaṃ.

175. “Bhikkhus, this Dhamma is with abandonment; this Dhamma is not without abandonment. And how, bhikkhus, is this Dhamma with abandonment, and not without abandonment? For one who destroys life, bhikkhus, abstaining from the destruction of life is the abandonment. For one who takes what is not given, bhikkhus, abstaining from taking what is not given is the abandonment. For one who engages in sexual misconduct, bhikkhus, abstaining from sexual misconduct is the abandonment. For one who speaks falsely, bhikkhus, abstaining from false speech is the abandonment. For one who speaks slanderously, bhikkhus, abstaining from slanderous speech is the abandonment. For one who speaks harshly, bhikkhus, abstaining from harsh speech is the abandonment. For one who engages in frivolous speech, bhikkhus, abstaining from frivolous speech is the abandonment. For one who is covetous, bhikkhus, non-covetousness is the abandonment. For one with a mind of ill will, bhikkhus, non-ill will is the abandonment. For one with wrong view, bhikkhus, right view is the abandonment. Thus, bhikkhus, this Dhamma is with abandonment; this Dhamma is not without abandonment.” The ninth.

10. Cundasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse with Cunda

176. Evaṃ me sutaṃ – ekaṃ [P 5.0263] samayaṃ bhagavā pāvāyaṃ campāyaṃ (ka. sī.) dī. ni. 2.189 passitabbaṃ viharati cundassa kammāraputtassa ambavane. Atha kho cundo kammāraputto yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṃ abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ [T 5.0284] nisinnaṃ kho cundaṃ kammāraputtaṃ bhagavā etadavoca – “kassa no tvaṃ, cunda, soceyyāni rocesī”ti? “Brāhmaṇā, bhante, pacchābhūmakā kamaṇḍalukā sevālamālikā sevālamālakā (sī. syā. pī.) aggiparicārikā udakorohakā soceyyāni paññapenti; tesāhaṃ soceyyāni rocemī”ti.

176. Thus have I heard. At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Pāvā in the mango grove of Cunda the smith’s son. Then Cunda the smith’s son approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side. The Blessed One said this to Cunda the smith’s son who was sitting to one side: “Whose purifications, Cunda, do you approve of?” “Venerable sir, the Western brahmins, who carry water pots, wear garlands of water-weeds, attend the fire, and descend into the water, prescribe purifications; I approve of their purifications.”

“Yathā kathaṃ pana, cunda, brāhmaṇā pacchābhūmakā kamaṇḍalukā sevālamālikā aggiparicārikā udakorohakā soceyyāni paññapentī”ti? “Idha, bhante, brāhmaṇā pacchābhūmakā kamaṇḍalukā sevālamālikā aggiparicārikā udakorohakā. Te sāvakaṃ sāvake (syā. ka.) evaṃ samādapenti – ‘ehi tvaṃ, ambho purisa, kālasseva sakālasseva (syā.) uṭṭhahantova uṭṭhahanto (syā.), vuṭṭhahantova (pī. ka.) sayanamhā pathaviṃ āmaseyyāsi; no ce pathaviṃ āmaseyyāsi, allāni gomayāni āmaseyyāsi; no ce allāni [V 3.0232] gomayāni āmaseyyāsi, haritāni tiṇāni āmaseyyāsi; no ce haritāni tiṇāni āmaseyyāsi, aggiṃ paricareyyāsi; no ce aggiṃ paricareyyāsi, pañjaliko ādiccaṃ namasseyyāsi; no ce pañjaliko ādiccaṃ namasseyyāsi, sāyatatiyakaṃ udakaṃ oroheyyāsī’ti. Evaṃ kho, bhante, brāhmaṇā pacchābhūmakā [M 3.0473] kamaṇḍalukā sevālamālikā aggiparicārikā udakorohakā soceyyāni paññapenti; tesāhaṃ soceyyāni rocemī”ti.

“And how, Cunda, do the Western brahmins, who carry water pots, wear garlands of water-weeds, attend the fire, and descend into the water, prescribe purifications?” “Here, venerable sir, are the Western brahmins, who carry water pots, wear garlands of water-weeds, attend the fire, and descend into the water. They instruct their disciples thus: ‘Come now, good man, rising early from your bed, you should touch the earth; if you do not touch the earth, you should touch wet cow dung; if you do not touch wet cow dung, you should touch green grass; if you do not touch green grass, you should attend the fire; if you do not attend the fire, you should pay homage to the sun with joined palms; if you do not pay homage to the sun with joined palms, you should descend into the water for the third time in the evening.’ Thus, venerable sir, the Western brahmins, who carry water pots, wear garlands of water-weeds, attend the fire, and descend into the water, prescribe purifications; I approve of their purifications.”

“Aññathā kho, cunda, brāhmaṇā pacchābhūmakā kamaṇḍalukā sevālamālikā aggiparicārikā udakorohakā soceyyāni paññapenti, aññathā ca pana [P 5.0264] ariyassa vinaye soceyyaṃ hotī”ti. “Yathā kathaṃ pana, bhante, ariyassa vinaye soceyyaṃ hoti? Sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā tathā dhammaṃ desetu yathā ariyassa vinaye soceyyaṃ hotī”ti.
