“Cunda, the Western brahmins, who carry water pots, wear garlands of water-weeds, attend the fire, and descend into the water, prescribe purifications in one way, but in the Noble One’s discipline, purification is otherwise.” “But how, venerable sir, is purification in the Noble One’s discipline? It would be good, venerable sir, if the Blessed One would teach me the Dhamma so that I may know how purification is in the Noble One’s discipline.”

“Tena hi, cunda, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi [T 5.0285] karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho cundo kammāraputto bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –

“In that case, Cunda, listen and pay close attention; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” Cunda the smith's son replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Tividhaṃ kho, cunda, kāyena asoceyyaṃ hoti; catubbidhaṃ vācāya asoceyyaṃ hoti; tividhaṃ manasā asoceyyaṃ hoti.

“Cunda, there is threefold bodily impurity, fourfold verbal impurity, and threefold mental impurity.”

“Kathañca, cunda, tividhaṃ kāyena asoceyyaṃ hoti? “Idha, cunda, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti luddo lohitapāṇi hatapahate niviṭṭho adayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtesu pāṇabhūtesu (ka.).

“And how, Cunda, is there threefold bodily impurity? Here, Cunda, someone is a killer of living beings, cruel, bloody-handed, devoted to killing and violence, merciless to all living beings.

“Adinnādāyī hoti. Yaṃ taṃ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṃ gāmagataṃ vā araññagataṃ vā taṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādātā hoti.

“He is one who takes what is not given. Whatever property belonging to another, whether in a village or in the wilderness, he takes it with thievish intent, it not having been given.

“Kāmesumicchācārī hoti. Yā tā māturakkhitā piturakkhitā mātāpiturakkhitā natthi sī. syā. pī. potthakesu bhāturakkhitā bhaginirakkhitā ñātirakkhitā gottarakkhitā natthi sī. syā. pī. potthakesu dhammarakkhitā sasāmikā saparidaṇḍā antamaso mālāguḷaparikkhittāpi, tathārūpāsu cārittaṃ āpajjitā hoti. Evaṃ kho, cunda, tividhaṃ kāyena asoceyyaṃ hoti.

“He engages in sexual misconduct. He has sexual relations with women who are protected by their mother, by their father, by both mother and father, by their brother, by their sister, by their relatives, by their clan, or by the Dhamma; women with a husband; women liable to punishment; or even those betrothed with a garland. Thus, Cunda, there is threefold bodily impurity.”

“Kathañca[V 3.0233], cunda, catubbidhaṃ vācāya asoceyyaṃ hoti? Idha, cunda, ekacco musāvādī hoti. Sabhaggato vā parisaggato vā ñātimajjhagato vā pūgamajjhagato vā rājakulamajjhagato vā abhinīto sakkhipuṭṭho – ‘ehambho [M 3.0474] purisa, yaṃ jānāsi taṃ vadehī’ti so ajānaṃ vā ahaṃ jānāmīti, jānaṃ vā ahaṃ na jānāmīti, apassaṃ vā ahaṃ passāmīti, passaṃ vā ahaṃ na passāmīti (pī. ka.) evamuparipi, so ajānaṃ vā āha ‘jānāmī’ti, jānaṃ vā āha ‘na jānāmī’ti; apassaṃ vā āha ‘passāmī’ti, passaṃ vā āha ‘na passāmī’ti so ajānaṃ vā ahaṃ jānāmīti, jānaṃ vā ahaṃ na jānāmīti, apassaṃ vā ahaṃ passāmīti, passaṃ vā ahaṃ na passāmīti (pī. ka.) evamuparipi. Iti attahetu [P 5.0265] vā parahetu vā āmisakiñcikkhahetu vā sampajānamusā bhāsitā hoti.

“And how, Cunda, is there fourfold verbal impurity? Here, Cunda, someone is a liar. When summoned to a council, an assembly, a gathering of relatives, a gathering of guilds, or to the royal court, and questioned as a witness: ‘Come, good man, say what you know,’ not knowing, he says, ‘I know’; or knowing, he says, ‘I do not know’; not seeing, he says, ‘I see’; or seeing, he says, ‘I do not see.’ Thus, for his own sake, for another’s sake, or for some trifling material gain, he knowingly speaks a lie.

“Pisuṇavāco hoti. Ito sutvā amutra akkhātā imesaṃ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā imesaṃ [T 5.0286] akkhātā amūsaṃ bhedāya. Iti samaggānaṃ vā bhettā bhedātā (ka.), bhinnānaṃ vā anuppadātā, vaggārāmo vaggarato vagganandī vaggakaraṇiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti.

“He speaks divisively. Having heard something here, he reports it elsewhere to create division among these people, or having heard something elsewhere, he reports it to these people to create division among those. Thus he is a splitter of the united, or one who encourages division among the divided; he delights in discord, enjoys discord, is pleased with discord, and speaks words that create discord.

“Pharusavāco hoti. Yā sā vācā aṇḍakā kakkasā parakaṭukā parābhisajjanī kodhasāmantā asamādhisaṃvattanikā, tathārūpiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti.

“He speaks harsh words. He utters such speech as is abrasive, coarse, bitter to others, stinging to others, close to anger, and not conducive to concentration.

“Samphappalāpī hoti akālavādī abhūtavādī anatthavādī adhammavādī avinayavādī; anidhānavatiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti akālena anapadesaṃ apariyantavatiṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ. Evaṃ kho, cunda, catubbidhaṃ vācāya asoceyyaṃ hoti.

“He is one who speaks frivolous chatter. He speaks at the wrong time, speaks what is not true, speaks what is unbeneficial, speaks what is not the Dhamma, and speaks what is not the Vinaya. He is one who utters speech that is not worth treasuring, at the wrong time, without reference, without limit, and unconnected with benefit. In this way, Cunda, there is fourfold impurity by way of speech.

“Kathañca, cunda, tividhaṃ manasā asoceyyaṃ hoti? Idha, cunda, ekacco abhijjhālu hoti. Yaṃ taṃ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṃ taṃ abhijjhātā abhijjhitā (ka.) ma. ni. 1.440 passitabbaṃ hoti – ‘aho vata yaṃ parassa taṃ mamassā’ti.

“And how, Cunda, is there threefold impurity by way of mind? Here, Cunda, a certain person is covetous. He is one who covets the property and belongings of another, thinking: ‘Oh, may what belongs to another be mine!’

“Byāpannacitto hoti paduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo – ‘ime sattā haññantu vā bajjhantu vā ucchijjantu vā vinassantu vā mā vā ahesu’nti mā vā ahesuṃ iti vā ti (sī. pī. ka.).

“He is one who has a mind of ill will, with corrupt mental intentions, thinking: ‘May these beings be killed, or bound, or cut off, or destroyed, or may they not exist at all!’

“Micchādiṭṭhiko hoti viparītadassano – ‘natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ, natthi hutaṃ, natthi sukaṭadukkaṭānaṃ natthettha pāṭhabhedo kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, natthi ayaṃ loko, natthi paro loko, natthi mātā, natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye [V 3.0234] imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. Evaṃ kho, cunda, manasā tividhaṃ asoceyyaṃ hoti.

“He is one who has wrong view, a distorted perspective, thinking: ‘There is nothing given, nothing offered, nothing sacrificed. There is no fruit or result of good and bad actions. There is no this world, no other world. There is no mother, no father. There are no spontaneously arisen beings. There are in the world no ascetics and brahmins who are rightly directed and rightly practicing, who, having realized this world and the other world for themselves through direct knowledge, make them known.’ In this way, Cunda, there is threefold impurity by way of mind.

“Ime [M 3.0475][P 5.0266] kho, cunda, dasa akusalakammapathā akusalā kammapathā (?). Imehi kho, cunda, dasahi akusalehi kammapathehi samannāgato kālasseva uṭṭhahantova [T 5.0287] sayanamhā pathaviṃ cepi āmasati, asuciyeva hoti; no cepi pathaviṃ āmasati, asuciyeva hoti.

“These, Cunda, are the ten unwholesome courses of action. One who is endowed with these ten unwholesome courses of action, Cunda, is impure indeed, even if, rising early from bed, he touches the earth; and he is impure indeed even if he does not touch the earth.

“Allāni cepi gomayāni āmasati, asuciyeva hoti; no cepi allāni gomayāni āmasati, asuciyeva hoti.

“He is impure indeed, even if he touches wet cow dung; and he is impure indeed even if he does not touch wet cow dung.

“Haritāni cepi tiṇāni āmasati, asuciyeva hoti; no cepi haritāni tiṇāni āmasati, asuciyeva hoti.

“He is impure indeed, even if he touches green grass; and he is impure indeed even if he does not touch green grass.

“Aggiṃ cepi paricarati, asuciyeva hoti, no cepi aggiṃ paricarati, asuciyeva hoti.

“He is impure indeed, even if he tends the fire; and he is impure indeed even if he does not tend the fire.

“Pañjaliko cepi ādiccaṃ namassati, asuciyeva hoti; no cepi pañjaliko ādiccaṃ namassati, asuciyeva hoti.

“He is impure indeed, even if he worships the sun with joined palms; and he is impure indeed even if he does not worship the sun with joined palms.

“Sāyatatiyakaṃ cepi udakaṃ orohati, asuciyeva hoti; no cepi sāyatatiyakaṃ udakaṃ orohati, asuciyeva hoti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ime, cunda, dasa akusalakammapathā asucīyeva asucicceva (syā.) honti asucikaraṇā ca.

“He is impure indeed, even if he descends into the water for the third time in the evening; and he is impure indeed even if he does not descend into the water for the third time in the evening. For what reason? These ten unwholesome courses of action, Cunda, are themselves impure and are makers of impurity.

“Imesaṃ pana, cunda, dasannaṃ akusalānaṃ kammapathānaṃ samannāgamanahetu nirayo paññāyati, tiracchānayoni paññāyati, pettivisayo paññāyati, yā vā yā ca (ka.) panaññāpi kāci duggatiyo duggati hoti (syā. ka.).

“Furthermore, Cunda, on account of being endowed with these ten unwholesome courses of action, hell is discerned, the animal realm is discerned, the sphere of afflicted spirits is discerned, or whatever other woeful destinations there may be.

“Tividhaṃ kho, cunda, kāyena soceyyaṃ hoti; catubbidhaṃ vācāya soceyyaṃ hoti; tividhaṃ manasā soceyyaṃ hoti.

“Indeed, Cunda, there is threefold purity by way of body, fourfold purity by way of speech, and threefold purity by way of mind.

“Kathaṃ[V 3.0235], cunda, tividhaṃ kāyena soceyyaṃ hoti? Idha, cunda, ekacco pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho, lajjī dayāpanno, sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati.

“And how, Cunda, is there threefold purity by way of body? Here, Cunda, a certain person, having abandoned the taking of life, abstains from the taking of life. With rod laid down and weapon laid down, he is conscientious, compassionate, and dwells with compassion for the welfare of all living beings.

“Adinnādānaṃ [M 3.0476] pahāya, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti. Yaṃ taṃ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṃ gāmagataṃ vā araññagataṃ vā, na taṃ adinnaṃ taṃ nādinnaṃ (ka. sī., ma. ni. 1.441) theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādātā hoti.

“Having abandoned taking what is not given, he abstains from taking what is not given. He is not one who takes what is not given, with thievish intent, be it the property and belongings of another in a village or in the wilderness.

“Kāmesumicchācāraṃ pahāya, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato [T 5.0288] hoti yā tā māturakkhitā piturakkhitā mātāpiturakkhitā bhāturakkhitā bhaginirakkhitā ñātirakkhitā gottarakkhitā dhammarakkhitā sasāmikā saparidaṇḍā antamaso [P 5.0267] mālāguḷaparikkhittāpi, tathārūpāsu na cārittaṃ āpajjitā hoti. Evaṃ kho, cunda, tividhaṃ kāyena soceyyaṃ hoti.

Having abandoned sexual misconduct, he abstains from sexual misconduct. He is not one who transgresses with such women as are protected by their mother, protected by their father, protected by both mother and father, protected by their brother, protected by their sister, protected by their relatives, protected by their clan, protected by the Dhamma; or those who have a husband, are under penalty, or are even betrothed by a garland of flowers. In this way, Cunda, there is threefold purity by way of body.

“Kathañca, cunda, catubbidhaṃ vācāya soceyyaṃ hoti? Idha, cunda, ekacco musāvādaṃ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti. Sabhaggato vā parisaggato vā ñātimajjhagato vā pūgamajjhagato vā rājakulamajjhagato vā abhinīto sakkhipuṭṭho – ‘ehambho purisa, yaṃ jānāsi taṃ vadehī’ti, so ajānaṃ vā āha ‘na jānāmī’ti, jānaṃ vā āha ‘jānāmī’ti, apassaṃ vā āha ‘na passāmī’ti, passaṃ vā āha ‘passāmī’ti. Iti attahetu vā parahetu vā āmisakiñcikkhahetu vā na sampajānamusā bhāsitā hoti.

And how, Cunda, is there fourfold purity by way of speech? Here, Cunda, a certain person, having abandoned false speech, abstains from false speech. When he has gone to a council, to an assembly, to the midst of his relatives, to his guild, or to the royal court, and is brought in and questioned as a witness, ‘Come, good man, tell what you know,’ not knowing, he says, ‘I do not know,’ and knowing, he says, ‘I know’; not seeing, he says, ‘I do not see,’ and seeing, he says, ‘I see.’ Thus he is not one who speaks a deliberate lie for his own sake, for the sake of another, or for the sake of some trivial material gain.

“Pisuṇaṃ vācaṃ pahāya, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti – na ito sutvā amutra akkhātā imesaṃ bhedāya, na amutra vā sutvā imesaṃ akkhātā amūsaṃ bhedāya. Iti bhinnānaṃ vā sandhātā sahitānaṃ vā anuppadātā samaggārāmo samaggarato samagganandī samaggakaraṇiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti.

Having abandoned slanderous speech, he abstains from slanderous speech. He is not one who, having heard something here, repeats it elsewhere to cause a division among these people; or, having heard something elsewhere, repeats it to these people to cause a division among those people. Thus, he is a reconciler of those who are divided and an encourager of those who are united. Delighting in concord, rejoicing in concord, finding joy in concord, he is one who speaks words that create concord.

“Pharusaṃ vācaṃ pahāya, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti. Yā sā vācā nelā kaṇṇasukhā pemanīyā hadayaṅgamā porī bahujanakantā bahujanamanāpā, tathārūpiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti.

Having abandoned harsh speech, he abstains from harsh speech. He is one who speaks such speech as is faultless, pleasing to the ear, endearing, goes to the heart, is civilized, is beloved by the many, and is agreeable to the many.

“Samphappalāpaṃ [V 3.0236] pahāya, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti kālavādī bhūtavādī atthavādī dhammavādī vinayavādī; nidhānavatiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti kālena sāpadesaṃ pariyantavatiṃ atthasaṃhitaṃ. Evaṃ kho, cunda[T 5.0289], catubbidhaṃ vācāya soceyyaṃ hoti.

Having abandoned frivolous chatter, he abstains from frivolous chatter. He speaks at the proper time, speaks what is true, speaks what is beneficial, speaks on the Dhamma, and speaks on the Vinaya. He is one who speaks, at the proper time, words that are worth treasuring, are accompanied by reason, are circumscribed, and are connected with benefit. In this way, Cunda, there is fourfold purity by way of speech.

“Kathañca[M 3.0477], cunda, tividhaṃ manasā soceyyaṃ hoti? Idha, cunda, ekacco anabhijjhālu hoti. Yaṃ taṃ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṃ taṃ anabhijjhitā hoti – ‘aho vata yaṃ parassa taṃ mamassā’ti.

And how, Cunda, is there threefold purity by way of mind? Here, Cunda, a certain person is not covetous. He does not covet the property and belongings of another, thinking: ‘Oh, may that which belongs to another be mine!’

“Abyāpannacitto hoti appaduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo – ‘ime sattā averā hontu idaṃ padaṃ sī. syā. pī. potthakesu natthi, tathā ma. ni. 1.441 abyāpajjā, anīghā sukhī attānaṃ pariharantū’ti.

He is of a mind without ill will, with a mental resolve uncorrupted by malice: ‘May these beings be without enmity, without affliction, without distress, and may they maintain themselves in happiness!’

“Sammādiṭṭhiko hoti [P 5.0268] aviparītadassano – ‘atthi dinnaṃ, atthi yiṭṭhaṃ, atthi hutaṃ, atthi sukaṭadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, atthi ayaṃ loko, atthi paro loko, atthi mātā, atthi pitā, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. Evaṃ kho, cunda, tividhaṃ manasā soceyyaṃ hoti.

He has right view, an undistorted vision: ‘There is what is given, there is what is sacrificed, there is what is offered; there is fruit and result of wholesome and unwholesome actions; there is this world, there is the next world; there is mother, there is father; there are spontaneously arisen beings; there are in the world ascetics and brahmins who are proceeding rightly and practicing rightly, who, having realized this world and the next for themselves through direct knowledge, make it known.’ In this way, Cunda, there is threefold purity by way of mind.

“Ime kho, cunda, dasa kusalakammapathā. Imehi kho, cunda, dasahi kusalehi kammapathehi samannāgato kālasseva uṭṭhahantova sayanamhā pathaviṃ cepi āmasati, suciyeva hoti; no cepi pathaviṃ āmasati, suciyeva hoti.

These, Cunda, are the ten wholesome courses of action. Endowed with these ten wholesome courses of action, Cunda, if one, rising early from bed, touches the earth, one is indeed pure; and if one does not touch the earth, one is indeed pure.

“Allāni cepi gomayāni āmasati, suciyeva hoti; no cepi allāni gomayāni āmasati, suciyeva hoti.

If one touches wet cow dung, one is indeed pure; and if one does not touch wet cow dung, one is indeed pure.

“Haritāni cepi tiṇāni āmasati, suciyeva hoti; no cepi haritāni tiṇāni āmasati, suciyeva hoti.

If one touches green grass, one is indeed pure; and if one does not touch green grass, one is indeed pure.

“Aggiṃ [V 3.0237] cepi paricarati, suciyeva hoti; no cepi aggiṃ paricarati, suciyeva hoti.

If one attends to a fire, one is indeed pure; and if one does not attend to a fire, one is indeed pure.

“Pañjaliko cepi ādiccaṃ namassati, suciyeva hoti; no cepi pañjaliko ādiccaṃ namassati[T 5.0290], suciyeva hoti.

If, with hands clasped in reverence, one pays homage to the sun, one is indeed pure; and if, with hands clasped in reverence, one does not pay homage to the sun, one is indeed pure.

“Sāyatatiyakaṃ cepi udakaṃ orohati, suciyeva hoti; no cepi sāyatatiyakaṃ udakaṃ orohati, suciyeva hoti. Taṃ kissa hetu? Ime, cunda, dasa kusalakammapathā sucīyeva honti sucikaraṇā ca.

If one descends into the water for the third time in the evening, one is indeed pure; and if one does not descend into the water for the third time in the evening, one is indeed pure. For what reason? These ten wholesome courses of action, Cunda, are themselves pure and are purifiers.

“Imesaṃ [M 3.0478] pana, cunda, dasannaṃ kusalānaṃ kammapathānaṃ samannāgamanahetu devā paññāyanti, manussā paññāyanti, yā vā panaññāpi kāci sugatiyo”ti sugati hotīti (syā.), sugati hoti (ka.).

Moreover, Cunda, it is because of being endowed with these ten wholesome courses of action that devas are discerned, humans are discerned, and whatever other good destinations there may be.

Evaṃ vutte cundo kammāraputto bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “abhikkantaṃ, bhante…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ, bhante, bhagavā dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Dasamaṃ.

When this was said, Cunda the smith’s son said this to the Blessed One: “Excellent, venerable sir! … May the Blessed One remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life, from this day forward.” The tenth.

11. Jāṇussoṇisuttaṃ

11. The Discourse to Jāṇussoṇi

177. Atha [P 5.0269] kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho jāṇussoṇi brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca –

177. Then the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he exchanged friendly greetings with the Blessed One. After concluding a pleasant and memorable conversation, he sat down to one side. Seated to one side, the brahmin Jāṇussoṇi said this to the Blessed One:

“Mayamassu, bho gotama, brāhmaṇā nāma. Dānāni dema, saddhāni karoma – ‘idaṃ dānaṃ petānaṃ ñātisālohitānaṃ upakappatu, idaṃ dānaṃ petā ñātisālohitā paribhuñjantū’ti. Kacci taṃ, bho gotama, dānaṃ petānaṃ ñātisālohitānaṃ upakappati; kacci te petā ñātisālohitā taṃ dānaṃ paribhuñjantī”ti? “Ṭhāne kho, brāhmaṇa, upakappati, no aṭṭhāne”ti.

“Master Gotama, we are indeed brahmins. We give gifts and make offerings for the deceased, thinking: ‘May this gift reach our departed relatives and kinsmen; may our departed relatives and kinsmen partake of this gift.’ Master Gotama, does that gift reach the departed relatives and kinsmen? Do those departed relatives and kinsmen partake of that gift?” “Brahmin, it reaches them in a possible case, but not in an impossible case.”

“Katamaṃ [V 3.0238] pana, bho katamañca pana bho (sī. pī.) katamaṃ (syā.) gotama, ṭhānaṃ, katamaṃ aṭṭhāna”nti? “Idha, brāhmaṇa, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, pisuṇavāco hoti, pharusavāco hoti, samphappalāpī hoti, abhijjhālu hoti, byāpannacitto hoti, micchādiṭṭhiko [T 5.0291] hoti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā nirayaṃ upapajjati. Yo nerayikānaṃ sattānaṃ āhāro, tena so tattha yāpeti, tena so tattha tiṭṭhati. Idampi idaṃ (syā.) kho, brāhmaṇa, aṭṭhānaṃ yattha ṭhitassa taṃ dānaṃ na upakappati.

“Master Gotama, what, then, is a suitable destination, and what is an unsuitable destination?” “Here, brahmin, a certain person destroys life, takes what is not given, engages in sexual misconduct, speaks falsehood, speaks slanderously, speaks harshly, engages in frivolous talk, is covetous, has a mind of ill will, and holds wrong view. With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in hell. Whatever is the food of beings in hell, on that he subsists there, by that he is sustained there. This, brahmin, is an unsuitable destination, where for one established therein, that gift does not reach him.

“Idha pana, brāhmaṇa, ekacco pāṇātipātī…pe… micchādiṭṭhiko hoti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā tiracchānayoniṃ upapajjati. Yo tiracchānayonikānaṃ sattānaṃ āhāro, tena so tattha yāpeti, tena [M 3.0479] so tattha tiṭṭhati. Idampi kho, brāhmaṇa, aṭṭhānaṃ yattha ṭhitassa taṃ dānaṃ na upakappati.

“Furthermore, brahmin, a certain person destroys life… and holds wrong view. With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the animal realm. Whatever is the food of beings in the animal realm, on that he subsists there, by that he is sustained there. This too, brahmin, is an unsuitable destination, where for one established therein, that gift does not reach him.

“Idha pana, brāhmaṇa, ekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya [P 5.0270] paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, anabhijjhālu hoti, abyāpannacitto hoti, sammādiṭṭhiko hoti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā manussānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Yo manussānaṃ āhāro, tena so tattha yāpeti, tena so tattha tiṭṭhati. Idampi kho, brāhmaṇa, aṭṭhānaṃ yattha ṭhitassa taṃ dānaṃ na upakappati.

“Furthermore, brahmin, a certain person abstains from destroying life, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from sexual misconduct, abstains from false speech, abstains from slanderous speech, abstains from harsh speech, abstains from frivolous talk, is not covetous, is without a mind of ill will, and holds right view. With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn into the companionship of human beings. Whatever is the food of human beings, on that he subsists there, by that he is sustained there. This too, brahmin, is an unsuitable destination, where for one established therein, that gift does not reach him.

“Idha pana, brāhmaṇa, ekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhiko hoti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Yo devānaṃ āhāro, tena so tattha yāpeti, tena so tattha tiṭṭhati. Idampi, brāhmaṇa, aṭṭhānaṃ yattha ṭhitassa [T 5.0292] taṃ dānaṃ upakappati.

“Furthermore, brahmin, a certain person abstains from destroying life… and holds right view. With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn into the companionship of devas. Whatever is the food of devas, on that he subsists there, by that he is sustained there. This too, brahmin, is an unsuitable destination, where for one established therein, that gift does not reach him.

“Idha pana, brāhmaṇa, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti…pe… micchādiṭṭhiko hoti. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā pettivisayaṃ upapajjati. Yo pettivesayikānaṃ sattānaṃ āhāro, tena so tattha yāpeti, tena so tattha tiṭṭhati, yaṃ vā panassa ito anuppavecchanti mittāmaccā [V 3.0239] vā ñātisālohitā vā mittā vā amaccā vā ñātī vā sālohitā vā (sī. pī.), tena so tattha yāpeti, tena so tattha tiṭṭhati. Idaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, ṭhānaṃ yattha ṭhitassa taṃ dānaṃ upakappatī”ti.

“Furthermore, brahmin, a certain person destroys life… and holds wrong view. With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the realm of petas. Whatever is the food of beings in the peta realm, on that he subsists there, by that he is sustained there. Or, whatever his friends, companions, relatives, or kinsmen send forth from here, on that he subsists there, by that he is sustained there. This, brahmin, is the suitable destination, where for one established therein, that gift reaches him.”

“Sace pana, bho gotama, so peto ñātisālohito taṃ ṭhānaṃ anupapanno hoti, ko taṃ dānaṃ paribhuñjatī”ti? “Aññepissa, brāhmaṇa, petā ñātisālohitā taṃ ṭhānaṃ upapannā honti, te taṃ dānaṃ paribhuñjantī”ti.

“But if, Master Gotama, that departed relative and kinsman has not been reborn in that place, who partakes of that gift?” “Brahmin, his other departed relatives and kinsmen who have been reborn in that place—they partake of that gift.”

“Sace pana, bho gotama, so ceva peto ñātisālohito taṃ ṭhānaṃ anupapanno hoti aññepissa ñātisālohitā petā taṃ [M 3.0480] ṭhānaṃ anupapannā honti, ko taṃ dānaṃ paribhuñjatī”ti? “Aṭṭhānaṃ kho etaṃ, brāhmaṇa, anavakāso yaṃ taṃ ṭhānaṃ vivittaṃ assa iminā dīghena addhunā yadidaṃ petehi [P 5.0271] ñātisālohitehi. Api ca, brāhmaṇa, dāyakopi anipphalo”ti.

“But if, Master Gotama, that very departed relative and kinsman has not been reborn in that place, and his other departed relatives and kinsmen have also not been reborn in that place, who partakes of that gift?” “Brahmin, it is impossible, there is no opportunity, that this place should be devoid of departed relatives and kinsmen for such a long time. And furthermore, brahmin, the giver is not without fruit.”

“Aṭṭhānepi bhavaṃ gotamo parikappaṃ vadatī”ti? “Aṭṭhānepi kho ahaṃ, brāhmaṇa, parikappaṃ vadāmi. Idha, brāhmaṇa, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, pisuṇavāco hoti, pharusavāco hoti, samphappalāpī hoti, abhijjhālu hoti, byāpannacitto hoti, micchādiṭṭhiko hoti; so dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṃ pānaṃ vatthaṃ [T 5.0293] yānaṃ mālāgandhavilepanaṃ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā hatthīnaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. So tattha lābhī hoti annassa pānassa mālānānālaṅkārassa mālāgandhavilepanassa nānālaṅkārassa (ka.).

“Does the venerable Gotama declare a provision even in an unsuitable destination?” “Brahmin, I do declare a provision even in an unsuitable destination. Here, brahmin, a certain person destroys life, takes what is not given, engages in sexual misconduct, speaks falsehood, speaks slanderously, speaks harshly, engages in frivolous talk, is covetous, has a mind of ill will, and holds wrong view; but he is a giver of food, drink, clothing, vehicles, garlands, scents, unguents, bedding, lodging, and lamps to an ascetic or a brahmin. With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn into the companionship of elephants. There he becomes a recipient of food, drink, garlands, and various ornaments.

“Yaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, idha pāṇātipātī adinnādāyī kāmesumicchācārī musāvādī pisuṇavāco pharusavāco samphappalāpī abhijjhālu byāpannacitto micchādiṭṭhiko, tena so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā hatthīnaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Yañca kho so dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṃ pānaṃ vatthaṃ yānaṃ mālāgandhavilepanaṃ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ, tena so tattha lābhī hoti annassa pānassa mālānānālaṅkārassa.

“Brahmin, in that he was one who here destroyed life, took what is not given, engaged in sexual misconduct, spoke falsehood, spoke slanderously, spoke harshly, engaged in frivolous talk, was covetous, had a mind of ill will, and held wrong view, because of that, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn into the companionship of elephants. And in that he was a giver of food, drink, clothing, vehicles, garlands, scents, unguents, bedding, lodging, and lamps to an ascetic or a brahmin, because of that he becomes a recipient there of food, drink, garlands, and various ornaments.”

“Idha pana, brāhmaṇa, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti…pe… micchādiṭṭhiko hoti. So dātā [V 3.0240] hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṃ pānaṃ vatthaṃ yānaṃ mālāgandhavilepanaṃ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā assānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati…pe… gunnaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati…pe… kukkurānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati “kukkurānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjatī”ti ayaṃ vāro kesuci sīhaḷapotthakesu na dissatīti iṅgalisapotthake adholipi. taṃ dasavāragaṇanāya sameti. So tattha lābhī hoti annassa pānassa mālānānālaṅkārassa.

“Furthermore, brahmin, a certain person is one who takes life… is one who has wrong view. That person is a giver to an ascetic or a brahmin of food, drink, clothing, vehicles, garlands, scents, and unguents, bedding, lodging, and lamps. With the breaking up of the body, after death, that person is reborn into the companionship of horses… is reborn into the companionship of cattle… is reborn into the companionship of dogs. There, that person is a recipient of food, drink, garlands, and various ornaments.

“Yaṃ [M 3.0481] kho, brāhmaṇa, idha pāṇātipātī…pe. [P 5.0272] … micchādiṭṭhiko, tena so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā kukkurānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Yañca kho [T 5.0294] so dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṃ pānaṃ vatthaṃ yānaṃ mālāgandhavilepanaṃ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ, tena so tattha lābhī hoti annassa pānassa mālānānālaṅkārassa.

Indeed, Brahmin, for the reason that a person here takes life... and has wrong view, due to that, with the breaking up of the body, after death, that person is reborn into the companionship of dogs. And for the reason that that person is a giver to an ascetic or a brahmin of food, drink, clothing, vehicles, garlands, scents, and unguents, bedding, lodging, and lamps, due to that, there, that person is a recipient of food, drink, garlands, and various ornaments.

“Idha pana, brāhmaṇa, ekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhiko hoti. So dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṃ pānaṃ vatthaṃ yānaṃ mālāgandhavilepanaṃ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā manussānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. So tattha lābhī hoti mānusakānaṃ pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ.

Brahmin, here in this world, a certain person is one who abstains from taking life... is one who has right view. That person is a giver to an ascetic or a brahmin of food, drink, clothing, vehicles, garlands, scents, and unguents, bedding, lodging, and lamps. With the breaking up of the body, after death, that person is reborn into the companionship of humans. There, that person is a recipient of the five human strands of sensual pleasure.

“Yaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, idha pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhiko, tena so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā manussānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Yañca kho so dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṃ pānaṃ vatthaṃ yānaṃ mālāgandhavilepanaṃ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ, tena so tattha lābhī hoti mānusakānaṃ pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ.

Indeed, Brahmin, for the reason that a person here abstains from taking life... and has right view, due to that, with the breaking up of the body, after death, that person is reborn into the companionship of humans. And for the reason that that person is a giver to an ascetic or a brahmin of food, drink, clothing, vehicles, garlands, scents, and unguents, bedding, lodging, and lamps, due to that, there, that person is a recipient of the five human strands of sensual pleasure.

“Idha pana, brāhmaṇa[T 5.0295], ekacco pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhiko hoti. So dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṃ pānaṃ vatthaṃ yānaṃ mālāgandhavilepanaṃ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ. So kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. So tattha lābhī [P 5.0273] hoti dibbānaṃ pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ.

Brahmin, here in this world, a certain person is one who abstains from taking life... is one who has right view. That person is a giver to an ascetic or a brahmin of food, drink, clothing, vehicles, garlands, scents, and unguents, bedding, lodging, and lamps. With the breaking up of the body, after death, that person is reborn into the companionship of devas. There, that person is a recipient of the five divine strands of sensual pleasure.

“Yaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, idha pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhiko, tena so kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā devānaṃ sahabyataṃ upapajjati. Yañca kho so dātā hoti samaṇassa vā brāhmaṇassa vā annaṃ pānaṃ vatthaṃ yānaṃ mālāgandhavilepanaṃ seyyāvasathapadīpeyyaṃ, tena [V 3.0241] so tattha lābhī hoti dibbānaṃ pañcannaṃ kāmaguṇānaṃ. Api ca, brāhmaṇa, dāyakopi anipphalo”ti.

Indeed, Brahmin, for the reason that a person here abstains from taking life... and has right view, due to that, with the breaking up of the body, after death, that person is reborn into the companionship of devas. And for the reason that that person is a giver to an ascetic or a brahmin of food, drink, clothing, vehicles, garlands, scents, and unguents, bedding, lodging, and lamps, due to that, there, that person is a recipient of the five divine strands of sensual pleasure. Moreover, Brahmin, a giver is not without result.

“Acchariyaṃ, bho gotama, abbhutaṃ, bho gotama! Yāvañcidaṃ, bho gotama, alameva dānāni dātuṃ, alaṃ saddhāni kātuṃ, yatra hi nāma dāyakopi [M 3.0482] anipphalo”ti. “Evametaṃ, brāhmaṇa evametaṃ brāhmaṇa evametaṃ brāhmaṇa (sī. syā.), dāyakopi hi, brāhmaṇa, anipphalo”ti.

“Wonderful, Venerable Gotama! Amazing, Venerable Gotama! How truly fitting it is, Venerable Gotama, to give gifts, how fitting to perform acts of faith, since indeed a giver is not without result.” “So it is, Brahmin. A giver, Brahmin, is indeed not without result.”

“Abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Ekādasamaṃ.

“Excellent, Venerable Gotama! Excellent, Venerable Gotama! … May Venerable Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge from this day forward for as long as life lasts.” The Eleventh Sutta.

Jāṇussoṇivaggo yamakavaggo (ka.) dutiyo.

The Second Chapter on Jāṇussoṇi is finished.

(18) 3. Sādhuvaggo

(18) 3. The Chapter on the Good

1. Sādhusuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Good

178. a. ni. 10.134 “Sādhuñca [V 3.0242] vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi asādhuñca. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ [T 5.0296] manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti [P 5.0274] kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

178. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the good and the not-good. Listen to it, attend closely; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus responded to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, asādhu? Pāṇātipāto, adinnādānaṃ, kāmesumicchācāro, musāvādo, pisuṇā vācā, pharusā vācā, samphappalāpo, abhijjhā, byāpādo, micchādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, asādhu.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the not-good? Destroying life, taking what is not given, sexual misconduct, false speech, divisive speech, harsh speech, idle chatter, covetousness, ill will, and wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the not-good.

“Katamañca, bhikkhave, sādhu? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī, adinnādānā veramaṇī, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇī, musāvādā veramaṇī, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇī, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇī, samphappalāpā veramaṇī, anabhijjhā, abyāpādo, sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sādhū”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the good? Abstinence from destroying life, abstinence from taking what is not given, abstinence from sexual misconduct, abstinence from false speech, abstinence from divisive speech, abstinence from harsh speech, abstinence from idle chatter, non-covetousness, non-ill will, and right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the good.” The First.

2. Ariyadhammasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Noble Dhamma

179. “Ariyadhammañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi anariyadhammañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, anariyo dhammo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, anariyo dhammo.

179. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the noble Dhamma and the ignoble Dhamma. Listen to it… And what, bhikkhus, is the ignoble Dhamma? Destroying life… wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the ignoble Dhamma.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, ariyo dhammo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyo dhammo”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the noble Dhamma? Abstinence from destroying life… right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the noble Dhamma.” The Second.

3. Kusalasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the Wholesome

180. “Kusalañca [V 3.0243][M 3.0483] vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi akusalañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamañca, bhikkhave, akusalaṃ? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, akusalaṃ.

180. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the wholesome and the unwholesome. Listen to it… And what, bhikkhus, is the unwholesome? Destroying life… wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the unwholesome.

“Katamañca[T 5.0297][P 5.0275], bhikkhave, kusalaṃ? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – idaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, kusala”nti. Tatiyaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the wholesome? Abstinence from destroying life… right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the wholesome.” The Third.

4. Atthasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Beneficial

181. “Atthañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi anatthañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, anattho? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, anattho.

181. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the beneficial and the unbeneficial. Listen to it… And what, bhikkhus, is the unbeneficial? Destroying life… wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the unbeneficial.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, attho? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, attho”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the beneficial? Abstinence from destroying life… right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the beneficial.” The Fourth.

5. Dhammasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on Dhamma

182. “Dhammañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi adhammañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, adhammo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, adhammo.

182. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma and the not-Dhamma. Listen to it… And what, bhikkhus, is the not-Dhamma? Destroying life… wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the not-Dhamma.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, dhammo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dhammo”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma? Abstinence from destroying life… right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the Dhamma.” The Fifth.

6. Āsavasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Taints

183. “Sāsavañca [V 3.0244] vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi anāsavañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, sāsavo dhammo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sāsavo dhammo.

183. “Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the dhamma with taints and the dhamma without taints. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the dhamma with taints? The destruction of life… wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the dhamma with taints.”

“Katamo [P 5.0276] ca, bhikkhave, anāsavo dhammo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, anāsavo [T 5.0298] dhammo”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the dhamma without taints? Abstinence from the destruction of life… right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the dhamma without taints.” The Sixth.

7. Vajjasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on What is Blameworthy

184. “Sāvajjañca [M 3.0484] vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi anavajjañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, sāvajjo dhammo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sāvajjo dhammo.

184. “Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the blameworthy dhamma and the blameless dhamma. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the blameworthy dhamma? The destruction of life… wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the blameworthy dhamma.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, anavajjo dhammo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, anavajjo dhammo”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the blameless dhamma? Abstinence from the destruction of life… right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the blameless dhamma.” The Seventh.

8. Tapanīyasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on What is Tormenting

185. “Tapanīyañca vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi atapanīyañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, tapanīyo dhammo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, tapanīyo dhammo.

185. “Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the tormenting dhamma and the non-tormenting dhamma. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the tormenting dhamma? The destruction of life… wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the tormenting dhamma.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, atapanīyo dhammo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, atapanīyo dhammo”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the non-tormenting dhamma? Abstinence from the destruction of life… right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the non-tormenting dhamma.” The Eighth.

9. Ācayagāmisuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on What Leads to Accumulation

186. “Ācayagāmiñca [V 3.0245] vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi apacayagāmiñca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, ācayagāmī dhammo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ācayagāmī dhammo.

186. “Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the dhamma that leads to accumulation and the dhamma that leads to diminution. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the dhamma that leads to accumulation? The destruction of life… wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the dhamma that leads to accumulation.”

“Katamo [P 5.0277] ca, bhikkhave, apacayagāmī dhammo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, apacayagāmī dhammo”ti. Navamaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the dhamma that leads to diminution? Abstinence from the destruction of life… right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the dhamma that leads to diminution.” The Ninth.

10. Dukkhudrayasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on What Results in Suffering

187. “Dukkhudrayañca [T 5.0299] vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi sukhudrayañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, dukkhudrayo dhammo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhudrayo dhammo.

187. “Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the dhamma that results in suffering and the dhamma that results in happiness. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the dhamma that results in suffering? The destruction of life… wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the dhamma that results in suffering.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sukhudrayo dhammo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sukhudrayo dhammo”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the dhamma that results in happiness? Abstinence from the destruction of life… right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the dhamma that results in happiness.” The Tenth.

11. Vipākasuttaṃ

11. The Discourse on Results

188. “Dukkhavipākañca [M 3.0485] vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi sukhavipākañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, dukkhavipāko dhammo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, dukkhavipāko dhammo.

188. “Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the dhamma that has painful results and the dhamma that has pleasant results. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the dhamma that has painful results? The destruction of life… wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the dhamma that has painful results.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sukhavipāko dhammo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sukhavipāko dhammo”ti. Ekādasamaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the dhamma that has pleasant results? Abstinence from the destruction of life… right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the dhamma that has pleasant results.” The Eleventh.

Sādhuvaggo tatiyo.

The Third Chapter on the Good.

(19) 4. Ariyamaggavaggo

(19) 4. The Chapter on the Noble Path

1. Ariyamaggasuttaṃ

1. The Discourse on the Noble Path

189. “Ariyamaggañca [V 3.0246][P 5.0278] vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi anariyamaggañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, anariyo maggo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, anariyo maggo.

189. “Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the noble path and the ignoble path. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the ignoble path? The destruction of life… wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the ignoble path.”

“Katamo ca[T 5.0300], bhikkhave, ariyo maggo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, ariyo maggo”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the noble path? Abstinence from the destruction of life… right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the noble path.” The First.

2. Kaṇhamaggasuttaṃ

2. The Discourse on the Dark Path

190. “Kaṇhamaggañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi sukkamaggañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, kaṇho maggo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, kaṇho maggo.

190. “Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the dark path and the bright path. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the dark path? The destruction of life… wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the dark path.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sukko maggo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sukko maggo”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the bright path? Abstinence from the destruction of life… right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the bright path.” The Second.

3. Saddhammasuttaṃ

3. The Discourse on the True Dhamma

191. “Saddhammañca vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi asaddhammañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, asaddhammo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, asaddhammo.

191. “Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the true dhamma and the false dhamma. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the false dhamma? The destruction of life… wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the false dhamma.”

“Katamo [M 3.0486][V 3.0247] ca, bhikkhave, saddhammo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, saddhammo”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the true dhamma? Abstinence from the destruction of life… right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the true dhamma.” The Third.

4. Sappurisadhammasuttaṃ

4. The Discourse on the Dhamma of a Good Person

192. “Sappurisadhammañca [P 5.0279] vo, bhikkhave, desessāmi asappurisadhammañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, asappurisadhammo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, asappurisadhammo.

192. “Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the dhamma of a good person and the dhamma of an unworthy person. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the dhamma of an unworthy person? The destruction of life… wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the dhamma of an unworthy person.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, sappurisadhammo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sappurisadhammo”ti. Catutthaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the dhamma of a good person? Abstinence from the destruction of life… right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the dhamma of a good person.” The Fourth.

5. Uppādetabbadhammasuttaṃ

5. The Discourse on the Dhamma to Be Aroused

193. “Uppādetabbañca vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi na uppādetabbañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, na uppādetabbo [T 5.0301] dhammo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, na uppādetabbo dhammo.

193. “Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the dhamma to be aroused and the dhamma not to be aroused. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the dhamma not to be aroused? The destruction of life… wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the dhamma not to be aroused.”

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, uppādetabbo dhammo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, uppādetabbo dhammo”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the dhamma to be aroused? Abstinence from the destruction of life… right view—this, bhikkhus, is called the dhamma to be aroused.” The Fifth.

6. Āsevitabbadhammasuttaṃ

6. The Discourse on the Dhamma to Be Cultivated

194. “Āsevitabbañca vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi nāsevitabbañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, nāsevitabbo dhammo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, nāsevitabbo dhammo.

194. “Bhikkhus, I shall teach you the dhamma to be cultivated and the dhamma not to be cultivated. Listen to that… And what, bhikkhus, is the dhamma not to be cultivated? The destruction of life… wrong view—this, bhikkhus, is called the dhamma not to be cultivated.”

“Katamo [V 3.0248] ca, bhikkhave, āsevitabbo dhammo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, āsevitabbo dhammo”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the dhamma to be practiced? Abstaining from taking life… right view—this, monks, is called the dhamma to be practiced.” The Sixth.

7. Bhāvetabbadhammasuttaṃ

7. The Discourse on the Dhamma to Be Developed

195. “Bhāvetabbañca [P 5.0280] vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi na bhāvetabbañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, na bhāvetabbo dhammo? Pāṇātipāto [M 3.0487] …pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, na bhāvetabbo dhammo.

195. “Monks, I will teach you the dhamma to be developed and the dhamma not to be developed. Listen to that… And what, monks, is the dhamma not to be developed? Taking life… wrong view—this, monks, is called the dhamma not to be developed.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, bhāvetabbo dhammo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bhāvetabbo dhammo”ti. Sattamaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the dhamma to be developed? Abstaining from taking life… right view—this, monks, is called the dhamma to be developed.” The Seventh.

8. Bahulīkātabbasuttaṃ

8. The Discourse on What Is to Be Frequently Practiced

196. “Bahulīkātabbañca vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi na bahulīkātabbañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, na bahulīkātabbo dhammo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, na bahulīkātabbo dhammo.

196. “Monks, I will teach you the dhamma to be frequently practiced and the dhamma not to be frequently practiced. Listen to that… And what, monks, is the dhamma not to be frequently practiced? Taking life… wrong view—this, monks, is called the dhamma not to be frequently practiced.

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, bahulīkātabbo dhammo? Pāṇātipātā [T 5.0302] veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, bahulīkātabbo dhammo”ti. Aṭṭhamaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the dhamma to be frequently practiced? Abstaining from taking life… right view—this, monks, is called the dhamma to be frequently practiced.” The Eighth.

9. Anussaritabbasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on What Is to Be Recollected

197. “Anussaritabbañca vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi nānussaritabbañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, nānussaritabbo dhammo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, nānussaritabbo dhammo.

197. “Monks, I will teach you the dhamma that is to be recollected and the dhamma that is not to be recollected. Listen to that... And what, monks, is the dhamma that is not to be recollected? Taking life... wrong view. This, monks, is called the dhamma that is not to be recollected.”

“Katamo [V 3.0249] ca, bhikkhave, anussaritabbo dhammo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, anussaritabbo dhammo”ti. Navamaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the dhamma that is to be recollected? Abstaining from taking life... right view. This, monks, is called the dhamma that is to be recollected.” The ninth.

10. Sacchikātabbasuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on What Is to Be Realized

198. “Sacchikātabbañca [P 5.0281] vo, bhikkhave, dhammaṃ desessāmi na sacchikātabbañca. Taṃ suṇātha…pe… katamo ca, bhikkhave, na sacchikātabbo dhammo? Pāṇātipāto…pe… micchādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, na sacchikātabbo dhammo.

198. “Monks, I will teach you the dhamma that is to be realized and the dhamma that is not to be realized. Listen to that... And what, monks, is the dhamma that is not to be realized? Taking life... wrong view. This, monks, is called the dhamma that is not to be realized.”

“Katamo [M 3.0488] ca, bhikkhave, sacchikātabbo dhammo? Pāṇātipātā veramaṇī…pe… sammādiṭṭhi – ayaṃ vuccati, bhikkhave, sacchikātabbo dhammo”ti. Dasamaṃ.

“And what, monks, is the dhamma that is to be realized? Abstaining from taking life... right view. This, monks, is called the dhamma that is to be realized.” The tenth.

Ariyamaggavaggo catuttho.

The Noble Path Chapter, the Fourth.

(20) 5. Aparapuggalavaggo

(20) 5. The Chapter on Other Persons

Nasevitabbādisuttāni

The Discourses Beginning with 'Not to be Associated With'

199. “Dasahi[V 3.0250], bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato puggalo na sevitabbo. Katamehi dasahi? Pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, pisuṇavāco hoti, pharusavāco [T 5.0303] hoti, samphappalāpī hoti, abhijjhālu hoti, byāpannacitto hoti, micchādiṭṭhiko hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato puggalo na sevitabbo.

199. “Monks, a person endowed with ten qualities is not to be associated with. What ten? He is a destroyer of life, one who takes what is not given, one who engages in sexual misconduct, a speaker of falsehoods, a divisive speaker, a harsh speaker, a frivolous talker, is covetous, has a mind of ill will, and is one of wrong view. Monks, a person endowed with these ten qualities is not to be associated with.”

“Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato puggalo sevitabbo. Katamehi dasahi? Pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato [P 5.0282] hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, anabhijjhālu hoti, abyāpannacitto hoti, sammādiṭṭhiko hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato puggalo sevitabbo”.

“Monks, a person endowed with ten qualities is to be associated with. What ten? He is one who abstains from taking life, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from sexual misconduct, abstains from false speech, abstains from divisive speech, abstains from harsh speech, abstains from frivolous talk, is uncovetous, has a mind free from ill will, and is one of right view. Monks, a person endowed with these ten qualities is to be associated with.”

200-209. “Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato puggalo na bhajitabbo…pe… bhajitabbo… na payirupāsitabbo… payirupāsitabbo… na pujjo hoti… pujjo hoti… na pāsaṃso hoti… pāsaṃso hoti… agāravo hoti… gāravo hoti… appatisso hoti… sappatisso hoti… na ārādhako hoti… ārādhako hoti… na visujjhati… visujjhati… mānaṃ nādhibhoti nābhibhoti (sī.) a. ni. 10.156-166 … mānaṃ adhibhoti… paññāya na vaḍḍhati… paññāya vaḍḍhati…pe….

200-209. “Monks, a person endowed with ten qualities is not to be resorted to... is to be resorted to... is not to be waited upon... is to be waited upon... is not worthy of veneration... is worthy of veneration... is not praiseworthy... is praiseworthy... is without reverence... is with reverence... is not deferential... is deferential... does not accomplish... accomplishes... is not purified... is purified... does not receive honor... receives honor... does not grow in wisdom... grows in wisdom...”

210. “Dasahi[M 3.0489], bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato puggalo bahuṃ apuññaṃ pasavati… bahuṃ puññaṃ pasavati. Katamehi dasahi? Pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti[V 3.0251], kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, anabhijjhālu hoti[T 5.0304], abyāpannacitto hoti, sammādiṭṭhiko hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato puggalo bahuṃ puññaṃ pasavatī”ti.

210. “Monks, a person endowed with ten qualities generates much demerit... generates much merit. With which ten does a person endowed with qualities generate much merit? He is one who abstains from taking life, abstains from taking what is not given, abstains from sexual misconduct, abstains from false speech, abstains from divisive speech, abstains from harsh speech, abstains from frivolous talk, is uncovetous, has a mind free from ill will, and is one of right view. Monks, a person endowed with these ten qualities generates much merit.”

Aparapuggalavaggo pañcamo.

The Chapter on Other Persons, the Fifth.

Catutthapaṇṇāsakaṃ samattaṃ.

The Fourth Fifty is concluded.

(21) 1. Karajakāyavaggo

(21) 1. The Chapter on the Body Originating from Action

1. Paṭhamanirayasaggasuttaṃ

1. The First Discourse on Hell and Heaven

211. “Dasahi[T 5.0305][M 3.0490][V 3.0252][P 5.0283], bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye. Katamehi dasahi? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti luddo lohitapāṇi hatapahate niviṭṭho adayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtesu natthettha pāṭhabhedo.

211. “Monks, one endowed with ten qualities is deposited in hell as if brought there. What ten? Here, monks, someone is a killer of living beings, cruel, bloody-handed, intent on striking and killing, without mercy for all living beings.

“Adinnādāyī hoti. Yaṃ taṃ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṃ gāmagataṃ vā araññagataṃ vā, taṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādātā hoti.

“He is one who takes what is not given. He takes, with thieving intent, whatever property or belongings of others, whether in a village or in the wilderness, that which is not given.

“Kāmesu micchācārī hoti. Yā tā māturakkhitā piturakkhitā mātāpiturakkhitā bhāturakkhitā bhaginirakkhitā ñātirakkhitā gottarakkhitā dhammarakkhitā sasāmikā saparidaṇḍā antamaso mālāguḷaparikkhittāpi, tathārūpāsu cārittaṃ āpajjitā hoti.

“He is one who engages in sexual misconduct. He engages in such conduct with women who are protected by their mother, protected by their father, protected by both mother and father, protected by their brother, protected by their sister, protected by relatives, protected by their clan, protected by the Dhamma, who have a husband, whose violation entails punishment, and even those betrothed with a garland.

“Musāvādī hoti. Sabhaggato vā parisaggato vā ñātimajjhagato vā pūgamajjhagato vā rājakulamajjhagato vā abhinīto sakkhipuṭṭho – ‘ehambho purisa, yaṃ jānāsi taṃ vadehī’ti, so ajānaṃ vā āha ‘jānāmī’ti, jānaṃ vā āha ‘na jānāmī’ti, apassaṃ vā āha ‘passāmī’ti, passaṃ vā āha ‘na passāmī’ti. Iti attahetu vā parahetu vā āmisakiñcikkhahetu vā sampajānamusā bhāsitā hoti.

“He is a speaker of falsehoods. When in an assembly, a gathering, among relatives, in a guild, or in the royal court, being brought forward as a witness and questioned, ‘Come, good man, say what you know,’ not knowing, he says, ‘I know,’ or knowing, he says, ‘I do not know.’ Not seeing, he says, ‘I see,’ or seeing, he says, ‘I do not see.’ Thus, for his own sake, for another's sake, or for some trifling material gain, he knowingly speaks a falsehood.

“Pisuṇavāco hoti – ito sutvā amutra akkhātā imesaṃ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā imesaṃ akkhātā amūsaṃ bhedāya. Iti samaggānaṃ vā bhettā bhinnānaṃ vā anuppadātā vaggārāmo [T 5.0306] vaggarato vagganandī, vaggakaraṇiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti.

“He is a divisive speaker. What he hears here, he repeats elsewhere to cause division among these people; or what he hears elsewhere, he repeats here to cause division among those people. Thus, he is one who breaks up those who are united or reinforces those who are divided, delighting in discord, rejoicing in discord, enjoying discord, speaking words that create discord.

“Pharusavāco [V 3.0253] hoti – yā sā vācā aṇḍakā kakkasā parakaṭukā parābhisajjanī kodhasāmantā asamādhisaṃvattanikā, tathārūpiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti.

“He is a harsh speaker. The words he utters are rough, hard, offensive to others, abusive, connected with anger, and unconducive to concentration. He speaks such words.

“Samphappalāpī [M 3.0491] hoti akālavādī abhūtavādī anatthavādī adhammavādī avinayavādī, anidhānavatiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti akālena anapadesaṃ apariyantavatiṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ.

“He is a frivolous talker, a speaker at the wrong time, a speaker of what is not true, a speaker of what is unbeneficial, a speaker of what is not the Dhamma, a speaker of what is not the Vinaya. He speaks words that are not worth treasuring, untimely, without reason, unbounded, and unconnected with benefit.

“Abhijjhālu [P 5.0284] hoti. Yaṃ taṃ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṃ taṃ abhijjhātā hoti – ‘aho vata yaṃ parassa taṃ mama assā’ti.

“He is covetous. He covets others' property and belongings, thinking: ‘Oh, would that what belongs to others were mine!’

“Byāpannacitto hoti paduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo – ‘ime sattā haññantu vā bajjhantu vā ucchijjantu vā vinassantu vā mā vā ahesu’nti.

“He has a mind of ill will, with corrupt intentions, thinking: ‘May these beings be slain, or bound, or annihilated, or perish, or not exist at all!’

“Micchādiṭṭhiko hoti viparītadassano – ‘natthi dinnaṃ, natthi yiṭṭhaṃ, natthi hutaṃ, natthi sukatadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, natthi ayaṃ loko, natthi paro loko, natthi mātā, natthi pitā, natthi sattā opapātikā, natthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye.

“He is one of wrong view, with distorted vision, holding: ‘There is no result in what is given, offered, or sacrificed. There is no fruit or result of good and bad actions. There is no this world, no other world. There is no mother, no father. There are no spontaneously arisen beings. There are no ascetics and brahmins in the world who have gone the right way and practiced rightly, who proclaim this world and the other world, having realized them for themselves by direct knowledge.’ Monks, one endowed with these ten qualities is deposited in hell as if brought there.

“Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge. Katamehi dasahi? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho lajjī dayāpanno, sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati.

“Monks, one endowed with ten qualities is deposited in heaven as if brought there. What ten? Here, monks, someone, abandoning the destruction of life, abstains from the destruction of life. Having laid aside rod and weapon, he is conscientious, full of kindness, and dwells compassionate for the welfare of all living beings.

“Adinnādānaṃ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti. Yaṃ taṃ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṃ gāmagataṃ vā araññagataṃ vā, na [T 5.0307] taṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādātā hoti.

“Abandoning the taking of what is not given, he abstains from taking what is not given. Whatever property or belongings of others, whether in a village or in the wilderness, he does not take that which is not given with thieving intent.

“Kāmesumicchācāraṃ pahāya kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti. Yā tā māturakkhitā…pe… antamaso mālāguḷaparikkhittāpi, tathārūpāsu na cārittaṃ āpajjitā hoti.

“Abandoning sexual misconduct, he abstains from sexual misconduct. He does not engage in such conduct with women who are protected by their mother... or even those betrothed with a garland.

“Musāvādaṃ [V 3.0254] pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti. Sabhaggato vā parisaggato vā ñātimajjhagato vā pūgamajjhagato vā rājakulamajjhagato vā abhinīto sakkhipuṭṭho – ‘ehambho purisa, yaṃ jānāsi taṃ vadehī’ti, so ajānaṃ vā āha ‘na jānāmī’ti, jānaṃ vā āha ‘jānāmī’ti, apassaṃ vā āha ‘na passāmī’ti, passaṃ vā āha ‘passāmī’ti. Iti attahetu vā parahetu vā āmisakiñcikkhahetu vā na sampajānamusā [P 5.0285] bhāsitā hoti.

“Abandoning false speech, he abstains from false speech. When in an assembly, a gathering, among relatives, in a guild, or in the royal court, being brought forward as a witness and questioned, ‘Good sir, say what you know,’ if he does not know, he says, ‘I do not know.’ If he does know, he says, ‘I know.’ If he has not seen, he says, ‘I do not see.’ If he has seen, he says, ‘I see.’ Thus, for his own sake, for another’s sake, or for some trifling material gain, he does not knowingly speak a falsehood.

“Pisuṇavācaṃ [M 3.0492] pahāya pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti – na ito sutvā amutra akkhātā imesaṃ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā imesaṃ akkhātā amūsaṃ bhedāya. Iti bhinnānaṃ vā sandhātā sahitānaṃ vā anuppadātā samaggārāmo samaggarato samagganandī, samaggakaraṇiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti.

“Abandoning divisive speech, he abstains from divisive speech. He does not repeat here what he heard there to divide these people, nor does he repeat there what he heard here to divide those people. Thus he is a reconciler of those who are divided and a supporter of those who are united, delighting in harmony, rejoicing in harmony, finding joy in harmony, speaking words that create harmony.

“Pharusavācaṃ pahāya pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti. Yā sā vācā nelā kaṇṇasukhā pemanīyā hadayaṅgamā porī bahujanakantā bahujanamanāpā, tathārūpiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti.

“Abandoning harsh speech, he abstains from harsh speech. He speaks words that are faultless, pleasing to the ear, affectionate, going to the heart, polite, liked by many, and agreeable to many.

“Samphappalāpaṃ pahāya samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti kālavādī bhūtavādī, atthavādī dhammavādī vinayavādī, nidhānavatiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti kālena sāpadesaṃ pariyantavatiṃ atthasaṃhitaṃ.

“Abandoning idle chatter, he abstains from idle chatter. He speaks at the right time, speaks what is true, speaks what is beneficial, speaks in accordance with the Dhamma, and speaks in accordance with the Vinaya. He speaks words that are worth treasuring, timely, reasoned, well-defined, and connected with benefit.

“Anabhijjhālu hoti[T 5.0308]. Yaṃ taṃ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṃ taṃ anabhijjhātā hoti – ‘aho vata yaṃ parassa taṃ mama assā’ti.

“He is uncovetous. He is not one to covet the property and belongings of others, thinking: ‘Oh, would that what belongs to others were mine!’

“Abyāpannacitto hoti appaduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo – ‘ime sattā averā hontu abyāpajjā anīghā, sukhī attānaṃ pariharantū’ti.

“He has a mind free from ill will, with uncorrupted intentions, thinking: ‘May these beings be free from animosity, free from affliction, free from trouble, and may they maintain themselves in happiness!’”

“Sammādiṭṭhiko hoti aviparītadassano – ‘atthi dinnaṃ, atthi yiṭṭhaṃ, atthi hutaṃ, atthi sukaṭadukkaṭānaṃ kammānaṃ phalaṃ vipāko, atthi ayaṃ loko, atthi paro loko, atthi mātā, atthi pitā, atthi sattā opapātikā, atthi loke samaṇabrāhmaṇā sammaggatā sammāpaṭipannā [V 3.0255] ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge”ti. Paṭhamaṃ.

“He has right view, an undistorted vision: ‘There is the result of what is given, there is the result of great sacrifices, there is the result of small sacrifices; there is fruit and result of good and bad actions; there is this world, there is the next world; there is the result of serving one's mother, there is the result of serving one's father; there are beings who are spontaneously reborn; there are in the world ascetics and brahmins who have fared rightly, who practice rightly, and who, having known for themselves with higher knowledge and having realized this world and the next world, make it known.’ Monks, one endowed with these ten qualities is placed in heaven just as if brought and set down.” First.

2. Dutiyanirayasaggasuttaṃ

2. The Second Sutta on Hell and Heaven

212. “Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye. Katamehi dasahi? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti luddo lohitapāṇi hatapahate niviṭṭho adayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtesu.

212. “Bhikkhus, one endowed with ten qualities is placed in hell just as if brought and set down. With what ten? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person is a destroyer of life, is cruel, has blood-stained hands, is given to striking and killing, and is without compassion for all living beings.

“Adinnādāyī hoti… kāmesumicchācārī hoti… musāvādī hoti… pisuṇavāco hoti… pharusavāco hoti [P 5.0286] … samphappalāpī hoti… abhijjhālu [M 3.0493] hoti… byāpannacitto hoti… micchādiṭṭhiko hoti viparītadassano – ‘natthi dinnaṃ…pe… sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye.

“He is one who takes what is not given... he is one who engages in sexual misconduct... he is one who speaks falsehood... he has divisive speech... he has harsh speech... he is one who speaks frivolous talk... he is covetous... he has a mind of ill will... he has wrong view, a distorted vision: ‘There is nothing given, no offering, no sacrifice; there is no fruit or result of good and bad actions; there is no this world, no next world; there is no mother, no father; there are no beings who are spontaneously reborn; there are no ascetics or brahmins in the world who have fared rightly, who practice rightly, and who, having known for themselves with higher knowledge and having realized this world and the next world, make it known.’ These, bhikkhus, are the ten qualities with which one endowed is placed in hell just as if brought and set down.

“Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge. Katamehi dasahi? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho lajjī dayāpanno, sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati.

“Bhikkhus, one endowed with ten qualities is placed in heaven just as if brought and set down. With what ten? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person, having abandoned the destruction of life, abstains from the destruction of life. He has laid down the rod, laid down the weapon; he is scrupulous, compassionate, and dwells sympathetic to the welfare of all living beings.

“Adinnādānaṃ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti… kāmesumicchācāraṃ pahāya kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti… musāvādaṃ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti… pisuṇaṃ vācaṃ pahāya pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti… pharusaṃ vācaṃ pahāya pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti… samphappalāpaṃ pahāya samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti… anabhijjhālu hoti… abyāpannacitto hoti… sammādiṭṭhiko hoti aviparītadassano – ‘atthi dinnaṃ…pe… ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge”ti. Dutiyaṃ.

“Having abandoned taking what is not given, he abstains from taking what is not given... having abandoned sexual misconduct, he abstains from sexual misconduct... having abandoned false speech, he abstains from false speech... having abandoned divisive speech, he abstains from divisive speech... having abandoned harsh speech, he abstains from harsh speech... having abandoned frivolous talk, he abstains from frivolous talk... He is not covetous... he does not have a mind of ill will... he has right view, an undistorted vision: ‘There is what is given, there is offering, there is sacrifice; there is fruit and result of good and bad actions; there is this world, there is the next world; there is mother, there is father; there are beings who are spontaneously reborn; there are in the world ascetics and brahmins who have fared rightly, who practice rightly, and who, having known for themselves with higher knowledge and having realized this world and the next world, make it known.’ These, bhikkhus, are the ten qualities with which one endowed is placed in heaven just as if brought and set down.” Second.

3. Mātugāmasuttaṃ

3. 3. The Discourse on Women

213. “Dasahi[V 3.0256], bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye. Katamehi dasahi? Pāṇātipātī [P 5.0287] hoti…pe… adinnādāyī hoti… kāmesumicchācārī hoti… musāvādī hoti… pisuṇavāco hoti… pharusavāco hoti… samphappalāpī hoti… abhijjhālu hoti… byāpannacitto hoti… micchādiṭṭhiko hoti…. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye.

213. “Bhikkhus, a woman endowed with ten qualities is deposited in hell as if brought there. What ten? She is one who kills living beings… takes what is not given… engages in sexual misconduct… speaks falsely… has divisive speech… has harsh speech… speaks frivolous talk… is covetous… has a mind of ill will… has wrong view. Bhikkhus, a woman endowed with these ten qualities is deposited in hell as if brought there.”

“Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge. Katamehi dasahi? Pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti…pe… adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti… kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti… musāvādā paṭivirato hoti… pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato [M 3.0494] hoti… pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti… samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti… anabhijjhālu hoti… abyāpannacitto hoti… sammādiṭṭhiko hoti… imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato mātugāmo yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge”ti. Tatiyaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, a woman endowed with ten qualities is deposited in heaven as if brought there. What ten? She abstains from killing living beings… abstains from taking what is not given… abstains from sexual misconduct… abstains from false speech… abstains from divisive speech… abstains from harsh speech… abstains from frivolous talk… is not covetous… has a mind free of ill will… has right view. Bhikkhus, a woman endowed with these ten qualities is deposited in heaven as if brought there.” Third.

4. Upāsikāsuttaṃ

4. 4. The Discourse on the Laywoman

214. “Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatā upāsikā yathābhataṃ nikkhittā evaṃ niraye. Katamehi dasahi? Pāṇātipātinī hoti…pe… micchādiṭṭhikā [T 5.0309] hoti…. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgatā upāsikā yathābhataṃ nikkhittā evaṃ niraye.

214. “Bhikkhus, a laywoman endowed with ten qualities is deposited in hell as if brought there. What ten? She is a killer of living beings… she holds wrong view… Bhikkhus, a laywoman endowed with these ten qualities is deposited in hell as if brought there.”

“Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatā upāsikā yathābhataṃ nikkhittā evaṃ sagge. Katamehi dasahi? Pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā hoti…pe… sammādiṭṭhikā hoti…. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgatā upāsikā yathābhataṃ nikkhittā evaṃ sagge”. Catutthaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, a laywoman endowed with ten qualities is deposited in heaven as if brought there. What ten? She abstains from killing living beings… she holds right view… Bhikkhus, a laywoman endowed with these ten qualities is deposited in heaven as if brought there.” Fourth.

5. Visāradasuttaṃ

5. 5. The Discourse on Confidence

215. “Dasahi[V 3.0257][P 5.0288], bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatā upāsikā avisāradā agāraṃ ajjhāvasati. Katamehi dasahi? Pāṇātipātinī hoti… adinnādāyinī hoti… kāmesumicchācārinī hoti… musāvādinī hoti… pisuṇāvācā hoti… pharusavācā hoti… samphappalāpinī hoti… abhijjhālunī hoti… byāpannacittā hoti… micchādiṭṭhikā hoti…. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgatā upāsikā avisāradā agāraṃ ajjhāvasati.

215. “Bhikkhus, a laywoman endowed with ten qualities dwells at home without confidence. What ten? She is a killer of living beings; she is one who takes what is not given; she is one who engages in sexual misconduct; she is a speaker of falsehood; she has divisive speech; she has harsh speech; she is a speaker of frivolous talk; she is covetous; she has a mind of ill will; she holds wrong view. Bhikkhus, a laywoman endowed with these ten qualities dwells at home without confidence.”

“Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgatā upāsikā visāradā agāraṃ ajjhāvasati. Katamehi dasahi? Pāṇātipātā paṭiviratā hoti… adinnādānā paṭiviratā hoti… kāmesumicchācārā paṭiviratā hoti… musāvādā paṭiviratā hoti… pisuṇāya vācāya paṭiviratā hoti… pharusāya vācāya paṭiviratā hoti… samphappalāpā paṭiviratā hoti… anabhijjhālunī hoti… abyāpannacittā hoti… sammādiṭṭhikā hoti…. Imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgatā upāsikā visāradā agāraṃ ajjhāvasatī”ti. Pañcamaṃ.

“Bhikkhus, a laywoman endowed with ten qualities dwells at home with confidence. What ten? She abstains from killing living beings; she abstains from taking what is not given; she abstains from sexual misconduct; she abstains from false speech; she abstains from divisive speech; she abstains from harsh speech; she abstains from frivolous talk; she is not covetous; she has a mind free of ill will; she holds right view. Bhikkhus, a laywoman endowed with these ten qualities dwells at home with confidence.” Fifth.

6. Saṃsappanīyasuttaṃ

6. 6. The Discourse on Moving On

216. “Saṃsappanīyapariyāyaṃ [M 3.0495] vo, bhikkhave, dhammapariyāyaṃ desessāmi. Taṃ suṇātha, sādhukaṃ manasi karotha; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bhante”ti kho te bhikkhū bhagavato paccassosuṃ. Bhagavā etadavoca –

216. “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the Dhamma exposition on moving on. Listen to it and attend carefully; I will speak.” “Yes, venerable sir,” those bhikkhus replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Katamo ca, bhikkhave, saṃsappanīyapariyāyo dhammapariyāyo? Kammassakā, bhikkhave, sattā kammadāyādā kammayonī kammabandhū kammapaṭisaraṇā, yaṃ kammaṃ karonti – kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakaṃ vā – tassa dāyādā bhavanti.

“And what, bhikkhus, is the Dhamma exposition on creeping? Bhikkhus, beings are owners of their kamma, heirs to their kamma, have kamma as their origin, have kamma as their kin, and have kamma as their refuge. Whatever kamma they do—whether good or bad—of that they will be the heirs.

“Idha[P 5.0289], bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātī [T 5.0310] hoti luddo lohitapāṇi hatapahate niviṭṭho, adayāpanno [V 3.0258] sabbapāṇabhūtesu. So saṃsappati kāyena, saṃsappati vācāya, saṃsappati manasā. Tassa jimhaṃ kāyakammaṃ hoti, jimhaṃ vacīkammaṃ, jimhaṃ manokammaṃ, jimhā gati, jimhupapatti.

“Here, bhikkhus, some person is a killer of living beings, brutal, bloody-handed, intent on striking and killing, without compassion for any living beings. He creeps with his body, he creeps with his speech, he creeps with his mind. His bodily kamma is crooked, his verbal kamma is crooked, his mental kamma is crooked; his destination is crooked, his rebirth is crooked.

“Jimhagatikassa kho panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, jimhupapattikassa dvinnaṃ gatīnaṃ aññataraṃ gatiṃ vadāmi – ye vā ekantadukkhā nirayā yā vā saṃsappajātikā tiracchānayoni. Katamā ca sā, bhikkhave, saṃsappajātikā tiracchānayoni? Ahi vicchikā satapadī nakulā biḷārā mūsikā ulūkā, ye vā panaññepi keci tiracchānayonikā sattā manusse disvā saṃsappanti. Iti kho, bhikkhave, bhūtā bhūtassa upapatti hoti. Yaṃ karoti tena upapajjati. Upapannamenaṃ phassā phusanti. Evamahaṃ, bhikkhave, ‘kammadāyādā sattā’ti vadāmi.

“For one with a crooked destination and a crooked rebirth, bhikkhus, I declare one of two destinations: either the hells, which are exclusively suffering, or the animal realm of a creeping nature. And what, bhikkhus, is the animal realm of a creeping nature? Snakes, scorpions, centipedes, mongooses, cats, rats, owls, or whatever other animals of the animal realm that creep when they see humans. Thus, bhikkhus, the rebirth of a being is from what has come to be. By what one does, by that one is reborn. Once reborn, contacts touch one. Thus, bhikkhus, I say: ‘Beings are heirs to their kamma.’”

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco adinnādāyī hoti…pe… kāmesumicchācārī hoti… musāvādī hoti… pisuṇavāco hoti… pharusavāco hoti… samphappalāpī hoti… abhijjhālu hoti… byāpannacitto hoti… micchādiṭṭhiko hoti viparītadassano – ‘natthi dinnaṃ…pe… sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. So saṃsappati kāyena, saṃsappati vācāya, saṃsappati manasā. Tassa jimhaṃ kāyakammaṃ [T 5.0311] hoti, jimhaṃ vacīkammaṃ, jimhaṃ manokammaṃ, jimhā gati, jimhupapatti[P 5.0290].

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, some person takes what is not given… engages in sexual misconduct… speaks falsehood… speaks divisive speech… speaks harsh speech… engages in idle chatter… is covetous… has a mind of ill will… holds wrong view, with perverted vision, thinking: ‘There is nothing given… there are no recluses and brahmins who, having directly known and realized for themselves this world and the other world, proclaim it.’ He creeps with his body, he creeps with his speech, he creeps with his mind. His bodily kamma is crooked, his verbal kamma is crooked, his mental kamma is crooked; his destination is crooked, his rebirth is crooked.
