“Jimhagatikassa kho panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, jimhupapattikassa dvinnaṃ gatīnaṃ aññataraṃ gatiṃ vadāmi – ye vā ekantadukkhā nirayā yā vā saṃsappajātikā tiracchānayoni. Katamā ca sā, bhikkhave, saṃsappajātikā tiracchānayoni[M 3.0496]? Ahi vicchikā satapadī nakulā biḷārā mūsikā ulūkā, ye vā panaññepi keci tiracchānayonikā sattā manusse disvā saṃsappanti. Iti kho, bhikkhave, bhūtā bhūtassa upapatti hoti, yaṃ karoti tena upapajjati. Upapannamenaṃ phassā phusanti. Evamahaṃ, bhikkhave, ‘kammadāyādā sattā’ti vadāmi. Kammassakā, bhikkhave, sattā kammadāyādā kammayonī kammabandhū kammapaṭisaraṇā, yaṃ kammaṃ karonti – kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakaṃ vā – tassa dāyādā bhavanti.

“For one with a crooked destination and a crooked rebirth, bhikkhus, I declare one of two destinations: either the hells, which are exclusively suffering, or the animal realm of a creeping nature. And what, bhikkhus, is the animal realm of a creeping nature? Snakes, scorpions, centipedes, mongooses, cats, rats, owls, or whatever other animals of the animal realm that creep when they see humans. Thus, bhikkhus, the rebirth of a being is from what has come to be. By what one does, by that one is reborn. Once reborn, contacts touch one. Thus, bhikkhus, I say: ‘Beings are heirs to their kamma.’ Bhikkhus, beings are owners of their kamma, heirs to their kamma, have kamma as their origin, have kamma as their kin, and have kamma as their refuge. Whatever kamma they do—whether good or bad—of that they will be the heirs.

“Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti nihitadaṇḍo [V 3.0259] nihitasattho, lajjī dayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati. So na saṃsappati kāyena, na saṃsappati vācāya, na saṃsappati manasā. Tassa uju kāyakammaṃ hoti, uju vacīkammaṃ, uju manokammaṃ, uju gati, ujupapatti.

“Here, bhikkhus, some person, having abandoned the killing of living beings, abstains from killing living beings. Having laid aside rod and weapon, being conscientious and full of compassion, he dwells sympathetic to the welfare of all living beings. He does not creep with his body, he does not creep with his speech, he does not creep with his mind. His bodily kamma is straight, his verbal kamma is straight, his mental kamma is straight; his destination is straight, his rebirth is straight.

“Ujugatikassa kho panāhaṃ, bhikkhave, ujupapattikassa dvinnaṃ gatīnaṃ aññataraṃ gatiṃ vadāmi – ye vā ekantasukhā saggā yāni vā pana tāni uccākulāni khattiyamahāsālakulāni vā brāhmaṇamahāsālakulāni vā gahapatimahāsālakulāni vā aḍḍhāni mahaddhanāni mahābhogāni pahūtajātarūparajatāni pahūtavittūpakaraṇāni pahūtadhanadhaññāni. Iti kho, bhikkhave, bhūtā bhūtassa [T 5.0312] upapatti hoti. Yaṃ karoti tena upapajjati. Upapannamenaṃ phassā phusanti. Evamahaṃ, bhikkhave, ‘kammadāyādā sattā’ti vadāmi.

“For one with a straight destination and a straight rebirth, bhikkhus, I declare one of two destinations: either the heavens, which are exclusively blissful, or those high families—great noble families, great brahmin families, or great householder families—that are affluent, with great wealth, with great possessions, abundant in gold and silver, abundant in property and equipment, and abundant in wealth and grain. Thus, bhikkhus, the rebirth of a being is from what has come to be. By what one does, by that one is reborn. Once reborn, contacts touch one. Thus, bhikkhus, I say: ‘Beings are heirs to their kamma.’”

“Idha pana, bhikkhave, ekacco adinnādānaṃ pahāya adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti…pe… kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti… musāvādaṃ [P 5.0291] pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti… pisuṇaṃ vācaṃ pahāya pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti… pharusaṃ vācaṃ pahāya pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti… samphappalāpaṃ pahāya samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti… anabhijjhālu hoti… abyāpannacitto hoti… sammādiṭṭhiko hoti aviparītadassano – ‘atthi dinnaṃ…pe… ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. So na saṃsappati kāyena, na saṃsappati vācāya, na saṃsappati manasā. Tassa uju kāyakammaṃ hoti, uju vacīkammaṃ, uju manokammaṃ, uju gati, ujupapatti.

“Furthermore, bhikkhus, some person, having abandoned taking what is not given, abstains from taking what is not given… abstains from sexual misconduct… having abandoned false speech, abstains from false speech… having abandoned divisive speech, abstains from divisive speech… having abandoned harsh speech, abstains from harsh speech… having abandoned idle chatter, abstains from idle chatter; he is not covetous, has a mind without ill will, and holds right view, with unperverted vision, thinking: ‘There is what is given… there are recluses and brahmins who, having directly known and realized for themselves this world and the other world, proclaim it.’ He does not creep with his body, he does not creep with his speech, he does not creep with his mind. His bodily kamma is straight, his verbal kamma is straight, his mental kamma is straight; his destination is straight, his rebirth is straight.

“Ujugatikassa [M 3.0497] kho pana ahaṃ, bhikkhave, ujupapattikassa dvinnaṃ gatīnaṃ aññataraṃ gatiṃ vadāmi – ye vā ekantasukhā saggā yāni vā pana tāni uccākulāni khattiyamahāsālakulāni vā brāhmaṇamahāsālakulāni vā gahapatimahāsālakulāni vā aḍḍhāni mahaddhanāni mahābhogāni pahūtajātarūparajatāni pahūtavittūpakaraṇāni pahūtadhanadhaññāni. Iti kho, bhikkhave, bhūtā bhūtassa [T 5.0313] upapatti hoti. Yaṃ karoti tena upapajjati. Upapannamenaṃ phassā phusanti. Evamahaṃ, bhikkhave, ‘kammadāyādā sattā’ti vadāmi.

“For one with a straight destination and a straight rebirth, bhikkhus, I declare one of two destinations: either the heavens, which are exclusively blissful, or those high families—great noble families, great brahmin families, or great householder families—that are affluent, with great wealth, with great possessions, abundant in gold and silver, abundant in property and equipment, and abundant in wealth and grain. Thus, bhikkhus, the rebirth of a being is from what has come to be. By what one does, by that one is reborn. Once reborn, contacts touch one. Thus, bhikkhus, I say: ‘Beings are heirs to their kamma.’”

“Kammassakā[V 3.0260], bhikkhave, sattā kammadāyādā kammayonī kammabandhū kammapaṭisaraṇā, yaṃ kammaṃ karonti – kalyāṇaṃ vā pāpakaṃ vā – tassa dāyādā bhavanti. Ayaṃ kho so, bhikkhave, saṃsappanīyapariyāyo dhammapariyāyo”ti. Chaṭṭhaṃ.

Monks, beings are owners of their kamma, heirs to their kamma, have kamma as their origin, have kamma as their kin, and have kamma as their refuge. Whatever kamma they do—whether good or bad—they will be the heirs of that. This, monks, is the Dhamma exposition on transmigration.” Sixth.

7. Paṭhamasañcetanikasuttaṃ

7. The First Discourse on Intention

217. “Nāhaṃ[P 5.0292], bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṃ kammānaṃ katānaṃ upacitānaṃ appaṭisaṃveditvā appaṭisaṃviditvā (sī. syā. pī.) byantībhāvaṃ vadāmi. Tañca kho diṭṭheva dhamme upapajje vā upapajjaṃ vā (ka.) a. ni. 6.63 passitabbaṃ, upapajja vā (ma. ni. 3.303) apare vā pariyāye. Na tvevāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṃ kammānaṃ katānaṃ upacitānaṃ appaṭisaṃveditvā dukkhassantakiriyaṃ vadāmi.

217. Monks, I do not declare the termination of intentional kammas that have been done and accumulated without their result having been experienced. And that result is to be experienced either in this very life, or in the next life, or in some subsequent life. Indeed, monks, I do not declare the making of an end to suffering without the result of intentional kammas that have been done and accumulated having been experienced.

“Tatra, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā akusalaṃ sañcetanikaṃ dukkhudrayaṃ dukkhavipākaṃ (ka.) hoti; catubbidhā vacīkammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti; tividhā manokammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti.

Therein, monks, the threefold faulty transgression of bodily kamma is unwholesome, intentional, has suffering as its outcome, and has suffering as its result. The fourfold faulty transgression of verbal kamma is unwholesome, intentional, has suffering as its outcome, and has suffering as its result. The threefold faulty transgression of mental kamma is unwholesome, intentional, has suffering as its outcome, and has suffering as its result.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātī hoti luddo lohitapāṇi hatapahate niviṭṭho adayāpanno sabbapāṇabhūtesu.

And how, monks, is the threefold faulty transgression of bodily kamma unwholesome, intentional, having suffering as its outcome, and having suffering as its result? Here, monks, a certain person destroys living beings; he is cruel, with blood-stained hands, given to killing and striking, without compassion for all living beings.

“Adinnādāyī [M 3.0498] hoti. Yaṃ taṃ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṃ gāmagataṃ vā araññagataṃ vā, taṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādātā hoti.

He is one who takes what is not given. Whatever property and resources of another, whether located in a village or in a forest, that not being given, he takes with thievish intent.

“Kāmesumicchācārī hoti. Yā tā māturakkhitā…pe… antamaso mālāguḷaparikkhittāpi[T 5.0314], tathārūpāsu cārittaṃ āpajjitā hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti.

He engages in wrong conduct in regard to sensual pleasures. He engages in transgression with such women as are protected by their mother... (and so on)... even down to those betrothed with a garland of flowers. In this way, monks, the threefold faulty transgression of bodily kamma is unwholesome, intentional, having suffering as its outcome, and having suffering as its result.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, catubbidhā vacīkammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā [V 3.0261] dukkhavipākā hoti? Idha[P 5.0293], bhikkhave, ekacco musāvādī hoti. Sabhaggato vā parisaggato vā ñātimajjhagato vā pūgamajjhagato vā rājakulamajjhagato vā abhinīto sakkhipuṭṭho ‘ehambho purisa, yaṃ jānāsi taṃ vadehī’ti, so ajānaṃ vā āha ‘jānāmī’ti, jānaṃ vā āha ‘na jānāmī’ti, apassaṃ vā āha ‘passāmī’ti, passaṃ vā āha ‘na passāmī’ti, iti attahetu vā parahetu vā āmisakiñcikkhahetu vā sampajānamusā bhāsitā hoti.

And how, monks, is the fourfold faulty transgression of verbal kamma unwholesome, intentional, having suffering as its outcome, and having suffering as its result? Here, monks, a certain person is a speaker of falsehood. When he has gone to an assembly, to a council, among his relatives, among a guild, or among the royal family, and is brought forth and questioned as a witness, ‘Come, good man, tell what you know,’ then, not knowing, he says, ‘I know,’ or knowing, he says, ‘I do not know’; not seeing, he says, ‘I see,’ or seeing, he says, ‘I do not see.’ Thus, for his own sake, for the sake of another, or for the sake of some trifling gain, he knowingly speaks a falsehood.

“Pisuṇavāco hoti. Ito sutvā amutra akkhātā imesaṃ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā imesaṃ akkhātā amūsaṃ bhedāya. Iti samaggānaṃ vā bhettā bhinnānaṃ vā anuppadātā vaggārāmo vaggarato vagganandī, vaggakaraṇiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti.

He is a speaker of divisive speech. What he has heard here, he tells elsewhere to cause a division among these people; what he has heard elsewhere, he tells to these people to cause a division among those people. Thus he is a divider of the united and one who encourages the divided. He delights in disunity, rejoices in disunity, finds pleasure in disunity, and is a speaker of words that create disunity.

“Pharusavāco hoti. Yā sā vācā aṇḍakā kakkasā parakaṭukā parābhisajjanī kodhasāmantā. Asamādhisaṃvattanikā, tathārūpiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti.

He is a speaker of harsh speech. He speaks such speech as is coarse, rough, bitter to others, abusive, close to anger, and not conducive to concentration.

“Samphappalāpī hoti akālavādī abhūtavādī anatthavādī adhammavādī avinayavādī, anidhānavatiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti akālena anapadesaṃ apariyantavatiṃ anatthasaṃhitaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, catubbidhā vacīkammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti.

He is a speaker of frivolous speech. He speaks at the wrong time, speaks what is not true, speaks what is not beneficial, speaks what is not the Dhamma, and speaks what is not the Vinaya. He speaks speech that is not worth treasuring, at the wrong time, without reason, without restraint, and unconnected with benefit. In this way, monks, the fourfold faulty transgression of verbal kamma is unwholesome, intentional, having suffering as its outcome, and having suffering as its result.

“Kathañca[T 5.0315], bhikkhave, tividhā manokammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco abhijjhālu hoti. Yaṃ taṃ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṃ, taṃ abhijjhātā hoti – ‘aho vata, yaṃ parassa taṃ mama assā’ti.

And how, monks, is the threefold faulty transgression of mental kamma unwholesome, intentional, having suffering as its outcome, and having suffering as its result? Here, monks, a certain person is covetous. He covets the property and resources of another, thinking: ‘Oh, that what belongs to another might be mine!’

“Byāpannacitto [M 3.0499] hoti paduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo – ‘ime sattā haññantu vā bajjhantu vā ucchijjantu vā vinassantu vā mā vā ahesu’nti.

He has a mind of ill will and a corrupt mental resolve: ‘May these beings be killed or bound or annihilated or perish, or may they not exist at all!’

Micchādiṭṭhiko hoti viparītadassano – ‘natthi dinnaṃ…pe. [P 5.0294]… ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ [V 3.0262] sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tividhā manokammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti.

He has wrong view, a distorted vision: ‘There is nothing given, nothing offered, nothing sacrificed. There is no fruit or result of good and bad kamma. There is no this world, no other world. There is no mother, no father. There are no beings who are spontaneously reborn. There are no ascetics and brahmins in the world who, having realized this world and the other world for themselves through direct knowledge, make it known.’ In this way, monks, the threefold faulty transgression of mental kamma is unwholesome, intentional, having suffering as its outcome, and having suffering as its result.

“Tividha kāyakammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikāhetu … sañcetanikahetu (ka.) vā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjanti; catubbidhavacīkammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikāhetu vā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjanti; tividhamanokammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikāhetu vā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjanti.

Monks, because of the threefold faulty transgression of bodily kamma, which is unwholesome and intentional, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell; because of the fourfold faulty transgression of verbal kamma, which is unwholesome and intentional, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell; because of the threefold faulty transgression of mental kamma, which is unwholesome and intentional, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, apaṇṇako maṇi uddhaṃkhitto yena yeneva patiṭṭhāti suppatiṭṭhitaṃyeva patiṭṭhāti[T 5.0316]; evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tividhakāyakammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikāhetu vā sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjanti; catubbidhavacīkammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikāhetu vā sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjanti; tividhamanokammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikāhetu vā sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjantīti.

Bhikkhus, just as a four-cornered gem, when thrown upwards, lands well-established on whichever side it lands; even so, bhikkhus, due to the cause of threefold faulty and transgressive bodily action, which is unwholesome and volitional, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell; due to the cause of fourfold faulty and transgressive verbal action, which is unwholesome and volitional, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell; due to the cause of threefold faulty and transgressive mental action, which is unwholesome and volitional, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a state of loss, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell.

“Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṃ kammānaṃ katānaṃ upacitānaṃ appaṭisaṃveditvā byantībhāvaṃ vadāmi, tañca kho diṭṭheva dhamme upapajje vā apare vā pariyāye. Na tvevāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṃ kammānaṃ katānaṃ upacitānaṃ appaṭisaṃveditvā dukkhassantakiriyaṃ vadāmi.

Bhikkhus, I do not declare the termination of volitional actions that have been done and accumulated without their result having been experienced. And that is to be experienced either in this very life, or in the next life, or in a subsequent life. Indeed, bhikkhus, I do not declare the making of an end to suffering without having experienced the result of volitional actions that have been done and accumulated.

“Tatra, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti; catubbidhā vacīkammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti; tividhā manokammantasampatti [P 5.0295] kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti.

In that regard, bhikkhus, the threefold accomplishment in bodily action, being wholesome and volitional, has a happy outcome and a happy result; the fourfold accomplishment in verbal action, being wholesome and volitional, has a happy outcome and a happy result; the threefold accomplishment in mental action, being wholesome and volitional, has a happy outcome and a happy result.

“Kathañca[M 3.0500], bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā [V 3.0263] hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco pāṇātipātaṃ pahāya pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti nihitadaṇḍo nihitasattho lajjī dayāpanno, sabbapāṇabhūtahitānukampī viharati…pe….

And how, bhikkhus, is the threefold accomplishment in bodily action, being wholesome and volitional, of happy outcome and happy result? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person, having abandoned the destruction of life, abstains from the destruction of life. With rod and weapon laid aside, scrupulous, endowed with kindness, he dwells compassionate for the welfare of all living beings and creatures...

“Adinnādānaṃ pahāya, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti. Yaṃ taṃ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṃ gāmagataṃ vā araññagataṃ vā, na taṃ adinnaṃ theyyasaṅkhātaṃ ādātā hoti.

Having abandoned taking what is not given, he abstains from taking what is not given. Whatever property and belongings of another there might be, whether in a village or in a forest, he is not one to take it, ungiven, with thievish intent.

“Kāmesumicchācāraṃ pahāya, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti. Yā tā māturakkhitā [T 5.0317] …pe… antamaso mālāguḷaparikkhittāpi, tathārūpāsu na cārittaṃ āpajjitā hoti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti.

Having abandoned misconduct in sensual pleasures, he abstains from misconduct in sensual pleasures. He does not fall into transgression with such women as are protected by their mother... down to those betrothed with a garland. In this way, bhikkhus, the threefold accomplishment in bodily action, being wholesome and volitional, has a happy outcome and a happy result.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, catubbidhā vacīkammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco musāvādaṃ pahāya musāvādā paṭivirato hoti. Sabhaggato vā parisaggato vā ñātimajjhagato vā pūgamajjhagato vā rājakulamajjhagato vā abhinīto sakkhipuṭṭho ‘ehambho purisa, yaṃ jānāsi taṃ vadehī’ti, so ajānaṃ vā āha ‘na jānāmī’ti, jānaṃ vā āha ‘jānāmī’ti, apassaṃ vā āha ‘na passāmī’ti, passaṃ vā āha ‘passāmī’ti, iti attahetu vā parahetu vā āmisakiñcikkhahetu vā na sampajānamusā bhāsitā hoti.

And how, bhikkhus, is the fourfold accomplishment in verbal action, being wholesome and volitional, of happy outcome and happy result? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person, having abandoned false speech, abstains from false speech. When he has gone to a council, to an assembly, to the midst of his relatives, to the midst of a guild, or to the midst of a royal family, and is brought in and questioned as a witness, ‘Come, good man, tell what you know,’ then, not knowing, he says, ‘I do not know,’ or knowing, he says, ‘I know’; not seeing, he says, ‘I do not see,’ or seeing, he says, ‘I see.’ Thus he is not one who knowingly speaks a falsehood for his own sake, for the sake of another, or for the sake of some trivial gain.

“Pisuṇaṃ vācaṃ pahāya, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti – na ito sutvā amutra akkhātā imesaṃ bhedāya, amutra vā sutvā na imesaṃ akkhātā amūsaṃ bhedāya. Iti bhinnānaṃ vā sandhātā [P 5.0296] sahitānaṃ vā anuppadātā samaggārāmo samaggarato samagganandiṃ, samaggakaraṇiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti.

Having abandoned divisive speech, he abstains from divisive speech. He does not repeat elsewhere what he has heard here in order to divide those people from these, nor does he repeat here what he has heard elsewhere in order to divide these people from those. Thus he is a reconciler of those who are divided and a promoter of those who are united. He delights in concord, rejoices in concord, is fond of concord, and is a speaker of words that create concord.

“Pharusaṃ vācaṃ pahāya, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti. Yā sā vācā nelā kaṇṇasukhā pemanīyā hadayaṅgamā porī bahujanakantā bahujanamanāpā, tathārūpiṃ vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti.

Having abandoned harsh speech, he abstains from harsh speech. He speaks such words as are faultless, pleasant to the ear, endearing, going to the heart, courteous, liked by the many, and agreeable to the many.

“Samphappalāpaṃ [V 3.0264] pahāya, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti kālavādī bhūtavādī atthavādī dhammavādī vinayavādī, nidhānavatiṃ [T 5.0318] vācaṃ bhāsitā hoti kālena [M 3.0501] sāpadesaṃ pariyantavatiṃ atthasaṃhitaṃ. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, catubbidhā vacīkammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti.

Having abandoned frivolous talk, he abstains from frivolous talk. He speaks at the proper time, speaks what is factual, speaks what is beneficial, speaks on the Dhamma, and speaks on the Vinaya. He speaks words worth treasuring, at the proper time, with illustrations, with a defined limit, and connected with benefit. In this way, bhikkhus, the fourfold accomplishment in verbal action, being wholesome and volitional, has a happy outcome and a happy result.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, tividhā manokammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti? Idha, bhikkhave, ekacco anabhijjhālu hoti. Yaṃ taṃ parassa paravittūpakaraṇaṃ taṃ anabhijjhātā hoti – ‘aho vata, yaṃ parassa taṃ mamassā’ti.

And how, bhikkhus, is the threefold accomplishment in mental action, being wholesome and volitional, of happy outcome and happy result? Here, bhikkhus, a certain person is not covetous. He does not covet the property and belongings of others, thinking: ‘Oh, that what belongs to others might be mine!’

“Abyāpannacitto hoti appaduṭṭhamanasaṅkappo – ‘ime sattā averā hontu abyāpajjā anīghā, sukhī attānaṃ pariharantū’ti.

He has a mind without ill will and intentions free of hate, thinking: ‘May these beings be free from enmity, free from affliction, free from distress, and may they maintain themselves in happiness!’

“Sammādiṭṭhiko hoti aviparītadassano – ‘atthi dinnaṃ, atthi yiṭṭhaṃ…pe… ye imañca lokaṃ parañca lokaṃ sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā pavedentī’ti. Evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tividhā manokammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti.

He has right view, an undistorted perspective: ‘There is a result of what is given, there is a result of what is offered... there are those ascetics and brahmins who, having directly known and realized this world and the next for themselves, make it known.’ In this way, bhikkhus, the threefold accomplishment in mental action, being wholesome and volitional, has a happy outcome and a happy result.

“Tividhakāyakammantasampattikusalasañcetanikāhetu vā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti; catubbidhavacīkammantasampattikusalasañcetanikāhetu vā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti; tividhamanokammantasampattikusalasañcetanikāhetu vā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti.

Bhikkhus, due to the cause of the threefold accomplishment in bodily action, which is wholesome and volitional, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Or, bhikkhus, due to the cause of the fourfold accomplishment in verbal action, which is wholesome and volitional, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Or, bhikkhus, due to the cause of the threefold accomplishment in mental action, which is wholesome and volitional, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.

“Seyyathāpi, bhikkhave, apaṇṇako maṇi uddhaṃkhitto yena yeneva patiṭṭhāti suppatiṭṭhitaṃyeva patiṭṭhāti; evamevaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tividhakāyakammantasampattikusalasañcetanikāhetu [P 5.0297] vā sattā [T 5.0319] kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti; catubbidhavacīkammantasampattikusalasañcetanikāhetu vā sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti; tividhamanokammantasampattikusalasañcetanikāhetu vā sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti. Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṃ [V 3.0265] kammānaṃ katānaṃ upacitānaṃ appaṭisaṃveditvā byantībhāvaṃ vadāmi. Tañca kho diṭṭheva dhamme upapajje vā apare vā pariyāye. Na tvevāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṃ kammānaṃ katānaṃ upacitānaṃ appaṭisaṃveditvā dukkhassantakiriyaṃ vadāmī”ti. Sattamaṃ. aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana aṭṭhamasuttampi ettheva pariyāpannaṃ viya saṃvaṇṇanā dissati

Just as, monks, a four-cornered gem, when thrown upwards, lands firmly on whichever side it lands; even so, monks, on account of the cause which is the wholesome volition for the threefold accomplishment of bodily action, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, arise in a good destination, a heavenly world. On account of the cause which is the wholesome volition for the fourfold accomplishment of verbal action, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, arise in a good destination, a heavenly world. On account of the cause which is the wholesome volition for the threefold accomplishment of mental action, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, arise in a good destination, a heavenly world. I do not declare, monks, the annulment of volitional actions that have been done and accumulated without their result having been experienced. And that is experienced either in this very life, or in the next life, or in subsequent existences. I do not, indeed, monks, declare the making of an end to suffering without having experienced the result of volitional actions that have been done and accumulated. The seventh.

8. Dutiyasañcetanikasuttaṃ

8. The Second Discourse on Volition

218. “Nāhaṃ[M 3.0502], bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṃ kammānaṃ katānaṃ upacitānaṃ appaṭisaṃveditvā byantībhāvaṃ vadāmi, tañca kho diṭṭheva dhamme upapajje vā apare vā pariyāye. Na tvevāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṃ kammānaṃ katānaṃ upacitānaṃ appaṭisaṃveditvā dukkhassantakiriyaṃ vadāmi.

218. I do not declare, monks, the annulment of volitional actions that have been done and accumulated without their result having been experienced, and that is experienced either in this very life, or in the next life, or in subsequent existences. I do not, indeed, monks, declare the making of an end to suffering without having experienced the result of volitional actions that have been done and accumulated.

“Tatra, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti; catubbidhā vacīkammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti; tividhā manokammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti.

Among these, monks, the threefold faulty transgression of bodily action, which is unwholesome and volitional, has suffering as its increase and has suffering as its result. The fourfold faulty transgression of verbal action, which is unwholesome and volitional, has suffering as its increase and has suffering as its result. The threefold faulty transgression of mental action, which is unwholesome and volitional, has suffering as its increase and has suffering as its result.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti.

And how, monks, is the threefold faulty transgression of bodily action, which is unwholesome and volitional, one that has suffering as its increase and has suffering as its result? ... Thus indeed, monks, the threefold faulty transgression of bodily action, which is unwholesome and volitional, has suffering as its increase and has suffering as its result.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, catubbidhā vacīkammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti…pe… evaṃ [P 5.0298] kho, bhikkhave, catubbidhā vacīkammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā [T 5.0320] hoti.

And how, monks, is the fourfold faulty transgression of verbal action, which is unwholesome and volitional, one that has suffering as its increase and has suffering as its result? ... Thus indeed, monks, the fourfold faulty transgression of verbal action, which is unwholesome and volitional, has suffering as its increase and has suffering as its result.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, tividhā manokammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tividhā manokammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikā dukkhudrayā dukkhavipākā hoti.

And how, monks, is the threefold faulty transgression of mental action, which is unwholesome and volitional, one that has suffering as its increase and has suffering as its result? ... Thus indeed, monks, the threefold faulty transgression of mental action, which is unwholesome and volitional, has suffering as its increase and has suffering as its result.

“Tividha [V 3.0266] kāyakammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikāhetu vā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjanti, catubbidhavacīkammanta…pe… tividhamanokammantasandosabyāpatti akusalasañcetanikāhetu vā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjanti.

Monks, on account of the cause which is the unwholesome volition for the threefold faulty transgression of bodily action, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, arise in the plane of misery, a bad destination, the downfall, in hell. On account of the fourfold faulty transgression of verbal action... Or, monks, on account of the cause which is the unwholesome volition for the threefold faulty transgression of mental action, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, arise in the plane of misery, a bad destination, the downfall, in hell.

“Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṃ kammānaṃ katānaṃ upacitānaṃ appaṭisaṃveditvā byantībhāvaṃ vadāmi, tañca kho diṭṭheva dhamme upapajje vā apare vā pariyāye[M 3.0503]. Na tvevāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṃ kammānaṃ katānaṃ upacitānaṃ appaṭisaṃveditvā dukkhassantakiriyaṃ vadāmi.

I do not declare, monks, the annulment of volitional actions that have been done and accumulated without their result having been experienced, and that is experienced either in this very life, or in the next life, or in subsequent existences. I do not, indeed, monks, declare the making of an end to suffering without having experienced the result of volitional actions that have been done and accumulated.

“Tatra kho, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti; catubbidhā vacīkammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti; tividhā manokammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti.

Indeed, monks, among these, the threefold accomplishment of bodily action, which is wholesome and volitional, has happiness as its increase and has happiness as its result. The fourfold accomplishment of verbal action, which is wholesome and volitional, has happiness as its increase and has happiness as its result. The threefold accomplishment of mental action, which is wholesome and volitional, has happiness as its increase and has happiness as its result.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tividhā kāyakammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti.

And how, monks, is the threefold accomplishment of bodily action, which is wholesome and volitional, one that has happiness as its increase and has happiness as its result? ... Thus indeed, monks, the threefold accomplishment of bodily action, which is wholesome and volitional, has happiness as its increase and has happiness as its result.

“Kathañca[T 5.0321], bhikkhave, catubbidhā vacīkammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, catubbidhā vacīkammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti[P 5.0299].

And how, monks, is the fourfold accomplishment of verbal action, which is wholesome and volitional, one that has happiness as its increase and has happiness as its result? ... Thus indeed, monks, the fourfold accomplishment of verbal action, which is wholesome and volitional, has happiness as its increase and has happiness as its result.

“Kathañca, bhikkhave, tividhā manokammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti…pe… evaṃ kho, bhikkhave, tividhā manokammantasampatti kusalasañcetanikā sukhudrayā sukhavipākā hoti.

And how, monks, is the threefold accomplishment of mental action, which is wholesome and volitional, one that has happiness as its increase and has happiness as its result? ... Thus indeed, monks, the threefold accomplishment of mental action, which is wholesome and volitional, has happiness as its increase and has happiness as its result.

“Tividhakāyakammantasampattikusalasañcetanikāhetu vā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti; catubbidhavacīkammantasampatti…pe… tividhamanokammantasampattikusalasañcetanikāhetu [V 3.0267] vā, bhikkhave, sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjanti…pe…. upapajjanti. (syā. ka.) tathā sati “nāhaṃ bhikkhave sañcetanikāna” miccādinā vuccamānavacanena saha ekasuttanti gahetabbaṃ. peyyālena pana purimasutte viya nigamanaṃ dassitaṃ Aṭṭhamaṃ.

Monks, on account of the cause which is the wholesome volition for the threefold accomplishment of bodily action, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, arise in a good destination, a heavenly world. On account of the fourfold accomplishment of verbal action... Or, on account of the cause which is the wholesome volition for the threefold accomplishment of mental action, beings, with the breakup of the body, after death, arise in a good destination, a heavenly world... The Eighth.

9. Karajakāyasuttaṃ

9. The Discourse on the Body Born of Kamma

219. “Nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṃ kammānaṃ katānaṃ upacitānaṃ appaṭisaṃveditvā byantībhāvaṃ vadāmi, tañca kho diṭṭheva dhamme upapajje vā apare vā pariyāye. Na tvevāhaṃ, bhikkhave, sañcetanikānaṃ kammānaṃ katānaṃ upacitānaṃ appaṭisaṃveditvā dukkhassantakiriyaṃ vadāmi.

219. Monks, I do not declare the ending of intentional actions that have been done and accumulated without their result having been experienced, and that, indeed, is to be experienced either in this very life, or in the next life, or in a subsequent one. I certainly do not declare the making of an end to suffering without having experienced the result of intentional actions that have been done and accumulated.

“Sa kho so, bhikkhave, ariyasāvako evaṃ vigatābhijjho vigatabyāpādo asammūḷho sampajāno paṭissato mettāsahagatena cetasā [M 3.0504] ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati tathā dutiyaṃ tathā tatiyaṃ tathā catutthaṃ catutthiṃ (?). Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ mettāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena [T 5.0322] appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.

That noble disciple, monks, thus devoid of covetousness, devoid of ill will, unconfused, clearly comprehending, and mindful, dwells pervading one direction with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, for all beings, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by loving-kindness—vast, exalted, measureless, without enmity, and without ill will.

“So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘pubbe kho me idaṃ cittaṃ parittaṃ ahosi abhāvitaṃ, etarahi pana me idaṃ cittaṃ appamāṇaṃ subhāvitaṃ. Yaṃ kho pana kiñci pamāṇakataṃ kammaṃ, na taṃ tatrāvasissati na taṃ tatrāvatiṭṭhatī’ti[P 5.0300].

He understands thus: ‘Formerly, this mind of mine was limited and undeveloped, but now this mind of mine is measureless and well-developed. Whatever kamma was done with limitation, it does not remain there, it does not persist there.’

“Taṃ kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, daharatagge ce so ayaṃ ce ayaṃ (syā.) kumāro mettaṃ cetovimuttiṃ bhāveyya, api nu kho api nu so (?) pāpakammaṃ kareyyā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

What do you think, monks? If that boy, from a tender age, were to develop loving-kindness, the liberation of mind, would he do an evil deed?” “Certainly not, venerable sir.”

“Akarontaṃ kho pana pāpakammaṃ api nu kho dukkhaṃ phuseyyā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante. Akarontañhi, bhante, pāpakammaṃ kuto dukkhaṃ phusissatī”ti!

And would suffering befall one who does not do an evil deed?” “Certainly not, venerable sir. Indeed, venerable sir, for one who does not do an evil deed, from where would suffering befall him?”

“Bhāvetabbā kho panāyaṃ, bhikkhave, mettācetovimutti itthiyā vā purisena vā. Itthiyā vā, bhikkhave, purisassa vā nāyaṃ kāyo ādāya gamanīyo. Cittantaro ayaṃ, bhikkhave[V 3.0268], macco. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘yaṃ kho me idaṃ kiñci pubbe iminā karajakāyena pāpakammaṃ kataṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ idha vedanīyaṃ; na taṃ anugaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, mettā cetovimutti anāgāmitāya saṃvattati, idha paññassa bhikkhuno uttari uttariṃ (sī. syā. pī.) vimuttiṃ appaṭivijjhato.

Monks, this liberation of mind by loving-kindness should be developed by a woman or a man. Monks, this body is not to be taken along by a woman or a man. This mortal being, monks, is accompanied by mind. One understands thus: ‘Whatever evil deed I have done in the past with this body born of kamma, all of that is to be experienced here; it will not follow along.’ Monks, when the liberation of mind by loving-kindness is developed in this way, it leads to non-returning for a monk with wisdom here who has not penetrated a higher liberation.

“Karuṇāsahagatena cetasā… muditāsahagatena cetasā… upekkhāsahagatena cetasā ekaṃ disaṃ pharitvā viharati tathā dutiyaṃ tathā tatiyaṃ tathā catutthaṃ. Iti uddhamadho tiriyaṃ sabbadhi sabbattatāya sabbāvantaṃ lokaṃ upekkhāsahagatena cetasā vipulena mahaggatena appamāṇena averena abyāpajjena pharitvā viharati.

With a mind accompanied by compassion… with a mind accompanied by appreciative joy… with a mind accompanied by equanimity, he dwells pervading one direction, likewise the second, likewise the third, likewise the fourth. Thus above, below, and across, everywhere, for all beings, he dwells pervading the entire world with a mind accompanied by equanimity—vast, exalted, measureless, without enmity, and without ill will.

“So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘pubbe kho me idaṃ cittaṃ parittaṃ ahosi abhāvitaṃ, etarahi pana me idaṃ cittaṃ appamāṇaṃ [T 5.0323] subhāvitaṃ. Yaṃ kho pana kiñci pamāṇakataṃ kammaṃ[P 5.0301], na taṃ tatrāvasissati na taṃ tatrāvatiṭṭhatī’ti.

He understands thus: ‘Formerly, this mind of mine was limited and undeveloped, but now this mind of mine is measureless and well-developed. Whatever kamma was done with limitation, it does not remain there, it does not persist there.’

“Taṃ [M 3.0505] kiṃ maññatha, bhikkhave, daharatagge ce so ayaṃ kumāro upekkhaṃ cetovimuttiṃ bhāveyya, api nu kho pāpakammaṃ kareyyā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante”.

What do you think, monks? If that boy, from a tender age, were to develop equanimity, the liberation of mind, would he do an evil deed?” “Certainly not, venerable sir.”

“Akarontaṃ kho pana pāpakammaṃ api nu kho dukkhaṃ phuseyyā”ti? “No hetaṃ, bhante. Akarontañhi, bhante, pāpakammaṃ kuto dukkhaṃ phusissatī”ti!

And would suffering befall one who does not do an evil deed?” “Certainly not, venerable sir. Indeed, venerable sir, for one who does not do an evil deed, from where would suffering befall him?”

“Bhāvetabbā kho panāyaṃ, bhikkhave, upekkhā cetovimutti itthiyā vā purisena vā. Itthiyā vā, bhikkhave, purisassa vā nāyaṃ kāyo ādāya gamanīyo. Cittantaro ayaṃ, bhikkhave, macco. So evaṃ pajānāti – ‘yaṃ kho me idaṃ kiñci pubbe iminā karajakāyena pāpakammaṃ kataṃ, sabbaṃ taṃ idha vedanīyaṃ; na taṃ anugaṃ bhavissatī’ti. Evaṃ bhāvitā kho, bhikkhave, upekkhā cetovimutti anāgāmitāya saṃvattati, idha paññassa bhikkhuno uttari vimuttiṃ appaṭivijjhato”ti. Navamaṃ.

Monks, this liberation of mind through equanimity should be developed by a woman or a man. Monks, this body is not to be taken along by a woman or a man. This mortal being, monks, is accompanied by mind. One understands thus: ‘Whatever evil deed I have done in the past with this body born of kamma, all of that is to be experienced here; it will not follow along.’ Monks, when the liberation of mind through equanimity is developed in this way, it leads to non-returning for a monk with wisdom here who has not penetrated a higher liberation. The Ninth.

10. Adhammacariyāsuttaṃ

10. The Discourse on Unrighteous Conduct

220. a. ni. 2.16 Atha [V 3.0269] kho aññataro brāhmaṇo yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṃ sammodi. Sammodanīyaṃ kathaṃ sāraṇīyaṃ vītisāretvā ekamantaṃ nisīdi. Ekamantaṃ nisinno kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavantaṃ etadavoca – “ko nu kho, bho gotama, hetu ko paccayo yenamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjantī”ti? “Adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu kho, brāhmaṇa, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjantī”ti.

220. Then a certain brahmin approached the Blessed One; having approached, he exchanged pleasantries with the Blessed One. Having concluded the pleasant and courteous talk, he sat down to one side. Sitting to one side, that brahmin said this to the Blessed One: 'What, Master Gotama, is the cause, what is the reason, whereby some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in the plane of deprivation, the bad destination, the state of ruin, in hell?' 'Brahmin, it is because of unrighteous conduct and uneven conduct that some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in the plane of deprivation, the bad destination, the state of ruin, in hell.'

“Ko pana, bho gotama, hetu ko paccayo [T 5.0324] yenamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā [P 5.0302] paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti? “Dhammacariyāsamacariyāhetu kho, brāhmaṇa, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti.

But what, Master Gotama, is the cause, what is the reason, whereby some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world?' 'Brahmin, it is because of righteous conduct and even conduct that some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.'

“Na kho ahaṃ imassa bhoto gotamassa saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājānāmi. Sādhu me bhavaṃ gotamo tathā dhammaṃ desetu yathāhaṃ imassa bhoto gotamassa saṃkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṃ ājāneyya”nti. “Tena hi, brāhmaṇa, suṇāhi, sādhukaṃ manasi karohi[M 3.0506]; bhāsissāmī”ti. “Evaṃ, bho”ti kho so brāhmaṇo bhagavato paccassosi. Bhagavā etadavoca –

I do not understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken in brief by Master Gotama. It would be good if Master Gotama would teach me the Dhamma in such a way that I might understand in detail the meaning of what was spoken in brief by him.' 'In that case, brahmin, listen and pay close attention; I will speak.' 'Very well, Master,' that brahmin replied to the Blessed One. The Blessed One said this:

“Tividhā [T 5.0325] kho, brāhmaṇa, kāyena adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti; catubbidhā vācāya adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti; tividhā manasā adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti.

'Brahmin, unrighteous and uneven conduct by way of the body is threefold; unrighteous and uneven conduct by way of speech is fourfold; unrighteous and uneven conduct by way of the mind is threefold.'

“Kathañca, brāhmaṇa, tividhā kāyena adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti…pe… evaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, tividhā kāyena adhammacariyā visamacariyā hoti.

'And how, brahmin, is unrighteous and uneven conduct by way of the body threefold? ... Thus, brahmin, unrighteous and uneven conduct by way of the body is threefold.'

“Kathañca, brāhmaṇa, catubbidhā vācāya adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti…pe… evaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, catubbidhā vācāya adhammacariyā visamacariyā hoti.

'And how, brahmin, is unrighteous and uneven conduct by way of speech fourfold? ... Thus, brahmin, unrighteous and uneven conduct by way of speech is fourfold.'

“Kathañca[V 3.0270], brāhmaṇa, tividhā manasā adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti…pe… evaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, tividhā manasā adhammacariyāvisamacariyā hoti. Evaṃ adhammacariyāvisamacariyāhetu kho, brāhmaṇa, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjanti.

'And how, brahmin, is unrighteous and uneven conduct by way of the mind threefold? ... Thus, brahmin, unrighteous and uneven conduct by way of the mind is threefold. Thus, brahmin, it is because of unrighteous and uneven conduct that some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in the plane of deprivation, the bad destination, the state of ruin, in hell.'

“Tividhā brāhmaṇa, kāyena dhammacariyāsamacariyā hoti; catubbidhā vācāya dhammacariyāsamacariyā hoti; tividhā manasā dhammacariyāsamacariyā hoti.

'Brahmin, righteous and even conduct by way of the body is threefold; righteous and even conduct by way of speech is fourfold; righteous and even conduct by way of the mind is threefold.'

“Kathañca, brāhmaṇa, tividhā kāyena dhammacariyāsamacariyā hoti…pe… evaṃ [P 5.0303] kho, brāhmaṇa, tividhā kāyena dhammacariyāsamacariyā hoti.

'And how, brahmin, is righteous and even conduct by way of the body threefold? ... Thus, brahmin, righteous and even conduct by way of the body is threefold.'

“Kathañca, brāhmaṇa, catubbidhā vācāya dhammacariyāsamacariyā hoti…pe… evaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, catubbidhā vācāya dhammacariyāsamacariyā hoti.

'And how, brahmin, is righteous and even conduct by way of speech fourfold? ... Thus, brahmin, righteous and even conduct by way of speech is fourfold.'

“Kathañca, brāhmaṇa, tividhā manasā dhammacariyāsamacariyā hoti…pe… evaṃ kho, brāhmaṇa, tividhā manasā dhammacariyāsamacariyā hoti. Evaṃ dhammacariyāsamacariyāhetu kho, brāhmaṇa, evamidhekacce sattā kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjantī”ti.

'And how, brahmin, is righteous and even conduct by way of the mind threefold? ... Thus, brahmin, righteous and even conduct by way of the mind is threefold. Thus, brahmin, it is because of righteous and even conduct that some beings here, with the breakup of the body, after death, are reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world.'

“Abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama, abhikkantaṃ, bho gotama…pe… upāsakaṃ maṃ bhavaṃ gotamo dhāretu ajjatagge pāṇupetaṃ saraṇaṃ gata”nti. Dasamaṃ.

'Excellent, Master Gotama! Excellent, Master Gotama! ... May Master Gotama remember me as a lay follower who has gone for refuge for life from this day forward.' The Tenth.

Karajakāyavaggo paṭhamo.

The First Karajakāya Chapter.

(22) 2. Sāmaññavaggo

(22) 2. The General Chapter

221. “Dasahi[V 3.0271][M 3.0507], bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye. Katamehi dasahi? Pāṇātipātī hoti, adinnādāyī hoti, kāmesumicchācārī hoti, musāvādī hoti, pisuṇavāco hoti, pharusavāco hoti, samphappalāpī hoti, abhijjhālu hoti, byāpannacitto hoti, micchādiṭṭhiko hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato [T 5.0326] yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye.

221. “Bhikkhus, one endowed with ten qualities is deposited in hell as if brought and cast there. What ten? One destroys life; one takes what is not given; one engages in sexual misconduct; one speaks falsely; one speaks divisively; one speaks harshly; one engages in idle chatter; one is covetous; one has a mind of ill will; and one has wrong view. Bhikkhus, one endowed with these ten qualities is deposited in hell as if brought and cast there.”

“Dasahi[P 5.0304], bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge. Katamehi dasahi? Pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, anabhijjhālu hoti, abyāpannacitto hoti, sammādiṭṭhiko hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, dasahi dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge”ti.

“Bhikkhus, one endowed with ten qualities is deposited in heaven as if brought and placed there. What ten? One abstains from destroying life; one abstains from taking what is not given; one abstains from sexual misconduct; one abstains from false speech; one abstains from divisive speech; one abstains from harsh speech; one abstains from idle chatter; one is not covetous; one has a mind without ill will; and one has right view. Bhikkhus, one endowed with these ten qualities is deposited in heaven as if brought and placed there.”

222. “Vīsatiyā, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye. Katamehi vīsatiyā? Attanā ca pāṇātipātī hoti, parañca pāṇātipāte samādapeti; attanā ca adinnādāyī hoti, parañca adinnādāne samādapeti; attanā ca kāmesumicchācārī hoti, parañca kāmesumicchācāre samādapeti; attanā ca musāvādī hoti, parañca musāvāde samādapeti; attanā ca pisuṇavāco hoti, parañca pisuṇāya vācāya samādapeti; attanā ca pharusavāco hoti, parañca pharusāya vācāya samādapeti; attanā ca samphappalāpī hoti, parañca samphappalāpe samādapeti; attanā ca abhijjhālu hoti, parañca abhijjhāya samādapeti; attanā ca byāpannacitto hoti, parañca byāpāde samādapeti; attanā ca micchādiṭṭhiko hoti, parañca micchādiṭṭhiyā samādapeti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, vīsatiyā dhammehi [T 5.0327] samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye.

222. “Bhikkhus, one endowed with twenty qualities is deposited in hell as if brought and cast there. What twenty? One personally destroys life and encourages others to destroy life; one personally takes what is not given and encourages others to take what is not given; one personally engages in sexual misconduct and encourages others in sexual misconduct; one personally speaks falsely and encourages others to speak falsely; one personally speaks divisively and encourages others to speak divisively; one personally speaks harshly and encourages others to speak harshly; one personally engages in idle chatter and encourages others to engage in idle chatter; one is personally covetous and encourages others in covetousness; one personally has a mind of ill will and encourages others in ill will; and one personally has wrong view and encourages others in wrong view. Bhikkhus, one endowed with these twenty qualities is deposited in hell as if brought and cast there.”

“Vīsatiyā[V 3.0272], bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge. Katamehi vīsatiyā? Attanā ca pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti[M 3.0508], parañca pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā samādapeti; attanā ca adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, parañca adinnādānā veramaṇiyā samādapeti; attanā ca kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, parañca kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇiyā samādapeti; attanā ca musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, parañca musāvādā veramaṇiyā samādapeti; attanā ca pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, parañca pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇiyā samādapeti; attanā ca [P 5.0305] pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, parañca pharusāya vācāya veramaṇiyā samādapeti; attanā ca samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, parañca samphappalāpā veramaṇiyā samādapeti; attanā ca anabhijjhālu hoti, parañca anabhijjhāya samādapeti; attanā ca abyāpannacitto hoti, parañca abyāpāde samādapeti; attanā ca sammādiṭṭhiko hoti, parañca sammādiṭṭhiyā samādapeti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, vīsatiyā dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge”ti.

“Bhikkhus, one endowed with twenty qualities is deposited in heaven as if brought there. What twenty? One personally abstains from destroying life and encourages others in abstinence from destroying life; one personally abstains from taking what is not given and encourages others in abstinence from taking what is not given; one personally abstains from sexual misconduct and encourages others in abstinence from sexual misconduct; one personally abstains from false speech and encourages others in abstinence from false speech; one personally abstains from divisive speech and encourages others in abstinence from divisive speech; one personally abstains from harsh speech and encourages others in abstinence from harsh speech; one personally abstains from idle chatter and encourages others in abstinence from idle chatter; one is personally not covetous and encourages others in non-covetousness; one personally has a mind without ill will and encourages others in non-ill will; and one personally has right view and encourages others in right view. Bhikkhus, one endowed with these twenty qualities is deposited in heaven as if brought there.”

223. “Tiṃsāya, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye. Katamehi tiṃsāya? Attanā ca pāṇātipātī hoti, parañca pāṇātipāte samādapeti, pāṇātipāte ca samanuñño hoti; attanā [T 5.0328] ca adinnādāyī hoti, parañca adinnādāne samādapeti, adinnādāne ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca kāmesumicchācārī hoti, parañca kāmesumicchācāre samādapeti, kāmesumicchācāre ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca musāvādī hoti, parañca musāvāde samādapeti, musāvāde ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca pisuṇavāco hoti, parañca pisuṇāya vācāya samādapeti, pisuṇāya vācāya ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca pharusavāco hoti, parañca pharusāya vācāya samādapeti, pharusāya vācāya ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca samphappalāpī hoti, parañca samphappalāpe samādapeti, samphappalāpe ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca abhijjhālu hoti, parañca abhijjhāya samādapeti, abhijjhāya ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca byāpannacitto hoti, parañca byāpāde samādapeti, byāpāde ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca micchādiṭṭhiko hoti, parañca micchādiṭṭhiyā samādapeti, micchādiṭṭhiyā ca samanuñño hoti – imehi kho[M 3.0509], bhikkhave, tiṃsāya dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye.

223. “Bhikkhus, one endowed with thirty qualities is deposited in hell as if brought there. What thirty? One personally destroys life, encourages others to destroy life, and approves of destroying life; one personally takes what is not given, encourages others to take what is not given, and approves of taking what is not given; one personally engages in sexual misconduct, encourages others in sexual misconduct, and approves of sexual misconduct; one personally speaks falsely, encourages others to speak falsely, and approves of false speech; one personally speaks divisively, encourages others to speak divisively, and approves of divisive speech; one personally speaks harshly, encourages others to speak harshly, and approves of harsh speech; one personally engages in idle chatter, encourages others to engage in idle chatter, and approves of idle chatter; one is personally covetous, encourages others in covetousness, and approves of covetousness; one personally has a mind of ill will, encourages others in ill will, and approves of ill will; and one personally has wrong view, encourages others in wrong view, and approves of wrong view. Bhikkhus, one endowed with these thirty qualities is deposited in hell as if brought there.”

“Tiṃsāya[V 3.0273], bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge. Katamehi tiṃsāya? Attanā [P 5.0306] ca pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, parañca pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, parañca adinnādānā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, adinnādānā veramaṇiyā [T 5.0329] ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, parañca kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇiyā ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, parañca musāvādā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, musāvādā veramaṇiyā ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca pisuṇāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, parañca pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇiyā samādapeti, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇiyā ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, parañca pharusāya vācāya veramaṇiyā samādapeti, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇiyā ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, parañca samphappalāpā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, samphappalāpā veramaṇiyā ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca anabhijjhālu hoti, parañca anabhijjhāya samādapeti, anabhijjhāya ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca abyāpannacitto hoti, parañca abyāpāde samādapeti, abyāpāde ca samanuñño hoti; attanā ca sammādiṭṭhiko hoti, parañca sammādiṭṭhiyā samādapeti, sammādiṭṭhiyā ca samanuñño hoti – imehi kho, bhikkhave, tiṃsāya dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge”ti.

“Bhikkhus, one endowed with thirty qualities is deposited in heaven as if brought there. What thirty? One personally abstains from destroying life, encourages others in abstinence from destroying life, and approves of abstinence from destroying life; one personally abstains from taking what is not given, encourages others in abstinence from taking what is not given, and approves of abstinence from taking what is not given; one personally abstains from sexual misconduct, encourages others in abstinence from sexual misconduct, and approves of abstinence from sexual misconduct; one personally abstains from false speech, encourages others in abstinence from false speech, and approves of abstinence from false speech; one personally abstains from divisive speech, encourages others in abstinence from divisive speech, and approves of abstinence from divisive speech; one personally abstains from harsh speech, encourages others in abstinence from harsh speech, and approves of abstinence from harsh speech; one personally abstains from idle chatter, encourages others in abstinence from idle chatter, and approves of abstinence from idle chatter; one is personally not covetous, encourages others in non-covetousness, and approves of non-covetousness; one personally has a mind without ill will, encourages others in non-ill will, and approves of non-ill will; and one personally has right view, encourages others in right view, and approves of right view. Bhikkhus, one endowed with these thirty qualities is deposited in heaven as if brought there.”

224. “Cattārīsāya, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye. Katamehi cattārīsāya? Attanā ca pāṇātipātī hoti, parañca pāṇātipāte samādapeti, pāṇātipāte ca samanuñño hoti[T 5.0330], pāṇātipātassa ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca adinnādāyī hoti, parañca adinnādāne samādapeti, adinnādāne ca samanuñño hoti, adinnādānassa ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca kāmesumicchācārī hoti[M 3.0510], parañca kāmesumicchācāre samādapeti, kāmesumicchācāre [P 5.0307] ca samanuñño hoti, kāmesumicchācārassa ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca musāvādī hoti, parañca musāvāde samādapeti, musāvāde ca samanuñño hoti, musāvādassa ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca pisuṇavāco hoti, parañca pisuṇāya vācāya samādapeti, pisuṇāya vācāya ca samanuñño hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca pharusavāco hoti, parañca pharusāya vācāya samādapeti, pharusāya [V 3.0274] vācāya ca samanuñño hoti, pharusāya vācāya ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca samphappalāpī hoti, parañca samphappalāpe samādapeti, samphappalāpe ca samanuñño hoti, samphappalāpassa ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca abhijjhālu hoti, parañca abhijjhāya samādapeti, abhijjhāya ca samanuñño hoti, abhijjhāya ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca byāpannacitto hoti, parañca byāpāde samādapeti, byāpāde ca samanuñño hoti, byāpādassa ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca micchādiṭṭhiko hoti, parañca micchādiṭṭhiyā samādapeti, micchādiṭṭhiyā ca samanuñño hoti, micchādiṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, cattārīsāya dhammehi samannāgato [T 5.0331] yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ niraye.

224. “Bhikkhus, one endowed with forty qualities is placed in hell just as if brought and deposited there. With which forty? One personally destroys life, encourages others in the destruction of life, approves of the destruction of life, and speaks in praise of the destruction of life; one personally takes what is not given, encourages others in taking what is not given, approves of taking what is not given, and speaks in praise of taking what is not given; one personally engages in sexual misconduct, encourages others in sexual misconduct, approves of sexual misconduct, and speaks in praise of sexual misconduct; one personally speaks falsely, encourages others in false speech, approves of false speech, and speaks in praise of false speech; one personally engages in divisive speech, encourages others in divisive speech, approves of divisive speech, and speaks in praise of divisive speech; one personally speaks harshly, encourages others in harsh speech, approves of harsh speech, and speaks in praise of harsh speech; one personally engages in frivolous chatter, encourages others in frivolous chatter, approves of frivolous chatter, and speaks in praise of frivolous chatter; one is personally covetous, encourages others in covetousness, approves of covetousness, and speaks in praise of covetousness; one personally has a mind of ill will, encourages others in ill will, approves of ill will, and speaks in praise of ill will; one personally holds wrong view, encourages others in wrong view, approves of wrong view, and speaks in praise of wrong view. Indeed, Bhikkhus, one endowed with these forty qualities is placed in hell just as if brought and deposited there.

“Cattārīsāya, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge. Katamehi cattārīsāya? Attanā ca pāṇātipātā paṭivirato hoti, parañca pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā ca samanuñño hoti, pāṇātipātā veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca adinnādānā paṭivirato hoti, parañca adinnādānā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, adinnādānā veramaṇiyā ca samanuñño hoti, adinnādānā veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca kāmesumicchācārā paṭivirato hoti, parañca kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇiyā ca samanuñño hoti, kāmesumicchācārā veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca musāvādā paṭivirato hoti, parañca musāvādā veramaṇiyā samādapeti, musāvādā veramaṇiyā ca samanuñño hoti, musāvādā veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca pisuṇāya [P 5.0308] vācāya paṭivirato hoti, parañca pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇiyā [M 3.0511] samādapeti, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇiyā ca samanuñño hoti, pisuṇāya vācāya veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca pharusāya vācāya paṭivirato hoti, parañca pharusāya vācāya veramaṇiyā ca samādapeti, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇiyā ca samanuñño hoti, pharusāya vācāya veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca samphappalāpā paṭivirato hoti, parañca samphappalāpā veramaṇiyā [T 5.0332] samādapeti, samphappalāpā veramaṇiyā ca samanuñño hoti, samphappalāpā veramaṇiyā ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca anabhijjhālu hoti, parañca anabhijjhāya samādapeti, anabhijjhāya ca samanuñño hoti, anabhijjhāya ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca abyāpannacitto hoti, parañca abyāpāde samādapeti, abyāpāde ca samanuñño hoti, abyāpādassa ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati; attanā ca sammādiṭṭhiko hoti[V 3.0275], parañca sammādiṭṭhiyā samādapeti, sammādiṭṭhiyā ca samanuñño hoti, sammādiṭṭhiyā ca vaṇṇaṃ bhāsati – imehi kho, bhikkhave, cattārīsāya dhammehi samannāgato yathābhataṃ nikkhitto evaṃ sagge”ti.

“Bhikkhus, one endowed with forty qualities is placed in heaven just as if brought and set down there. With which forty? One personally abstains from the destruction of life, encourages others in abstention from the destruction of life, approves of abstention from the destruction of life, and speaks in praise of abstention from the destruction of life; one personally abstains from taking what is not given, encourages others in abstention from taking what is not given, approves of abstention from taking what is not given, and speaks in praise of abstention from taking what is not given; one personally abstains from sexual misconduct, encourages others in abstention from sexual misconduct, approves of abstention from sexual misconduct, and speaks in praise of abstention from sexual misconduct; one personally abstains from false speech, encourages others in abstention from false speech, approves of abstention from false speech, and speaks in praise of abstention from false speech; one personally abstains from divisive speech, encourages others in abstention from divisive speech, approves of abstention from divisive speech, and speaks in praise of abstention from divisive speech; one personally abstains from harsh speech, encourages others in abstention from harsh speech, approves of abstention from harsh speech, and speaks in praise of abstention from harsh speech; one personally abstains from frivolous chatter, encourages others in abstention from frivolous chatter, approves of abstention from frivolous chatter, and speaks in praise of abstention from frivolous chatter; one is personally non-covetous, encourages others in non-covetousness, approves of non-covetousness, and speaks in praise of non-covetousness; one personally has a mind without ill will, encourages others in non-ill will, approves of non-ill will, and speaks in praise of non-ill will; one personally holds right view, encourages others in right view, approves of right view, and speaks in praise of right view. Indeed, Bhikkhus, one endowed with these forty qualities is placed in heaven just as if brought and set down there.”

225-228. “Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato khataṃ upahataṃ attānaṃ pariharati…pe… akkhataṃ anupahataṃ attānaṃ pariharati…pe… vīsatiyā, bhikkhave…pe… tiṃsāya, bhikkhave…pe… cattārīsāya, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato khataṃ upahataṃ attānaṃ pariharati…pe….

“Bhikkhus, one endowed with ten qualities carries oneself as wounded and damaged… one carries oneself as unwounded and undamaged… Bhikkhus, with twenty… Bhikkhus, with thirty… Bhikkhus, one endowed with forty qualities carries oneself as wounded and damaged… and so on.”

229-232. “Dasahi[T 5.0333], bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato idhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ [P 5.0309] upapajjati…pe… idhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati. Vīsatiyā, bhikkhave…pe… tiṃsāya, bhikkhave,…pe… cattārīsāya, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato idhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā apāyaṃ duggatiṃ vinipātaṃ nirayaṃ upapajjati…pe… idhekacco kāyassa bhedā paraṃ maraṇā sugatiṃ saggaṃ lokaṃ upapajjati”.

“Bhikkhus, endowed with ten qualities, a certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell… A certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world. Bhikkhus, with twenty… Bhikkhus, with thirty… Bhikkhus, endowed with forty qualities, a certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in a state of deprivation, a bad destination, a place of ruin, in hell… A certain person here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in a good destination, in the heavenly world.”

233-236. “Dasahi, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bālo veditabbo…pe… paṇḍito veditabbo…pe… vīsatiyā, bhikkhave…pe… tiṃsāya, bhikkhave…pe… cattārīsāya, bhikkhave, dhammehi samannāgato bālo veditabbo…pe… paṇḍito veditabbo [M 3.0512] …pe… imehi kho, bhikkhave, cattārīsāya dhammehi samannāgato paṇḍito veditabbo”ti.

“Bhikkhus, one endowed with ten qualities is to be known as a fool… is to be known as a wise person… Bhikkhus, with twenty… Bhikkhus, with thirty… Bhikkhus, one endowed with forty qualities is to be known as a fool… is to be known as a wise person… Indeed, bhikkhus, one endowed with these forty qualities is to be known as a wise person.”

Sāmaññavaggo dutiyo.

The Second Chapter on the Ascetic Life.

23. Rāgapeyyālaṃ

23. The Repetition Section on Lust

237. “Rāgassa[V 3.0276], bhikkhave, abhiññāya dasa dhammā bhāvetabbā. Katame dasa? Asubhasaññā, maraṇasaññā, āhāre paṭikūlasaññā, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññā, aniccasaññā, anicce dukkhasaññā, dukkhe anattasaññā, pahānasaññā, virāgasaññā, nirodhasaññā – rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime dasa dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.

237. “Bhikkhus, for the direct knowledge of lust, ten qualities are to be developed. What ten? The perception of unattractiveness, the perception of death, the perception of repulsiveness in food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in what is impermanent, the perception of not-self in what is suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, and the perception of cessation. Bhikkhus, for the direct knowledge of lust, these ten qualities are to be developed.”

238. “Rāgassa[P 5.0310], bhikkhave, abhiññāya dasa dhammā bhāvetabbā. Katame dasa? Aniccasaññā, anattasaññā, āhāre paṭikūlasaññā, sabbaloke anabhiratasaññā, aṭṭhikasaññā, puḷavakasaññā pulavakasaññā (sī.) puḷuvakasaññā (ka.), vinīlakasaññā, vipubbakasaññā, vicchiddakasaññā, uddhumātakasaññā – rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime dasa dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.

238. “Bhikkhus, for the direct knowledge of lust, ten qualities are to be developed. What ten? The perception of impermanence, the perception of not-self, the perception of repulsiveness in food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of a skeleton, the perception of a worm-infested corpse, the perception of a discolored corpse, the perception of a festering corpse, the perception of a dismembered corpse, and the perception of a bloated corpse. Bhikkhus, for the direct knowledge of lust, these ten qualities are to be developed.”

239. “Rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya dasa dhammā bhāvetabbā. Katame dasa[T 5.0334]? Sammādiṭṭhi, sammāsaṅkappo, sammāvācā, sammākammanto, sammāājīvo, sammāvāyāmo, sammāsati, sammāsamādhi, sammāñāṇaṃ, sammāvimutti – rāgassa, bhikkhave, abhiññāya ime dasa dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.

239. “Bhikkhus, for the direct knowledge of lust, ten qualities are to be developed. What ten? Right View, Right Intention, Right Speech, Right Action, Right Livelihood, Right Effort, Right Mindfulness, Right Concentration, Right Knowledge, and Right Liberation. Bhikkhus, for the direct knowledge of lust, these ten qualities are to be developed.”

240-266. “Rāgassa, bhikkhave, pariññāya…pe… parikkhayāya… pahānāya… khayāya… vayāya… virāgāya… nirodhāya… ( ) (upasamāya) (sī. syā. pī.) aññesaṃ pana nipātānaṃ pariyosāne idaṃ padaṃ na dissati cāgāya… paṭinissaggāya…pe… ime dasa dhammā bhāvetabbā.

“Bhikkhus, for the full understanding of lust… for its complete destruction… for its abandonment… for its destruction… for its fading away… for dispassion… for its cessation… for its relinquishment… for its renunciation… these ten qualities are to be developed.”

267-746. “Dosassa [M 3.0513] …pe… mohassa… kodhassa… upanāhassa… makkhassa… paḷāsassa… issāya… macchariyassa… māyāya… sāṭheyyassa… thambhassa… sārambhassa… mānassa… atimānassa… madassa… pamādassa pariññāya…pe… parikkhayāya… pahānāya [V 3.0277] … khayāya… vayāya… virāgāya… nirodhāya… ( ) (upasamāya) (sī. syā. pī.) aññesaṃ pana nipātānaṃ pariyosāne idaṃ padaṃ na dissati cāgāya… paṭinissaggāya…pe… ime dasa dhammā bhāvetabbā”ti.

“For hatred… for delusion… for anger… for hostility… for contempt… for domineering… for envy… for miserliness… for deceit… for treachery… for stubbornness… for rivalry… for conceit… for arrogance… for vanity… for heedlessness: for their full understanding… for their complete destruction… for their abandonment… for their destruction… for their fading away… for dispassion… for their cessation… for their relinquishment… for their renunciation… these ten qualities are to be developed.”

Rāgapeyyālaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Repetition Section on Lust is concluded.

Dasakanipātapāḷi niṭṭhitā.

The Book of the Tens is concluded.
